# Workflow tabs — research report

Date: 2026-11-16 · Status: report only, nothing built · Decisions 1–5 agreed (section 9), 6 open · Next: the user picks the first wave, then a design doc

---

## 1. The concept

Every workspace keeps the tabs it has today. They are the NetworkBase workflow and they never go away:

> Overview · About · Documents · Updates · Sprints · Tasks · Files · Members · Settings (+ Workspaces in an organization)

At the end of the tab row sits a new **+ Add workflow** button. It opens a list of **workflow tabs**. Picking one adds it as a new tab in that workspace, next to Tasks and Sprints. Different kinds of users add different tabs:

```
Overview  About  Documents  Updates  Sprints  Tasks  Files  Members  Settings  │ Content calendar  Pipeline  │ + Add workflow
└──────────────────────────── defaults (always there) ───────────────────────┘ └──── added by this workspace ───┘
```

- A workflow tab is a ready-made way of working: its own **items** (episodes, clients, events, goals…), its own **fields** (publish date, deal value, venue…), its own **views** (timeline, calendar, table, board, gallery) and its own **actions** (move a stage, send an invoice, register for an event).
- The list is ours (curated). A marketplace where anyone publishes tabs is a later idea, maybe never.
- When someone creates a workspace and picks a category, we can suggest the tabs that fit that category.
- An organization can add a tab to all its workspaces, for example a Course planner for every class.

Why: today a Podcast workspace and a Developer tool workspace get exactly the same tabs. The category picked at creation changes nothing afterwards. Workflow tabs make NetworkBase useful for every category, not only for coders.

---

## 2. How Notion was checked

- NetworkBase's 15 workspace categories come from `src/lib/workspaces/workspace-create-options.ts`.
- Each one was matched to the closest category in the Notion Marketplace (from Notion's own category sitemap, 693 categories). The first page of each was read in Notion's default **Popular** order, which Notion describes as "the most used templates from the past week".
- Notion does not publish all-time usage numbers, so "top 10" means **this week's top 10 in Notion's own Popular order**.
- Broad categories mix in personal templates (holiday planners, habit trackers, fan pages). Those are skipped and the list continues with the next work template; each table says when this happened.
- Four NetworkBase categories have no Notion category of their own:

| NetworkBase category | Notion category used |
|---|---|
| Open source | Engineering |
| Developer tool | Issue tracking |
| Hackathon | Event site + Design sprint |
| Freelance | Client portal + Invoicing + CRM (Notion's broad Freelance list was only personal planners) |

## 4. Workflow tab catalog

Each tab lists: who it's for · items · fields · views · actions · what NetworkBase already has · what it needs (building blocks from section 5).

### Part A — partly there today

#### A1. Project planner (the user's screenshot)
- **For:** Startup, Open source, Dev tool, Web app, Game, Hackathon, Video; organizations (each child workspace is a project)
- **Items:** Projects (or the tasks of one big project)
- **Fields:** status, owner, start date, end date, % progress, priority, depends on
- **Views:** Timeline (bars, Today line, dependency arrows, Month/Quarter zoom) · Active (in-progress only) · Board by status · All (table)
- **Actions:** drag a bar to change dates; drag an edge to change length; draw an arrow to add a dependency; progress comes from finished subtasks
- **Already have:** dependencies (`task_dependencies`), subtasks, assignee, status, priority, due date; sprints have start/end dates
- **Needs:** B1 start date · B2 timeline + table views · B6 progress
- **Organization version:** the org's child workspaces as bars on one timeline (a portfolio view)

#### A2. Roadmap & launches
- **For:** Startup, Web app, Game, Side project, Podcast (season launch)
- **Items:** Milestones and releases, each with a launch checklist
- **Fields:** target date, status (Planned / In progress / Shipped), linked tasks, version, quarter
- **Views:** Timeline by quarter · Board by status · Checklist per launch
- **Actions:** start a launch from a ready-made checklist (pre-launch, launch day, post-launch); finishing all linked tasks marks the milestone shipped
- **Already have:** sprint timeline, sprint goal, tasks, subtasks
- **Needs:** B1 · B2 timeline · B7 checklist presets · B6 progress

#### A3. Bug tracker
- **For:** Open source, Dev tool, Web app, Game
- **Items:** Bugs (an item type next to task)
- **Fields:** severity (Critical / High / Medium / Low), status (New → Triaged → In progress → Fixed → Verified), environment / version, steps to reproduce, reporter, assignee, linked PR
- **Views:** Triage table (new bugs first) · Board by status · By severity
- **Actions:** report a bug from a form (members, or outsiders on public workspaces); triage = set severity + assignee; link the fixing PR
- **Already have:** tasks with priority, labels, assignee, comments; `task_links` already stores PR and issue links; GitHub sync
- **Needs:** B3 fields · B4 item type · B5 form · B2 table

#### A4. Course planner
- **For:** Learning workspaces; every school organization
- **Items:** Units → Lessons, plus the assignments that already exist
- **Fields:** week/unit, lesson date, materials (files, docs), learning goals, linked assignment, done per learner
- **Views:** Calendar (lessons and due dates) · Syllabus (list by unit) · Progress (who finished what) · Grades
- **Actions:** publish a lesson to all classes; attach an assignment; learners tick a lesson as done
- **Already have:** org assignments + hand-in + review queue, sprints already called Unit/Week, sprint materials, org doc templates
- **Needs:** B2 calendar view (the old sprint calendar was removed) · B4 lesson item · B6 progress per learner
- **Note:** grades with weights only if schools ask for it

#### A5. Meetings & decisions
- **For:** Startup, Open source, Dev tool; every team
- **Items:** Meetings (agenda, notes, action items) and Decisions (context, options, choice, owner)
- **Fields:** date, attendees, type (standup, retro, kickoff, 1:1), action items → tasks, decision status
- **Views:** List by date · Decision log table · Calendar
- **Actions:** start from a template (the chat canvas templates already exist: Meeting notes, Weekly status, Retrospective, Decision, Incident report); turn an action item into a task
- **Already have:** canvas templates (in chat channels only), Documents, org doc templates
- **Needs:** a workspace-level home for them · B3 fields · B2 table/calendar

#### A6. Asset library
- **For:** Creative, Video, Podcast, Content, Game
- **Items:** Assets (images, clips, audio takes, brand files) and moodboards
- **Fields:** type, tags, status (Raw / Edited / Final), used in (link to episode, post or task), license / source
- **Views:** Gallery (big thumbnails) · Moodboard (free grid) · Table
- **Actions:** drop files in; tag them; link an asset to a content item
- **Already have:** Files tab (folders, versions, previews, storage limits)
- **Needs:** B2 gallery view · B3 fields on files

### Part B — missing today

#### B1. Content calendar
- **For:** Content/Blog, Podcast, Video, Creative, E-commerce (promotions), Startup (social)
- **Items:** Content pieces: posts, episodes, videos, newsletters
- **Fields:** publish date, channel (Blog, YouTube, Instagram, LinkedIn, Podcast, Newsletter…), stage (Idea → Script/Draft → Record/Shoot → Edit → Scheduled → Published), owner, guest (podcast), SEO keyword, link to the draft doc, published URL
- **Views:** Calendar (month/week by publish date) · Pipeline board by stage · Ideas pool · Table
- **Actions:** move through stages; drag on the calendar to reschedule; a reminder before the publish date; "Published" asks for the live URL and can post an Update
- **Already have:** Documents (drafts), Files (media), Updates (announce), reminders
- **Needs:** B1 dates · B2 calendar · B3 fields · B4 content item type
- **Variants as presets:** Blog, YouTube, Podcast (adds guests), Social

#### B2. Pipeline (clients, sponsors, donors, investors, grants)
- **For:** Freelance, Startup, Creative, Non-profit, Podcast, Video, E-commerce (suppliers), Side project. It came up most often (8 of 15).
- **Items:** Contacts / organizations moving through stages
- **Fields:** name, company, email/link, stage, value (money), probability, owner, next step + date, last contact, notes, source
- **Stage presets:**
  - Clients: New → Contacted → Proposal → Won → Active → Done
  - Sponsors: Prospect → Pitched → Negotiating → Signed → Delivered
  - Donors: Prospect → Asked → Pledged → Received
  - Investors: Target → Intro → Meeting → Due diligence → Committed
  - Grants: Found → Writing → Submitted → Awarded / Declined, with a deadline
- **Views:** Board by stage (with total value per column) · Table · Follow-ups due (calendar)
- **Actions:** log a touch (call, email, meeting); set the next follow-up (reminder); Won turns into a project or an invoice
- **Already have:** board, reminders, comments
- **Needs:** B3 fields · B4 contact item · B6 sums
- **Watch out:** contact details are personal data, so the trust boundary and privacy rules apply

#### B3. Event planner
- **For:** Hackathon, Non-profit, Creative (exhibitions), schools (events, fairs)
- **Items:** Events → schedule blocks, people (guests, volunteers, speakers, judges), vendors, budget lines
- **Fields:** date and time, venue / online link, capacity, role, shift, RSVP status, cost
- **Views:** Run of show (timeline of one day) · Calendar · People table · Checklist · Budget
- **Actions:** public registration / RSVP form; assign volunteers to shifts; day-of checklist
- **Hackathon add-on:** teams form up; projects are handed in through the **existing organization assignments**; judges score through the **existing review queue**
- **Already have:** sprints (time-boxed), assignments + review, members, Cloudflare check for forms
- **Needs:** B1 · B2 timeline + calendar · B3 · B4 · B5 forms · B6 sums (budget, headcount)

#### B4. Goals & OKRs
- **For:** Startup, Non-profit, Web app; organizations
- **Items:** Objectives → Key results
- **Fields:** owner, period (quarter), start value → target value → current value, confidence, linked tasks/projects
- **Views:** Goal tree · Progress table · By owner
- **Actions:** check in weekly (update the value and add a note); progress rolls up from key results to the objective
- **Already have:** sprint goal text
- **Needs:** B3 number fields · B4 · B6 progress roll-up

#### B5. Feedback & requests
- **For:** Web app, Open source, Dev tool, Podcast (listener questions), Creative (critique)
- **Items:** Requests, ideas, support tickets
- **Fields:** type (bug / idea / question), submitted by, votes, status (New → Planned → Building → Done / Won't do), linked task, priority
- **Views:** Inbox table · Top voted · Board by status
- **Actions:** public submit form; members vote; turn a request into a task or a bug; tell voters when it's done
- **Already have:** comments, likes (on updates), notifications, moderation and reporting for public content
- **Needs:** B3 · B4 · B5 forms (with moderation)

#### B6. Money (invoices, budget, expenses, time)
- **For:** Freelance, Side project, Startup, Creative, Non-profit, E-commerce, Video. It came up 7 of 15 times.
- **Items:** Invoices, expenses, income, time entries
- **Fields:** amount, currency, date, category, client/project, status (Draft → Sent → Paid / Overdue), due date, hours × rate
- **Views:** Table with totals · Overdue list · Month summary (in, out, balance) · Budget vs actual
- **Actions:** log time on a task, turn the hours into an invoice line, mark paid, overdue reminder
- **Not in scope:** NetworkBase does **not** take payments or move money. This tab only keeps records.
- **Already have:** reminders
- **Needs:** B3 money/number fields · B4 · B6 sums · B8 time log

#### B7. Inventory & orders
- **For:** E-commerce, Side project (Etsy, print-on-demand), Creative (artwork)
- **Items:** Products, orders, suppliers
- **Fields:** SKU, stock count, reorder level, cost, price, supplier, order status (New → Packed → Shipped → Delivered / Returned)
- **Views:** Product gallery · Stock table (low stock first) · Orders board
- **Actions:** low-stock alert; an order lowers the stock count; a return raises it
- **Already have:** Files for product images
- **Needs:** B2 gallery · B3 · B4 · B6 sums

## 5. Building blocks (what all the tabs share)

The 13 tabs are mostly presets made from these blocks. Build a block once and every tab that uses it gets it.

| # | Block | Today in NetworkBase | Used by |
|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | Start + end date on items | Only sprints have start/end; tasks have only a due date | Planner, Roadmap, Content, Event, Course |
| B2 | Views: Table, Timeline, Calendar, Gallery | Board only; the sprint calendar was removed | Every tab |
| B3 | Custom fields: text, number, money, single/multi select, date, person, URL, checkbox, file, link to another item | Fixed task columns + labels | Every Part B tab, Bug, Meetings, Assets |
| B4 | Item types beyond "task" (Client, Episode, Event, Goal, Bug, Product…) | `tasks.kind` exists (task / assignment) | Every Part B tab, Bug, Course |
| B5 | Forms: people outside the workspace submit an item | Cloudflare check + moderation exist; no forms | Bug, Feedback, Event registration, client intake |
| B6 | Sums & progress: column totals, % from subtasks, roll-ups | Subtasks exist; no sums | Planner, Roadmap, Pipeline, Money, Goals, Inventory |
| B7 | Checklist presets (an item starts with ready-made subtasks) | Subtasks exist | Roadmap & launches, Event, Content |
| B8 | Time log on items | None | Money (freelance) |
| B9 | Guest access to one tab (client portal) | Members and public visibility only | Freelance, Agency (later, security-heavy) |
| B10 | The tab switch: add / remove a workflow tab per workspace; an org adds it to all its workspaces | A per-workspace tab switch exists for **public visibility** (`publicTabVisibility`) | The + Add workflow button itself |

**Already in place and reusable:** board · dependencies · subtasks · comments · watchers · reminders · `task_links` (PR/issue) · labels · `tasks.kind` · assignments + review queue · org doc templates · chat canvas templates · Files · Cloudflare check · moderation · notifications · storage limits.

## 7. Left out on purpose

- **Personal life templates:** habit tracker, journal, wishlists, holiday planners, reading and watch lists, recipes, personal finance, flashcards. They're popular on Notion but they're single-person tools, and NetworkBase is for working together.
- **AI writing helpers** (proofread, PRD from notes, reply drafter). These are agent features, not tabs.
- **Taking real payments.** The Money tab keeps records only.
- **The marketplace** (anyone publishing tabs). It comes after the curated list proves itself.
- **Guest/client portal (B9).** It's valuable for freelancers, but it opens the workspace to outsiders and needs its own security design.

---

## 9. Decisions (agreed 2026-11-16)

Questions 1–5 were answered with the recommended answers below, and the user accepted them. Question 6 is still open.

### 1. Are workflow items tasks? → Work items yes, plain records no
- **Work items are tasks:** Episode, Client, Bug, Event, Goal, Lesson, Request, Milestone and Order. Each has someone doing it, a stage and a date. As tasks they get what already exists: My Work, assignee, comments, subtasks, watchers, reminders, dependencies, sprints, review, notifications, CLI and agents. `tasks.kind` already exists (task / assignment), so each one becomes a new kind, plus the workflow tab it belongs to and its own field values.
- **Plain records are not tasks:** expense lines, time entries, products and stock counts. Nobody "does" them, and putting them in tasks would break task numbers, inflate board counts and clutter My Work. They go in one small table of their own.
- **Assets stay files:** the Asset library uses Files with extra fields, not tasks.
- **Why:** no rebuilding of a dozen working features, and task numbers stay honest.

### 2. Removing a tab → Hide by default; deleting is explicit and goes through Trash
- The remove dialog shows what the tab holds (e.g. "Content calendar has 24 items, 6 open") and offers two choices:
  - **Hide tab (default):** the items are kept but stop showing everywhere (Tasks, My Work, reminders). Adding the tab back restores everything.
  - **Delete tab and items:** the items go to Trash for 30 days (the existing Trash rule), then they're gone for good.
- **Why:** nobody loses work by accident, and deleting follows a rule users already know.

### 3. Who can add and remove tabs → Owners and admins (the same people who can open Settings)
- Reuses the existing Settings permission: owner, workspace admin, or an inherited org admin (`canManageSettings` in `WorkspaceDashboardClient.tsx`). No new permission rule.
- Members use the tab but can't add or remove it.
- **Why:** a tab changes the whole team's workspace, so it's an admin decision like any other setting.

### 4. Org-added tabs → Locked in workspaces; workspaces can still add their own
- An org-added tab shows "Added by [org name]", and its remove option is greyed out inside the workspace.
- Workspace admins can still add other tabs for themselves.
- Only the organization can remove its tab, and that removes it everywhere using the decision 2 choices.
- **Why:** pushing a tab (e.g. a Course planner for every class) is about everyone working the same way. One rule, no "required vs suggested" setting to explain.

### 5. Suggest at creation → Yes, on the wizard's Settings step, with only the top one ticked
- `Phase4Settings` (after the category is picked) shows "Add workflow tabs" with the category's suggestions from section 6. Example for Podcast: Content calendar (ticked), Pipeline and Asset library (not ticked).
- A new organization gets the same choice, aimed at its child workspaces (e.g. Course planner for an education org).
- **Why:** if users never see these tabs, they won't find them. One tick gives a useful start without crowding the tab row.

### 6. Free vs Pro → Open
Decided by the user in the monetization work (Free + Pro, numeric limits). The question: does Free get a set number of workflow tabs, or every tab with limits on items?

### 7. A tab is a job, not a pile of data (section 28.1, agreed 2026-11-16)
Views and fields blend into a default tab. A workflow with a different job (Bugs, Requests, Content, Roadmap) gets its own tab over the same tasks. Replaces the earlier "display choice, movable later".

### 8. + Add workflow adds to a default tab or adds a same-data tab; own tabs with their own data are parked (section 28.2, agreed 2026-11-16)

---

## 10. How each workflow is designed: the 18 layers

Every workflow is designed end to end against these layers. Categories are done one at a time. The first time a shared tab comes up, it's designed in full; later categories add only their presets, views and document templates.

### What the tab is
1. **Getting it:** where the tab is offered (the create wizard on its Settings step, + Add workflow, or added by an organization) and what it looks like the first time, before it has any items.
2. **Setting it up:** the starting stages, fields, wording and example items for this category, and what an admin can change afterwards.
3. **Items:** what one item holds, every way it can be created (button, form, from another item, chat, CLI), and whether it's a task kind, a record or a file (decision 1).

### How it looks and works
4. **Views:** each view, what's on screen, and what you can drag, filter, sort, group and search.
5. **Actions and flow:** how an item moves from start to finish, who does each step, and what happens at each change (reminders, linked items, Updates).
6. **The tab's own surfaces, at Tasks-level depth:** each tab gets its own surfaces, shaped by what it's for, never a copy of the Tasks layout. Each surface gets the same care Tasks got:
   - a calm first screen, with depth one step away in ⋯ menus, panel sections, shortcuts and filters
   - every control, count and message specified for every view and role
   - its own create flow
   - its own item panel, with sections chosen for that item type
   - built from NetworkBase's own shared parts wherever one fits
   - finished only when it holds up next to the Tasks tab

### How it fits NetworkBase
7. **Design spec:** the colour tokens, fonts, corner shapes, badges, movement, Lucide icons, density and empty states each surface uses, cited by section of `docs/design/networkbase-application-design-specification.html`. Each tab also gets its own design contract test, like `tests/unit/task-design-contract.test.ts`.
8. **Words:** item names, stage names, buttons and empty messages, matched to `src/lib/copy/terms.ts` and `docs/design/settings-copy-glossary.md`.
9. **Links to the rest of NetworkBase:** Tasks, My Work, sprints, review, Files, Documents, Updates, chat, global search, deep links, the CLI and agents.
10. **People:** what owners, admins, members and the public each see and can do; the organization version (locked tabs, decision 4); and who can add or remove the tab (decision 3).

### When things aren't normal
11. **States:** loading skeleton, error, read-only public view, no permission, live updates from other people, two people editing at once, undo.
12. **Edges:** empty, too many items, deleted or departed people, mistakes, and removing the tab (hide versus delete, decision 2).
13. **Phone:** how each surface works on a narrow screen, with touch alternatives to dragging.
14. **Accessibility:** keyboard paths, screen-reader labels, and a way to do every drag action without dragging.

### Behind the scenes
15. **Notifications and activity:** which events notify whom, at which level (Required / Important / Normal / Summary), and what goes into the activity history.
16. **Trust and data:** who can read or write each piece, what's personal data, moderation of public forms, and the limits we track (Free/Pro left blank until decision 6).
17. **Reuse vs new:** which parts already exist in the code, and which building blocks (B1–B10) the tab needs.
18. **How we know it works:** one usage signal per tab, and the checks to run once it's built.

### How the reference template is chosen (agreed 2026-11-16)
For every own tab, preset or view, the Notion reference is picked on **two things together**:
1. **Rating:** the score and the number of ratings (more ratings weigh more than a slightly higher score).
2. **UI quality, at the level of "Anthropic's project planner"** (the user's reference screenshot):
   - calm and clean, with few colours
   - a clear hierarchy (title → views → filters → content)
   - real views (timeline, board, table), not just a long page
   - tidy property lists on item pages
   - nothing decorative that gets in the way

The top candidates are opened live. Each design round shows a **candidates table** (rating + UI verdict) and says why the chosen one wins on both. A highly rated template with a messy UI is used only for its ideas, never as the layout model.

### How each Notion template is sorted, and how deep it goes

| Label | Meaning | Layers |
|---|---|---|
| **Own tab** | A full workflow tab | All 18 |
| **Tab preset** | A version of a shared tab (e.g. Pipeline → Sales) | Only those that differ from the shared tab, usually 2, 3, 5, 8 and 18 |
| **View** | A new view inside an existing tab | 4, 5, 6, 7, 11–14 |
| **Document template** | A ready-made doc in Documents | 1, 3, 8, 9 |
| **Already covered** | NetworkBase already does it | What covers it, plus any small gaps |

### 11.2 Pipeline (own tab, all 18 layers)

**Updated 2026-11-16 by 12.3 (the Clients round).** Notion's **Sales CRM** (4.8 from 900+) became the layout reference for every pipeline, on rating and UI quality. It brought five upgrades for **all presets**, written into the layers below:
1. a **Dashboard** view (now the desktop default)
2. a one-click **Contacted** button
3. a **Priority** field
4. the Table's sum row (already in place)
5. a **one-scroll item page** with Background info and History of interactions (replacing the section tabs)

Marked **[call]** = a decision made in this design that the user can overrule.

#### 1. Getting it
- **Where it's offered:**
  - **+ Add workflow** at the end of the tab row (owners and admins, decision 3).
  - The create wizard's Settings step for Startup, Freelance, Creative, Non-profit, E-commerce, Podcast, Video and Side project (decision 5).
  - Added by an organization (decision 4).
- **The + Add workflow list:** a dialog listing every workflow tab as a row with an icon, a name, one line on what it's for, and "Suggested for [category]" when it fits. Picking **Pipeline** goes to a second step: **Choose your first pipeline**, offering:
  - Sales
  - Investors
  - Collaborations
  - Clients
  - Sponsors
  - Donors
  - Grants
  - Blank

  Each preset shows its stages as a small row of stage names, so the user sees what they'll get.
- **One tab, many pipelines [call]:** a workspace has at most one Pipeline tab. A startup that wants Sales and Investors adds a second pipeline inside the tab (see the pipeline switcher in layer 6). This keeps the tab row short.
- **First look:** the board shows the preset's stage columns, all empty. Each column has a one-line hint, and the first column's hint is the strongest. For Sales: "Add the people or companies you're talking to." There are **no example items [call]**: fake data has to be cleaned up and gets mistaken for real data.

#### 2. Setting it up
- **The Startup presets:**

| Preset | Item name | Stages (open → closed) | Extra fields |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Sales** | Deal | New → Contacted → Meeting → Proposal → Negotiating → **Won** / **Lost** | Value, Expected close, Source |
| **Investors** | Investor | Target → Intro → First meeting → Partner meeting → Due diligence → Term sheet → **Committed** / **Passed** | Firm, Check size, Round, Intro by (member), Data room shared |
| **Collaborations** | Collab | Prospect → Pitched → Negotiating → Signed → Live → **Paid** / **Dropped** | Platform, Audience size, Deliverables, Fee |

- **Stage types:** every stage is **Open**, **Won** or **Lost**. Won and Lost stages close the item. Each pipeline needs at least one Open stage and exactly one Won and one Lost stage, so totals and win rates stay meaningful.
- **Probability per stage** (for weighted value): set by the preset, for example Sales goes 10 / 20 / 40 / 60 / 80 %. Admins can change it, and a single item can override it.
- **What admins can change afterwards** (⋯ → Edit stages / Edit fields):
  - rename, reorder, add or remove stages
  - change a stage's type or probability
  - add, hide or rename fields
  - Removing a stage that still holds items asks where to move them first.
  - The preset itself never changes, so the next workspace still starts clean.
- **Currency:** each pipeline has one currency, defaulting to the workspace owner's locale. Items can't mix currencies inside one pipeline **[call]**, so totals stay correct without currency conversion.

#### 3. Items
- **What one item is:** a **task of kind `deal`** (decision 1). It inherits assignee, comments, files, watchers, reminders, activity, undo and My Work. It belongs to one pipeline and one stage.
- **What an item holds:**
  - **Always:** name, stage, assigned to (one person, default = creator), value, **priority** (Low / Medium / High / Urgent, the task scale), next step (text) + next step date, background info (free text)
  - **Contact:** company / organisation, contact person, email, link (website or LinkedIn). Phone is **off by default** (it's personal data, see layer 16).
  - **Preset fields** (section 2), source, labels, notes (the description)
  - **Automatic:** created date, days in stage, last touch date, closed date, lost reason
- **Every way to create one:**
  1. **+ New [item name]** in the header
  2. **+** at the top of a stage column (creates it in that stage)
  3. **Quick add** in the Follow-ups view (name + next step date only)
  4. **From a closed Won item:** "New deal with this client" copies the contact fields
  5. **CSV import** (⋯ menu, admins): map the columns, preview the first 5 rows, then import
  6. **CLI / agents** (layer 9)
- **Duplicates:** on create, if the company or email matches an open item, a quiet note appears under the field: "Acme already has an open deal: Acme renewal". The user can still save.

#### 4. Views
| View | What's on screen | Drag | Filter / sort / group |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Dashboard** (default on desktop) | From Sales CRM: a labelled **ring of value by stage**, one big **Open value** number (with weighted value and "Won this month" under it), **bars of value by person**, then the board below them. Plain SVG, muted colours | Cards on the board part, as on Board | Assigned to, priority, source, labels |
| **Board** | Stage columns. Each header shows name, count and total value | Cards between stages; Won and Lost drop zones slide up from the bottom while dragging | Assigned to, priority, source, labels, value range; sorted by next step date |
| **Follow-ups** (default on phone) | A list grouped **Overdue · Today · This week · Later · No next step** | — | Mine / everyone |
| **Table** | One row per item, all fields as columns, a totals row at the bottom | Reorder columns | Any column; group by stage or assigned to |
| **Closed** | Won and Lost items: closed date, value, lost reason | — | Won / Lost, date range |

- The header filter switches between **Open · Won · Lost · All**, and **Mine / Everyone** is a separate toggle. A **High priority** filter is one click (from the reference's "High Priority" view).
- The Clients preset adds a **Directory** view (12.3).
- Search covers name, company, contact person and email.

#### 5. Actions and flow
1. **Create** → the item starts in the first Open stage, assigned to its creator.
2. **Work it:**
   - **Log a touch** (call, email, meeting or note) with a date and a short note. Every touch updates "last touch". On the item page this is **+ New interaction**.
   - **Contacted** (one click on a card, row or item page): logs a touch "Contacted today" and updates last touch, the reference's fastest action.
   - **Set the next step** (what + when). The date becomes a reminder to the assignee.
3. **Move stages:** drag, or **Move to…** in the card's ⋯. The stage's probability updates the weighted total.
4. **Won:** a small dialog asks:
   - closed date (default today)
   - final value (default the current value)
   - **Then what?** (all optional): Create a project task in Tasks · Create an invoice (only when a Money tab exists) · Post an Update (off by default, because deals are often private)
5. **Lost:** a reason is required, picked from a short list (Price, Timing, Went with someone else, No reply, Not a fit, Other) plus a note. The reasons feed the Closed view.
6. **Reopen:** a closed item can be moved back to an Open stage. Its history is kept.
7. **Gone quiet:** an open item with no touch for N days (default 14, set per pipeline) shows a "Quiet 14d" chip. It also appears in the assignee's weekly summary.

Who does what: whoever the item is assigned to works it. Any member can log touches and comment. Admins edit stages, fields and pipelines.

#### 6. The tab's own surfaces
**S1. Header** (one line on desktop)
- **Pipeline switcher:** "Sales ▾". The menu lists the workspace's pipelines with their open counts, then **+ Add pipeline** (opens the preset picker). Only shown once there are 2 or more pipelines, or to admins.
- **Totals:** "12 open · ₹4,20,000 · weighted ₹1,86,000". Numbers use the mono font. All counts load in one read and update live, with no polling.
- **Search field**, **Open / Won / Lost / All** filter, **Mine / Everyone** toggle, **view switcher** (Dashboard / Board / Follow-ups / Table / Closed, plus Directory in the Clients preset).
- **+ New [item name]** (primary button).
- **⋯ menu:** Edit stages · Edit fields · Who can see this pipeline · Import CSV · Export CSV · Hide pipeline. Admins see all of these; members see Export only if the admin allows it **[call: off by default]**.

**S2. Board**
- **Column header:** stage name, count and total value; for Open stages, the probability % in muted text.
- **Column body:** cards in next-step-date order, overdue first.
- **Column foot:** "Show 25 more" when a column holds more than 25.
- **While dragging:** Won and Lost drop zones slide up (the existing assignment drop-sheet pattern). Dropping on either opens its dialog (layer 5).
- **Empty column:** a dashed area with the stage's hint.

**S3. Card** (small on purpose, like the task card)
- **Line 1:** name, then the value on the right (mono)
- **Line 2:** company · the assignee's avatar
- **Line 3:** next step date (overdue = danger colour + icon + "2d overdue"), "12d in stage" (mono, muted), and a touch-count icon
- **Chips only when they apply:** "Quiet 14d", "No next step"
- **Priority badge** when High or Urgent.
- **⋯ on hover or focus:** Contacted · Move to… · Log a touch · Set next step · Assign · Copy link · Delete

**S4. Follow-ups list**
- Rows: name · company · next step text · date · assignee
- Two quick buttons on each row: **Log a touch** and **Snooze** (+1 day, +3 days, next Monday, pick a date)
- A **Quick add** line at the top

**S5. Table**
- Sticky name column, inline editing of fields, a totals row (sum of value and weighted value), column picker in ⋯.

**S6. Item page** (side panel, **one scroll**, as in the Sales CRM reference and our other tabs; **Open as full page** in ⋯)
```
Shri Ansari                                     [ Contacted ]  ⋯
  Added          Mar 10, 2026
  Assigned to    (A) Asha
  Stage          Proposal          Priority   High
  Company        Mode              Value      ₹1,25,000
  Email          shri@mode.co      Phone      +91 …
  Last contact   Feb 9, 2026       Expected close  Apr 5, 2026
  Next step      Send revised quote · Nov 20
  Rate           Hourly · ₹1,500   (Clients preset)
──────────────────────────────
Background info      free text: who they are, what they need
──────────────────────────────
History of interactions                         + New interaction
  Nov 12 · Meeting  "Walked through the proposal…"   (from ⚡ Client meeting)
  Nov 3  · Email    "Sent first quote"
──────────────────────────────
Comments · Files · Activity
```
- **Properties:** a label-and-value list, each value editable in place; the preset's own fields follow the shared ones.
- **Next step:** always in the property list, with its date; changing it updates the reminder.
- **History of interactions:** the touches, newest first; **+ New interaction** opens the composer (type, date, note). Meetings from the Meetings tab linked to this item appear here too.
- **Comments · Files · Activity:** at the bottom (UnderlineTabs), reusing the task comments, task files and activity.

**S7. Create dialog**
- Asks for **name, company, value, stage** (default = the first stage, or the column it was opened from), **assigned to** (default = me) and **next step + date** (optional).
- **More fields** expands the rest.
- After saving, a toast offers **Open** and **Add another**.

**S8. Won / Lost dialogs** (layer 5)

**S9. Stage editor**
- A list of stages with drag handles: name, type (Open / Won / Lost), probability, and a remove button.
- Removing a stage that holds items asks where to move them.
- Rules are checked live (at least one Open stage, exactly one Won and one Lost).

**S10. Field editor**
- A list of fields with name, type (text, number, money, select, date, person, link, checkbox) and shown / hidden.
- Preset fields can be hidden but not deleted.

**S11. Overview card** (on the workspace's Overview tab)
- Open count, total value, follow-ups due today, and a link to the tab.

#### 7. Design spec
- **Type (Section 04):** Instrument Sans for names, headings and buttons; JetBrains Mono for money, counts, days in stage and "12 open".
- **Motion (Section 05):** card drag and the drop-zone slide use 180 ms ease-out with no spring, the same as the Tasks board.
- **Badges (Section 10):** stage badges and the "Quiet" / "No next step" chips use the precision badge geometry. No fully round pills.
- **Colour:**
  - Clay (brand primary) for the primary button only
  - Ink neutrals for structure
  - Paper surfaces
  - status colours: Won = success, Lost = muted ink, overdue = danger
  - colour never appears alone: overdue always carries an icon and words
- **Filters:** the segmented control from the Tasks filters (Section 05 drafting segmented control).
- **Icons (Lucide):**
  - Handshake: the tab
  - Phone, Mail, Users, StickyNote: touch types
  - CircleCheck: Won
  - CircleX: Lost
  - Clock: next step
- **Density, spacing, corner radii:** follow the spec's "Density in use", spacing scale and corner radii sections.
- **Empty states:** follow the empty-state contract.
- **Contract test:** `tests/unit/pipeline-design-contract.test.ts`, with the same rules as the task contract (no rounded-full, no raw zinc/indigo/blue, 180 ms motion, badge geometry, typography).

#### 8. Words
- **Tab name:** "Pipeline". The item name comes from the preset: Deal / Investor / Collab / Client / Sponsor / Donor / Grant. "CRM" never appears in the interface.
- **Use "Assigned to", never "Owner" [call]:** "Owner" is already a workspace role, and tasks already say "Assigned to".
- **Never "Lead":** the terms file bans "Lead" on its own and "a/new/the lead". The first Sales stage is therefore **New**, and people being pursued are "deals", "contacts" or "prospects".
- **Key phrases:**
  - "Next step"
  - "Log a touch"
  - "Won" / "Lost" (or the preset's own words: Committed / Passed)
  - "Quiet for 14 days"
  - "12d in stage"
  - "weighted"
- **Empty messages by view:**
  - Board (empty): "No deals yet. Add the people or companies you're talking to."
  - Follow-ups (nothing due): "Nothing due. Every open deal has a next step later than today."
  - Closed (empty): "Nothing closed yet."
- All words are checked against `src/lib/copy/terms.ts` and the settings copy glossary before building.

#### 9. Links to the rest of NetworkBase
- **My Work:** an item whose next step is due shows up for its assignee as "Follow up: Acme · Send proposal". This works because it's a task kind.
- **Tasks board:** pipeline items **don't appear** on the Tasks board or in its counts **[call]**, because they have their own tab. A Won item's "Create a project task" puts a normal task on the Tasks board, linked back to the deal.
- **Sprints:** pipeline items can't be added to sprints **[call]**, because sales doesn't run in sprints.
- **Review:** not used.
- **Files:** each item's files sit with the item (as task files do). The Investors preset adds a **Data room** folder in Files and a "Data room shared" checkbox per investor.
- **Documents:** an item can link to a doc (e.g. the proposal).
- **Updates:** only through the optional Won → Post an Update.
- **Chat:** an item can be shared into a channel as a card (the chat card kinds include "task", so it reuses that with a deal snapshot). Card contents follow the same visibility rules (layer 16).
- **Global search:** finds items by name and company, for members only.
- **Deep links:** every item has its own link that opens its panel. "Copy link" is in the ⋯ menus.
- **CLI and agents:** the existing task commands and tools work with a kind filter (`nb tasks --kind deal`; MCP `networkbase_task_list` with `kind: "deal"`). Two small additions: **log a touch** and **move to stage**. The agent briefing includes "follow-ups due today".

#### 10. People
| Who | Can |
|---|---|
| Owner / admin | Everything: pipelines, stages, fields, who can see, import, export, delete any item, hide or remove the tab |
| Member | Create, edit, move, log touches, comment, attach files; delete items they created; export only if allowed |
| Public / non-member | **Never sees the Pipeline tab**, even on a public workspace. Its public-visibility switch is fixed to "Members only" **[call]**, because it holds other people's contact details. |
| Organization | An org can add Pipeline to itself (e.g. an incubator tracking sponsors). If it pushes the tab to child workspaces, each child gets its **own, empty** pipeline; the org can't read child pipelines unless its admins already have inherited admin rights. |

- **Private pipelines:** each pipeline has **Who can see: Everyone in the workspace / Owners and admins only**. Example: Investors is often founders-only. A hidden pipeline doesn't appear in the switcher, search, My Work, chat cards or counts for people who can't see it.

#### 11. States
- **Loading:** a skeleton of the stage columns with 3 card shapes each (like the Tasks skeleton). The header totals show "—" until loaded.
- **Error:** the existing tab error boundary with a Retry button. One failed column never blanks the whole board.
- **No permission:** a private pipeline simply isn't listed. A direct link to an item in it opens "You don't have access to this item."
- **Live updates:** moves, new items and touches from other people appear without a refresh (the same live channel as tasks).
- **Two people at once:** if two people move the same card, the last move wins, and the other person sees a toast: "Moved to Proposal by Asha just now".
- **Undo:** moving, closing, deleting and bulk changes show an **Undo** toast (the existing undo system).

#### 12. Edges
- **Empty:** covered in layers 1 and 8.
- **Too many items:** columns show 25 at a time; the Closed view pages by month; the table pages at 100 rows. Totals are always computed on the server, never from the cards on screen.
- **Assignee leaves the workspace:** their items stay and show "Former member". The "Assigned to" filter gets an **Unassigned / former** option, and admins can reassign in bulk.
- **Contact data entered by mistake:** clearing a field really clears it, and the activity history notes "email removed" without showing the old value.
- **A stage removed while it holds items:** blocked until the items are moved (S9).
- **Value left empty:** allowed. The item counts in the column but adds nothing to the totals.
- **Removing the tab:** decision 2. **Hide** keeps everything and pauses reminders. **Delete** sends all items to Trash for 30 days, and the contact data is deleted for good after that.

#### 13. Phone
- **Follow-ups is the default view**, because the board is too wide for a phone.
- **Board on a phone:** one stage at a time, with a row of stage chips to switch (scrolls sideways) and the stage's count and total under it.
- **Moving a card:** the card's ⋯ → **Move to…** (a bottom sheet listing the stages), with no dragging needed.
- **Item panel:** opens as a full-screen sheet. The **Log a touch** buttons sit at the bottom within thumb reach.

#### 14. Accessibility
- **Keyboard:** arrow keys move between cards and columns; Enter opens the panel; **M** opens Move to…; **T** opens Log a touch; **N** opens New. The same keys work in the Follow-ups list.
- **Screen readers:** each card reads as one sentence: "Acme, 50,000 rupees, Proposal, next step overdue by 2 days, assigned to Asha."
- **No dragging needed:** every drag action has a menu version (Move to…, Won, Lost).
- **Colour is never the only signal:** overdue, quiet and won/lost always carry words and icons too.

#### 15. Notifications and activity
| Event | Who | Level |
|---|---|---|
| Item assigned to you | New assignee | Important |
| Next step due today | Assignee | Normal (the existing task reminder) |
| Next step overdue | Assignee | Summary (daily) |
| Won / Lost | Assignee + watchers | Normal |
| Mentioned in a comment or touch | The mentioned person | Important (existing) |
| Gone quiet | Assignee | Summary (weekly) |

- **Activity history per item:** created, every stage move (from → to), value change, assignee change, touch logged, next step set or changed, won/lost with reason, reopened.

#### 16. Trust and data
- **Personal data:** contact names, emails, phones and links belong to people outside NetworkBase. Because of that:
  - members only (layer 10)
  - never shown publicly
  - not in search for outsiders
  - kept out of chat cards for people who can't see the pipeline
- **Agents:** an agent reads pipeline items only with a member's own access, the same as tasks.
- **Export:** admins by default; every export is written to the activity history (who, when, how many rows).
- **Import:** CSV only, with a size cap. Rows are checked; bad rows are skipped and listed, never half-imported.
- **Deletion:** a deleted item goes to Trash for 30 days, then its contact data is gone for good.
- **Non-goals:** NetworkBase doesn't send emails to contacts, track email opens, or scrape LinkedIn.
- **Limits to track** (values come with decision 6): pipelines per workspace, open items per pipeline, CSV rows per import.

#### 17. Reuse vs new
- **Reused as is:**
  - task data (assignee, comments, files, watchers, reminders, activity, undo, My Work)
  - the board drag engine and the assignment drop sheets
  - the task panel shell
  - ConfirmDialog, dropdown menu, filter panel, SearchField, EmptyState, skeleton, UnderlineTabs
  - DateTimeField, UserAvatar, the badge styles
  - the tab error boundary, live updates, the chat task card, task tools in the CLI/MCP
- **New:**
  - kind `deal` (B4)
  - pipeline + stage tables (stage type, probability, order)
  - item fields (B3: value, company, contact, source, preset fields)
  - totals and weighted value (B6)
  - a touch type and date on comments
  - views: Follow-ups, Table, Closed (B2)
  - Won/Lost dialogs, stage editor, field editor, pipeline switcher
  - CSV import/export
  - the Overview card
  - the tab switch itself (B10)
  - the "members only" lock on the tab's public visibility

#### 18. How we know it works
- **Usage signal:** the share of workspaces with a Pipeline tab that still log at least one touch a week, 3 weeks after adding it.
- **Checks once built:**
  - the design contract test
  - unit tests: totals and weighted value, stage rules (one Won, one Lost, at least one Open), duplicate note, quiet chip
  - permission tests: a private pipeline is invisible everywhere for members; the tab is never public
  - end to end: create → log a touch → move → Won → project task created
  - phone check
  - keyboard-only check
