### 11.3 Project planner (own tab, all 18 layers)

**Look and layout come from the user's reference:** Notion's "Anthropic's project planner", all three of its screens (Timeline, Active table, project page). It's built from NetworkBase's own parts (fonts, colours, shared components), not Notion's look and not Anthropic's logo or illustration. Notion calls the template a "dual-database": a Projects list plus a Tasks list, linked together. Here that's the Project planner tab plus the existing Tasks tab, joined by **Part of**.

**Agreed changes from an exact copy (2026-11-16):**
1. **No cover picture, logo tile or page title.** The workspace header already sits above the tabs; the "◎ Projects" title row stands in for them.
2. **Project icons:** each project can have an emoji **or** a Lucide icon. This is the only exception to the Lucide rule, because it's content people create, not interface.
3. **Badge shape:** status, priority and filter chips keep the same colours and the same places, but use our badge shape (no fully round pills).
4. **"Assigned to" instead of "Owner"**, because Owner is a workspace role.
5. **Today marker and arrows in Clay**, the brand colour, close to the reference's terracotta/orange. Red stays for overdue.

Marked **[call]** = a decision made in this design that the user can overrule.

#### 1. Getting it
- **Where it's offered:**
  - **+ Add workflow** (owners and admins)
  - the wizard's Settings step: **ticked by default** for Startup and Game dev (where it's the first suggestion), and shown unticked for Open source, Hackathon, Web app, Developer tool and Video (section 6)
  - added by an organization
- **In the + Add workflow dialog:** a Project planner row with a small preview of the timeline. There are no presets to choose; the tab works the same in every category, and only the words and example hints change (layer 2).
- **First look:**
  - the Timeline view, empty, with the Today marker and the current month in view
  - the three status groups shown, each with 0
  - one hint in the middle of the grid: "A project groups tasks with a start and an end. Drag across the timeline to add one, or press **+ New project**."

#### 2. Setting it up
- **Statuses**, in the reference's groups (*Planning* sits in the *In progress* group). The groups are fixed so the counts stay meaningful; admins can rename the statuses.

| Group | Statuses |
|---|---|
| To do | Not started |
| In progress | Planning · In progress · Paused |
| Complete | Done · Cancelled |

- **Fields:** icon, name, status, assigned to (one person), people (several), dates (start → end), completion, priority, blocked by / blocking, summary, labels, plus the "About this project" document area. Admins can add their own fields (B3), for example "Budget" or "Client".
- **Priority** uses the task scale that already exists: Low / Medium / High / Urgent.
- **Per-category hints only:** for example, Video's empty hint says "e.g. Episode 12 production" and Hackathon's says "e.g. Build the demo".
- **Zoom default:** Month. Admins can change it to Week or Quarter.
- **Working days:** weekends are shaded. Admins can turn shading off.

#### 3. Items
- **What one item is:** a **task of kind `project`** (decision 1). It inherits assignee, people (the existing team members), comments, files, watchers, reminders, activity, undo, labels and **blocked by** (the existing `task_dependencies`, which already refuses loops).
- **Tasks belong to projects:** a normal task gets a new **Part of** field pointing at a project **[call]**. One task can belong to one project. It stays a normal task on the Tasks board and in sprints, and shows a small project chip.
- **What an item holds:**
  - icon, name, status, dates, assigned to, people, priority, labels
  - summary: one short paragraph, shown in the properties
  - "About this project": a free document area (goals, scope, notes)
  - blocked by / blocking
  - tasks that are part of it
- **Completion [call]:**
  - **automatic:** done tasks ÷ all tasks that are part of the project, ignoring cancelled ones
  - **no tasks yet:** completion comes from the project's own checklist (subtasks)
  - **neither:** an admin can type a % by hand, shown with a small "set by hand" mark
- **Every way to create one:**
  1. **+ New project** in the title row
  2. **Drawing on the timeline:** drag across an empty row; a quick-create bubble opens with those dates filled in
  3. **+** in a status group (creates it with that status)
  4. **From Tasks:** select several tasks → ⋯ → **Group into a project** (makes a project and sets their Part of)
  5. **From a Won Pipeline deal:** "Create a project" (alongside "Create a project task")
  6. **CLI / agents** (layer 9)

#### 4. Views
The view tabs are an underline row with icons: **Timeline · Active · Board · All**. Timeline is the default on desktop; Active is the default on a phone.

| View | What's on screen | Drag | Filter / sort / group |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Timeline** | Left: project names in status groups. Right: bars on a date grid with the Today marker and dependency arrows (S4) | Move a bar; stretch either end; drag from a bar's end dot onto another bar to add "blocked by"; drag from the No dates tray onto the grid | The filter chips; zoom Week / Month / Quarter; ‹ **Today** › |
| **Active** | A table grouped by status (Planning, In progress) with columns **Project name · Status · Assigned to · Dates · Priority · Completion · Blocked by** (S5) | — | Starts filtered to `Status: In progress group`; sort by any column |
| **Board** | Columns by status, with cards (S6) | Cards between statuses | The filter chips |
| **All** | Every project in one table with every field, plus a totals row (count, average completion) | Reorder columns | Any column; group by status or assigned to |

- **Show sprints** (a toggle in ⋯ on Timeline) draws the workspace's sprints as a thin band across the top of the grid, so plans and sprints can be read together.
- **Search** covers project names and summaries.

#### 5. Actions and flow
1. **Create** → status **Not started**. If it has no dates, it waits in the **No dates** tray.
2. **Plan:**
   - give it dates (drag, or set them on the project page)
   - add tasks to it (Part of)
   - draw dependencies
   - move it to **Planning**
3. **Start:** move it to **In progress**. If something it's blocked by isn't Done, it can still start, but a "Blocked by [name]" chip appears **[call]**. Real work often overlaps, so it's a warning, not a hard stop.
4. **Run:** completion moves as tasks finish. Dates can be dragged.
   - **Moving a blocker later:** if a project others depend on is moved so it ends after they start, NetworkBase asks "Move 3 projects that depend on this by 5 days?" with **Move them / Leave them**. It never moves them silently **[call]**.
   - **Conflicts:** when a project starts before its blocker ends, the arrow turns to the warning colour and the bar shows "Starts before [name] ends".
5. **Finish:** **Done**. If tasks are still open, NetworkBase asks: "4 tasks are still open: leave them, or move them to the Backlog?" Done projects go into the Complete group.
6. **Pause / Cancel:**
   - **Paused** keeps the bar but greys it out.
   - **Cancelled** keeps the item for history; its tasks are not changed.
7. **Overdue:** an end date in the past while not Done shows "Ended 3 days ago" on the bar and in Active.

Who does what: the assignee runs the project; anyone in **people** can add tasks to it; admins can rename statuses, edit fields and change defaults.

#### 6. The tab's own surfaces
**S1. View tabs**
- An underline row with icons: `Timeline · Active · Board · All` (the existing UnderlineTabs).

**S2. Title row**
- Left: `◎ Projects` (the icon and title stand in for Notion's page header) and a count in mono: "5 in progress · 2 overdue".
- Right: search, **+ New project** (primary), and ⋯: Edit statuses · Edit fields · Show sprints · Weekend shading · Export CSV · Print / save as PDF.

**S3. Filter chips**
- `Status ▾ · Assigned to ▾ · Dates ▾ · + Filter` (Priority, Labels, People).
- An active filter turns into a chip like `Status: In progress ▾`, with ✕ to clear it.

**S4. Timeline grid**
```
October 2026   November            December                January        Quarter ▾  ‹ Today ›
 30    6    13    20    27    4    11   (18)   25    1    8    15 …
▾ ○ To do 0          │
▾ ◐ In progress 3    │      [🌍 New market expansion] In progress  (A) 0% ──
                     │            ╰──▶ [🎯 Customer engagement strategy] Planning (S) 50% ━━─
                     │                        ╰──▶ [📈 Performance enhancements] Planning (S) 0% ──
▾ ✓ Complete 0       │
```
- **Top rows:** months (the first one with its year), then week dates. **Today** is a filled Clay circle on its date with a Clay line down the grid.
- **Top right:** zoom (Week / Month / Quarter) and ‹ **Today** ›.
- **Grid:** vertical lines on the spec's blueprint grid, stronger at month boundaries.
- **Left column (pinned):** status groups with ▾, a status icon, a coloured group name and a count. Hovering a project name shows ⋯.
- **Bar:**
  - spans start to end date and holds the project's icon and name (the name moves outside the bar when it doesn't fit)
  - after the bar: status badge, assignee avatar, completion % and a thin progress line
  - stretch handles at both ends on hover or focus
  - a small dot at the end for drawing dependencies
- **Arrows:** curve from the end of the blocker to the start of the project it blocks; Clay normally, the warning colour on conflict.
- **No dates tray:** pinned under the left column, "No dates (3)". Drag an item onto the grid, or press "Set dates". Hidden when empty.
- **Drawing:** dragging on an empty part of a row draws a ghost bar, then opens the quick-create bubble (S8).
- **Bars outside the view:** an edge marker like "‹ Mar 12" jumps to the bar when clicked.

**S5. Active table**
- Grouped by status with ▾ and a count per group (`▾ Planning 2`, `▾ In progress 1`).
- Columns:
  - **Project name** (icon + name)
  - **Status** (badge)
  - **Assigned to** (avatar + name)
  - **Dates** ("Dec 18, 2026 → Dec 24, 2026", mono)
  - **Priority** (the task priority badge)
  - **Completion** ("50%" + bar)
  - **Blocked by** (the blocker's icon + name)
- Rows open the project page; cells can be edited in place.
- Chips appear only when they apply: "Ended 3 days ago", "Paused".

**S6. Board card**
- Icon + name, status badge, dates (mono), assignee avatar, completion line + %.
- **⋯** (also on Active rows and timeline names): Set dates · Move to status · Blocked by… · Assign · Copy link · Delete.

**S7. Project page** (the reference's third screen)
- Opens as a side panel like a task, with **Open as full page** in its ⋯ (Copy link, Duplicate, Delete as well).
- Laid out as one scroll:
```
🎯
Customer engagement strategy
  Status        Planning
  Assigned to   (S) Sohrab
  Completion    50% ━━━━──
  Dates         Dec 18, 2026 → Dec 24, 2026
  Blocked by    🌍 New market expansion
  Blocking      📈 Performance enhancements
  Priority      Low
  Summary       One short paragraph…
──────────────────────────────
Tasks                                    + New task
  Develop a survey for direct feedback   In progress  (S)  Dec 20   High
  Analyze current customer engagement    In progress  (S)  Dec 21   Medium
──────────────────────────────
About this project
  (a free document area: goals, scope, notes)
──────────────────────────────
Comments · Files · Activity
```
- **Icon:** click to pick an emoji or a Lucide icon.
- **Properties:** a label-and-value list; every value is editable in place. Blocked by / Blocking use a project picker; the existing loop check refuses circles with "That would make a loop: A is blocked by B, which is blocked by A."
- **Tasks:** the real tasks that are Part of this project, with status, assignee, due date and priority. **+ New task** creates one already linked; **Add existing task** searches the workspace. Each task opens the normal task panel.
- **About this project:** a free rich-text area.
- **Comments · Files · Activity:** at the bottom (UnderlineTabs), reusing the task comments, task files and activity. Activity shows status changes, date changes (from → to), completion milestones (25 / 50 / 75 / 100 %) and dependency changes.

**S8. Quick-create bubble** (after drawing on the timeline)
- Icon, name (focused), dates already filled in, assigned to (default me), **Create** / **More…** (opens the full dialog).

**S9. Create dialog**
- **Asks for:** icon, name, dates (optional), status (default Not started), assigned to (default me), people, blocked by.
- **More fields** expands the rest.

**S10. Shift-dependents dialog** (layer 5, step 4)
- Lists the projects that would move, with old → new dates, and **Move them / Leave them**.

**S11. Done-with-open-tasks dialog** (layer 5, step 5)

**S12. Status and field editors**
- Rename statuses (their groups stay fixed); add, hide or rename fields.

**S13. Overview card** (on the workspace's Overview tab)
- In progress count, the next project to end, overdue count, and a link to the tab.

**S14. Organization portfolio** (layer 10)
- One bar per **workspace in the organization** instead of projects, using the same grid, view tabs and filter chips.

#### 7. Design spec
- **Type (Section 04):** Instrument Sans for names, headings and the title row; JetBrains Mono for dates, %, counts and the date rows.
- **Grid:** the spec's **Blueprint grid** section is used for the timeline's lines.
- **Colour:**
  - **Bars:** Paper raised surface with an Ink border.
  - **Status groups and badges:** status colours (to do = muted Ink, in progress = the in-progress status colour, complete = success), always with an icon.
  - **Completion line:** Ink.
  - **Today marker and arrows:** Clay (agreed change 5).
  - **Conflict arrows:** the warning status colour. **Overdue:** danger, always with words.
  - **Paused:** muted Ink.
- **Badges (Section 10):** status, priority and filter chips use the precision badge geometry (agreed change 3). No fully round pills.
- **Motion (Section 05):** bar snapping, stretching and arrow redraws use 180 ms ease-out with no spring.
- **Elevation:** the bar being dragged lifts one elevation step and drops back on release.
- **Icons (Lucide):**
  - GanttChart: the tab
  - Target: the "Projects" title
  - CalendarRange: dates
  - Link2: blocked by / blocking
  - Circle / CircleDot / CircleCheck: the To do / In progress / Complete groups
  - Pause: Paused
  - Project icons may be emoji (agreed change 2).
- **Density, spacing, corner radii and empty states:** per the spec and the empty-state contract.
- **Contract test:** `tests/unit/project-planner-design-contract.test.ts`, with the same rules as the task contract, plus: the emoji exception applies only to project icons.

#### 8. Words
- **Tab:** "Project planner". **Title row:** "Projects". **Item:** "Project". In an organization's portfolio the bars are called **Workspaces**, never "child projects" (a banned term).
- **Words from the reference, kept:**
  - Timeline, Active, Board, All
  - Status, Dates, Priority
  - **Completion**
  - **Blocked by** / **Blocking** (the code already says "blocked by")
  - **Summary**, **About this project**
  - To do / In progress / Complete
  - **Today**
- **Changed:** "Owner" → **Assigned to** (agreed change 4).
- **Our own:**
  - "Part of" (task → project)
  - "No dates", "Set dates"
  - "Ended 3 days ago", "Starts before [name] ends", "set by hand"
- Never "Lead", "Owner" or "project lead".
- **Empty messages:**
  - Timeline: "No projects yet. A project groups tasks with a start and an end."
  - Active: "Nothing in progress."
  - Board column: the status name and "Nothing here."
  - Project page, Tasks section: "No tasks yet. Add one, or link tasks from the Tasks tab."

#### 9. Links to the rest of NetworkBase
- **Tasks:** tasks get **Part of** (in the create dialog, the task panel's Details and the card chip). The Tasks filter gains **Project**. Project items themselves don't appear on the Tasks board or in its counts **[call]**.
- **Sprints:** projects can't be put in sprints, but their tasks can. **Show sprints** draws sprint bands on the timeline. A sprint's page lists which projects its tasks belong to.
- **My Work:** shows projects assigned to you that are overdue or ending this week ("Ends Friday: Launch site").
- **Review:** not used for projects; their tasks keep using review as today.
- **Files / Documents:** files attach to a project; "About this project" can link to docs.
- **Updates:** marking a project Done offers **Post an Update** (off by default).
- **Chat:** share a project as a card (the existing "task" chat card with a project snapshot: icon, name, dates, completion).
- **Global search and deep links:** projects are found by name. Every project has a link that opens its page.
- **Roadmap & launches / Goals & OKRs (later sections):** milestones and key results can link to projects and read their completion.
- **CLI and agents:** the task commands and tools with `kind: "project"`, plus small additions:
  - `nb tasks set-dates`
  - `nb tasks part-of <project>`
  - the existing blocked-by edit for dependencies
  - the briefing names projects ending this week

#### 10. People
| Who | Can |
|---|---|
| Owner / admin | Everything, plus statuses, fields, defaults, export, hide/remove the tab |
| Member | Create projects, edit any project's dates, status and tasks **[call: same as tasks today]**, draw dependencies, comment; delete projects they created |
| Public (public workspace) | Follows the workspace's public-visibility switch for this tab, as Tasks does. If public: a read-only Timeline, Active and All (icons, names, statuses, dates, completion). No comments, files, "About this project" or people's names. |
| Organization | An org can push Project planner to its workspaces (decision 4). The org itself gets the **Portfolio** (S14): one bar per workspace, using new **start / end dates on the workspace** **[call]**; completion = that workspace's done tasks ÷ all its tasks. Org admins see every workspace; other org members see only workspaces they belong to. |

#### 11. States
- **Loading:** a skeleton of the view tabs, title row, filter chips, the left column (3 groups × 2 rows) and faint bars on the grid. Counts show "—".
- **Error:** the tab error boundary with Retry. If the arrows fail to load, bars still show, with a note: "Dependencies couldn't load. Retry."
- **No permission:** members of a private workspace only; a public visitor sees the read-only view (layer 10).
- **Live updates:** someone else dragging a bar moves it live for everyone. While you're dragging a bar, live moves to **that** bar wait until you drop.
- **Two people at once:** last write wins, and a toast says "Dates changed by Asha just now".
- **Undo:** moving, stretching, status changes, dependency changes, shifting dependents (all of them as one undo) and deleting.

#### 12. Edges
- **Empty:** layers 1 and 8. The No dates tray appears only when something is in it.
- **Too many projects:** rows are drawn only while on screen; groups collapse; group counts come from the server. Hundreds of projects stay smooth.
- **Very long projects (over a year) or far-off dates:** Quarter zoom, plus edge markers that jump to the bar.
- **End before start:** the date fields refuse it ("The end date can't be before the start date"). Stretching a bar past its other end stops at one day.
- **Dependency loops:** refused by the existing loop check (S7 message).
- **A dependency is deleted:** its arrow disappears and the activity notes it.
- **Assignee leaves:** the project shows "Former member"; the filter offers "Unassigned / former"; admins reassign in bulk.
- **A task that's Part of a project is deleted or moved to another workspace:** completion recalculates; the activity notes it.
- **Time zones:** dates are whole days in the workspace's time zone, so a bar never shifts by a day for someone abroad.
- **Removing the tab:** decision 2. Hide keeps projects and the tasks' Part of links (the chips hide too). Delete sends projects to Trash, and their tasks lose Part of but are **never deleted**.

#### 13. Phone
- **Active is the default view**, shown as stacked rows (icon + name, status, dates, completion) instead of a wide table.
- **Timeline on a phone:**
  - the left column narrows to icons, with a tap-to-show name
  - Month zoom only
  - the grid scrolls sideways
  - tapping a bar opens a bottom sheet with its dates and **Set dates**
  - no dragging needed
- **Filter chips** scroll sideways in one row.
- **Board:** one status at a time, with status chips to switch.
- **Project page:** opens full-screen; properties collapse to the first four with **Show all**.

#### 14. Accessibility
- **Keyboard:**
  - Tab into the grid, arrow keys move between bars
  - **←/→** moves a bar by one day (one week with Shift)
  - **Alt + ←/→** moves only its end
  - **Enter** opens the project page
  - **D** opens Set dates
  - **B** opens Blocked by…
  - **T** jumps to today
- **Screen readers:** the timeline is announced as a table with one row per project: "Customer engagement strategy, Planning, December 18 to December 24, 50 percent, blocked by New market expansion". Arrows are described in words, never only drawn. Emoji icons get the project's name as their label, not the emoji's name.
- **No dragging needed:** every drag (move, stretch, draw dependency, drag out of No dates) has a menu or dialog version.
- **Colour is never the only signal:** groups, conflicts and overdue always carry words and an icon.

#### 15. Notifications and activity
| Event | Who | Level |
|---|---|---|
| Project assigned to you | New assignee | Important |
| Ends in 3 days and not Done | Assignee | Normal |
| Overdue | Assignee | Summary (daily) |
| Its blocker is Done ("You can start: …") | Assignee of the blocked project | Normal |
| A move creates a conflict for your project | Its assignee | Normal |
| Done / Cancelled | Assignee, people, watchers | Normal |
| Mentioned | The mentioned person | Important (existing) |

- **Activity history:** created, status changes, date changes (from → to), completion milestones, blocked by added/removed, tasks added/removed, shifted together with others (with who moved the blocker).

#### 16. Trust and data
- Holds only workspace work, no outside personal data. It follows the same read/write rules as tasks.
- **Public view:** no people's names, comments, files or "About this project" (layer 10).
- **Agents:** read and edit projects only with a member's own access.
- **Export:** CSV / PDF for members **[call]**, because nothing in it is more private than the Tasks tab.
- **Limits to track** (values come with decision 6): projects per workspace; the organization portfolio as a possible Pro feature.

#### 17. Reuse vs new
- **Reused as is:**
  - task data: assignee, team members as "people", comments, files, watchers, reminders, labels, priority scale, activity, undo, My Work
  - `task_dependencies` with its loop check (`src/lib/domain/task-meta.ts`)
  - subtasks (for checklist-based completion)
  - sprints (for the sprint band)
  - the board drag engine, the task panel shell, TaskPriorityBadge / TaskStatusBadge styles, UnderlineTabs, DateTimeField, ConfirmDialog, dropdown menu, filter panel, SearchField, EmptyState, skeleton
  - the tab error boundary, live updates, the chat task card, task tools in the CLI/MCP
  - workspace time zone
- **New:**
  - kind `project` (B4)
  - **start date on tasks** (B1)
  - the **Part of** link from a task to a project
  - a **project icon** field (emoji or Lucide) with its picker
  - the **Timeline view** (B2), the biggest new part: date rows, grid, bars, arrows, No dates tray, drawing, zoom, edge markers, a keyboard model and a screen-reader table
  - completion roll-up (B6)
  - the filter chip row (as a reusable part for every workflow tab)
  - Active and All tables
  - the one-scroll project page with "About this project"
  - shift-dependents and done-with-open-tasks dialogs
  - status and field editors
  - the Overview card
  - **start / end dates on workspaces** and the organization **Portfolio** (S14)
  - the tab switch (B10)
- **Shared:** the Timeline view and the filter chip row built here are reused by Roadmap & launches, Event planner and Content calendar.

#### 18. How we know it works
- **Usage signal:** the share of workspaces with Project planner where, 2 weeks after adding it, at least one project has dates **and** at least one task that's Part of it.
- **Checks once built:**
  - the design contract test (including the emoji exception only on project icons)
  - side-by-side check against the reference screenshot: view tabs, title row, filter chips, timeline header, status groups, bar contents, arrows, Active columns, project page order
  - unit tests: completion (tasks / checklist / by hand, cancelled ignored), conflict detection, shift-dependents maths, end-before-start refused, whole-day dates in the workspace time zone
  - the existing loop-check tests cover dependencies
  - end to end: draw a project → add tasks → draw a dependency → move the blocker → accept "Move them" → finish tasks → Done
  - public read-only view shows no names
  - phone check; keyboard-only check (move, stretch, link, open)

---

### 11.4 Goals & OKRs (own tab, all 18 layers)

**References (checked live on 2026-11-16):**
- **OKR Tracker by Sentele** (4.9 from 80 ratings, the most reviewed OKR template on Notion). This is the main reference for the layout.
  - **Main page:** a left rail (Quick actions: New objective / New key result; Stats: a bar chart of each key result's progress; Navigation) next to two stacked sections:
    - **Objectives:** views Gallery · On track · At risk. Cards show icon, name, owner and a status tag.
    - **Key results:** views By objective · By quarter. A table with Key result · Progress · Goal type (Increase / Decrease) · Current · Target · Quarter · Lead · Date created · Notes.
  - **Objective page:** icon, title, Owners, Status, Date created, Deadline, Description, a Done checkbox, and its key results.
  - **Weak spot:** a reviewer calls the progress formula "a bit confusing". It stores no start value, so "Reduce churn 15% → 10%" shows 106% at current 85 / target 90.
- **OKRs by Notion** (4.7 from 13 ratings). Doc-style: team + quarter as the frame, objectives with key results under them, and an FAQ on writing OKRs. Two ideas are taken from it: **team + period as the frame**, and **built-in guidance**.

It's built from NetworkBase's own parts (fonts, colours, shared components), not either template's look.

**Agreed changes from an exact copy (2026-11-16):**
1. **No cover banner or big title.** The "◎ Goals" title row, with its period and team switchers, takes their place.
2. **The black filled heading bars become our own section headings.**
3. **The vertical bar chart becomes horizontal progress bars.** There's no chart library in the app, and the reference's rotated, cut-off labels are hard to read.
4. **Column names:** "Goal type" → **Direction**. "Lead" and "Owners" → **Assigned to** ("Lead" is banned in the terms file; "Owner" is a role). "Date created" moves to Activity.
5. **The Navigation box is dropped**, because the workspace tabs already do that job.

Marked **[call]** = a decision made in this design that the user can overrule.

#### 1. Getting it
- **Where it's offered:**
  - **+ Add workflow** (owners and admins)
  - the wizard's Settings step, shown unticked for Startup, Non-profit and Web app (section 6)
  - added by an organization; for an organization it's the place where org-wide objectives live (layer 10)
- **In the + Add workflow dialog:** a Goals row with a small preview of the objective cards. No presets to choose.
- **First look:**
  - the title row with the current quarter selected
  - the rail with + New objective / + New key result, and the period tile ("Q4 2026 · week 7 of 13")
  - the Objectives section empty, with a guidance hint: "An objective is where you want to be. Key results are 2–4 numbers that prove you got there." plus an example ("Grow paying customers → Paid accounts 20 → 60")
  - the Key results section hidden until the first objective exists

#### 2. Setting it up
- **Period:** **Quarter** by default, starting on the workspace's chosen month (default January). Admins can switch to **Month**, **Half year**, **Year**, or, for organizations with term dates, **Term** (using the term start/end that already exist).
- **Check-in day:** the weekday reminders go out (default Monday). Admins can turn reminders off.
- **Statuses:** On track · At risk · Off track (while the period runs); Done · Missed (after it closes). Fixed, so roll-ups stay meaningful.
- **Pace bands [call]:** on track = progress at or above pace − 10 points; at risk = within 25 points below pace; off track = further behind. Admins can adjust the two numbers.
- **Teams:** optional. Objectives can carry a team; the list of teams comes from the team names tasks already use.
- **Fields:** admins can add their own fields to objectives or key results (B3).

#### 3. Items
- **Objective:** a **task of kind `objective`** (decision 1). Holds icon, name, status, assigned to (one or more), period, team, progress (automatic), description, contributes to (organizations), linked work.
- **Key result:** a **task of kind `key_result`**, part of one objective. Holds name, direction, unit, start, target, current, progress (automatic), confidence, assigned to, measured by, notes.
  - **Direction:** Increase · Decrease · Done / not done.
  - **Unit:** number, %, currency (one per key result), count, or time (days / hours).
  - **Measured by:** a number someone updates (default) · a linked Project's completion · linked tasks done · **money raised** (Money income) · **volunteer hours** (Event planner) — the last two added by 17.6.
- **Check-in:** a comment on a key result carrying a value, a confidence and a date (the same mechanism as Pipeline's "touch").
- **Progress maths (fixes the reference's weak spot):**

| Direction | Progress |
|---|---|
| Increase | (current − start) ÷ (target − start) |
| Decrease | (start − current) ÷ (start − target) |
| Done / not done | 0% or 100% |

  - Above 100% shows as **Exceeded** (stored, but capped at 100% in averages).
  - An objective's progress = the average of its key results' progress **[call]**; a weighting per key result is left for later.
- **Every way to create one:**
  1. **+ New objective** / **+ New key result** in the rail and the title row
  2. **+ New key result** inside an objective's page or its group in the table
  3. **Carry forward** when a period closes (layer 5)
  4. **From the organization:** "Add a workspace objective under this" on an org objective
  5. **CLI / agents** (layer 9)

#### 4. Views
| Section | Views | What's on screen | Filter / sort |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Objectives** | All · On track · At risk · Done | Gallery cards (S5) | Period, team, assigned to |
| **Key results** | By objective · By period · Mine | A table grouped by objective (S6) | Period, team, assigned to, status, confidence; sort by any column |

- The **rail** (S4) is always visible on desktop.
- **Search** covers objective and key result names.
- There's no drag-and-drop here **[call]**: status is calculated, so there's nothing to drag between columns. Order inside the gallery is by status (off track first), then progress.

#### 5. Actions and flow
1. **Set (start of the period):** create objectives, then 2–4 key results each, with start, target and direction. The dialog warns softly if an objective has fewer than 2 or more than 5 key results.
2. **Check in (weekly):** on the check-in day, each key result's assignee gets a reminder. **Check in** asks for the new current value (or shows the linked project / tasks value), confidence and a note. Progress, status and the history chart update.
3. **Watch the pace:** status is recalculated after every check-in and every night. Moving to At risk or Off track notifies the assignee (layer 15).
   - **Override:** the assignee can set the status by hand with a reason; the badge shows "set by hand" until the next check-in.
4. **Close the period:** after the period ends, admins see **Close Q4**:
   - each key result's final value is confirmed (it can be edited)
   - each objective becomes **Done** (all key results ≥ 70% **[call]**) or **Missed**, which an admin can change
   - a short "What we learned" note per objective
   - **Carry forward:** unfinished objectives can be copied into the next period with their key results; the new start value is the last current value
   - **Post an Update** with the summary (off by default)
5. **Reopen:** a closed period can be reopened by an admin for corrections; the activity history records it.

Who does what: key result assignees check in; objective assignees keep the description and links current; admins set the period, close it and change settings; any member can create objectives and key results **[call]**.

#### 6. The tab's own surfaces
**S1. Title row**
- `◎ Goals`, the **period switcher** (`Q4 2026 ▾`, listing past, current and next periods), the **Team** switcher (`Team: All ▾`), search, **+ New objective** (primary), ⋯: Period settings · Check-in day · Pace bands · Edit fields · Close period · Export CSV.

**S2. Filter chips**
- `Assigned to ▾ · Status ▾ · Confidence ▾ · + Filter` (the row built for the Project planner).

**S3. Section view tabs**
- An underline row above each section: Objectives `All · On track · At risk · Done`; Key results `By objective · By period · Mine`.

**S4. Rail** (left, as in the reference)
- **Quick actions:** + New objective, + New key result.
- **Period tile:** "Q4 2026 · week 7 of 13" with a thin time bar.
- **Summary tiles** (Sprint insights style): "3 of 4 on track", "Average progress 61%", "2 check-ins due" (clicking filters to them).
- **Progress by key result:** one horizontal bar per key result in the current filter, labelled in full, with % in mono and a small pace tick on each bar.

**S5. Objective card**
- Icon + name, assignee avatars, status badge, progress % + bar, "2 key results", team (when set).
- Chips only when they apply: "set by hand", "No check-in for 2 weeks".
- **⋯:** Add key result · Change status · Contributes to… · Copy link · Delete.

**S6. Key results table**
- Grouped by objective (`▾ ◎ Grow paying customers 2`).
- Columns: **Key result · Progress · Direction · Start · Current · Target · Unit · Assigned to · Last check-in · Confidence**.
- Numbers in mono; Current is editable in place, which counts as a check-in without a note.
- **⋯ per row:** Check in · Change target · Measured by… · Move to another objective · Copy link · Delete.

**S7. Objective page** (side panel, one scroll, **Open as full page** in ⋯)
```
◎
Grow paying customers
  Status          On track
  Assigned to     (A) Asha  (S) Sohrab
  Period          Q4 2026  (Oct 1 → Dec 31)
  Progress        72% ━━━━━━──
  Contributes to  ◎ Org: Reach 500 schools        (organizations only)
  Team            Growth
  Description     Why this matters, in a sentence or two…
──────────────────────────────
Key results                                   + New key result
  Paid accounts 20 → 60      49   72% ━━─   On track   (A)
  Churn rate 15% → 10%       12%  60% ━─    At risk    (S)
──────────────────────────────
Linked work      🎯 Pricing page relaunch (project · 50%)   + Link
──────────────────────────────
Comments · Files · Activity
```

**S8. Key result page** (side panel)
```
Paid accounts
  Objective      ◎ Grow paying customers
  Direction      Increase          Unit   Number
  Start → Target 20 → 60           Current 49   Progress 72%
  Confidence     High              Assigned to (A) Asha
  Measured by    Number I update ▾  (or: Linked project's completion · Linked tasks done)
──────────────────────────────
Check-ins                                      [ Check in ]
  ●──●───●────●   (weekly values, with a dashed "expected by now" pace line)
  Nov 10  49  High   "Two schools signed after the demo day."
  Nov 3   41  Medium "Slow week, trial-to-paid dropped."
──────────────────────────────
Comments · Files · Activity
```
- The history chart is drawn in plain SVG (no chart library), from check-ins only.

**S9. Check-in dialog**
- New value (or the linked value, read-only), confidence (Low / Medium / High), note (optional), **Check in**. Shows "Last: 41 on Nov 3" for context.

**S10. Create dialogs**
- **New objective:** icon, name, assigned to (default me), period (default current), team, description, contributes to (organizations), and "Add key results now" (inline rows: name, direction, start → target, unit).
- **New key result:** objective, name, direction, unit, start, target, assigned to (default me), measured by.
- Both show one line of guidance (layer 1).

**S11. Close period review**
- One row per objective, with its key results' final values, Done / Missed, a "What we learned" box, and a **Carry forward** checkbox. Buttons: **Close Q4**, **Post an Update** (off by default).

**S12. Settings dialogs:** period, check-in day, pace bands, fields.

**S13. Overview card** (on the workspace's Overview tab)
- "3 of 4 on track · Q4 week 7", check-ins due, and a link to the tab.

**S14. Organization view** (layer 10)
- The org's own objectives, each with the workspace objectives that contribute to it listed underneath and rolled into its progress.

#### 7. Design spec
- **Type (Section 04):** Instrument Sans for names and headings; JetBrains Mono for numbers (start, current, target, %, week counts).
- **Colour:**
  - **Progress bars:** Ink fill on a Paper track. The pace tick is muted Ink.
  - **Status badges:** On track = success, At risk = warning, Off track = danger, Done = success with a check icon, Missed = muted Ink. Always with an icon and words.
  - **Primary button:** Clay.
- **Badges (Section 10):** status, confidence and filter chips use the precision badge geometry. No fully round pills.
- **Section headings:** our heading style (replacing the reference's black bars, agreed change 2).
- **Charts:** the rail bars and the check-in history are plain SVG/CSS, following the spec's colour and type rules (agreed change 3).
- **Motion (Section 05):** progress bars animate to their new value in 180 ms ease-out, no spring.
- **Icons (Lucide):**
  - Target: the tab and objectives
  - TrendingUp / TrendingDown / CheckSquare: Increase / Decrease / Done-not-done
  - Gauge: confidence
  - CalendarClock: period and check-in day
  - GitMerge: contributes to
- **Objective icons:** emoji or Lucide, as for projects (the same exception).
- **Density, spacing, corner radii and empty states:** per the spec and the empty-state contract.
- **Contract test:** `tests/unit/goals-design-contract.test.ts`, with the same rules as the task contract.

#### 8. Words
- **Tab:** "Goals" **[call]** (shorter in the tab row; "OKRs" appears in the + Add workflow description). **Items:** "Objective", "Key result".
- **Kept from the references:** Objectives, Key results, Progress, Current, Target, On track, At risk, Quarter, Description.
- **Ours:** Direction (Increase / Decrease / Done-not-done), Start, Unit, Confidence, Check in / Check-in, Measured by, Contributes to, Exceeded, Off track, Missed, Close Q4, Carry forward, "What we learned", "set by hand".
- **Changed:** "Lead" and "Owners" → **Assigned to**; "Goal type" → **Direction**.
- Never "Lead", "Owner" or "child projects".
- **Empty messages:**
  - Objectives: "No objectives for Q4 2026 yet. An objective is where you want to be. Key results are 2–4 numbers that prove you got there."
  - Key results (objective has none): "Add 2–4 numbers that show this objective is done."
  - At risk view: "Nothing at risk."
  - Check-ins (none yet): "No check-ins yet. The first one sets the line."

#### 9. Links to the rest of NetworkBase
- **My Work:** "Check-in due: Paid accounts" on the check-in day, for the key result's assignee.
- **Project planner:** a key result can be measured by a project's completion; a project page shows "Moves: Paid accounts" when linked.
- **Tasks:** a key result can be measured by linked tasks done; the task panel shows which key result it moves.
- **Sprints:** a sprint's goal can point at a key result; the sprint page then shows that key result's progress.
- **Updates:** closing a period offers **Post an Update** with the summary (off by default).
- **Overview:** the Goals card (S13).
- **Chat:** share an objective or key result as a card (the existing "task" chat card with a goal snapshot: name, progress, status).
- **Global search and deep links:** objectives and key results are found by name; each has its own link.
- **CLI and agents:** the task commands and tools with `kind: "objective"` / `"key_result"`, plus:
  - `nb goals check-in <key result> <value> [--confidence high] [--note "…"]`
  - the agent briefing lists check-ins due and anything that turned At risk this week

#### 10. People
| Who | Can |
|---|---|
| Owner / admin | Everything, plus period settings, check-in day, pace bands, fields, closing and reopening periods, export |
| Member | Create objectives and key results **[call]**, check in on key results assigned to them, edit objectives assigned to them, comment; delete what they created |
| Public (public workspace) | The tab's public switch **defaults to Members only [call]**, because goals often hold revenue and other private numbers. If made public: read-only objectives and progress, no numbers (only %), no names, no comments. |
| Organization | The org's own Goals tab holds **org objectives**. A workspace objective can **Contribute to** one; the org view lists contributing workspace objectives under each org objective and rolls their progress in. Org admins see all of them; other org members see only workspaces they belong to. If the org pushes the tab to its workspaces (decision 4), each workspace gets its own, empty Goals tab. |

#### 11. States
- **Loading:** skeletons for the rail tiles, three objective cards and five table rows. Numbers show "—".
- **Error:** the tab error boundary with Retry; a failed rail never blanks the sections.
- **No permission:** private workspace = members only; public visitors follow layer 10.
- **Live updates:** check-ins by others update progress, status and the rail without a refresh.
- **Two people at once:** two check-ins on the same key result are both kept, ordered by time; the latest sets Current.
- **Undo:** check-ins, target changes, status overrides, closing a period (as one undo) and deleting.

#### 12. Edges
- **Empty:** layers 1 and 8.
- **Start equals target:** refused ("Start and target can't be the same").
- **Mixed units:** never averaged as numbers; objectives always average **percentages**.
- **Linked project or tasks deleted:** the key result falls back to "Number I update", keeping its last value; the activity notes it.
- **A check-in in a closed period:** asks to reopen the period first.
- **Assignee leaves:** shows "Former member"; check-in reminders go to the objective's assignees instead; admins reassign in bulk.
- **Too many:** objectives page by period; the key results table pages at 100 rows; totals come from the server.
- **Period changed mid-way** (e.g. quarter start month): existing objectives keep their dates; only new periods use the new setting.
- **Removing the tab:** decision 2. Hide keeps everything and stops reminders. Delete sends objectives and key results to Trash; linked projects and tasks are **never deleted**.

#### 13. Phone
- **First screen:** "Check-ins due" (the summary tile becomes a list), then the objective cards stacked.
- **Check in** is one bottom sheet: value, confidence, note, done.
- **Key results table:** becomes stacked rows (name, progress bar, current → target, status).
- **Rail:** moves above the sections as a row of tiles that scrolls sideways.
- **Objective and key result pages:** full-screen.

#### 14. Accessibility
- **Keyboard:** Tab through cards and rows; **Enter** opens; **C** opens Check in on a focused key result; **N** opens New objective.
- **Screen readers:** every bar has a text version ("Paid accounts, 72 percent, expected 54 by now, on track, last check-in November 10"). The history chart has a table of check-ins as its text alternative.
- **Colour is never the only signal:** statuses always carry an icon and words; the pace tick has a label.

#### 15. Notifications and activity
| Event | Who | Level |
|---|---|---|
| Key result or objective assigned to you | New assignee | Important |
| Check-in due | Key result assignee | Normal (the existing reminder) |
| No check-in for 2 weeks | Key result + objective assignees | Summary (weekly) |
| Turned At risk / Off track | Key result + objective assignees | Normal |
| Period ending in 7 days | Admins + objective assignees | Normal |
| Period closed (summary) | All workspace members | Summary |
| Mentioned in a check-in or comment | The mentioned person | Important (existing) |

- **Activity history:** created, target/start changes (from → to), each check-in (value, confidence), status changes (calculated or by hand, with reason), measured-by changes, period closed / reopened, carried forward.

#### 16. Trust and data
- Only workspace data, but often **business-sensitive numbers** (revenue, churn). Hence the Members-only default (layer 10) and, when public, percentages only.
- **Agents:** read and check in only with a member's own access.
- **Export:** CSV for admins by default **[call]**.
- **Limits to track** (values come with decision 6): objectives per period; the organization roll-up as a possible Pro feature.

#### 17. Reuse vs new
- **Reused as is:**
  - task data (assignee, comments, files, watchers, reminders, activity, undo, My Work)
  - the pace idea and tile style from Sprint insights (`src/lib/workspaces/sprint-plan.ts`, `SprintInsights.tsx`)
  - organization term dates and workspace time zone
  - team names on tasks
  - from the Project planner: the filter chip row, the one-scroll item page, emoji-or-Lucide icons, project completion
  - UnderlineTabs, ConfirmDialog, dropdown menu, SearchField, EmptyState, skeleton, the tab error boundary, live updates, the chat task card, task tools in the CLI/MCP
- **New:**
  - kinds `objective` and `key_result` (B4)
  - key result fields: direction, unit, start, target, current, confidence, measured by (B3)
  - the period model (quarter / month / half / year / term) and the check-in day
  - progress maths and pace-based status (B6)
  - check-ins as comments carrying a value
  - the rail, objective cards, key results table, both item pages, the check-in dialog and its SVG history chart
  - the close-period review with carry forward
  - Contributes-to between org and workspace objectives, with roll-up
  - the Overview card, `nb goals check-in`
  - the tab switch (B10)

#### 18. How we know it works
- **Usage signal:** the share of workspaces with Goals where, 4 weeks after adding it, at least half the key results got a check-in in each of the last 2 weeks.
- **Checks once built:**
  - the design contract test
  - side-by-side check against the reference layout (rail + two sections, card contents, table columns, objective page order)
  - unit tests: progress for Increase / Decrease / Done-not-done (including the reference's churn example: 15% → 10% at 12% = 60%), Exceeded capping, objective averaging, pace bands, start = target refused
  - end to end: create objective + 2 key results → check in twice → status turns At risk → override with reason → close the period → carry forward
  - organization roll-up and visibility test
  - public view shows percentages only, no names
  - phone check-in; keyboard-only check

### 11.5 Roadmap & launches (own tab, all 18 layers)

**References (ranked by rating and checked on 2026-11-16):**
- **Roadmap by Notion** (4.9 from 100+ ratings). A status board of Epics, Tasks, Bugs and Sprints, with views by status, engineer, product manager and calendar. This is task management, which Tasks and Sprints already cover, so it's **not copied**.
- **Product Roadmap Timeline by desbyseb** (4.8 from 40). The main reference for the roadmap half:
  - views **By status · Timeline · Quarterly roadmap · Backlog**
  - columns Backlog · Planned · In progress · Testing · Launched
  - cards show name, priority, type (Feature / Improvement / Bug fix), assignee and a short description
  - a reviewer values it because it "describes the necessary milestones … unlike many other templates which are task management templates"
- **Product launch checklist by Notion** (4.9 from 32). The main reference for the launch half: one page with 7 numbered stages (Market research · Goal identification · Marketing plan · Sales and support training · Testing and beta testing · Launch event · Post-launch evaluation). Each stage has one line on why it matters, then checklist items with a person and a date, and nested sub-items.

It's built from NetworkBase's own parts, not either template's look.

**Agreed changes from an exact copy (2026-11-16):**
1. **Notion's own Roadmap template is not copied.** Epics, tasks, bugs and sprints already live in Tasks and Sprints; this tab is only about what ships to users and when.
2. **Status columns run in delivery order:** Backlog · Planned · In progress · Testing · Launched. The reference showed Launched before Planned and Testing.
3. **Checklist items become tasks with a stage**, not plain checkboxes, so they get people, dates, reminders and My Work.
4. **The Notion Tip box becomes a one-line hint** in the empty state.
5. **The usual changes:** our badge shape (no fully round pills), "Assigned to" never "Owner" or "Lead", our section headings, and emoji-or-Lucide icons.

Marked **[call]** = a decision made in this design that the user can overrule.

#### 1. Getting it
- **Where it's offered:**
  - **+ Add workflow** (owners and admins)
  - the wizard's Settings step, shown unticked for Startup, Side project, Game dev and Web app (section 6)
  - added by an organization
- **In the + Add workflow dialog:** a Roadmap & launches row with a small preview of the status board. No presets at this step; checklist presets are picked per launch.
- **First look:**
  - the By status board with its five empty columns
  - a one-line hint: "Add what users will get, then group it into launches. Day-to-day work stays in Tasks."
  - the Launches view says "No launches yet. A launch has a date, the items it ships and a checklist."

#### 2. Setting it up
- **Roadmap item statuses** (fixed order; admins can rename them): Backlog → Planned → In progress → Testing → Launched. Plus **Won't do** (hidden from the board, shown in Backlog with a filter).
- **Types:** Feature · Improvement · Fix (admins can add more).
- **Priority:** the task scale: Low / Medium / High / Urgent.
- **Quarters:** follow the Goals period setting when Goals exists, otherwise calendar quarters.
- **Launch statuses:** Planning → Getting ready → Launched → Closed, plus Cancelled.
- **Checklist presets:**

| Preset | Stages |
|---|---|
| **Product launch** (from Notion's checklist) | Market research · Goal identification · Marketing plan · Sales and support training · Testing and beta testing · Launch day · After launch |
| **Feature release** | Build done · QA · Docs · Announce · Watch |
| **Content / episode launch** | Script · Record · Edit · Publish · Promote (reused by Podcast and Video later) |
| **Blank** | One stage, "Checklist" |

  Each preset stage has a one-line "why" and a few starter checklist items (no people or dates yet). Admins can save a launch's checklist as a new preset for the workspace.
- **Fields:** admins can add their own fields to roadmap items or launches (B3).

#### 3. Items
- **Roadmap item:** a **task of kind `roadmap_item`** (decision 1). Holds icon, name, status, type, priority, assigned to, target quarter, ships in (one launch), progress (from links), moves (a Goals key result), show publicly, why (one paragraph), built by (projects / tasks).
- **Launch:** a **task of kind `launch`**. Holds icon, name (e.g. "v2.4: Faster and safer sign-in"), launch date, status, assigned to, the items it ships, its checklist, a "What's new" draft.
- **Checklist item:** a **normal task**, **Part of** the launch, with a **stage** **[call]**. It has a person, a due date, reminders, comments; it appears on the Tasks board, in sprints and in My Work. Its sub-items are its subtasks. (Subtasks today have no person or date, so making each item a task is the cheapest way to match the reference.)
- **Part of** (introduced by the Project planner) now points at a project **or** a launch.
- **Progress of a roadmap item:** from a linked project's completion, or the share of linked tasks done. With nothing linked, it shows status only, with no %.
- **Every way to create one:**
  1. **+ New item** / **+ New launch** in the title row
  2. **+** at the top of a status column or a quarter column
  3. **+ Add roadmap item** on a launch page (create new or pick existing)
  4. **From a project:** "Add to roadmap" in the project page's ⋯
  5. **From Feedback & requests** (later tab): "Add to roadmap" on a request
  6. **CLI / agents** (layer 9)

#### 4. Views
| View | What's on screen | Drag | Filter / sort |
|---|---|---|---|
| **By status** (desktop default) | The reference's board, five columns in delivery order | Cards between statuses | Type, priority, assigned to, quarter, launch |
| **Timeline** | The Project planner's timeline: items as bars (from first linked work to launch date), launches as **diamonds** on their date | Move a launch diamond (asks to move its items' target too) | As above; zoom Month / Quarter |
| **Quarters** | One column per quarter (current · next · the one after · **Later**) | Cards between quarters (changes target quarter) | As above |
| **Backlog** | A table of items in Backlog / Won't do, sorted by priority | Reorder rows (sets backlog order) | As above |
| **Launches** (phone default) | One row per launch: name, date + countdown, status, items shipping (count), checklist progress | — | Status; upcoming / past |

- **Search** covers item names, launch names and "Why" text.

#### 5. Actions and flow
**Roadmap items**
1. **Capture:** created in Backlog.
2. **Plan:** give it a target quarter and, when known, a launch → status **Planned**.
3. **Build:** link a project or tasks → status **In progress**; progress follows the linked work.
4. **Test:** moved to **Testing** by hand.
5. **Ship:** becomes **Launched** automatically when its launch is launched.
6. **Drop:** **Won't do**, with a reason; it leaves the board but stays searchable.

**Launches**
1. **Planning:** pick a date, add roadmap items, choose a checklist preset (it creates the checklist tasks in their stages, unassigned, with no dates yet).
2. **Getting ready:** assign people and dates to checklist tasks; tick them off. The countdown and checklist progress show on the launch, the Launches view, the timeline diamond and the Overview card.
   - **Warning:** if the date is close and items are not in Testing or later, the launch shows "3 items not ready".
3. **Launch day:** the **Launch** button (admins and the launch's assignee) opens a dialog:
   - mark the shipped items **Launched** (each item can be unticked)
   - move unfinished items to the next launch, or back to Planned
   - **Post an Update** (opens the What's new draft as a release Update; never posted automatically **[call]**)
4. **After launch:** status **Launched**. The "After launch" stage stays open; 14 days after the launch date NetworkBase suggests **Close launch** (the remaining checklist tasks can be finished, moved to the Backlog of Tasks, or cancelled).
5. **Cancel:** its items return to **Planned**; its checklist tasks are kept, and a dialog offers to cancel them.
6. **Move the date:** asks "Also move the 3 items' target quarter?" when the new date falls in another quarter.

Who does what: item assignees keep status and links current; checklist task assignees do the steps; the launch's assignee and admins press **Launch** and **Close launch**.

#### 6. The tab's own surfaces
**S1. View tabs:** `By status · Timeline · Quarters · Backlog · Launches` (UnderlineTabs).

**S2. Title row:** `◈ Roadmap`, counts in mono ("12 planned · next launch in 23 days"), search, **+ New item** (primary), **+ New launch**, ⋯: Edit statuses · Edit types · Checklist presets · Edit fields · Public roadmap settings · Export CSV.

**S3. Filter chips:** `Type ▾ · Priority ▾ · Assigned to ▾ · + Filter` (Quarter, Launch, Public). The row built for the Project planner.

**S4. Status board**
```
┌ Backlog 4 ─────┐┌ Planned 3 ─────┐┌ In progress 2 ┐┌ Testing 1 ─────┐┌ Launched 5 ────┐
│ Dark mode      ││ Mobile speed   ││ Sign-in with   ││ AI search      ││ Dashboard      │
│ Low · Feature  ││ High · Improve ││ SSO            ││ Medium·Feature ││ redesign       │
│ (D)            ││ ➜ v2.4 · Dec 12││ High · Feature ││ ➜ v2.4 · Dec 12││ ✓ v2.3 · Nov 3 │
│ Short why…     ││ ━━━━── 60%     ││ (S) ━━── 40%   ││ (D) ━━━━━ 90%  ││                │
└────────────────┘└────────────────┘└────────────────┘└────────────────┘└────────────────┘
```
- Column headers: status, count. Launched shows the last 10 with "Show all".

**S5. Card**
- Icon + name, priority badge, type badge, assignee avatar, `➜ launch · date` (or `Q1 2027` when no launch), progress line + % when linked, the first line of "Why".
- Chips only when they apply: "Public", "Not ready for v2.4".
- **⋯:** Move to status · Set quarter · Add to launch… · Link project / tasks · Show publicly · Copy link · Delete.

**S6. Quarters board:** like S4, with quarter columns and a "Later" column; each column header shows the launches in that quarter as small diamonds with dates.

**S7. Backlog table:** columns Item · Type · Priority · Assigned to · Requested by (from Feedback, later) · Created; drag handle for order.

**S8. Launches list:** rows with icon, name, date + "in 23 days" (mono), status badge, "3 items", checklist bar "14 of 31".

**S9. Roadmap item page** (side panel, one scroll, **Open as full page** in ⋯)
```

  Priority      High                 Assigned to (S) Sohrab

  Moves         ◎ Paid accounts (key result)
  Public        Shown on public roadmap ✓
  Why           Schools asked for one login… (one paragraph, shown publicly if Public)

```

**S10. Launch page** (side panel, one scroll, **Open as full page** in ⋯)
```

  Status   Getting ready     Assigned to (A) Asha     Checklist  14 of 31 ✓  ━━━━──
──────────────────────────────
Shipping in this launch (3)                         + Add roadmap item
  ✦ Sign-in with SSO      In progress   40%
  ✦ Mobile speed          Planned       60%
  ✦ AI search             Testing       90%

Checklist                                     Stages from: Product launch ▾

   ☐ Create buyer personas → (A) Asha · Dec 1
   ☑ Competitive analysis → (S) Sohrab · Nov 28
       ☐ Identify direct competitors
```

- **Checklist rows:** checkbox, name, `→ person · date` (click to set), ⋯ (open as task, move to stage, delete). **+ Add item** at the end of each stage. Sub-items are the task's subtasks, shown indented.
- **Stage headers:** number, name, the one-line why, and "3 of 5" on the right; stages fold.
- **"Stages from"** changes the preset only while no checklist task has been ticked; afterwards it's read-only.

**S11. Launch dialog** (layer 5, launch day) and **S12. Close launch dialog**.

**S13. Create dialogs**
- **New item:** icon, name, type, priority, assigned to (default me), target quarter, launch, why, show publicly.
- **New launch:** icon, name, launch date, assigned to (default me), checklist preset, items to ship (picker).

**S14. Public roadmap** (what visitors see when the tab is public). **Replaced by 13.3:** public roadmap items now appear on the workspace's single public **Feedback page**; the rules below (only items marked Show publicly; no names, %, checklists or comments) still apply there.
- Three columns **Planned · In progress · Launched** (Backlog and Testing are hidden; Testing shows as In progress), cards with icon, name, type, quarter and "Why". No names, %, launches' checklists or comments.

**S15. Overview card:** next launch, its date and countdown, checklist progress, "3 items not ready" when it applies, and a link to the tab.

#### 7. Design spec
- **Type (Section 04):** Instrument Sans for names and headings; JetBrains Mono for dates, countdowns, versions ("v2.4"), counts and %.
- **Colour:**
  - **Status badges:** Backlog = muted Ink, Planned = Ink, In progress = in-progress status colour, Testing = warning, Launched = success. Always with an icon.
  - **Launch diamonds and the countdown:** Clay.
  - **"Not ready" warning:** warning colour with words.
  - **Progress lines:** Ink.
- **Badges (Section 10):** status, type, priority and filter chips use the precision badge geometry. No fully round pills.
- **Motion (Section 05):** card drags and checklist ticks use 180 ms ease-out, no spring.
- **Icons (Lucide):**
  - Map: the tab
  - Sparkle: roadmap items
  - Diamond: launches
  - Rocket: the Launch button
  - ListChecks: the checklist
  - Globe: "Show publicly"
- **Item icons:** emoji or Lucide (the same exception as projects).
- **Density, spacing, corner radii and empty states:** per the spec and the empty-state contract.
- **Contract test:** `tests/unit/roadmap-design-contract.test.ts`, with the same rules as the task contract.

#### 8. Words
- **Tab:** "Roadmap". **Items:** "Roadmap item" (shown as "item"), "Launch", "Checklist".
- **Kept from the references:** Backlog, Planned, In progress, Testing, Launched; Feature, Improvement; the 7 checklist stage names (with "Launch event" → **Launch day** and "Post-launch evaluation" → **After launch** **[call]**, shorter and plainer).
- **Ours:** Fix (instead of "Bug fix"), Won't do, Target, Ships in, Built by, Moves, Why, Show publicly, What's new, Launch / Close launch, "not ready", "in 23 days".
- Never "Lead", "Owner", "Epic" (epics are a Tasks idea and stay out of this tab).
- **Empty messages:**
  - Board: "Nothing on the roadmap yet. Add what users will get, then group it into launches."
  - Launches: "No launches yet. A launch has a date, the items it ships and a checklist."
  - A launch with no items: "Add the roadmap items this launch ships."
  - Public roadmap with nothing public: "Nothing shared yet."

#### 9. Links to the rest of NetworkBase
- **Tasks:** checklist items are tasks (Part of the launch, with a stage); roadmap items can be built by tasks. Roadmap items and launches themselves don't appear on the Tasks board **[call]**.
- **Sprints:** checklist tasks can go in sprints like any task.
- **Project planner:** an item can be built by a project; launches show as diamonds on the planner's timeline when "Show launches" is on.
- **Goals:** an item can **move** a key result (shown on both pages).
- **My Work:** checklist tasks assigned to you; "Launch in 3 days: v2.4" for the launch's assignee.
- **Updates:** **Post an Update** on launch uses the existing **release** Update type, with the What's new list; drafts only, never automatic.
- **Feedback & requests (later tab):** requests can become roadmap items; the Backlog table's "Requested by" column comes from there.
- **Chat:** share an item or a launch as a card (the existing "task" chat card).
- **Global search and deep links:** items and launches are found by name; each has its own link.
- **CLI and agents:** task commands and tools with `kind: "roadmap_item"` / `"launch"`, plus `nb launch status [<launch>]` (countdown, items, open checklist tasks). The agent briefing includes "launch in N days, X checklist items open".

#### 10. People
| Who | Can |
|---|---|
| Owner / admin | Everything, plus statuses, types, presets, fields, public roadmap settings, export |
| Member | Create and edit items and launches, move cards, tick checklist tasks, comment; delete what they created. **Launch** and **Close launch** only if they're the launch's assignee **[call]** |
| Public (public workspace) | The tab is **Members only by default [call]**. If an admin turns on the public roadmap, visitors see S14: only items marked **Show publicly**, with no names, %, checklists or comments. |
| Organization | Can push the tab to its workspaces (decision 4). **No roll-up [call]**: roadmaps are per product, so the org doesn't merge them. |

#### 11. States
- **Loading:** skeletons for the view tabs, title row, filter chips and five columns with two cards each; counts show "—".
- **Error:** the tab error boundary with Retry; a failed progress read shows the card without a %.
- **No permission:** members only, or the public roadmap (S14).
- **Live updates:** card moves, checklist ticks and countdowns update without a refresh.
- **Two people at once:** last write wins, with a toast ("Moved to Testing by Sohrab just now").
- **Undo:** moves, quarter changes, adding/removing items from a launch, the Launch action (all its changes as one undo, within the undo window), deleting.

#### 12. Edges
- **Empty:** layers 1 and 8.
- **An item in two launches:** not allowed; adding it to a second launch asks to move it.
- **A launch date in the past while still Getting ready:** shows "Launch date passed" and asks to launch or move the date.
- **Too many items:** columns show 25 with "Show more"; Launched shows the last 10; tables page at 100.
- **Linked project or tasks deleted:** the item falls back to status only; the activity notes it.
- **Deleting a launch:** its items return to Planned; its checklist tasks are **never deleted**, only unlinked (the dialog says so).
- **Changing the checklist preset after ticks:** blocked (S10).
- **Public item made private again:** disappears from the public roadmap at once.
- **Removing the tab:** decision 2. Hide keeps everything; checklist tasks stay on the Tasks board without their launch chip. Delete sends items and launches to Trash; checklist tasks and linked projects are **never deleted**.

#### 13. Phone
- **Launches is the default view:** the next launch on top with its countdown and checklist; tapping opens the launch page full-screen with stages folded except the current one.
- **Checklist:** one tap ticks; a long press opens person and date.
- **Status board:** one column at a time, with status chips to switch.
- **Quarters / Timeline:** quarter chips; timeline uses Month zoom with bars and diamonds, no dragging (Set quarter / Set date sheets instead).

#### 14. Accessibility
- **Keyboard:** arrows move between cards and columns; **Enter** opens; **M** opens Move to status; **Q** opens Set quarter; **L** opens Add to launch; in a checklist, **Space** ticks the focused item and **P** / **D** set person / date.
- **Screen readers:** cards read as one sentence ("Sign-in with SSO, Feature, High, In progress, 40 percent, ships in v2.4 on December 12"). Diamonds on the timeline are listed as "Launch v2.4, December 12, in 23 days, 14 of 31 checklist items done".
- **No dragging needed:** every drag has a menu version.
- **Colour is never the only signal.**

#### 15. Notifications and activity
| Event | Who | Level |
|---|---|---|
| Item or launch assigned to you | New assignee | Important |
| Checklist task assigned to you | Its assignee | Important (existing task rule) |
| Checklist task due | Its assignee | Normal (existing reminder) |
| Launch in 7 days / in 1 day | Launch assignee + checklist task assignees | Normal |
| "Items not ready" appears 7 days before launch | Launch assignee + item assignees | Normal |
| Launched | All workspace members | Summary |
| An item you're watching is launched | Watchers | Normal |
| Mentioned | The mentioned person | Important (existing) |

- **Activity history:** items: status moves, quarter changes, added/removed from a launch, linked work changes, public on/off, won't do with reason. Launches: date changes, items added/removed, preset chosen, launched (with what shipped), closed, cancelled.

#### 16. Trust and data
- Workspace data only. Internal notes, people and checklists never reach the public roadmap; "Why" is the only text shown publicly, and only for items marked **Show publicly** (the item page labels it "shown publicly").
- **Agents:** read and edit only with a member's own access.
- **Export:** CSV for members **[call]** (nothing here is more private than Tasks).
- **Limits to track** (values come with decision 6): launches per month, checklist presets per workspace, the public roadmap as a possible Pro feature.

#### 17. Reuse vs new
- **Reused as is:**
  - task data (assignee, comments, files, watchers, reminders, activity, undo, My Work)
  - from the Project planner: the Timeline view, filter chips, the one-scroll item page, emoji-or-Lucide icons, **Part of**, project completion
  - from Goals: quarters (period setting) and key result links
  - Updates' existing **release** and **milestone** types (`workspace_updates.update_type`)
  - the board drag engine, UnderlineTabs, ConfirmDialog, dropdown menu, SearchField, EmptyState, skeleton, the tab error boundary, live updates, the chat task card, task tools in the CLI/MCP
- **New:**
  - kinds `roadmap_item` and `launch` (B4)
  - a **stage** on tasks that are Part of a launch
  - Part of extended to point at a launch
  - checklist presets (B7) and "save as preset"
  - the status board, Quarters board, Backlog table and Launches list
  - the launch page, the Launch and Close launch dialogs, the What's new draft
  - the per-item **Show publicly** switch and the public roadmap view (S14)
  - launch diamonds on timelines
  - the Overview card, `nb launch status`
  - the tab switch (B10)

#### 18. How we know it works
- **Usage signal:** the share of workspaces with Roadmap & launches that complete at least one launch (Launch pressed) within 6 weeks of adding the tab.
- **Checks once built:**
  - the design contract test
  - side-by-side checks against the references (status board columns and card contents; launch page stage layout)
  - unit tests: item auto-Launched on launch, progress from project vs tasks, "not ready" rule, one launch per item, preset locked after ticks, quarter move prompt
  - end to end: create items → create a launch with the Product launch preset → assign and tick checklist tasks → Launch → What's new draft → post the release Update → Close launch
  - public roadmap shows only public items, with no names or %
  - phone checklist ticking; keyboard-only check
