### 11.6 Meetings & decisions (own tab, all 18 layers)

**References (ranked by rating and checked on 2026-11-16):**
- **Meetings by Notion** (4.8 from 200+, the top meeting template). The main reference for the meetings half:
  - a list with views **Meetings · Mine · Calendar**; each row has an icon, a name, a date and attendee avatars
  - a meeting page with **Attendees · Created by · Date · Last edited by · Meeting type**, then an AI notes block (Notes / Transcript, "Start transcribing")
  - a reviewer says it's missing "insights from the meeting, an integrated calendar, topic tags, automations with tasks"
- **Retrospective by Notion** (4.8 from 100+): **What went well · What needs improvement · Ideas for what to do differently · Action items**, each with an **"Add a point"** button that inserts "@you —".
- **Standup Meeting** (4.9 from 67): standup notes, one block per person.
- **Meeting Notes** (Gaurav Vermma, 4.8 from 44) and **Team Meeting Notes** (desbyseb, 5.0 from 21): agenda, key points, decisions and action items in one place.
- **Decision templates** (Decision Library; Architecture Decision Record 4.4 from 5; Decision Making 4.8 from 4): context → options → chosen solution → why → expected outcome.
- **Lessons Learned** (5.0 from 3) and **Mistake Log** (Startup #9): what happened, good or bad, so the next project goes better.

**Already in NetworkBase:** chat canvas templates for **Meeting notes** (Attendees · Agenda · Notes · Decisions · Action items), **Weekly status**, **Retrospective**, **Decision** (Status · Decided by · Context · Options · Decision) and **Incident report** (`src/lib/messaging/canvas-store.ts`); and the **"decision"** Update type. They are reused here.

**Agreed changes from an exact copy (2026-11-16):**
1. **No AI transcription block.** It becomes plain Notes, with an optional agent summary (no audio recording).
2. **"Created by / Last edited by" move to Activity**, so the property list stays short.
3. **Meeting bodies come from our existing chat canvas templates**, so the same words appear in chat and in the tab.
4. **Retro "Add a point" is kept**, but points can become Lessons, and action items become tasks.
5. **The usual changes:** our badge shape (no fully round pills), "Assigned to" never "Owner" or "Lead", our section headings, and emoji-or-Lucide icons.

Marked **[call]** = a decision made in this design that the user can overrule.

#### 1. Getting it
- **Where it's offered:**
  - **+ Add workflow** (owners and admins)
  - the wizard's Settings step, shown unticked for Startup, Open source and Developer tool (section 6)
  - added by an organization
- **In the + Add workflow dialog:** a Meetings & decisions row with a small preview of the meeting list. No presets at this step; meeting types are picked per meeting.
- **First look:**
  - the Meetings view, empty, with a hint: "Notes, decisions and action items from your meetings, in one place. Action items become tasks."
  - **+ New meeting** opens with the type picker
  - the Decisions and Lessons views say what they collect (layer 8)

#### 2. Setting it up
- **Meeting types** (each with a ready body; admins can rename, hide, add, or edit the body):

| Type | Body sections |
|---|---|
| **Weekly / Team** | Agenda · Notes · Decisions · Action items |
| **Standup** | one block per attendee: Yesterday · Today · Blockers |
| **Planning** | Goal · What's in · What's out · Action items (can link a sprint) |
| **Retrospective** | What went well · What needs improvement · Ideas for what to do differently · Action items, each with **Add a point** |
| **Kickoff** | Why · Scope · People · Dates · Risks · Action items |
| **1:1** | Their topics · My topics · Action items (private to the two attendees) |
| **Client** | Agenda · Notes · Next steps (can link a Pipeline deal) |
| **Recording session** (added by 18.3) | Tech checklist · Prep questions · Timings (for podcast and video recordings) |
| **Shoot day** (added by 19.4) | Call time · Location · Crew and cast · Equipment · Shots to get · Weather and notes; makes a Call sheet |
| **User interview** (added by 20.6) | Participant · Consent to record · Research goal · Script questions · Notes · Insights |
| **Incident review** (added by 21.2) | The incident's timeline · Root cause · Actions · Lessons (blameless) |
| **Playtest** (added by 22.3) | Build · Tester · Minutes played · What I saw · Fun moments · Confusion points · Bugs · Ideas |
| **Blank** | Notes |

- **Decision statuses:** Proposed → Decided; later Superseded or Reversed. Fixed.
- **Lesson types:** Went well · Mistake · Idea. **Impact:** Low / Medium / High.
- **Default meeting length:** 30 minutes. **Reminder:** 15 minutes before (admins can change or turn off).
- **Fields:** admins can add their own fields to meetings, decisions or lessons (B3).

#### 3. Items
- **Meeting:** a **task of kind `meeting`** (decision 1). Holds icon, name, type, attendees, date and time (start–end), series, labels, channel, body (sections from the type), action items, decisions, status (Upcoming → Finished; Cancelled).
- **Decision:** a **task of kind `decision`**. Holds name, status, decided by, date decided, revisit on, labels, context, options and trade-offs (rows: option, good, bad), decision, why, expected outcome, links (meeting, project, roadmap item, key result), superseded by.
- **Lesson:** a **task of kind `lesson`**. Holds name, type, impact, from (retro meeting, launch, project, Goals note), labels, what happened, why it happened, what we'll do differently, action (a task).
- **Action item:** a **normal task** with a **From** link to its meeting **[call]**. It has an assignee, due date, reminders; it shows on the Tasks board and in My Work.
- **Series:** a meeting can belong to a series ("Every Monday 10:00", "Every 2 weeks", "Every weekday"). The series isn't a separate item; each meeting knows its series and the next one is created on Finish (layer 5).
- **Every way to create one:**
  1. **+ New meeting** in the title row (type picker first)
  2. **Click a day/time** in the Calendar view
  3. **Record a decision** inside a meeting, or **+ New decision** in the Decisions view
  4. **Save as lesson** from a retro point, a closed launch's "After launch" stage, a finished project, or Goals' "What we learned"
  5. **From chat:** "Move to Meetings" on a Meeting notes / Retrospective / Decision canvas (copies it into the tab as the matching item)
  6. **CLI / agents** (layer 9)

#### 4. Views
| View | What's on screen | Filter / sort |
|---|---|---|
| **Meetings** (desktop default) | Rows grouped **Today · Upcoming · Past**: icon, name, time, type badge, attendee avatars, and "3 action items open" or "2 decisions" | Type, attendees, labels, series |
| **Mine** | The same, only meetings you attend | As above |
| **Calendar** | Month and week; meetings as blocks at their time; series shown as repeats | Type, attendees |
| **Decisions** | A table: name, status, decided by, date, revisit on, from | Proposed · Decided · Revisit due · All; labels |
| **Lessons** | A list: name, type, impact, from, action status | All · Went well · Mistakes · Ideas · By project |

- **Search** covers meeting names and body text, decision text and lesson text.
- **Labels** work as topic tags across all three kinds (the reviewer's "topic tags").

#### 5. Actions and flow
**Meetings**
1. **Create:** pick type, name, attendees, date and time, optional series and channel. The body is filled from the type.
2. **Before:** attendees add agenda items; standup attendees can fill in their block early.
3. **During:** write notes; **+ Add action item** (name → person · date) creates a task; **Record a decision** creates a Decision with status Decided (or Proposed).
4. **Finish meeting** (any attendee):
   - locks the date and marks the meeting **Finished**
   - lists action items with no assignee so they can be assigned
   - posts a notes card to the linked **Channel**, if set
   - for Retros, offers **Save as lessons** on its points
   - for a series, creates the next meeting with **carry over**: unfinished agenda items move across, and the still-open action items are listed at the top
5. **Cancel:** marks it Cancelled (a series continues); action items are untouched.

**Decisions**
1. **Propose:** context and options.
2. **Decide:** pick the option, write why; the dialog asks **who decided** and sets the date.
3. **Revisit:** on the revisit date the decider gets a reminder; they can **Keep**, **Reverse** (status Reversed, with why) or **Replace** (creates a new decision; the old one becomes Superseded, linked both ways).
4. **Post as an Update** (optional, off by default) uses the existing "decision" Update type.

**Lessons**
1. **Save** from one of the sources, or write one directly.
2. **Act:** optionally create an action task (for example "Add a Docs step to the Feature release preset").
3. Lessons don't close; they stay as the team's record.

#### 6. The tab's own surfaces
**S1. View tabs:** `Meetings · Mine · Calendar · Decisions · Lessons` (UnderlineTabs).

**S2. Title row:** `▤ Meetings`, counts in mono ("2 today · 5 action items open"), search, **+ New meeting** (primary; in Decisions it becomes **+ New decision**, in Lessons **+ New lesson**), ⋯: Meeting types · Reminder · Edit fields · Export CSV.

**S3. Filter chips:** `Type ▾ · Attendees ▾ · + Filter` (Labels, Series, Status). The row built for the Project planner.

**S4. Meetings list**
```
Today
  ⚡ Weekly team meeting      10:00–10:30   Weekly     (A)(S)(D)+2   ● 3 action items open
Upcoming
  🐟 Sprint 31 planning       Thu 14:00     Planning   (A)(S)
Past
  🧑‍🎨 Design standup          Nov 11        Standup    (D)            ✓ 2 decisions
```
- Row ⋯: Open · Join notes · Add to calendar · Copy link · Cancel · Delete.

**S5. Calendar:** month / week toggle, ‹ Today ›; clicking an empty slot opens the create dialog with that time.

**S6. Meeting page** (side panel, one scroll, **Open as full page** in ⋯)
```
⚡ Weekly team meeting
  Attendees     (A) Asha  (S) Sohrab  (D) Dev  + add
  Date          Mon, Nov 16 · 10:00–10:30        Add to calendar (.ics)
  Meeting type  Weekly         Series  Every Monday 10:00
  Labels        Hiring · Q4
  Channel       #team (notes get posted here when done)
──────────────────────────────
Agenda                          (carried over from last week: 1 item)
  1. Hiring plan for Q1
  2. Launch v2.4 status
Notes
  …free writing, @mentions…
Decisions                                             + Record a decision
  ◇ Move launch to Dec 12          Decided · Asha
Action items                                          + Add action item
  ☐ Draft job post → (S) Sohrab · Nov 20     (a real task)
  ☐ Share v2.4 checklist → (A) Asha · Nov 18
──────────────────────────────
[ Finish meeting ]   Comments · Files · Activity
```
- **Body:** the docs editor, with the type's sections as headings. Two people typing at once is handled as in Documents.
- **Standup body:** one block per attendee, each editable only by that person (others can comment).
- **Retro body:** each section has **Add a point** (inserts "@you —"); each point has ⋯ → **Save as lesson** / **Make an action item**.
- **Action item rows:** checkbox, name, `→ person · date`, ⋯ (open task, delete). Ticking completes the task.

**S7. Decision page** (side panel, one scroll). **Type:** Decision or **Architecture decision** (numbered ADR-0001…, statuses Proposed → Accepted → Deprecated / Superseded, Consequences section; see 13.6).
```
◇ Pricing: per seat or flat?
  Status        Proposed            Decided by   —
  Revisit on    —                   Labels       Pricing
  From          ⚡ Weekly team meeting · Nov 16
──────────────────────────────
Context        What needs deciding and why now…
Options and trade-offs
  1. Per seat      + grows with teams      − hurts big classes
  2. Flat          + simple                − leaves money on the table
  3. Hybrid        + …                      − …
Decision       (empty until decided)
Why            …
Expected outcome …
Links          ✦ Pricing page (roadmap item) · ◎ Paid accounts (key result)
──────────────────────────────
[ Decide ]   Comments · Files · Activity
```
- **Decide** opens S10. Once decided, the page shows "Decided by Asha on Nov 16" and the **Revisit / Reverse / Replace** actions in ⋯.
- A superseded decision shows a banner: "Superseded by → Hybrid pricing (Jan 4)".

**S8. Lesson page** (side panel, one scroll): type and impact badges, from, labels; What happened · Why it happened · What we'll do differently; **Action** (create or link a task).

**S9. New meeting dialog:** type picker (cards with the body's section names), then name, attendees (default me), date and time, length, series (none / weekly / every 2 weeks / weekdays / monthly), channel, labels.

**S10. Decide dialog:** pick the option (or write one), why, decided by (people picker, default me), revisit on (optional).

**S11. Finish meeting dialog:** unassigned action items with person and date pickers; "Post notes to #team" (on when a channel is set); for Retros, the list of points with **Save as lesson** checkboxes; for a series, "Next meeting: Mon, Nov 23 · carry over 1 agenda item".

**S12. Decisions table** and **S13. Lessons list** (layer 4).

**S14. Overview card:** "2 meetings today · 5 action items open · 1 decision to revisit", with a link to the tab.

#### 7. Design spec
- **Type (Section 04):** Instrument Sans for names, headings and body headings; JetBrains Mono for times, dates and counts.
- **Colour:**
  - **Meeting type badges:** muted Ink with an icon (no colour coding needed).
  - **Decision status:** Proposed = warning, Decided = success, Superseded / Reversed = muted Ink. Always with words.
  - **Lesson type:** Went well = success, Mistake = danger, Idea = in-progress status colour. Always with an icon.
  - **"Action items open" dot:** Clay.
- **Badges (Section 10):** all badges and filter chips use the precision badge geometry. No fully round pills.
- **Motion (Section 05):** 180 ms ease-out for ticks and list changes, no spring.
- **Icons (Lucide):**
  - NotebookPen: the tab and meetings
  - Repeat: series
  - Diamond (outline): decisions
  - Lightbulb: lessons
  - CheckSquare: action items
  - CalendarPlus: Add to calendar
- **Item icons:** emoji or Lucide (the same exception as projects).
- **Density, spacing, corner radii and empty states:** per the spec and the empty-state contract.
- **Contract test:** `tests/unit/meetings-design-contract.test.ts`, with the same rules as the task contract.

#### 8. Words
- **Tab:** "Meetings" **[call]** (shorter; "decisions and lessons" appears in the + Add workflow description). **Items:** Meeting, Decision, Lesson, Action item.
- **Kept from the references:** Meetings, Mine, Calendar, Attendees, Date, Meeting type; What went well · What needs improvement · Ideas for what to do differently · Action items; Add a point; Context, Options, Decision.
- **Ours:** Finish meeting, Series, Carry over, Record a decision, Decide, Decided by, Revisit on, Superseded by, Reverse, Replace, Save as lesson, Went well · Mistake · Idea, What happened · Why it happened · What we'll do differently, From.
- Never "Lead", "Owner", "minutes" (old-fashioned), "MoM".
- **Empty messages:**
  - Meetings: "No meetings yet. Notes, decisions and action items from your meetings, in one place. Action items become tasks."
  - Decisions: "No decisions recorded yet. Write down what you decided and why, so nobody has to ask later."
  - Lessons: "No lessons yet. They collect here from retros, launches and finished projects."
  - Action items (none): "No action items."

#### 9. Links to the rest of NetworkBase
- **Tasks:** action items are tasks with a **From** link; the task panel shows "From: Weekly team meeting". Meetings, decisions and lessons themselves don't appear on the Tasks board **[call]**.
- **My Work:** today's meetings you attend (with time), your action items, decisions to revisit.
- **Sprints:** a Planning meeting can link a sprint; the sprint page lists its planning and retro meetings.
- **Project planner / Roadmap / Goals:** decisions link to projects, roadmap items and key results (shown on their pages as "Decisions: 2"). Finished projects, closed launches and Goals' "What we learned" offer **Save as lesson**.
- **Pipeline:** a Client meeting can link a deal; it then appears in the deal's Touches as a meeting touch.
- **Chat:**
  - a meeting can have a **Channel**; Finish posts a notes card there
  - the existing chat canvases keep working; "Move to Meetings" copies a canvas into the tab
  - meeting, decision and lesson cards can be shared (the existing "task" chat card)
- **Updates:** a decision can be posted with the existing **"decision"** Update type (off by default).
- **Documents:** the meeting body uses the same editor; a meeting can link docs.
- **Global search and deep links:** all three kinds are found by name and text (1:1s only by their attendees); each has its own link.
- **CLI and agents:** task commands and tools with `kind: "meeting"` / `"decision"` / `"lesson"`, plus:
  - `nb meetings today`
  - `nb meetings summary <meeting>` (an agent writes a summary into the Notes, marked "Summary by agent")
  - the agent briefing lists today's meetings and open action items

#### 10. People
| Who | Can |
|---|---|
| Owner / admin | Everything (except reading 1:1s they're not in), plus meeting types, reminder, fields, export |
| Member | Create meetings, decisions and lessons; edit the body of meetings they attend; add action items; finish meetings they attend; propose and decide decisions (the Decide dialog records who decided); delete what they created |
| 1:1 attendees | The only two people who can see a 1:1 meeting, its notes and its action items' link back **[call]**. The action items themselves are normal tasks, visible as tasks usually are, without the meeting's notes. |
| Public | **Never.** The tab is members-only and can't be made public **[call]**, because notes are internal. |
| Organization | Can push the tab to its workspaces (decision 4). No roll-up. The organization's own Meetings tab works the same for org-level meetings. |

#### 11. States
- **Loading:** skeletons for the view tabs, title row, filter chips and three grouped rows each; counts show "—".
- **Error:** the tab error boundary with Retry; a failed body load shows the properties with "Notes couldn't load. Retry."
- **No permission:** members only; a 1:1 link opened by someone else shows "This meeting is private to its attendees."
- **Live updates:** notes, ticks and new action items appear for everyone in the meeting without a refresh (the Documents editor's live editing for the body).
- **Two people at once:** the body merges like Documents; property changes are last-write-wins with a toast.
- **Undo:** adding/removing action items, Finish meeting (as one undo, within the undo window, including the next series meeting it created), Decide, deleting.

#### 12. Edges
- **Empty:** layers 1 and 8.
- **Meetings in other time zones:** times are stored with time zone and shown in each viewer's own; the meeting page shows the organiser's zone when it differs.
- **A series whose organiser leaves:** passes to the next attendee; the activity notes it.
- **An attendee leaves the workspace:** shows "Former member"; their standup block stays; their open action items appear under "Unassigned / former" for admins.
- **A 1:1 attendee leaves:** loses access; the notes stay with the other attendee.
- **Finishing a meeting with no notes:** allowed; the notes card says "No notes".
- **Deleting a meeting:** its action-item tasks and its decisions are **never deleted** (the dialog says so); their "From" link shows "deleted meeting".
- **A decision linked to something deleted:** the link shows "deleted"; the decision stays.
- **Too many:** Past meetings page by month; decisions and lessons tables page at 100 rows.
- **Removing the tab:** decision 2. Hide keeps everything (action items stay on the Tasks board without the "From" chip). Delete sends meetings, decisions and lessons to Trash; action-item tasks are **never deleted**.

#### 13. Phone
- **Today** first: today's meetings, then "Your action items".
- **Opening a meeting** puts the cursor in Notes; **+ Action item** is pinned at the bottom within thumb reach.
- **Standup:** your own block opens directly, so it can be filled in before the meeting.
- **Calendar:** week view as a day-by-day list.
- **Decide / Finish:** bottom sheets.

#### 14. Accessibility
- **Keyboard:** **N** new meeting; inside a meeting, **A** adds an action item, **D** records a decision, **Ctrl/Cmd + Enter** finishes the meeting (with the dialog); arrows move between rows.
- **Screen readers:** rows read as "Weekly team meeting, today 10 to 10:30, Weekly, 5 attendees, 3 action items open". Standup blocks are labelled with the person's name. Calendar has a list alternative.
- **Colour is never the only signal.**

#### 15. Notifications and activity
| Event | Who | Level |
|---|---|---|
| Added as an attendee | That person | Normal |
| Meeting in 15 minutes | Attendees | Normal |
| Meeting time changed or cancelled | Attendees | Important |
| Action item assigned | Its assignee | Important (existing task rule) |
| Meeting finished, notes posted | The linked channel (as a message), attendees | Summary |
| Decision decided | Watchers + assignees of linked items | Normal |
| Revisit date reached | The decider | Normal |
| Mentioned in notes | The mentioned person | Important (existing) |

- 1:1 notes and mentions inside them never notify anyone but the two attendees.
- **Activity history:** meetings: time changes, attendees added/removed, finished, cancelled, action items added; decisions: status changes (with who decided), revisit set, superseded/reversed; lessons: created from (source), action linked.

#### 16. Trust and data
- Notes are internal; the tab is never public. 1:1s are private to their two attendees, **including from admins** **[call]**; export never includes 1:1s.
- **Agents:** read meetings only with a member's own access; an agent summary is marked as such and can be removed.
- **Export:** CSV of meetings (no bodies), decisions and lessons, for admins **[call]**.
- **.ics files:** contain only name, time and attendees' display names (no notes).
- **Limits to track** (values come with decision 6): meetings per month, series per workspace.

#### 17. Reuse vs new
- **Reused as is:**
  - task data (assignee, comments, files, watchers, reminders, activity, undo, My Work)
  - the chat canvas templates' sections (`src/lib/messaging/canvas-store.ts`) as meeting bodies; chat channels and the "task" chat card
  - the Documents editor and its live editing for the body
  - Updates' existing **"decision"** type
  - from the Project planner: filter chips, the one-scroll item page, emoji-or-Lucide icons; from Content calendar (later) the Calendar view
  - UnderlineTabs, ConfirmDialog, dropdown menu, SearchField, EmptyState, skeleton, DateTimeField, the tab error boundary, live updates, task tools in the CLI/MCP
- **New:**
  - kinds `meeting`, `decision`, `lesson` (B4)
  - meeting types with bodies, series and carry over
  - **From** links on tasks (action items)
  - Finish meeting, Decide, Save as lesson (wired into retros, launches, projects and Goals)
  - options and trade-offs rows; superseded-by and revisit on decisions
  - private 1:1 visibility (a per-item rule the other tabs don't have)
  - .ics export, "Move to Meetings" from chat canvases
  - the Overview card, `nb meetings today` / `summary`
  - the tab switch (B10)

#### 18. How we know it works
- **Usage signal:** the share of workspaces with Meetings where, 3 weeks after adding it, at least one meeting a week was finished with at least one action item.
- **Checks once built:**
  - the design contract test
  - side-by-side checks against the references (list views and row contents; meeting page property list; retro sections with Add a point)
  - unit tests: series next date (including month ends and time zones), carry over, Finish meeting effects, superseded links both ways, revisit reminders
  - privacy tests: a 1:1 is invisible to admins and in search, export and notifications for anyone but its attendees
  - end to end: create a weekly series → add agenda → add two action items and a decision → Finish → notes posted to the channel → next meeting has the carry-over; a retro point saved as a lesson
  - phone note-taking; keyboard-only check

### 11.7 Tasks → Matrix view (view, layers 4, 5, 6, 7, 11–14)

**References (checked on 2026-11-16):**
- **Eisenhower Matrix** (4.9 from 500+, the most used Startup-related template): a 2×2 grid with **Important / Not important** down the side and **Urgent / Not urgent** across the top. The four boxes are **Do first · Schedule · Delegate · Eliminate**, each holding checkbox items, with a Tasks list underneath.
- **Automated Eisenhower Matrix** (4.6 from 14, Startup #2): places tasks in the boxes from their fields instead of by hand.

It's a **view inside the Tasks tab**, not a new tab, and works on existing tasks; nothing new needs to be entered.

Marked **[call]** = a decision made in this design that the user can overrule.

#### 4. View
```
Tasks   Board · Matrix        Mine ▾                         + New task
                URGENT (due in 3 days or overdue)      NOT URGENT
IMPORTANT   ┌ Do first 3 ───────────────────┐ ┌ Schedule 5 ──────────────────┐
(High,      │ #142 Fix sign-in bug  Today   │ │ #150 Pricing page    Dec 2   │
 Urgent)    │ #139 Investor update  Nov 18  │ │ #151 Hiring plan     —       │
            └───────────────────────────────┘ └──────────────────────────────┘
NOT         ┌ Delegate 2 ───── [Assign…] ───┐ ┌ Drop 4 ─── [Move to Backlog] ┐
IMPORTANT   │ #147 Book venue       Nov 19  │ │ #120 Old logo ideas  —       │
            └───────────────────────────────┘ └──────────────────────────────┘
```
- **Placement [call]:**
  - **Important** = priority High or Urgent.
  - **Urgent** = due within 3 days, or overdue (admins can change the number of days in the Tasks ⋯ menu).
  - No due date = not urgent.
- **Scope:** defaults to **Mine**, because a matrix is mainly for personal prioritising; every existing Tasks scope and filter still applies.
- **Hidden:** done and cancelled tasks, and items of other kinds (projects, deals, meetings…).
- **Order inside a box:** due date (soonest first), then priority.
- **Counts:** each box header shows its count, from the same single read as the board's counts.

#### 5. Actions
- **Move up or down** (important ↔ not important) changes the task's **priority** (to High, or to Medium).
- **Move into the Urgent column** opens a due-date quick picker (Today · Tomorrow · In 3 days · Pick a date), because urgency only ever comes from the due date. Nothing extra is stored that could fall out of sync **[call]**.
- **Move out of the Urgent column** asks whether to clear or push the due date.
- **Delegate box:** an **Assign…** button on the header (assign several selected tasks) and on each card.
- **Drop box** ("Eliminate" renamed **[call]**): **Move to Backlog** / **Cancel** on the header (for selected tasks) and on each card.
- **Clicking a card** opens the normal task panel.

#### 6. Surfaces
- **S1. View switch:** "Matrix" joins the Tasks view options next to the board; the choice is remembered per person.
- **S2. Axis labels:** "URGENT", "NOT URGENT", "IMPORTANT", "NOT IMPORTANT" with the rule in small text under each ("due in 3 days or overdue", "High, Urgent").
- **S3. Boxes:** name, count, header action (Assign… / Move to Backlog), then compact task cards.
- **S4. Compact task card:** the existing task card in its compact form: number, title, due date, assignee avatar, priority badge.
- **S5. Due-date quick picker** (when moving into Urgent).
- **S6. Empty box:** "Nothing here." (Do first: "Nothing urgent and important. Good.")

#### 7. Design spec
- Box labels in JetBrains Mono capitals, as in the reference; box names in Instrument Sans.
- No colour meaning per box **[call]**: the boxes are told apart by labels and position, so the grid stays calm. Overdue dates keep the danger colour with words, as everywhere in Tasks.
- 180 ms ease-out on moves, no spring; precision badges; no fully round pills.
- Icons (Lucide): Grid2x2 for the view; Flame (Do first), CalendarClock (Schedule), UserPlus (Delegate), Archive (Drop).
- Covered by the existing `tests/unit/task-design-contract.test.ts` (extended to include the Matrix component).

#### 11. States
- **Loading:** four box skeletons with two card shapes each.
- **Error:** the existing Tasks error handling.
- **Live updates:** a task whose priority or due date changes elsewhere moves box live.
- **Undo:** every move (priority / due date change) and the bulk Assign / Move to Backlog actions show **Undo**.

#### 12. Edges
- **More than 50 tasks in a box:** shows 50 with "Show all"; the count stays exact.
- **Priority "Urgent" with no due date:** important, not urgent (Schedule), with a small "No date" mark.
- **Assignments in organizations:** follow their own due dates and appear like other tasks.

#### 13. Phone
- Four folding sections in reading order (Do first, Schedule, Delegate, Drop), each with its count; Do first open by default.
- Moving: the card's ⋯ → **Move to box…** (a bottom sheet with the four boxes).

#### 14. Accessibility
- Each box is a labelled region ("Do first, important and urgent, 3 tasks").
- **Keyboard:** arrows move between cards and boxes; **M** opens "Move to box…"; **Enter** opens the task.
- No dragging needed: every move has the menu version.

**Links:** My Work can offer the same Matrix for "my tasks across workspaces" later **[call: not in this round]**.

### 11.8 Document templates (layers 1, 3, 8, 9)

**What's missing in the code today:** the New doc dialog (`src/components/workspaces/doc/AddDocDialog.tsx`) only offers templates inside **organizations** (docs an org marked as "template"). Ordinary workspaces get no templates.

**What changes:**
- New doc gets a **NetworkBase templates** section in every workspace, listing the built-in templates with the workspace category's templates first (for Startup: the four below). Organization templates stay as they are, in their own section.
- One new building block: a **`canvas` smart block** in docs. Docs already support smart blocks (`src/lib/workspaces/doc-blocks.ts`: roles, contributors, files, tasks, sprints, projects), so this follows the existing pattern. It shows boxes in a fixed grid, while each box's text is normal Markdown under its own heading, so the doc still reads, searches and exports correctly.
- A second new smart block: **`goals`**, which shows chosen key results with their current value, target and progress (used by the Investor update).

**Agreed change:** **Investor update replaces Investment memo** (2026-11-16). Notion's "Investment Memo Example" is a tool for investors to record their own investments (round terms, check size, conviction). A startup is on the other side: what founders send investors each month is an **update**, and Notion's own Investor update template is rated higher.

#### Business model canvas
- **Reference:** **Business model canvas by Notion** (4.8 from 100+): 9 cards, each with a group tag (Offering, Customers, Infrastructure, Finances); each card opens a page with a summary.
- **1. Getting it:** New doc → NetworkBase templates → "Business model canvas" (Startup first; also suggested for Side project, E-commerce and Freelance).
- **3. Contents:** the `canvas` smart block in the classic layout:

```
┌ Key partners ─┬ Key activities ┬ Value          ┬ Customer       ┬ Customer      ┐
│ Infrastructure│ Infrastructure │ propositions   │ relationships  │ segments      │
│               ├ Key resources ─┤ Offering       ├ Channels ──────┤ Customers     │
│               │ Infrastructure │                │ Customers      │               │
├ Cost structure ── Finances ────┴────────────────┴ Revenue streams ── Finances ───┤
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
  - Each box: its group label, a one-line prompt in muted text ("Who are we creating value for?"), and bullet points under its heading.
  - Box links: Customer segments → **Pipeline**, Key activities → **Project planner**, Revenue streams and Cost structure → **Money** (when those tabs exist; otherwise the links are hidden).
- **8. Words:** the standard canvas terms (Key partners, Key activities, Key resources, Value propositions, Customer relationships, Channels, Customer segments, Cost structure, Revenue streams) and the reference's group labels. "Key partners" is a standard term, not the banned "collaborators".
- **9. Links:** a normal doc (versions, search, links, Copy link); can be shared into chat as a doc card; the phone shows the boxes stacked in reading order.

#### Value proposition
- **Reference:** **Value Proposition Canvas** (5.0 from 10).
- **1. Getting it:** New doc → NetworkBase templates → "Value proposition" (Startup first; also Web app and Side project).
- **3. Contents:** a two-sided `canvas` smart block:
  - **Customer:** Jobs · Pains · Gains
  - **Our offer:** Products and services · Pain relievers · Gain creators
  - then a **Fit check** section: a table pairing each pain with what relieves it, and each gain with what creates it; an empty pairing is marked "No answer yet".
- **8. Words:** Jobs, Pains, Gains, Products and services, Pain relievers, Gain creators, Fit check.
- **9. Links:** the Customer side can link Pipeline deals or Feedback requests (later tab) as evidence.

#### Assumptions check
- **References:** Business Model Contradiction Finder and Venture Assumption Dependency Map (both RunBook, not yet rated; merged as agreed in 11.1).
- **1. Getting it:** New doc → NetworkBase templates → "Assumptions check" (Startup first; also Side project and Web app).
- **3. Contents:** a short intro ("What has to be true for this to work?"), then a table:

| Assumption | Depends on | Evidence | If it's wrong, what breaks | Cheapest test | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Schools will pay per seat | Teachers want it | Weak | Pricing, revenue plan | 5 calls with heads of IT | Testing |

  - **Evidence:** None / Weak / Strong. **Status:** Untested / Testing / Holds / Broken.
  - **Cheapest test → Make a task** (one click; the task links back to the row).
  - A row marked **Broken** offers **Record a decision** (creates a Proposed decision in Meetings & decisions with the row as its context).
  - **Depends on** can point at another row; rows that others depend on are marked "load-bearing".
- **8. Words:** Assumption, Depends on, Evidence, Cheapest test, Holds, Broken, load-bearing.
- **9. Links:** tasks (tests), Meetings & decisions (broken assumptions), Goals (an assumption can name the key result it risks).

#### Investor update
- **Reference:** **Investor update by Notion** (4.8 from 17). Its live page didn't load, so the sections come from Notion's description plus the common investor-update format; the other three references were checked live.
- **1. Getting it:** New doc → NetworkBase templates → "Investor update" (Startup only). Pipeline's **Investors** preset also offers "Write an investor update" in its ⋯.
- **3. Contents:**
  - **TL;DR** (three lines)
  - **Key numbers:** a `goals` smart block showing the chosen key results' current value, target and change since the last update (so numbers are never typed twice)
  - **Highlights · Lowlights · Asks** (what investors can help with) · **Hiring** · **Runway** (months of cash left, typed by hand)
  - each new update starts with the previous update's Asks for follow-up
- **Actions:** **Copy as email** (plain text with the numbers filled in) and **Save as PDF**. NetworkBase doesn't send it **[call]**.
- **8. Words:** TL;DR, Key numbers, Highlights, Lowlights, Asks, Hiring, Runway.
- **9. Links:** Goals (numbers), Pipeline Investors (who it went to, logged as a touch when "Copy as email" is used from a pipeline), Documents versions (each month is a new doc or a new version **[call: a new doc per month, named "Investor update – Nov 2026"]**).
- **Trust:** the doc follows the workspace's Documents visibility; the template reminds the writer that numbers inside are as private as the doc.

### 11.9 Already covered items, and the Startup summary

| Notion template | Covered by | Gap to close |
|---|---|---|
| Startup Team Management · Staff Directory (#6, #15) | Members + Tasks + My Work | A **Title** on each person's workspace membership (e.g. "Designer"), shown on member cards and in people pickers **[call]** |
| Business Owner OS · Founder OS (#8, #11) | The Overview tab | Closed by the **Overview cards** each tab already has (Pipeline, Project planner, Goals, Roadmap, Meetings), shown in tab order |
| Find the Trade-Offs (#17) | Decision page → **Options and trade-offs** (11.6) | None |
| Product Backlog and Grooming (#18) | Tasks → Backlog + Sprints | None |
| Payment Collection Tracker (#4) | Money → **Invoices** preset | Designed in full under Freelance |
| Social Media Metrics Dashboard (#5) | Content calendar → **Performance** view | Designed in full under Content/Blog |

**Startup is complete.** What a Startup workspace gets:
- **Wizard (decision 5):** Project planner ticked; Goals & OKRs, Pipeline, Roadmap & launches and Meetings shown unticked.
- **Tabs:** Pipeline (Sales, Investors, Collaborations presets) · Project planner · Goals · Roadmap & launches · Meetings (with decisions and lessons).
- **Inside Tasks:** the Matrix view.
- **Documents:** Business model canvas · Value proposition · Assumptions check · Investor update.
- **Small gaps:** member Title.
- **Designed in other categories:** Money (Freelance), Content calendar (Content/Blog).

**New shared parts built for Startup and reused later:** the Timeline view, the filter chip row, the one-scroll item page, emoji-or-Lucide item icons, **Part of** and **From** links, check-ins/touches as comments carrying a value, the period model, checklist presets, the `canvas` and `goals` doc smart blocks, and the NetworkBase templates section in New doc.

**Next category:** to be chosen by the user. Every later category reuses these parts, so its sections are mostly presets, views and document templates.

**Status (2026-11-17, section 28.2):** 12.2 Money · **Parked** | 12.3 Clients preset · **Parked** | 12.4 Client portal · **Parked** | 12.5 Client report · **Documents** (its time block waits for Money)

Notion source: the "Client portal", "Invoicing" and "CRM" categories (Notion's broad Freelance list was only personal planners), plus the highest-rated money templates (Popular order and ratings, 2026-11-16).

| 17 | Expense & Budget Tracker (Sentele) | 4.8 / 48 | Own tab | **Money → Transactions / Budget** |
| 18 | Subscription Tracker | 4.8 / 46 | Own tab | **Money → recurring entries** |

**Order for Freelance:** Money (12.2) → Pipeline **Clients** preset with Directory and onboarding → **Client portal** → **Client report** doc.

### 12.2 Money (own tab, all 18 layers)

**References (2026-11-16):**
- **Finance Tracker by Pablo** (4.8 from 300+, the most rated money template; checked live): Navigation · **Accounts** (Main, Joint, Savings, Cash cards) · **Overview** (Savings, Investments) · **Budget** (category cards: Food, Rent, Utilities, Shopping…) · **Expense Tracker** and **Income Tracker** tables side by side (Date · Name · Amount · Account) · Transfers · Subscriptions · Goals · Reports.
- **Expense & Budget Tracker by Sentele** (4.8 from 48): a spending-against-budget dashboard. Its live page didn't load; taken from its description.
- **Time Tracker** (4.8 from 12): "track your time so that your projects are financially profitable". Description only.
- **Freelance Income / Invoice / Payment Collection trackers** (unrated or low): invoice number, client, dates, status (Sent / Paid / Overdue), rate type (hourly, fixed, retainer), time log → invoice.
- **Lesson:** the most popular template is for **personal** finance (bank accounts, investments, transfers). A freelancer needs **business** records: invoices, time, expenses and a budget, tied to clients and projects.

**What the code has today:** no currency or money fields, no time tracking (the task "Estimate" is story points). A `viewer` workspace role exists (`src/lib/workspaces/settings-policies.ts`), used by the Client portal later.

**Agreed changes from an exact copy (2026-11-16):**
1. **No bank accounts, transfers, investments or debt.** Business records only; no bank connections.
2. **One Transactions view with Money in and Money out side by side** replaces the separate Expense Tracker and Income Tracker pages, keeping the reference's side-by-side look.
3. **Budget category cards become rows with spent bars.**
4. **NetworkBase never collects or moves money.** "Pay by" is text the user writes on their own invoice; payment is marked by hand.
5. **The usual changes:** our badge shape (no fully round pills), "Assigned to", our section headings, plain SVG charts.

Marked **[call]** = a decision made in this design that the user can overrule.

#### 1. Getting it
- **Where it's offered:**
  - **+ Add workflow** (owners and admins)
  - the wizard's Settings step: shown unticked for Freelance (Pipeline is ticked first there), Side project, Startup, Creative, Non-profit, E-commerce and Video (section 6)
  - added by an organization
- **Second step in the + Add workflow dialog: Choose a setup** (it decides which views start switched on; all can be changed later):

| Preset | Views switched on | For |
|---|---|---|
| **Freelance** | Overview · Invoices · Time · Transactions | Freelance, Creative, Video |
| **Startup** | Overview · Invoices · Transactions, plus a **Runway** tile (months of cash left) | Startup (Payment Collection Tracker) |
| **Non-profit** | Overview · Transactions · Budget, with grant income categories, plus **restricted / unrestricted funds** with a balance per fund (17.6) | Non-profit |
| **Shop** | Overview · Transactions with sales categories (Inventory adds orders later) | E-commerce, Side project |

- **First look:** Overview with all tiles at "₹0" (in the workspace currency) and one hint: "Invoices, time and spending for this workspace. NetworkBase never moves money; you mark what's paid." Then **Set up your details** (business name, address, tax ID, default currency, invoice prefix), which can be skipped.

#### 2. Setting it up (Money settings, admins)
- **Your business details:** name, address, tax ID, logo (from Files), shown only on invoices and their PDFs.
- **Default currency:** from the workspace owner's locale; each invoice or entry can use another.
- **Invoice prefix and next number:** default "INV-" and 0001.
- **Default tax %** and its name (e.g. "GST", "VAT"); default **payment terms** (14 days).
- **Default hourly rate.** Clients override it (layer 3).
- **Categories:** money in (Client work, Grants, Sales, Other) and money out (Software, Equipment, Travel, Fees, Subcontractors, Rent, Other); admins can add, rename and hide.
- **Budget:** a monthly amount per money-out category (Budget view only).
- **Who can see Money:** **Owners and admins (default) / Everyone in the workspace** **[call]**. Members always see their own time and expenses.
- **Expenses need approval:** on by default when members can submit expenses.

#### 3. Items
- **Invoice:** a **task of kind `invoice`** **[call]**. Holds number, client (a Pipeline client or a typed name), currency, issued date, due date, status, lines, subtotal, tax %, discount, total, payments, notes, pay-by text, assigned to.
  - **Line:** description, quantity or hours, rate, amount; optionally linked to time entries or an expense.
  - **Payment:** date, amount (partial payments allowed).
- **Money records** (one small table, decision 1) **[call]**:
  - **Time entry:** person, date, start/end or duration, task / project / client, billable, billed (invoice), note.
  - **Expense:** date, name, amount, currency, category, client/project, billable, receipt (a file), recurring (none / monthly / yearly), approval status.
  - **Income:** date, name, amount, currency, category, client/project (money in that isn't an invoice, e.g. a grant or a sale).
- **Client rates** (on Pipeline clients): **Hourly** (rate), **Fixed** (price per project), **Retainer** (monthly amount + day of month).
- **Every way to create:**
  1. **+ New invoice**, **+ Expense**, **+ Income**, **⏱ Start timer** in the title row
  2. **Turn into invoice** from unbilled time or billable expenses
  3. **Retainer drafts:** created automatically on the client's day, as **Draft**, never sent
  4. **From a Won Pipeline deal:** "Create an invoice"
  5. **▶ on a task** (task panel) starts the timer for that task
  6. **CLI / agents:** `nb time start <task>`, `nb time stop`, `nb expense add` (layer 9)

#### 4. Views
| View | What's on screen | Filter / sort |
|---|---|---|
| **Overview** (default) | Five tiles · Last 12 months bars · By client · Unbilled time · Due soon (S4) | Month, currency |
| **Invoices** | A table grouped **Draft · Sent · Overdue · Paid**: Number · Client · Issued · Due · Total · Status | Client, status, date range, currency |
| **Time** | Your timer on top, then entries by week: date · task or project · client · hours · billable · billed; day and week totals | Person (admins), client, project, billable, unbilled |
| **Transactions** | **Money in** and **Money out** tables side by side: date · name · category · client/project · amount · receipt | Month, category, client, recurring, approval |
| **Budget** | One row per money-out category: budget, spent, left, a spent bar | Month |

- **Search** covers invoice numbers, client names, entry names and notes.
- Views can be switched on or off per workspace (layer 1 presets).

#### 5. Actions and flow
**Invoices**
1. **Create** (Draft): pick the client (their currency and rate fill in), add lines or pull in unbilled time / billable expenses.
2. **Mark sent:** records the date; the invoice locks (editing needs **Draft again**, noted in Activity).
3. **Save as PDF:** a clean invoice with your business details and the pay-by text; also stored in Files ("Invoices" folder).
4. **Due:** a reminder 3 days before the due date; after it, status becomes **Overdue** automatically.
5. **Copy reminder text:** a polite message with the number, total and due date to paste into an email. NetworkBase sends nothing to clients **[call]**.
6. **Mark paid:** date and amount; partial payments keep it "Partly paid" until the total is covered.
7. **Cancel:** status Cancelled; its time entries become unbilled again; its number is never reused.

**Time**
1. **Start** (tab, task ▶ or CLI); one running timer per person.
2. **Stop:** saves an entry against the task, its project and its client; manual entries work too.
3. **Turn into invoice:** pick a client and period; unbilled billable entries become lines grouped by task or project; entries are marked billed.

**Expenses and income**
1. **Add** with a receipt (photo or PDF, stored in Files → "Receipts").
2. **Members' expenses** wait for **Approve / Decline** by an admin when approval is on.
3. **Recurring** entries repeat automatically on their day and show in Due soon first.

**Profit per project:** the Project planner's project page shows a **Money** line: hours logged, cost of hours (hours × rate), amount invoiced, and the difference.

#### 6. The tab's own surfaces
**S1. View tabs:** `Overview · Invoices · Time · Transactions · Budget` (UnderlineTabs; only switched-on views show).

**S2. Title row:** `₹ Money` (the icon follows the default currency), the **month switcher**, **Currency** switcher (when more than one currency is used), **+ New invoice** (primary), **⏱ Start timer** (shows the running time when on), ⋯: + Expense · + Income · Money settings · Export CSV.

**S3. Filter chips:** per view (layer 4), the row built for the Project planner.

**S4. Overview**
```
┌ Earned ─────┐┌ Waiting ────┐┌ Overdue ────┐┌ Spent ──────┐┌ Net ────────┐
│ ₹1,20,000   ││ ₹45,000     ││ ₹15,000 (2) ││ ₹18,400     ││ ₹1,01,600   │
└─────────────┘└─────────────┘└─────────────┘└─────────────┘└─────────────┘
Last 12 months   ▇ in  ▁ out    (plain bars, labelled)
By client        Acme  ₹60,000 ━━━━━━   ·  Bloom ₹40,000 ━━━━   ·  …
Unbilled time    14h 30m across 3 clients            [ Turn into invoices ]
Due soon         INV-0012 Bloom ₹15,000 due Nov 20   ·   Retainer draft for Acme ready
```
- Tiles: **Earned** (paid invoices + income), **Waiting** (sent, unpaid), **Overdue** (with count), **Spent**, **Net**; the Startup preset adds **Runway** (cash ÷ average monthly spend, with the cash figure typed by an admin).
- Clicking a tile opens the matching view with its filter.

**S5. Invoices table:** grouped by status with counts and totals per group; row ⋯: Open · Mark sent · Mark paid · Save as PDF · Copy reminder text · Duplicate · Cancel.

**S6. Invoice page** (side panel, one scroll, **Open as full page**)
```
INV-0012                                   Status  Sent · due Nov 20 (in 4 days)
  Client     Bloom Studio (from Pipeline)        Currency  INR
  Issued     Nov 6, 2026     Due  Nov 20, 2026   Assigned to (A) Asha
──────────────────────────────
  Description                         Qty / hours   Rate      Amount
  Logo design (fixed)                 1             ₹10,000   ₹10,000
  Revisions: 5h 0m (from Time)        5.0           ₹1,000    ₹5,000
                                         Subtotal   ₹15,000
                                         Tax 18%    ₹2,700
                                         Total      ₹17,700
  Paid       —                        [ Mark paid ]
──────────────────────────────
  From       Your business details (set once in Money settings)
  Pay by     Text you write: bank details, UPI ID or your payment link
  Notes      Thank you!
──────────────────────────────
[ Mark sent ] [ Save as PDF ] [ Copy reminder text ]   Comments · Files · Activity
```

**S7. Timer bar:** on the Time view and as a small chip in the title row while running: task name, client, elapsed time (mono), **Stop**, **Switch task**.

**S8. Time entries list:** grouped by week; each row editable in place; bulk select → **Turn into invoice**, **Mark not billable**.

**S9. Transactions:** two tables side by side (stacked on narrow screens), each with **+ Add** and a total row; receipt icon opens the file.

**S10. Budget rows:** category, budget, spent, left, a spent bar; 80% shows a warning mark, over 100% shows "Over by ₹2,000".

**S11. Dialogs:** New invoice · Turn into invoice (client, period, entries with checkboxes, grouping) · Mark paid (date, amount) · New expense / income (with receipt drop zone) · Approve expense · Money settings.

**S12. Invoice PDF:** your business details and logo, client, number, dates, lines, totals, pay-by text, notes. Plain, printable, in the spec's type.

**S13. Overview card** (workspace Overview tab): Earned this month, Waiting, Overdue (with count), and a link; visible only to people who can see Money.

#### 7. Design spec
- **Type (Section 04):** Instrument Sans for names and headings; **JetBrains Mono for every amount, hour count and invoice number**, right-aligned in tables.
- **Money formatting:** `Intl.NumberFormat` with the currency and the viewer's locale (₹1,20,000 for India, $120,000 for US).
- **Colour:**
  - Invoice status: Draft = muted Ink, Sent = in-progress status colour, Overdue = danger, Paid = success, Cancelled = muted Ink; always with words.
  - Money in / out bars: Ink and muted Ink (no green/red meaning on their own).
  - Budget over 80% = warning; over 100% = danger with words.
  - Primary buttons: Clay.
- **Badges (Section 10):** status and category chips use the precision badge geometry. No fully round pills.
- **Charts:** plain SVG/CSS, as in Goals.
- **Motion (Section 05):** 180 ms ease-out; the running timer updates once a second without animation.
- **Icons (Lucide):** the currency's icon (IndianRupee, DollarSign, Euro…) for the tab; FileText (invoices), Timer (time), ArrowDownLeft / ArrowUpRight (money in / out), PiggyBank (budget), Receipt (receipts), Repeat (recurring).
- **Density, spacing, corner radii and empty states:** per the spec and the empty-state contract.
- **Contract test:** `tests/unit/money-design-contract.test.ts`, with the task contract's rules plus: every amount renders in mono through the shared money formatter.

#### 8. Words
- **Tab:** "Money". **Items:** Invoice, Time entry, Expense, Income.
- **Kept from the references:** Budget, Income, Expenses, Subscriptions (shown as "Recurring"), Overview.
- **Ours:** Earned, Waiting, Overdue, Spent, Net, Runway, Unbilled, Billable, Billed, Turn into invoice, Mark sent, Mark paid, Partly paid, Draft again, Pay by, Your business details, Copy reminder text, Money in / Money out, Receipts.
- Never "Lead", "Owner", "payment processing", "charge" (we don't charge anyone).
- **Empty messages:**
  - Invoices: "No invoices yet. Create one, or turn logged time into one."
  - Time: "No time logged. Start the timer on any task."
  - Transactions: "Nothing recorded for November."
  - Budget: "No budget set. Give each category a monthly amount."

#### 9. Links to the rest of NetworkBase
- **Pipeline:** clients carry rate type and rate; a Won deal offers "Create an invoice"; a client's page shows invoiced and outstanding totals.
- **Project planner:** profit per project (layer 5); time entries roll up to projects.
- **Tasks:** ▶ timer on the task panel; a task shows "3h 20m logged"; time entries link back to tasks.
- **My Work:** "Invoice overdue: INV-0012", "Retainer draft ready: Acme", your running timer, expenses waiting for approval (admins).
- **Files:** receipts ("Receipts" folder) and invoice PDFs ("Invoices" folder), under the normal storage limits.
- **Overview:** the Money card (S13), for people who can see Money.
- **Chat:** an invoice can be shared as a card only with people who can see Money.
- **Global search and deep links:** invoices by number and client, for people who can see Money.
- **CLI and agents:** `nb time start <task>`, `nb time stop`, `nb time today`, `nb expense add <amount> <name> [--receipt file]`; the invoice tools are read-only for agents **[call]**.

#### 10. People
| Who | Can |
|---|---|
| Owner / admin | Everything: settings, invoices, all time and money records, approve expenses, export |
| Member (default) | See and edit **only their own** time entries and submitted expenses; run the timer; nothing else in Money |
| Member (when "Everyone" can see Money) | See Overview, invoices and transactions; create invoices; still can't change settings, approve expenses or export **[call]** |
| Viewer | Nothing in Money |
| Public | **Never** |
| Organization | Can add Money to itself or push it to workspaces (decision 4); **no roll-up** across workspaces **[call]** |

#### 11. States
- **Loading:** tile skeletons with "—", table skeletons with five rows.
- **Error:** the tab error boundary with Retry; totals never show partial sums (a failed read shows "—", not a wrong number).
- **No permission:** members see only their Time view and their expenses; the other views are hidden, not greyed out.
- **Live updates:** a payment, a new entry or a stopped timer updates the tiles and tables without a refresh.
- **Two people at once:** an invoice being edited shows "Asha is editing"; the second editor gets read-only until it's saved.
- **Undo:** mark sent / paid, turn into invoice (all its changes as one undo), deleting entries.

#### 12. Edges
- **Mixed currencies:** totals and tiles show per currency (₹… · $…), never converted **[call]**.
- **Numbers are never reused:** cancelled or deleted invoices keep their number; the next invoice continues the sequence.
- **Billing twice:** an entry already on an invoice can't be added to another.
- **A client deleted from Pipeline:** old invoices keep the client's name and details as they were.
- **Editing a sent invoice:** needs **Draft again**; Activity records the change.
- **Timer left running:** after 8 hours, a "Still working?" reminder; entries over 12 hours ask to confirm on stop.
- **Rounding:** amounts are stored in the currency's smallest unit (paise, cents), so totals never drift.
- **Tax:** one rate per invoice; a line can be marked "no tax".
- **Removing the tab:** decision 2. Hide keeps everything and stops reminders, recurring entries and retainer drafts. Delete sends invoices and records to Trash for 30 days; invoice PDFs and receipts stay in Files until deleted there.

#### 13. Phone
- **Start / Stop timer** comes first, then "Due soon".
- **+ Expense** opens the camera for the receipt.
- **Invoices:** a list by status; the invoice page full-screen; **Save as PDF** uses the phone's share sheet.
- **Transactions:** Money in and Money out stacked, with a toggle.

#### 14. Accessibility
- **Keyboard:** **T** starts/stops the timer; **N** new invoice; **E** new expense; arrows move through table rows; **Enter** opens.
- **Screen readers:** amounts are read with their currency ("17,700 rupees"); tiles read as "Overdue, 15,000 rupees, 2 invoices"; the 12-month bars have a table alternative.
- **Colour is never the only signal:** statuses and budget warnings always carry words.

#### 15. Notifications and activity
| Event | Who | Level |
|---|---|---|
| Invoice due in 3 days | Its assignee | Normal |
| Invoice overdue | Its assignee + admins | Important |
| Invoice paid | Its assignee | Normal |
| Retainer draft ready | Admins | Normal |
| Timer running 8 hours | The person | Normal |
| Budget at 80% / 100% | Admins | Normal |
| Expense submitted for approval | Admins | Normal |
| Expense approved / declined | The submitter | Normal |

- **Activity history:** invoice created, lines changed, sent, drafted again, payments, cancelled; expenses approved/declined; settings changes (who changed the prefix, rates, tax); exports (who, when, how many rows).

#### 16. Trust and data
- **The most sensitive tab:** admins only by default; never public; agents can't mark invoices paid or edit them **[call]**.
- **Business details and pay-by text** appear only on the invoice and its PDF; NetworkBase never sends invoices or reminders to clients, never stores card numbers, and never connects to banks.
- **Export:** CSV for admins (invoices, payments, time, expenses), written to Activity; for an accountant, not tax filing.
- **Receipts:** stored as workspace files with the same access as Money.
- **Limits to track** (values come with decision 6): invoices per month, receipt storage, members logging time.

#### 17. Reuse vs new
- **Reused as is:**
  - task data for invoices (assignee, reminders, comments, files, activity, undo, My Work)
  - Pipeline clients and its one-currency-per-total rule
  - Project planner projects (profit), tasks (timer ▶)
  - Files for receipts and PDFs; storage limits
  - the Overview card pattern, filter chips, the one-scroll item page, SVG bars from Goals, the PDF approach from the Project planner
  - the `viewer` role (excluded here)
- **New:**
  - kind `invoice` (B4) with lines, payments, number sequence, tax and discount
  - the money records table: time entries, expenses, income (B8 time log)
  - client rate types and retainer drafts
  - the timer (one per person), ▶ on tasks, "logged" on tasks
  - Turn into invoice; profit on project pages
  - categories, budget, recurring entries, expense approval
  - the shared money formatter (`Intl.NumberFormat`, smallest-unit storage)
  - invoice PDF, CSV export, `nb time` / `nb expense` commands
  - Money settings, presets, the Overview card, the tab switch (B10)

#### 18. How we know it works
- **Usage signal:** the share of workspaces with Money that mark at least one invoice paid within 6 weeks of adding the tab.
- **Checks once built:**
  - the design contract test (amounts in mono through the shared formatter)
  - side-by-side check against the reference layout (Overview tiles, In/Out side by side, budget rows)
  - unit tests: totals with tax and discount in smallest units, partial payments, overdue rule, number sequence never reused, billed entries can't be billed twice, per-currency totals, retainer draft dates (month ends), runway maths
  - permission tests: members see only their own time and expenses; viewers and the public see nothing; agents can't mark paid
  - end to end: log time with the timer → turn into an invoice → mark sent → overdue reminder → mark paid → Overview tiles update → CSV export logged
  - phone receipt capture; keyboard-only check

### 12.3 Pipeline → Clients preset (tab preset: layers 2, 3, 5, 8, 18, plus the Directory view)

**Choosing the reference (rating + UI quality, section 10):**

| Template | Rating | UI verdict (against the Anthropic planner) | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Sales CRM** by Notion | **4.8 from 900+**, the most rated CRM | **Clean, planner level.** A calm table with a sum under Estimated value, small status and priority badges; views **Dashboard · All records · By status · High priority · Value over $100k**. The Dashboard has a value ring, one big pipeline number, bars per person, then the status board. The contact page is a tidy property list, then **Background info**, then **History of interactions** with a **"New interaction"** button; a one-click **"Contacted"** button. | **Chosen** (layout for every pipeline, see the 11.2 update) |
| Client List (CRM) by EdriansNotes | 4.9 from 500+ | **Busy:** promotional banners, a left-hand menu, colour-filled rows. One good idea: Clients, Deals and Meetings kept separate, with "New client" / "New deal" buttons. | Ideas only |
| Leads Tracker | 5.0 from 15 | Kanban with pipeline numbers; too few ratings | Ideas only |
| Client Directory | 5.0 from 5 | A directory of every client; the idea behind the Directory view | Ideas only |
| Personal CRM / Contact list | 4.8 from 100+ | Personal contacts, not clients | Skip |
| Client portal templates | 4.8–4.9 | Saved for the Client portal round | Later |

**Why Sales CRM wins:** nearly twice the ratings of the next one, built by Notion, and as calm and clear as the planner. Client List's ratings are high but its page is cluttered.

**Agreed changes from an exact copy (2026-11-16):**
1. **Charts become plain SVG with labels**, in muted colours (ring, big number, bars per person).
2. **"Account owner" → Assigned to; "Lead" → New.**
3. **The "Contacted" button is kept** as a one-click interaction.
4. **No separate Clients / Deals / Meetings databases** (Client List's idea); instead one Pipeline with a **Directory** view, plus the Meetings tab for meetings.
5. **The usual changes:** our badge shape (no fully round pills), our section headings.

The shared Pipeline design (11.2, with the upgrades above) applies; only what differs is written here. Marked **[call]** = a decision the user can overrule.

#### 2. Setting it up
| | Clients |
|---|---|
| **Item name** | Client |
| **Stages** | **New → Contacted → Proposal → Won / Lost** (11.2's rules: at least one Open, exactly one Won and one Lost). Probabilities 10 / 30 / 60 %. |
| **Client status (after Won)** | **Onboarding → Active → Past**, kept separate from the stages so every pipeline still has exactly one Won and one Lost. Shown in the Directory. |
| **Fields** | Company · Contact person · Email · **Phone (on in this preset [call])** · Website · Location / time zone · Value · Expected close · Priority · Source · **Rate type and rate** (Hourly / Fixed / Retainer, feeding Money, 12.2) · Background info |

- **Admins can change afterwards:** rename the client status values; edit the onboarding checklist and save it as a workspace preset; turn off the "Past after 90 days" offer.
- **Wizard:** for Freelance, Pipeline is ticked with **Clients** as its first pipeline (decision 5).

#### 3. Items
- A client is a pipeline item (task kind `deal`, shown as "Client").
- **Onboarding tasks** are normal tasks that are **Part of** the client. **Part of** now covers projects, launches and pipeline items.
- **Repeat work:** **New deal for this client** starts a new item with the contact details copied. The Directory groups a client's deals into one row by **company + email** **[call]**. The limit of grouping this way: a renamed company splits into two rows until merged by hand (⋯ → Merge with…); a separate client record can come later if this becomes a real problem.

#### Directory view (layers 4, 5, 6, 7, 11–14)
```
Directory           Onboarding · Active · Past · All
  Client         Company   Status      Rate            Invoiced   Waiting   Last contact   Projects
  Shri Ansari    Mode      Active      Hourly ₹1,500   ₹2,40,000  ₹17,700   Nov 12         2
  Bloom Studio   Bloom     Onboarding  Fixed           —          —         Nov 14         1
```
- **4. What's on screen:** one row per client (grouped deals), every Won item; filters Onboarding · Active · Past · All, plus Assigned to and Priority; sort by any column.
  - **Invoiced** and **Waiting** come from Money; **Projects** from the Project planner. Each column only shows when that tab exists (and Money columns only to people who can see Money).
- **5. Actions:** open the client page; **New deal for this client**; **Mark past**; **Merge with…**; **Contacted**.
- **6. Surfaces:** the table (sticky name column, mono numbers, sum row for Invoiced and Waiting); on narrow screens, stacked rows (name, company, status, waiting).
- **7. Design:** status badges Onboarding = in-progress status colour, Active = success, Past = muted Ink, always with words; precision badges; mono for amounts and dates.
- **11. States:** skeleton rows; "—" for numbers until loaded; live updates when an invoice is paid or a project added.
- **12. Edges:** a client with deals in two currencies shows both totals; a merged client keeps all deals and history; a client whose deals are all Lost doesn't appear.
- **13. Phone:** stacked rows; tapping opens the client page full-screen.
- **14. Accessibility:** rows read as "Shri Ansari, Mode, Active, waiting 17,700 rupees, last contact November 12"; keyboard arrows and Enter.

#### 5. Actions and flow
1. **New → Contacted → Proposal** as in 11.2 (Contacted button, interactions, next steps).
2. **Won:** for the Clients preset, the Won dialog offers these, all ticked by default:
   - **Start onboarding:** a checklist preset whose items are real tasks, Part of the client:
     1. Welcome message sent
     2. Contract signed
     3. Deposit invoice (creates a Money **draft**)
     4. Kickoff meeting (creates a Meetings **Kickoff** with the client linked)
     5. Files and access shared
     6. Project created (in the Project planner)
   - **Create project**, **Create deposit invoice**, **Schedule kickoff** (each can be unticked; each only appears when its tab exists)
3. **Onboarding → Active:** automatic when every onboarding task is done.
4. **Active → Past:** by hand, or offered after 90 days with no open project and no unpaid invoice.
5. **Again:** **New deal for this client** for repeat work.
- **Already covered:** Client Follow-Up Tracker = the Follow-ups view; client meetings = the Meetings tab's **Client** type, which appears in History of interactions.

#### 8. Words
- Client, Directory, Onboarding, Active, Past, Contacted, History of interactions, New interaction, Background info, Start onboarding, New deal for this client, Merge with.
- The onboarding checklist's six item names (above).
- Never "Lead" (the first stage is **New**) or "Owner" / "Account owner" (**Assigned to**).
- **Empty messages:**
  - Board: "No clients yet. Add the people or companies you're talking to."
  - Directory: "Clients you win show up here, with what they've been invoiced."

#### 18. How we know it works
- **Usage signal:** the share of Freelance workspaces where a Won client reaches **Active** through the onboarding checklist within 3 weeks.
- **Checks:**
  - the Directory groups repeat deals by company + email; Merge with… joins rows
  - Won → onboarding creates its tasks, a draft deposit invoice and a kickoff meeting (only for tabs that exist)
  - onboarding done → Active; the 90-day Past offer
  - the Contacted button updates Last contact and adds an interaction
  - Dashboard totals match the Table's sum row
  - Money columns hidden from people who can't see Money
