### 12.4 Client portal (own feature, all 18 layers)

**Choosing the reference (rating + UI quality, section 10; all three opened live on 2026-11-16):**

| Template | Rating | UI verdict | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Client Portal Starter** | **4.9 from 30** | **Calm and client-facing.** Neutral palette, clear blocks: **Hello [Client name]** welcome card · client contact card · **Project timeline** (start → end) · Quick actions (New task, New meeting) · **Deliverables** gallery grouped by stage (First draft…) · **Tasks** (Due today / By status) · **Payments** (Due soon / Paid, instalments with amount, date, "Mark paid") · **Upcoming meetings**. Two small promo boxes are the only noise. | **Chosen** |
| Agency Client Portal | 4.9 from 42 | Opens with a large pink promo block, and it's an **internal** CRM (leads, clients, projects, meetings), not a page a client sees. | Not used |
| Branding Client Portal | 4.8 from 69 | Hand-made pink boxes and emoji clutter, below the planner bar. Ideas: a welcome note with the week's agenda, contacts, Proposal & Contract, Brand assets. | Ideas only |

**Why Client Portal Starter wins:** it's the only one built for the client to look at, its layout is calm, and its blocks match what a freelancer shares.

**What the code has today:** a `viewer` role exists (`src/lib/workspaces/settings-policies.ts`) but can only comment, can't be assigned, and still sees every member tab, so it **can't** be used for clients. Invitations (`workspace_invitations`) only cover role applications and mentor appointments.

**Agreed changes from an exact copy (2026-11-16):**
1. **Notion's portal is a shared page; ours is scoped access with nothing shared by default.** Each item has its own **Show to client** switch, and **View as client** checks it.
2. **Promo boxes, "Please don't delete" and "Grab the premium template" are removed.**
3. **Deliverables get Approve / Request changes** instead of plain gallery cards.
4. **The client can't mark payments paid;** only the freelancer can.
5. **The usual changes:** our badges and headings; the portal shows **the freelancer's** workspace name and avatar, with only a small "on NetworkBase" at the bottom.

Marked **[call]** = a decision made in this design that the user can overrule.

#### 1. Getting it
- **Not a tab in the tab row [call].** The freelancer manages each portal from the client's page in Pipeline (Clients preset). Clients see only their portal.
- **Where it's offered:**
  - **Set up client portal** on any client's page (Clients preset)
  - the Won dialog's onboarding step offers "Set up a portal for this client" (unticked by default)
  - a one-line mention in the Freelance and Creative wizard hints
- **First look (freelancer):** the client page's Portal section says "Off. Share progress, deliverables and invoices with this client in one private page." with **Set up portal**.
- **First look (client, after accepting the invite):** their portal with the welcome note; any empty section says "Nothing here yet. [Workspace name] will share updates soon."

#### 2. Setting it up (per client, owners and admins)
- **Welcome note:** free text shown at the top.
- **People:** invite by email (one or more people at the client).
- **What's shared** (each a switch; all on except the email):
  - Project timeline (pick one or more projects)
  - Deliverables (tasks marked Show to client)
  - Tasks marked Show to client
  - Invoices for this client
  - Meetings with this client linked
  - A "From client" upload folder
  - Reports shared to the portal (12.5)
  - Your email on the contacts card (**off**)
- **Contacts card:** which workspace people appear, with their workspace Title (11.9).
- **Client notifications default:** email on for deliverables, invoices and meetings.

#### 3. Items
- **Client access:** a new access kind, **not** a workspace member or viewer **[call]**. Each access row links one person to one client (pipeline item) in one workspace, with its own revocation. A person can hold access to several clients (a portal switcher appears).
- **Invitation:** a new kind on the existing invitations table, `client_portal`, carrying the client and the inviter. Accepting requires signing in or signing up through the normal flow with its checks.
- **Show to client:** a per-item switch on tasks and files (and therefore on deliverables).
- **Deliverable:** a task marked Show to client that has files; its **stage** (First draft · Revisions · Final) is set on the task.
- **Portal message thread:** one comment thread per portal, between the client's people and the workspace.
- **"From client" folder:** a Files folder per client, created when uploads are switched on.
- **Nothing new is created for invoices or meetings:** the portal reads the existing ones for this client.

#### 4. Views
**Client side (one page):**
```
[your workspace avatar]  Asha Design × Bloom Studio                 Signed in as Fariba ▾
Hello, Fariba
  Welcome note written by you: "This week: final logo + brand fonts."
┌ Your contacts ────────┐  ┌ Project ───────────────────────────────────┐
│ (A) Asha · Designer    │  │ Bloom rebrand · Jun 18 → Jul 16 · 60% ━━━─ │
│ asha@ (if you show it) │  │ Next: Final logo review · Jul 2            │
└────────────────────────┘  └────────────────────────────────────────────┘
Deliverables            First draft · Revisions · Final
  ┌ Logo design ┐ ┌ Brand fonts ┐ ┌ Post graphics ┐
  │ (preview)   │ │ (preview)   │ │ (preview)     │
  │ Waiting for │ │ Approved ✓  │ │ In progress   │
  │ you [Approve] [Request changes]                │
Tasks you can see       Due soon · By status
  ☐ Send brand questionnaire → you · Jun 20
Payments                Due soon · Paid
  INV-0012 · ₹17,700 · due Nov 20 · Sent          [ Download PDF ]   Pay by: (your text)
Meetings                Upcoming
  Kickoff · Thu 14:00                               [ Add to calendar ]
Files from you          [ Upload ]   brief.pdf · logo-old.ai
Messages                a thread between you and the client
                                                    — on NetworkBase
```
**Freelancer side (a section on the client's page):**
```
Client portal          ● On · 2 people invited          [ View as Bloom ]  [ Turn off ]
  Welcome note         "This week: final logo + brand fonts."
  People               fariba@bloom.co (joined) · ashley@bloom.co (invited)   + Invite
  What's shared        ☑ Project timeline (Bloom rebrand)
                       ☑ Deliverables (tasks marked "Show to client")
                       ☑ Tasks marked "Show to client"
                       ☑ Invoices for this client
                       ☑ Meetings with this client linked
                       ☑ A "From client" upload folder
                       ☐ Your email on the contacts card
```
- **Tasks you can see** has the reference's two views: Due soon · By status. **Payments**: Due soon · Paid. **Deliverables**: grouped by stage.

#### 5. Actions and flow
1. **Set up:** turn the portal on, write the welcome note, choose what's shared, mark tasks and files **Show to client**.
2. **Check:** **View as [client]** opens exactly what they'll see, read-only, with a banner "You're viewing as Bloom Studio".
3. **Invite:** emails go out with an invite link; accepting needs sign-in or sign-up.
4. **Work together:**
   - **Deliverables:** the client presses **Approve** (completes the task; activity notes "Approved by Fariba") or **Request changes** (a note is required; reopens the task and adds the note as a comment). This follows the existing review step, with the client as the reviewer.
   - **Tasks assigned to the client** (e.g. "Send brand questionnaire") can be ticked by them; these are tasks with **Show to client** and the client named as "For client" (clients can't be assignees, since they aren't members **[call]**).
   - **Payments:** the client downloads PDFs and sees the "Pay by" text; **only the freelancer marks paid**.
   - **Uploads:** go to the "From client" folder.
   - **Messages:** one thread; the freelancer replies from the client page or My Work.
5. **End:** **Turn off** closes the portal for everyone; removing a person ends their access immediately. They see "This portal is closed."

#### 6. Surfaces
- **S1. Portal header:** freelancer's workspace avatar and name × client name; "Signed in as" menu (Portal switcher when several · Notification settings · Sign out).
- **S2. Welcome card** and **S3. Contacts card** (people, Title, optional email).
- **S4. Project card(s):** name, dates, completion bar, the next milestone or task (from the Project planner; read-only).
- **S5. Deliverables gallery:** grouped by stage; card = file preview (existing media viewer), name, state (Waiting for you · Approved · In progress · Changes requested), **Approve** / **Request changes** when waiting.
- **S6. Tasks list:** Due soon · By status; ticking only for "For client" tasks.
- **S7. Payments list:** Due soon · Paid; number, amount (mono), due date, status, **Download PDF**, pay-by text.
- **S8. Meetings list:** upcoming and past; **Add to calendar** (.ics).
- **S9. Files from you:** upload drop zone and list.
- **S10. Messages thread.**
- **S10b. Reports** (added by 12.5): shared client reports, newest first, frozen as sent, with **Download PDF**.
- **S11. Freelancer-side Portal section** (on the client page) and **S12. Invite dialog** (emails, a preview of the email text).
- **S13. View-as banner.**
- **S14. Request changes dialog** (note required).

#### 7. Design spec
- Same tokens, type and badges as the rest of NetworkBase; the page uses Paper surfaces and generous spacing so it reads as a calm client page.
- **Branding:** the freelancer's workspace avatar and name lead; "on NetworkBase" is small, muted, at the bottom.
- **Status badges:** Waiting for you = warning, Approved = success, Changes requested = danger, In progress = in-progress status colour; always with words.
- **Buttons:** Approve = Clay primary; Request changes = secondary.
- **Icons (Lucide):** UserRoundCheck (portal), Eye (View as / Show to client), CheckCircle2 (Approve), MessageSquareWarning (Request changes), Upload, CalendarPlus, FileDown.
- **Contract test:** `tests/unit/client-portal-design-contract.test.ts` (task contract rules, plus: no workspace navigation rendered for a client session).

#### 8. Words
- **Freelancer side:** Client portal, Set up portal, What's shared, Show to client, View as [client], Invite, Turn off, Welcome note, For client.
- **Client side:** Hello [name], Your contacts, Deliverables, Waiting for you, Approve, Request changes, Approved, Changes requested, Tasks you can see, Payments, Download PDF, Pay by, Meetings, Add to calendar, Files from you, Messages, "This portal is closed".
- Never "Lead", "Owner", "guest", "viewer" on the client side (it's their portal, not a guest view).

#### 9. Links to the rest of NetworkBase
- **Pipeline (Clients):** the portal lives on the client's page; History of interactions logs approvals, change requests and messages as interactions.
- **Tasks / Files:** Show to client on tasks and files; deliverable stage on tasks; approvals complete tasks.
- **Project planner:** project timeline cards (read-only).
- **Money:** this client's invoices and PDFs (read-only; pay-by text).
- **Meetings:** meetings with this client linked; .ics.
- **My Work (freelancer):** "Bloom requested changes: Logo design", "New message from Bloom".
- **Chat / Updates / global search:** **never** expose portal content to clients; the freelancer's own search finds portal messages.
- **CLI and agents:** agents can mark items Show to client only with a member's own access; agents **never act inside a portal** (no approving, no messaging as the client) **[call]**.

#### 10. People
| Who | Can |
|---|---|
| Owner / admin | Turn portals on/off, invite and remove client people, choose what's shared, write the welcome note, View as client |
| Member | Mark tasks and files Show to client for clients they can see; reply in the portal thread; View as client |
| Viewer | Nothing in portals |
| Client person | Only their portal(s): view what's shared, Approve / Request changes, tick "For client" tasks, download PDFs, upload, message, manage their own notifications |
| Public | **Never**; portals can't be made public and aren't in search |
| Organization | Portals are per workspace; an org has no view into its workspaces' portals |

#### 11. States
- **Loading:** a skeleton of the cards and lists.
- **Error:** a plain retry message; never a partially rendered portal with the wrong data.
- **Nothing shared:** "Nothing here yet. [Workspace] will share updates soon."
- **Portal closed / access removed:** "This portal is closed." with the workspace's name.
- **Live updates:** newly shared items, approvals and messages appear without a refresh.
- **Undo (freelancer side):** turning Show to client on/off, removing a person (within the undo window), turning the portal off.

#### 12. Edges
- **A client person invited to two clients:** a portal switcher in the header.
- **Show to client removed:** the item disappears at once; any open approval is cancelled.
- **A shared task deleted or moved to another workspace:** it disappears from the portal.
- **The client deletes their NetworkBase account:** access ends; their messages stay as "Former client".
- **Pipeline tab hidden or deleted:** all portals close (decision 2); reopening restores them only when the tab is added back.
- **The client won't approve:** the deliverable stays "Waiting for you"; the freelancer can mark it done themselves (noted "Completed without client approval").
- **Large files:** previews use the existing media viewer; downloads follow existing storage rules.
- **Invite email typo:** invites expire after 14 days and can be cancelled.

#### 13. Phone
- **Client side is phone-first:** "Waiting for you" deliverables on top, then payments, then meetings, then messages.
- **Approve / Request changes** are full-width buttons; previews open full-screen.
- **Freelancer side:** the Portal section on the client page stacks; View as client works on phones.

#### 14. Accessibility
- Every deliverable card is labelled ("Logo design, waiting for your approval").
- Keyboard: Tab through cards; Enter opens the preview; Approve / Request changes are reachable buttons, not hover-only.
- Email notifications have plain-text versions.

#### 15. Notifications and activity
| Event | Who | How |
|---|---|---|
| New deliverable to review | Client people | Email (they can switch off) |
| Invoice sent / overdue | Client people | Email (they can switch off) |
| Meeting scheduled / changed | Client people | Email (they can switch off) |
| New message | Client people / the workspace | Email / Important |
| Client approved or requested changes | Task assignee + client's Assigned to | Important |
| Client uploaded a file | Client's Assigned to | Normal |
| Invite accepted | The inviter | Normal |

- **Activity:** every client action (view of a deliverable, approval, change request, upload, message, download) and every sharing change (Show to client on/off, invite, removal, portal on/off) is recorded on the client's page.

#### 16. Trust and data (the most important layer here)
- **Server-side checks for every read and action:** a client session can only reach rows linked to its client access; nothing is hidden only on screen.
- **No workspace navigation** is ever rendered or routable for a client session; workspace URLs return "not found" to them.
- **Nothing shared by default;** View as client before inviting.
- **Uploads:** rate-limited, through existing upload checks and storage limits.
- **Emails:** clients' addresses visible only to owners and admins (and members who can see the client); never shown to other clients.
- **Agents:** never act in a portal (layer 9).
- **Limits to track** (values come with decision 6): portals per workspace, client people per portal, upload storage; the portal is a likely Pro feature.

#### 17. Reuse vs new
- **Reused:** existing auth and sign-up checks; the invitations table (new kind); tasks, files, the review step and the media viewer; Money invoices and PDFs; Meetings and .ics; comments for the thread; Files storage limits; the Pipeline client page.
- **New:** client access (kind, scope, revocation, portal switcher); per-item **Show to client**; deliverable stage; the portal page and **View as client**; client Approve / Request changes; "For client" tasks; the "From client" folder; client email notifications and preferences; activity entries for client actions; a design contract test; security tests.

#### 18. How we know it works
- **Usage signal:** the share of portals where the client approves at least one deliverable within 2 weeks of the invite.
- **Must-pass security checks:** from a client session, no route, API call, file URL or search can reach any workspace tab, another client's portal, an item not marked Show to client, money totals, deal values or member emails. Revocation takes effect on the next request.
- **Other checks:** View as client matches the real client view; approve / request changes update the task and History of interactions; invites expire; portal closes when the Pipeline tab is removed; phone approval flow; keyboard-only flow.

### 12.5 Client report (document template, layers 1, 3, 8, 9, plus one flow)

**Choosing the reference (rating + UI quality, section 10; opened live on 2026-11-16):** client report templates have almost no ratings (the best is Notion's own Status update, 4.5 from 2), so **the UI decided**.

| Template | Rating | UI verdict | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Monthly Client Report** (Still Linda) | not yet rated | **Clean at the top, planner level.** A left rail (Quick entry → Add report; Reminders; a small To-do), then report lists **Reports to finish · All reports · Ready to share · Shared reports**, with columns **Report · Client / Project · Reporting period · Project health (On track / At risk / Blocked) · Report status (Draft → In progress → Ready to share → Shared)**. Each report covers goals, results, work completed, blockers, decisions needed and next steps. A long promo footer below the fold is the only noise. | **Chosen** |
| Client Reporting Dashboard | not yet rated | The live page didn't load; from its description: progress reports, KPIs, milestones, risks and decisions | Ideas only |
| Status update by Notion | 4.5 from 2 | An AI helper that turns work items into a short status update | Idea: fill a report from real work |
| Client Report & KPI Hub, Project Status Report, Weekly Update | not yet rated | Narrower or busier dashboards | Skip |

**Why Monthly Client Report wins:** the only one with a clear report lifecycle (Draft → Ready to share → Shared) and a health signal per report, and its main screen meets the planner bar.

**Agreed changes from an exact copy (2026-11-16):**
1. **No separate reports database.** Reports are docs, plus a Reports list on the client page.
2. **Sections fill themselves from real work** (tasks done, hours, projects, decisions), from the Status update idea.
3. **"Share to portal" with a frozen copy**, instead of a "Shared" label.
4. **The rail's To-do and Reminders become a monthly My Work reminder.**
5. **No promo footer;** our usual badges and headings.

Marked **[call]** = a decision made in this design that the user can overrule.

#### 1. Getting it
- **New doc → NetworkBase templates → "Client report"** (Freelance and Creative first).
- **"Write a report"** on a client's page in Pipeline (Clients preset): fills in the client and the previous month as the period.
- **Monthly reminder:** on the 1st, the client's assignee gets "Write November's report for Bloom" in My Work, for **active clients with a portal** **[call]**; it can be turned off per client.

#### 3. Contents
```
Bloom Studio · Report for October 2026          Health  On track ▾    Status  Draft ▾
  Period   Oct 1 → Oct 31, 2026        Client  Bloom Studio        Prepared by (A) Asha
──────────────────────────────
Summary            three lines: where things stand
Progress           [projects block]  Bloom rebrand 60% ━━━─  · next: Final logo review Jul 2
Work completed     [tasks block, filtered]  tasks done for Bloom in October (auto)
Time               [time block]  18h 30m · 14h billable · by project            (if Money is on)
Results            numbers you add, or [goals block] when a key result is linked
Blockers           what's in the way
Decisions needed   [decisions]  Proposed decisions linked to Bloom, from Meetings
Next steps         what happens next month, with dates
──────────────────────────────
[ Share to Bloom's portal ]   [ Save as PDF ]   [ Copy as email ]
```
- **Header:** Health (**On track / At risk / Blocked**, set by hand, with a hint from the projects' status) and Status (**Draft → Ready to share → Shared**), shown as small badges; Period, Client, Prepared by.
- **Smart blocks** (`src/lib/workspaces/doc-blocks.ts` already has `projects` and `tasks` blocks, chosen by id):
  - **tasks block gets filters:** client + period + done, so "Work completed" fills itself
  - **new `time` block:** hours from Money, total and billable, by project
  - **`goals` block** (planned for the Investor update, 11.8)
  - **new `decisions` block:** Proposed decisions from Meetings linked to this client
  - each block appears only when its tab exists; the `time` block only renders for people who can see Money
- **Freezing on share [call]:** **Share to portal** freezes every block as it was that day; the client sees what was sent, and later changes don't alter it. Drafts stay live. A new version can be shared later (the portal shows the latest, with "Updated Nov 4").
- **Actions:** **Share to [client]'s portal** (sets Shared), **Save as PDF**, **Copy as email** (plain text with the numbers filled in).

#### 8. Words
- Client report, Report for [month], Health (On track · At risk · Blocked), Status (Draft · Ready to share · Shared), Summary, Progress, Work completed, Time, Results, Blockers, Decisions needed, Next steps, Prepared by, Share to portal, Write a report.
- Never "Lead" or "Owner".
- **Empty block messages:** "No tasks finished for Bloom in October." · "No time logged in this period."

#### 9. Links
- **Pipeline client page:** a **Reports** list (period · health · status · shared date), the reference's "Reports to finish / Shared" in one place.
- **Documents:** reports are normal docs (versions, search, links), filterable by the "Client report" template; **Reports to finish** is a saved filter (Draft or Ready to share).
- **Client portal (12.4):** a **Reports** section shows shared reports only, newest first, with **Download PDF**.
- **Project planner** (progress), **Tasks** (work completed), **Money** (time), **Goals** (results), **Meetings** (decisions needed).
- **My Work:** the monthly reminder; "Report ready to share: Bloom, October".

**Must-pass check:** a report shared to a portal contains only items marked **Show to client**; the filtered blocks leave out anything hidden from the client, and money totals appear only if the freelancer typed them **[call]**.

### 13.2 Bug tracker (own tab, all 18 layers)

**Choosing the reference (rating + UI quality, section 10; opened live on 2026-11-16):**

| Template | Rating | UI verdict | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Bug Tracker** by Notion | **4.7 from 50** | **Calm, planner level.** A board with **To review · Validating · Solving** columns; cards show an icon, the title, the reporter and a type tag (**Urgent / Major bug / Minor bug**). Views **Board · Potential bugs only · Bug report (a form) · User bug reports**, plus a small **"Status per type"** chart. The bug page: Status · Reporter · Type, then **Background** (Browser: Firefox / Safari / Chrome / Other; Mobile app: iOS / Android) · **What happened?** (steps) · **What was the expected behaviour?** · **Screenshot or video**. | **Chosen** |
| Report a Bug by Notion | 4.7 from 36 | A one-button page that files a bug | Idea: a fast report form |
| Project Issue Tracker | 4.9 from 30 | The live page didn't load; from its description: views across status, priority, project and deadline | Ideas only |
| Bug Tracker Lite · Bug Tracker database · Software Dev Bugs | 4.8–5.0 from 13–30 | Small samples; similar fields | Ideas only |

**Why Notion's wins:** a close rating backed by more people, the calmest board and bug page of the set, and the only one with a reporting form and a "user reports" view built in, which matters most for open source.

**What the code has today:** `task_links` stores pull-request and issue links on tasks; GitHub sync copies repository **files** only (no issues); the Tasks tab isn't public by default; Cloudflare checks and moderation exist for public forms and content.

**Agreed changes from an exact copy (2026-11-16):**
1. **Statuses renamed:** New → Confirmed → Fixing → Fixed → Verified, plus close reasons, instead of To review / Validating / Solving ("Review" already means the review queue in Tasks).
2. **"Type" is called Severity** and also sets the task priority.
3. **The form shows similar open bugs and "I see this too"**, to cut duplicates.
4. **The Background checkboxes become a "Where" field** (web: browser + version; app: platform + version).
5. **The usual changes:** our badges and headings, emoji-or-Lucide icons, "Reported by" and "Assigned to".

Marked **[call]** = a decision made in this design that the user can overrule.

#### 1. Getting it
- **Where it's offered:** **+ Add workflow** (owners and admins); the wizard's Settings step, **ticked by default** for Open source, Web app and Developer tool (its first suggestion there) and shown unticked for Game dev (section 6); added by an organization.
- **In the + Add workflow dialog:** a Bug tracker row with a small preview of the board; one question: **"Let people outside the workspace report bugs?"** (only on public workspaces; default off).
- **First look:** the board with five empty columns, the "Open by severity" strip at zero, and a hint: "Bugs come in on the left and leave on the right. Anyone in the workspace can report one." **+ Report a bug** is the primary button.

#### 2. Setting it up
- **Statuses** (fixed order, admins can rename): New → Confirmed → Fixing → Fixed → Verified. **Close reasons:** Won't fix · Duplicate · Can't reproduce.
- **Severity:** Urgent · Major · Minor, mapped to task priority Urgent / High / Medium **[call]**.
- **Ready-made labels:** good first issue · help wanted (plus the workspace's own labels).
- **"Where" options:** web browsers (Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Edge, Other) and app platforms (iOS, Android, Desktop); admins can add their own (e.g. "CLI", "API").
- **Triage person:** who gets new-bug notifications (default: owners and admins).
- **Outside reports:** **Anyone signed in can report** (public workspaces only; off by default) **[call]**.
- **Auto-verify after:** 14 days after the fix ships (can be turned off).
- **Fields:** admins can add their own (B3), e.g. "Component".

#### 3. Items
- **Bug:** a **task of kind `bug`** (decision 1). Holds icon, title, status, severity, reported by, assigned to, where (web/app + version), found in (a launch or a version text), fixed in (a launch), labels, pull request (existing `task_links`, kind `pull_request`), "I see this too" (people), duplicate of, what happened, what was expected, screenshots / video (files).
- **Every way to create one:**
  1. **+ Report a bug** (the form, S6)
  2. **From Feedback & requests** (next round): "This is a bug" on a request
  3. **From a Client portal change request** (12.4): "Turn into a bug"
  4. **From chat:** "Report as bug" on a message (copies the text and attachments)
  5. **CLI / agents:** `nb bugs report` (agents can report bugs they hit while working, marked "Reported by agent")

#### 4. Views
| View | What's on screen | Drag | Filter / sort |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Board** (desktop default) | Status columns with cards | Cards between statuses (closing asks for a reason) | Severity, assigned to, labels, where, found in |
| **Triage** | New bugs, oldest first, with quick **Confirm · Severity · Assign · Close** buttons per row | — | Severity, where |
| **Mine** | Bugs assigned to you, by severity | — | Status |
| **Reported** | Bugs filed through the form (the reference's "User bug reports"), with reporter and "I see this too" count | — | Outside / members, status |
| **Fixed** | Fixed and verified bugs grouped by the launch that shipped them | — | Launch, period |

- **Open by severity:** a strip above every view with Urgent / Major / Minor counts as labelled bars (the reference's chart).
- **Search** covers titles, steps and expected text.

#### 5. Actions and flow
1. **Report** (form) → **New**.
2. **Triage:** **Confirm** (sets severity and an assignee) → **Confirmed**; or close as **Won't fix**, **Duplicate of…** (moves reporters and "I see this too" people to the original) or **Can't reproduce** (asks the reporter for details; closes after 14 days with no reply).
3. **Fix:** move to **Fixing** (the bug appears on the Tasks board with a 🐞 chip, and can go in a sprint); attach the pull request link.
4. **Fixed:** asks which launch it ships in (**Fixed in**); the bug is added under **"Fixed"** in that launch's What's new draft (11.5, groups from 13.7).
5. **Verified:** by the reporter or a member, or automatically 14 days after its launch ships **[call]**.
6. **Reopen:** a Verified or closed bug can be reopened; "I see this too" on a closed bug offers **Reopen** to members.

Who does what: the triage person (or admins) triage; assignees fix; reporters and members verify.

#### 6. The tab's own surfaces
- **S1. View tabs:** `Board · Triage · Mine · Reported · Fixed` (plus **Incidents**, added by 21.2).
- **S2. Title row:** `🐞 Bugs`, counts in mono ("2 urgent · 5 to triage"), search, **+ Report a bug** (primary), ⋯: Bug settings · Edit fields · Export CSV · Copy report link (public workspaces).
- **S3. Filter chips:** `Severity ▾ · Assigned to ▾ · Labels ▾ · + Filter` (Where, Found in, Reported by).
- **S4. Open by severity strip.**
- **S5. Board**
```
┌ New 3 ──────────┐┌ Confirmed 1 ────┐┌ Fixing 1 ───────┐┌ Fixed 2 ────────┐┌ Verified ───┐
│ 🐞 Payment      ││ 🐞 Profile load ││ 🐞 Firefox      ││ 🐞 PNG upload   ││             │
│ gateway is down ││ takes 30s+      ││ crash           ││ error           ││             │
│ Urgent · Abhi.  ││ Minor · Seo     ││ Minor · (F)     ││ ↗ PR #412       ││             │
│ 2 people see it ││                 ││ ↗ PR #418       ││ ➜ v2.4          ││             │
└─────────────────┘└─────────────────┘└─────────────────┘└─────────────────┘└─────────────┘
```
  - **Card:** icon + title, severity badge, reporter or assignee, "2 people see it", PR link chip, "➜ v2.4" when fixed in a launch, labels (good first issue shown as a chip).
  - **Card ⋯:** Confirm · Set severity · Assign · Duplicate of… · Close… · Copy link.
- **S6. Report a bug form**
```
Report a bug                                          [ Cancel ]  [ Send report ]
  Title                 Payment gateway is down
  Similar open bugs     🐞 Checkout fails on Safari (3 people see it)  [ That's my bug ]
  What happened?        Steps you took, one per line
  What did you expect?
  Where                 ◉ Web: Chrome ▾ · version …   ○ App: iOS / Android · version …
  Screenshot or video   [ drop files ]
```
  - Similar open bugs appear as the title is typed (search over open bugs); **That's my bug** adds "I see this too" instead of filing.
  - For outside reporters: a short note "Your report is visible to the [workspace] team"; Cloudflare check; rate limit.
- **S7. Triage rows:** title, where, reported by, age (mono), and the four quick buttons.
- **S8. Bug page** (side panel, one scroll, **Open as full page**)
```
🐞 Payment gateway is down
  Status        Confirmed            Severity   Urgent
  Reported by   Abhishek (outside reporter)     Assigned to  (F) Felix
  Where         Web · Chrome 131 · macOS
  Found in      v2.3          Fixed in   —          Labels   payments · help wanted
  Pull request  ↗ github.com/…/pull/418           I see this too   2 people
  Duplicate of  —
──────────────────────────────
What happened?        1. Add item to cart  2. Pay with card  3. Spinner never ends
What did you expect?  Payment goes through and shows the receipt
Screenshot or video   (preview)
──────────────────────────────
Comments · Files · Activity
```
- **S9. Dialogs:** Close (reason, and for Duplicate a bug picker) · Fixed in (launch picker) · Can't reproduce (message to the reporter).
- **S10. Good first issues list** (public workspaces, optional): a read-only public list of open bugs labelled good first issue: title, severity, labels.
- **S11. Overview card:** "2 urgent · 5 to triage · 3 fixed this week".

#### 7. Design spec
- **Type (Section 04):** Instrument Sans for titles; JetBrains Mono for counts, ages, versions and PR numbers.
- **Colour:** severity Urgent = danger, Major = warning, Minor = muted Ink; statuses New = muted Ink, Confirmed = Ink, Fixing = in-progress status colour, Fixed / Verified = success; closed = muted Ink with the reason in words. Always with words and icons.
- **Badges (Section 10):** precision geometry; no fully round pills.
- **Motion (Section 05):** 180 ms ease-out for card moves.
- **Icons (Lucide):** Bug (the tab and items), ShieldAlert (Urgent), CopyCheck (Duplicate), GitPullRequest (PR), Users (I see this too), Sprout (good first issue).
- **Contract test:** `tests/unit/bugs-design-contract.test.ts`, with the task contract's rules.

#### 8. Words
- **Tab:** "Bugs". **Item:** Bug.
- **Kept from the reference:** Bug report, Reported by (for "Reporter"), What happened?, What did you expect?, Screenshot or video, Urgent / Major / Minor.
- **Ours:** New, Confirmed, Fixing, Fixed, Verified, Won't fix, Duplicate of, Can't reproduce, Severity, Where, Found in, Fixed in, I see this too, That's my bug, good first issue, help wanted, Triage.
- Never "Lead", "Owner", "ticket" (we say bug).
- **Empty messages:**
  - Board: "No bugs yet. Anyone in the workspace can report one."
  - Triage: "Nothing to triage."
  - Reported: "No reports from outside the workspace yet."

#### 9. Links to the rest of NetworkBase
- **Tasks:** bugs appear on the Tasks board once **Fixing** or in a sprint, with a 🐞 chip **[call]**; Tasks gains a **Type: Task / Bug** filter; the Matrix view uses severity through priority.
- **Sprints:** bugs can be put in sprints like tasks.
- **Roadmap & launches:** Found in / Fixed in point at launches; fixed bugs fill the "Fixes" part of What's new.
- **Feedback & requests (next round):** a request can become a bug; a bug can link to the requests it answers.
- **Client portal:** a change request can become a bug.
- **Chat:** "Report as bug" on a message; bug cards (the existing task card).
- **My Work:** bugs assigned to you; "Can't reproduce: details needed" for reporters.
- **GitHub:** pull-request links through `task_links`. **No two-way sync with GitHub Issues in this round [call]**; today's GitHub sync handles files only.
- **CLI and agents:** `nb bugs list [--mine] [--severity urgent]`, `nb bugs report`; task tools with `kind: "bug"`; the agent briefing lists urgent bugs.

#### 10. People
| Who | Can |
|---|---|
| Owner / admin | Everything, plus bug settings, the outside-reports switch, export |
| Member | Report, triage, fix, verify, comment; delete bugs they reported |
| Viewer | Report and comment |
| Outside reporter (signed in, when allowed) | File through the form, add "I see this too", comment on and follow their own bugs, provide details when asked |
| Public (public workspace) | Sees bugs only if the tab is made public: title, status, severity, labels; never the reporter's details or the "Where" details. The **Good first issues** list can be public on its own |
| Organization | Can push the tab to workspaces; no roll-up |

#### 11. States
- **Loading:** skeletons for the strip and five columns.
- **Error:** the tab error boundary with Retry.
- **Live updates:** new reports and moves appear without a refresh.
- **Two people at once:** last write wins, with a toast.
- **Undo:** moves, closes (including duplicates, which also undo the moved watchers), severity changes.

#### 12. Edges
- **Duplicate chains** always point at the oldest open bug; a bug can't be a duplicate of itself or of a bug that is its duplicate.
- **Deleting a launch** clears "Fixed in" on its bugs.
- **Spam reports:** **Report** sends them to moderation; the reporter can be blocked from reporting.
- **An outside reporter deletes their account:** their bugs stay as "Former reporter".
- **Too many:** columns show 25 with "Show more"; Fixed pages by launch.
- **Removing the tab:** decision 2. Hide keeps bugs (those on the Tasks board stay there with the chip); Delete sends bugs to Trash; linked tasks, launches and PR links are untouched.

#### 13. Phone
- **Triage** first, with Confirm and Close as big buttons.
- **Report a bug** opens the camera for a screenshot.
- **Board:** one status at a time.

#### 14. Accessibility
- **Keyboard:** **R** report a bug; in Triage, **C** confirm, **S** severity, **A** assign, **X** close; arrows move between cards.
- **Screen readers:** cards read as "Payment gateway is down, Urgent, New, reported by Abhishek, 2 people see it".
- **Colour is never the only signal.**

#### 15. Notifications and activity
| Event | Who | Level |
|---|---|---|
| New bug reported | Triage person (or admins) | Normal |
| Urgent bug reported or raised to Urgent | Same + assignee | Important |
| Bug assigned to you | New assignee | Important |
| Fixed / Verified / closed as duplicate | Reporter and "I see this too" people | Normal |
| Can't reproduce, details needed | Reporter | Important |
| Someone else sees it too | Assignee | Summary |

- **Activity:** reported, confirmed, severity changes, assigned, status moves, PR linked, fixed in, verified, closed with reason, duplicate links, reopened.

#### 16. Trust and data
- **Outside reporting:** signed-in only, Cloudflare check, rate limits, moderation; off by default.
- **Reporter details** (name beyond display name, "Where" details) are members-only; never public.
- **Screenshots:** stored as workspace files with the tab's access; outside reporters see only their own.
- **Agents:** report and comment only with a member's own access; agent reports are marked.
- **Limits to track** (values come with decision 6): outside reports per day, attachments per report.

#### 17. Reuse vs new
- **Reused:** task data and the board engine; `task_links` for pull requests; Cloudflare checks, rate limits and moderation; Files for screenshots; Roadmap launches; the Matrix view, filter chips and one-scroll item page; chat cards.
- **New:** kind `bug` with severity → priority; the report form with similar-bug search and "I see this too"; Triage, Reported and Fixed views; duplicate handling; Found in / Fixed in; the Good first issues public list; the Type filter on Tasks; outside-reporter access; `nb bugs` commands; the Overview card; the tab switch (B10).

#### 18. How we know it works
- **Usage signal:** the share of workspaces with Bugs where new bugs are triaged within 3 days on average.
- **Checks once built:**
  - the design contract test
  - unit tests: duplicate chains and watcher moves, severity → priority mapping, auto-verify timing, Fixed in → What's new
  - permission tests: outside reporters see only their own bugs; the public view hides reporter and "Where" details; rate limits hold
  - end to end: report from the form (with a similar-bug match) → triage → Fixing (appears on Tasks) → PR linked → Fixed in v2.4 → What's new lists it → Verified
  - phone triage; keyboard-only triage

---

### 13.3 Feedback & requests (own tab + public page, all 18 layers)

**Choosing the reference (rating + UI quality, section 10; opened live on 2026-11-16):**

| Template | Rating | UI verdict | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Public Roadmap with features & bug forms** by Notion | **4.7 from 45**, the most rated in this group | **Clean, planner level, public-facing.** A short intro, a status board **Considering · To plan · Pickup next · In progress** (cards: title, type New feature / Improvement / Bug, area), views **By status · Backlog · Feature request form · Bug report form**, then side-by-side **Feature requests** (Status · Name · "Tell us more", **+ Feature request**) and **Bug reports** (**+ Bug report**), then **Contact us**. | **Chosen** |
| Feedback tracker by Notion | 5.0 from 19 | Accurate but dense: five linked lists as wide tables. Strong idea: **each request linked to the customers who asked**. | Idea: link requests to clients |
| Feature Requests by Notion | 4.8 from 14 | Internal request list with several views | Ideas only |
| SaaS Builder Roadmap · Feature Request Tracker (desbyseb, NimbleGot) | 4.8–5.0 from 2–11 | Small samples; NimbleGot's adds voting | Idea: votes |

**Why Public Roadmap wins:** most ratings in the group, as calm as the planner, and the only one designed for outside people to read and submit to, which is what open-source projects need.

**What the code has today:** likes on Updates, moderation and reporting, Cloudflare checks; the "I see this too" pattern from Bugs (13.2).

**Agreed changes from an exact copy (2026-11-16):**
1. **One public Feedback page built from the tabs that exist**, plus a separate internal tab for sorting.
2. **Status names:** "To plan / Pickup next" → **Planned / Up next**; **Shipped**, **Not planned** and **Merged** added.
3. **Votes and similar-request suggestions** added.
4. **Requests link to Pipeline clients** (Feedback tracker idea); client value shown to admins only.
5. **The usual changes:** our badges and headings; "Contact us" points to an address or link the admin chooses.

**Change to 11.5:** this public Feedback page **replaces** the Roadmap tab's separate public roadmap view (11.5 S14). Roadmap items marked **Show publicly** now appear on the Feedback page's board.

Marked **[call]** = a decision made in this design that the user can overrule.

#### 1. Getting it
- **Where it's offered:** **+ Add workflow** (owners and admins); the wizard's Settings step, shown unticked for Open source, Web app and Developer tool (section 6); added by an organization.
- **In the + Add workflow dialog:** a Feedback & requests row; one question: **"Turn on a public Feedback page?"** (public workspaces only; default off).
- **First look (internal):** the **New** view, empty: "Requests from your team and, if you turn on the public page, from anyone signed in. Votes show what matters most." **+ Add request** is the primary button.
- **First look (public page, when turned on):** the intro text the admin wrote, an empty board ("Nothing here yet"), the Feature requests section with **+ Request a feature**.

#### 2. Setting it up
- **Statuses** (fixed order, admins can rename): Considering → Planned → Up next → In progress → Shipped. **Closed:** Not planned (reason required) · Merged.
- **Types:** Feature · Improvement · Question (admins can add more). **Bug** isn't a type: "This is a bug" moves the request to the Bug tracker.
- **Areas:** the workspace's product areas (e.g. Payments, Analytics), used for grouping (the reference's "Projects").
- **Public page settings:** on/off; intro text; which sections show (board · feature requests · bug reports · contact); the contact address or link; "Shipped" shows the last 30 days (adjustable).
- **Triage person:** who gets new-request notifications (default: owners and admins).
- **Fields:** admins can add their own (B3).

#### 3. Items
- **Request:** a **task of kind `request`** (decision 1). Holds icon, title, status, type, area, tell us more, votes (people, each with an optional one-line "why"), requested by clients (Pipeline clients), roadmap item (link), merged requests, team notes (members only).
- **Vote:** one per signed-in person per request; can be taken back.
- **Every way to create one:**
  1. **+ Add request** (members, internal)
  2. **+ Request a feature** on the public page (signed-in outsiders, when on)
  3. **From chat:** "Save as request" on a message
  4. **From a client meeting or portal message:** "Save as request" (the client is attached)
  5. **From a bug:** "This is a request" in the Bug tracker
  6. **CLI / agents:** `nb feedback add`

#### 4. Views
| View | What's on screen | Filter / sort |
|---|---|---|
| **New** (internal default) | Unsorted requests: votes, title, type, area, "from 3 people · 1 client", with **Plan · Merge into… · Not planned** | Type, area, source (members / outside / clients) |
| **Board** | Status columns, as in the reference | Type, area |
| **Top voted** | Ranked by votes, then by number of clients asking | Status, area |
| **By area** | Grouped by area | Status |
| **Not planned** | Closed requests with their reason | Area |
| **Public page** | The reference's layout (S5) | — |

- **Search** covers titles, "tell us more" and why-notes.

#### 5. Actions and flow
1. **Submit** (form, with similar requests suggested while typing; **That's my request** votes instead) → **New** (status Considering).
2. **Sort:** **Plan** (→ Planned, optionally **Add to roadmap**), **Merge into…** (votes, clients and notes move; duplicate voters counted once), **Not planned** (reason; voters told), or **This is a bug** (moves to Bugs; votes become "I see this too").
3. **Roadmap link [call]:** after **Add to roadmap**, the request's status **follows the roadmap item** (Planned → Up next when it's added to a launch → In progress → **Shipped** when the launch ships). Without a Roadmap tab, statuses are set by hand.
4. **Shipped:** every voter is told, with a link to the release Update.
5. **Reopen:** a Not planned request can be reconsidered (→ Considering); voters are told.

Who does what: the triage person sorts; members plan and merge; admins run the public page.

#### 6. The tab's own surfaces
- **S1. View tabs:** `New · Board · Top voted · By area · Not planned`.
- **S2. Title row:** `💡 Feedback`, counts in mono ("5 new · top ▲ 21"), search, **+ Add request** (primary), ⋯: Feedback settings · Public page settings · Open public page · Export CSV.
- **S3. Filter chips:** `Type ▾ · Area ▾ · + Filter` (Source, Status).
- **S4. New list**
```
New (to sort) 5
  ▲ 7   Auto-generate thumbnails      Feature   Analytics   from 3 people · 1 client   [Plan] [Merge] [Not planned]
  ▲ 1   Export to CSV                 Feature   —           from Mira (member)         [Plan] [Merge] [Not planned]
```
- **S5. Public Feedback page**
```
[workspace avatar] NetworkBase CLI · Feedback
  "A live list of what we're considering, planning and building. Ask for what you need."
Considering 4      Planned 1        Up next 1          In progress 2        Shipped (last 30 days) 3
┌──────────────┐  ┌────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌───────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐
│ Euros for    │  │ Mobile     │  │ Query cache  │  │ Third-party   │  │ Dark mode    │
│ purchases    │  │ checkout   │  │ rewrite      │  │ integrations  │  │ ✓ v2.3       │
│ Improvement  │  │ Bug        │  │ Improvement  │  │ Improvement   │  │              │
│ Payments ▲ 12│  │       ▲ 4  │  │ Analytics ▲ 7│  │ Analytics ▲ 9 │  │       ▲ 21   │
└──────────────┘  └────────────┘  └──────────────┘  └───────────────┘  └──────────────┘
┌ Feature requests ───────────────────────┐  ┌ Bug reports ─────────────────────────┐
│ Can't find it above? Ask for it.        │  │ Something broken? Tell us.           │
│ ▲ 12 Euros for purchases · Considering  │  │ Checkout cut off on mobile · Fixing  │
│ ▲ 7  Auto-generate thumbnails · New     │  │                                      │
│ [ + Request a feature ]                 │  │ [ + Report a bug ]  (Bug tracker)    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘  └──────────────────────────────────────┘
Contact us   [ the contact you chose: an email address or a link ]
```
  - **Board source:** Roadmap items marked Show publicly when the Roadmap tab exists; otherwise the requests themselves. Bugs on the board come from the Bug tracker only when the Bug tracker tab is public.
  - **Cards:** title, type, area, vote count (▲) with a vote button for signed-in visitors.
- **S6. Request page** (side panel, one scroll; on the public page a read-only version with the vote button and "why" notes)
```
💡 Euros for purchases
  Status        Considering           Type   Improvement      Area   Payments
  Votes         ▲ 12  (A)(S)(M)+9     Requested by clients   Bloom · Mode   (admins see ₹ value)
  Roadmap item  —   [ Add to roadmap ]                         Merged in   2 requests
──────────────────────────────
Tell us more     "Exchange fee is not negligible and is stopping us from using your service."
Why people want it   short notes left by voters, newest first
Team notes       members only
──────────────────────────────
Comments (members) · Files · Activity
```
- **S7. Request form:** title, similar requests (with **That's my request**), tell us more, type, area (optional), Cloudflare check for outsiders.
- **S8. Dialogs:** Merge into… (request picker), Not planned (reason, shown to voters), Add to roadmap (create or link).
- **S9. Overview card:** "5 new · top request ▲ 21 · 2 shipped this month".

#### 7. Design spec
- **Type (Section 04):** Instrument Sans for titles; JetBrains Mono for vote counts and dates.
- **Colour:** statuses Considering = muted Ink, Planned = Ink, Up next = warning, In progress = in-progress status colour, Shipped = success, Not planned = muted Ink with the reason in words. The vote button uses Clay when voted.
- **Badges (Section 10):** precision geometry; no fully round pills.
- **Public page:** Paper surfaces, the workspace's avatar and name; "on NetworkBase" small at the bottom.
- **Icons (Lucide):** Lightbulb (the tab), ChevronUp (vote), Merge (merge), Ban (not planned), Map (linked roadmap item), Rocket (shipped).
- **Contract test:** `tests/unit/feedback-design-contract.test.ts`.

#### 8. Words
- **Tab:** "Feedback". **Item:** Request.
- **Kept from the reference:** Considering, In progress, Feature request, Bug report, Tell us more, Contact us.
- **Ours:** Planned, Up next, Shipped, Not planned, Merged, I want this too / That's my request, Why people want it, Requested by clients, Add to roadmap, Area, Team notes.
- Never "Lead", "Owner", "upvote spam".
- **Empty messages:** New: "Nothing to sort." · Board: "No requests yet." · Public page: "Nothing here yet. Ask for what you need."

#### 9. Links to the rest of NetworkBase
- **Roadmap & launches:** Add to roadmap; status sync; Shipped when the launch ships; the public board shows public roadmap items (replacing 11.5 S14).
- **Bug tracker:** "This is a bug" / "This is a request" move items between the two; the public page's Bug reports section uses the Bug tracker's form.
- **Pipeline:** requests list the clients who asked; a client's page shows "Requests: 3"; Top voted ranks by clients too.
- **Meetings / Client portal / chat:** "Save as request" with the source attached.
- **Updates:** the shipped notification links to the release Update.
- **My Work:** "5 requests to sort" for the triage person.
- **CLI and agents:** `nb feedback list [--top]`, `nb feedback add`; agents never vote.

#### 10. People
| Who | Can |
|---|---|
| Owner / admin | Everything, plus feedback and public page settings, export, see client values |
| Member | Add, sort, plan, merge, close, comment, write team notes, vote |
| Viewer | Add and vote |
| Signed-in outsider (public page on) | Submit requests, vote, add a "why", follow requests they voted on; **no public comment threads [call]** |
| Public (not signed in) | Read the public page |
| Organization | Can push the tab; no roll-up |

#### 11. States
- **Loading:** skeletons for lists and board columns; vote counts show "—".
- **Error:** the tab error boundary; the public page shows a plain retry message.
- **Live updates:** votes and status changes appear without a refresh, on the tab and the public page.
- **Undo:** plan, merge (including moved votes), not planned, add to roadmap.

#### 12. Edges
- **Merging requests voted by the same person:** one vote is kept.
- **Linked roadmap item deleted:** the request returns to **Considering**; voters aren't notified (nothing changed for them).
- **A request merged into one that's later Not planned:** voters of both are told.
- **Spam:** **Report** sends a request to moderation; the person can be blocked from submitting.
- **Public page turned off:** hidden at once; requests and votes kept.
- **Removing the tab:** decision 2; the public page closes with it.

#### 13. Phone
- **Public page:** the board becomes status chips, then the lists; the vote button is large.
- **Internal:** **New** first, with Plan / Merge / Not planned as large buttons.

#### 14. Accessibility
- **Vote buttons** say "Vote for Euros for purchases, 12 votes" and announce the change.
- **Keyboard:** in New, **P** plan, **M** merge, **X** not planned; **V** votes on the focused request.
- **Colour is never the only signal.**

#### 15. Notifications and activity
| Event | Who | Level |
|---|---|---|
| New request | Triage person (or admins) | Normal |
| A request reaches 10 votes | Admins | Summary |
| Planned / Shipped / Not planned / reconsidered | Voters | Normal |
| A client asked for it | That client's assigned person (Pipeline) | Summary |
| Mentioned in team notes | The mentioned person | Important (existing) |

- **Activity:** created (with source), votes (count over time), status changes, merges, roadmap link, clients added.

#### 16. Trust and data
- **Outside submissions:** signed-in only, Cloudflare check, rate limits, moderation.
- **Client names and values** never appear publicly.
- **Voters** are shown publicly only as a count, never as a list **[call]**; their "why" notes appear without names.
- **Team notes** are members-only.
- **Limits to track** (values come with decision 6): requests per day per outsider, the public page as a possible Pro feature.

#### 17. Reuse vs new
- **Reused:** the Bug tracker's form pattern (similar items, "I see this too"); roadmap items, launches and release Updates; Pipeline clients; moderation and Cloudflare checks; filter chips and the one-scroll item page; chat cards.
- **New:** kind `request`; votes with "why" notes; the public **Feedback page** (replacing 11.5's separate public roadmap view); request ↔ roadmap item status sync; Merge into…; closing-the-loop notifications; `nb feedback` commands; the Overview card; the tab switch (B10).

#### 18. How we know it works
- **Usage signal:** the share of workspaces with a public Feedback page that ship at least one voted request within 8 weeks.
- **Checks once built:**
  - the design contract test
  - side-by-side check against the reference layout (intro, board, two sections, contact)
  - unit tests: status follows the roadmap item; merge moves votes without double counting; Not planned requires a reason
  - permission tests: client names and values never reach the public page; voters shown only as a count; outsiders can't see team notes
  - end to end: outsider submits (similar request offered) → member plans and adds to roadmap → launch ships → request Shipped → every voter notified with the release link
  - phone voting; keyboard-only sorting

### 13.4 Tech spec (document template, layers 1, 3, 8, 9)

**References (rating + UI quality, section 10):**

| Template | Rating | UI verdict | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Engineering Tech Spec** by Notion | **5.0 from 26** | **Clean, planner level** (opened live). One page with a table of contents: **Problem statement** (Goals, Non-goals) · **Proposed solution** (Risks) · **Alternative solutions** · **Implementation and rollout plan** (Success criteria, **Ready for review?**) | **Chosen** |
| Technical Design Document (Mochi) | 4.8 from 24 | A longer "Google / Meta style" document | Ideas: data model, API changes, security |

- **1. Getting it:** New doc → NetworkBase templates → **Tech spec** (first for Open source, Web app, Developer tool and Game dev); "Write a tech spec" in a project's or roadmap item's ⋯.
- **3. Contents:**
```
Tech spec: Sign-in with SSO                     Status  Draft ▾   Reviewers (D)(S)
  Author (A) Asha     Project 🎯 SSO project     Roadmap item ✦ Sign-in with SSO
──────────────────────────────
Problem statement     Goals · Non-goals
Proposed solution     how it works · data model · API changes · Risks
Alternatives          what else we considered and why not
Rollout plan          steps · Success criteria · how we'll know
Decisions             [decisions block] decisions recorded from this spec
──────────────────────────────
[ Request review ]
```
  - **Status:** Draft → In review → Approved.
  - **Request review [call]:** creates a **"Review: Tech spec – SSO" task** for each reviewer (normal tasks, My Work, reminders); when all are done the status becomes **Approved**. A reviewer can comment on the doc or reopen with "Changes needed".
  - **Record a decision** from the spec creates a decision (11.6) that appears in its Decisions block (the `decisions` smart block from 12.5).
- **8. Words:** Tech spec, Problem statement, Goals, Non-goals, Proposed solution, Risks, Alternatives, Rollout plan, Success criteria, Request review, In review, Approved, Changes needed.
- **9. Links:** Project planner (project), Roadmap (item), Meetings & decisions (decisions), Tasks (review tasks), Documents (versions; the Approved version is marked).

### 13.6 Meetings & decisions → Architecture decision preset (preset)

**References:** **Lightweight ADRs for Engineering Leaders** (4.7 from 10, opened live; built on the classic ADR format: a numbered list, each with **Title · Status (Proposed / Accepted / Deprecated / Superseded) · Context · Decision · Consequences**) and **Architecture Decision Record** (4.4 from 5, the same shape).

- **2. Setting it up:** the decision page (11.6) gets a **type: Decision / Architecture decision**. For the Architecture type:

| | Architecture decision |
|---|---|
| **Number** | ADR-0001, ADR-0002… one sequence per workspace, never reused |
| **Status words** | **Proposed → Accepted**, later **Deprecated** or **Superseded** (the ADR names for 11.6's Proposed / Decided / Reversed / Superseded) |
| **Sections** | Context · Options and trade-offs (optional) · **Decision** · **Consequences** (what gets easier, what gets harder) |
| **View** | The Decisions view gets an **Architecture** filter: a numbered log, newest first |

- **3. Items:** still a task of kind `decision`, with a type and a number.
- **5. Flow:** propose → accept (who decided, date) → later deprecate or supersede (the old ADR shows "Superseded by → ADR-0007").
  - **Save to Files as Markdown [call]:** an accepted ADR can be written to `docs/adr/0001-title.md` in Files, so open-source projects that keep ADRs in their repository get them through the existing git sync. Later changes ask whether to update the file.
- **8. Words:** Architecture decision, ADR-0001, Accepted, Deprecated, Superseded, Consequences, Save to Files.
- **18. How we know it works:** numbers never repeat or get reused; superseding links both ways; the saved Markdown matches the page.

### 14.2 Content calendar (own tab, all 18 layers)

**Choosing the reference (rating + UI quality, section 10; 2026-11-16):**

| Template | Rating | UI verdict | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Social Media Content Planner** | **4.9 from 800+** | **Calendar-first and calm.** A row of quick-add buttons per platform (Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Facebook, X, Cross-platform); a left rail with **Post ideas** (cards: format, platform, date) and **Social media** accounts (followers per platform); a **Content calendar** month grid with a Today marker, ‹ Today ›, and views **Calendar · Today · This week · By social platform · By status · To schedule**; cards show platform and status. | **Chosen** |
| Blog Editorial Calendar by Notion | 4.9 from 99 | **Clean table.** Views All items · Calendar · **By content type · By status · By writer**; columns Name · Status (Backlog / Drafting / Published) · **Type of content** · **Audience** · **Writer**. | Views and fields |
| Social Media Calendar by Notion | 4.8 from 700+ | A clean post list (Status · Name · Date · Type) and a **posts-per-week chart split by platform** | The chart |
| Social Media Content Tracker (pugo) | 4.8 from 200+ | Numbers on published posts | The Performance view |

**Why it wins:** the most ratings of any content template and a calm, calendar-first screen. Its live page didn't load in time, so it was judged from its marketplace preview, as were Notion's two calendars (Notion's live pages stopped loading partway through this round).

**What the code has today:** no calendar grid (the sprint calendar was removed) and no date library; Updates already work as public posts with likes, comments and Discover; Files hold assets; the "Content / episode launch" checklist preset exists in Roadmap (11.5).

**Agreed changes from an exact copy (2026-11-16):**
1. **No follower counts pulled from platforms;** audience size is typed by hand.
2. **One item can cover several channels,** each with its own published link.
3. **Status gets "Editing" and "Scheduled",** with an editor step using a review task.
4. **Publishing is a reminder plus "Mark published"**, except for NetworkBase Updates, which can publish automatically on schedule.
5. **The usual changes:** our badges and headings, emoji-or-Lucide icons, plain SVG charts.

Marked **[call]** = a decision made in this design that the user can overrule.

#### 1. Getting it
- **Where it's offered:** **+ Add workflow** (owners and admins); the wizard's Settings step, **ticked by default** for Content/Blog, Podcast and Video (its first suggestion there) and shown unticked for E-commerce (section 6); added by an organization.
- **Second step: Choose a setup** (layer 2), then **Pick your channels** (checkboxes, with "Add your own").
- **First look:** this month's empty grid with the Today marker, the channel quick-add buttons, the Ideas rail with **+ Add idea**, and a hint: "Plan what you'll publish and when. Ideas wait on the left until they get a date."

#### 2. Setting it up
- **Setups:**

| Setup | Channels | Extra |
|---|---|---|
| **Blog** | Blog (NetworkBase Updates or an outside blog) · Newsletter | Keyword, Audience; views by writer and type |
| **Social** | Instagram · TikTok · YouTube · LinkedIn · X · Facebook | Format (Post, Reel, Carousel, Story, Short, Thread); Ideas rail on |
| **Podcast** | Episodes | Guest (Pipeline), the Content / episode launch checklist (designed in full in **18.2**) |
| **Video** | YouTube | Script → Shoot → Edit → Publish (designed in full in **19.2**) |

- **Statuses** (fixed order, admins can rename): Idea → Drafting → Editing → Scheduled → Published; also Cancelled.
- **Types** (Article, Post, Video, Episode, Newsletter, Thread…) each with an optional **checklist** (e.g. Article: Header image · SEO title · Links checked), reusing the checklist presets (B7).
- **Channels:** name, icon, optional audience size (typed), optional "publishes to NetworkBase Updates".
- **Default publish time** (e.g. 10:00) and the workspace time zone.
- **Fields:** admins can add their own (B3).

#### 3. Items
- **Content item:** a **task of kind `content`** **[call]** (decision 1). Holds icon, title, status, channels (one or more), publish date and time, type, format, writer (assigned to), editor, audience, keyword, campaign (a label), draft doc (link), assets (files / Asset library), checklist, brief, and **per channel**: published link and results (views, likes, comments, clicks).
- **Idea:** a content item with status Idea and no date.
- **Every way to create one:**
  1. **Channel quick-add buttons** and **+ New ▾**
  2. **Click an empty day** on the calendar
  3. **+ Add idea** in the Ideas rail
  4. **From a roadmap launch:** "Plan launch content" creates items for the launch's channels on the launch date
  5. **From a Feedback request or a meeting:** "Save as content idea"
  6. **CLI / agents:** `nb content add`

#### 4. Views
| View | What's on screen | Drag | Filter / sort |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Calendar** (desktop default) | Month grid (week toggle), Ideas rail and Channels on the left | Ideas onto days; cards between days | Channel, status, writer, campaign, type |
| **This week** (phone default) | Day-by-day list of this week | — | As above |
| **To schedule** | Items past Idea with no date | Onto the calendar (in split view) | As above |
| **By channel** | Grouped by channel | — | Status, period |
| **By status** | A board | Cards between statuses | Channel, writer |
| **By person** | Grouped by writer (Notion's "By writer") | — | Status, period |
| **Performance** | Published items × channel with results, plus a posts-per-week by channel chart | — | Channel, period, campaign |

#### 5. Actions and flow
1. **Idea** (rail) → drag onto a day, or set a date → **Drafting**.
2. **Write draft:** creates a doc from the **Blog post** template (or the type's doc template), linked to the item; the item shows word count.
3. **Ready for edit:** → **Editing**; creates a review task for the **Editor** (like Tech spec, 13.4). Approval → **Scheduled**; "Changes needed" → back to Drafting with the note.
4. **Publish time:**
   - **Outside channels [call]:** the writer gets "Publish now: Pricing guide on LinkedIn"; **Mark published** asks for the live link for each channel.
   - **NetworkBase Updates:** a **scheduled Update** is posted automatically at the time (from the linked draft doc); the item becomes Published with the Update's link.
5. **Results:** typed by hand per channel for outside platforms (an optional reminder 7 days after publishing); filled automatically for NetworkBase Updates (views, likes, comments).
6. **Move / cancel:** dragging a Scheduled item to another day moves its reminder (and its scheduled Update); **Cancel** keeps it in history.

Who does what: writers draft and publish; editors review; admins set channels and setups.

#### 6. The tab's own surfaces
- **S1. Title row:** `✎ Content`, month name + ‹ Today ›, **+ New ▾** (primary), ⋯: Setups · Channels · Types and checklists · Edit fields · Export CSV.
- **S2. Channel quick-add row:** one button per channel plus **+ Cross-channel**.
- **S3. View tabs:** `Calendar · This week · To schedule · By channel · By status · By person · Performance`.
- **S4. Filter chips:** `Channel ▾ · Status ▾ · Writer ▾ · + Filter` (Campaign, Type).
- **S5. Calendar grid**
```
┌ Ideas ────────────┐  ┌ Mo ──── Tu ──── We ──── Th ──── Fr ──── Sa ──── Su ─┐
│ Morning routine    │  │ 2       3       4       5       6       7       8   │
│ Video · Instagram  │  │                 ▣ IG    ✎ Blog                      │
│ Summer travel vlog │  │                 Launch  Pricing                     │
│ Video · YouTube    │  │                 reel    guide                       │
│ + Add idea         │  │                 Sched.  Editing                     │
├ Channels ─────────┤  │ 9       10     (11)     12      13      14      15  │
│ Blog               │  │ ✉ News-          ▶ YT                              │
│ Instagram 28.7k    │  │ letter #12       Demo   …                           │
│ YouTube   3.1k     │  │ Published ✓      Draft                               │
└────────────────────┘  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
  - Day cells: date (mono; today in a Clay circle), up to 3 cards then "+2 more"; click empty space to create.
  - Card: channel icon(s), title, status badge; a small clock when scheduled to publish automatically.
- **S6. This week list:** days as headings, items with time, channel, status, writer.
- **S7. Content item page** (side panel, one scroll)
```
✎ Pricing guide for schools
  Status        Editing             Channels   Blog · Newsletter · LinkedIn
  Publish       Thu, Nov 5 · 10:00  Type       Article        Audience   Teachers
  Writer        (A) Asha            Editor     (S) Sohrab     Campaign   Back to school
  Keyword       school pricing      Draft      📄 Pricing guide (doc · 1,240 words)
  Assets        3 files (Asset library)
  Published at  —                   Results    —
──────────────────────────────
Brief          what it's for, key points, call to action
Checklist      ☐ Header image  ☐ SEO title  ☐ Links checked   (from the type's checklist)
──────────────────────────────
Comments · Files · Activity
```
  - After publishing, "Published at" lists each channel's link and "Results" each channel's numbers.
- **S8. Performance view:** a table (item · channel · date · views · likes · comments · clicks) and the posts-per-week chart (stacked plain SVG bars by channel, labelled).
- **S9. Dialogs:** Mark published (a link per channel) · Ready for edit (editor, note) · Results (numbers per channel).
- **S10. Overview card:** "3 publishing this week · 2 waiting for edit · next: Pricing guide, Thu".

#### 7. Design spec
- **Type (Section 04):** Instrument Sans for titles; JetBrains Mono for dates, times, counts and results.
- **Colour:** Today marker Clay (as in the Project planner); statuses Idea = muted Ink, Drafting = Ink, Editing = warning, Scheduled = in-progress status colour, Published = success; channels told apart by **icon and name**, never colour alone.
- **Badges (Section 10):** precision geometry; no fully round pills.
- **Grid:** the blueprint grid for day cells; weekends lightly shaded.
- **Motion (Section 05):** 180 ms ease-out for drags.
- **Icons (Lucide):** PenLine (the tab), Lightbulb (ideas), CalendarDays (calendar), Send (publish), Clock (scheduled), BarChart3 (performance); channel icons: Rss (blog), Mail (newsletter), Instagram, Youtube, Linkedin, Twitter, Facebook, Music2 (TikTok), Mic (podcast). Brand-like channel icons appear only as small channel markers.
- **Contract test:** `tests/unit/content-calendar-design-contract.test.ts`; the calendar grid gets its own unit tests (month boundaries, time zones).

#### 8. Words
- **Tab:** "Content". **Item:** Content item (shown as the type: "Article", "Post"…), Idea.
- **Kept from the references:** Content calendar, Today, This week, To schedule, By status, Published, Drafting, Audience, Writer (shown as **Writer** but stored as Assigned to).
- **Ours:** Idea, Editing, Scheduled, Channel, Cross-channel, Campaign, Keyword, Brief, Write draft, Ready for edit, Mark published, Results, Performance.
- Never "Lead", "Owner".
- **Empty messages:** Calendar: "Nothing planned this month. Drag an idea onto a day." · Ideas: "Jot ideas here; they wait until they get a date." · Performance: "Results show here after you publish."

#### 9. Links to the rest of NetworkBase
- **Updates:** **scheduled Updates** (new): a content item with the NetworkBase Updates channel publishes automatically as an Update; its views, likes and comments fill Results.
- **Documents:** Write draft (Blog post, Newsletter, Content brief templates).
- **Asset library (next round):** assets attached to items; "Used in" shows on the asset.
- **Roadmap & launches:** "Plan launch content"; launch day items show on both.
- **Pipeline:** Collaborations (sponsored posts) and the Podcast guest field link to Pipeline items.
- **Feedback / Meetings:** "Save as content idea".
- **My Work:** "Publish now", "Ready for your edit", drafts due.
- **CLI and agents:** `nb content week`, `nb content add`; agents can draft into the linked doc with a member's own access, never mark published **[call]**.

#### 10. People
| Who | Can |
|---|---|
| Owner / admin | Everything, plus setups, channels, types and checklists, export |
| Member | Create, write, edit, schedule, publish, enter results |
| Viewer | View and comment |
| Public | Never sees this tab; only published Updates are public |
| Organization | Can push the tab to its workspaces; no roll-up |

#### 11. States
- **Loading:** a month skeleton with faint cards; the Ideas rail skeleton.
- **Error:** the tab error boundary; a failed month still shows the grid with "Couldn't load items. Retry."
- **Live updates:** moves and status changes appear for everyone.
- **Two people at once:** last write wins, with a toast.
- **Undo:** reschedule, status moves, mark published (within the undo window; a scheduled Update that already went out isn't unpublished by undo, it asks first).

#### 12. Edges
- **Moving a Scheduled item to the past:** asks "Publish now or pick a date?"
- **A scheduled Update whose draft doc was deleted or emptied:** doesn't post; the writer is told.
- **Time zones:** publish times are in the workspace's time zone; viewers abroad see their own time with the workspace time on hover.
- **Days with many items:** "+N more" opens the day as a list.
- **A channel removed:** its items keep the channel name as text; the quick-add button disappears.
- **Removing the tab:** decision 2. Hide keeps everything and pauses publish reminders and **scheduled Updates** (they're unscheduled and listed). Delete sends items to Trash; draft docs and assets are never deleted.

#### 13. Phone
- **This week** is the default; **+ Idea** is one tap.
- The publish reminder opens straight onto **Mark published** with a paste field per channel.
- The calendar on phones is a week strip with the day's list below.

#### 14. Accessibility
- **Keyboard:** arrows move between days; **Enter** opens the day; **N** new item on the focused day; **M** moves the focused item to a date picker.
- **Screen readers:** each day reads as "Thursday November 5, 2 items: Pricing guide, Blog, Editing; …"; the chart has a table alternative.
- **No dragging needed:** "Set date" and "Move to…" on every card.

#### 15. Notifications and activity
| Event | Who | Level |
|---|---|---|
| Publish time reached (outside channels) | Writer | Important |
| Scheduled Update posted / failed | Writer | Normal / Important |
| Ready for edit | Editor | Important |
| Due in 1 day and still Drafting | Writer | Normal |
| Published | Watchers | Summary |
| Results reminder (7 days after) | Writer | Summary |

- **Activity:** created, date changes, status moves, editor approvals, published links per channel, results entered.

#### 16. Trust and data
- Workspace data only; no connection to social accounts, no tokens stored for them.
- **Scheduled Updates** follow the workspace's Updates visibility and moderation like any Update.
- **Agents:** draft only with a member's own access; never publish or mark published **[call]**.
- **Limits to track** (values come with decision 6): scheduled Updates per month, channels per workspace.

#### 17. Reuse vs new
- **Reused:** task data; Documents and doc templates; Updates (posting, likes, views, moderation); Files; checklist presets (11.5); review tasks (13.4); filter chips and the one-scroll item page; SVG bars (Goals); workspace time zone.
- **New:** the **Calendar view (B2)**, built once here and reused by Meetings (11.6) and Course planner; kind `content` with multi-channel published links and per-channel results; channel quick-add buttons; the Ideas rail; setups, types and checklists, campaigns; the Performance view; **scheduled Updates**; the Overview card; a design contract test; the tab switch (B10).

#### 18. How we know it works
- **Usage signal:** the share of workspaces with a Content calendar that publish at least four items a month after their first month.
- **Checks once built:**

  - scheduled Updates post on time in the workspace's time zone and fill Results
  - a cross-channel item keeps one status but separate links and results
