**What the code has today:** no products, stock or orders anywhere. Money (12.2), the Asset library's gallery grid (14.3), Pipeline's CSV importer (11.2), Cloudflare checks, rate limits and moderation are designed or exist.

**Agreed changes from an exact copy (2026-11-16):**
1. **Products are records, orders are tasks, stock is a history,** so every number can be traced.
2. **Orders, Money and stock are connected.**
3. **No store syncing or payment collection;** CSV import instead.
4. **No banners;** the clean inventory table and order cards are kept.
5. **The usual changes:** our badges and headings; "Packed by" / "Assigned to", never "Owner" or "Lead".

**Agreed exception (2026-11-16): order requests without signing in.** Every other outside form needs a NetworkBase account; a shop's customers usually don't have one. The public **Order form** accepts requests **without sign-in**, protected by the Cloudflare check, rate limits and moderation; **off by default**; each request must be **confirmed** before it becomes an order; no payment is taken; customer details are **members only** and are deleted with the order after Trash's 30 days.

Marked **[call]** = a decision made in this design that the user can overrule.

#### 1. Getting it
- **Where it's offered:** **+ Add workflow** (owners and admins); the wizard's Settings step, **ticked by default** for E-commerce (its first suggestion) and shown unticked for Side project (section 6); also listed in + Add workflow as "Suggested" for Creative workspaces that sell artwork; added by an organization.
- **Second step:** currency (defaults to Money's), and whether to start the **Shop** setup in Money if it isn't there.
- **First look:** the Dashboard with zeroed tiles and two buttons: **+ Product** and **Import products (CSV)**; a hint: "Add your products, then orders keep stock and Money up to date."

#### 2. Setting it up
- **Order statuses** (fixed order, renameable): New → Packed → Shipped → Delivered; Cancelled; Returned.
- **Channels:** Website · Etsy · Amazon · Instagram · WhatsApp · In person (editable).
- **Categories** for products; **locations** (shelves, warehouses).
- **Default reorder level** and default ship-by (e.g. 2 days after the order).
- **Order form:** on / off, which products it shows, custom requests on / off, the "Pay by" text, the confirmation message.
- **Return reasons:** Damaged · Wrong item · Changed mind · Other.
- **Fields:** admins can add their own (B3).

#### 3. Items
- **Product:** a **record** (decision 1): name, SKU, photos (Asset library), category, **variants** (e.g. Blue / Green / White, each with its own stock) **[call]**, price, cost, **profit** (worked out), reorder level, **status** (In stock / Low stock / Out of stock, automatic), supplier (23.3), location, channels it's listed on.
- **Stock history line:** product (variant), change (+ / −), reason (Order shipped · Return to stock · Purchase order received · Adjustment with note), link to the order or purchase order, date, who. **The stock count is the total of its lines [call].**
- **Order:** a **task of kind `order`** (decision 1): number (#1042), customer (name, contact, address; members only), channel, lines (product × quantity × price, plus shipping and extras), total, payment status (marked by hand), tracking number (text), ship-by date, assigned to (packer), status.
- **Purchase order:** a record: supplier, lines (product × quantity × cost), expected date, status (Ordered → Received; Cancelled).
- **Return:** a record on an order: lines returned, reason, refund amount (a record only), back to stock or damaged.
- **Order request:** what the public form creates; becomes an Order when confirmed.
- **Every way to create:** **+ Order** / **+ Product**; **Create purchase order** from Low stock; the public **Order form**; **CSV import** of products or orders (store exports); CLI `nb orders` / `nb products`.

#### 4. Views
| View | What's on screen | Filter / sort |
|---|---|---|
| **Dashboard** (default) | Tiles (to pack today · low stock · sold this month · stock value), the items-by-category ring, recent order cards | Channel, period |
| **Orders** | Board by status with the reference's cards (customer · date · amount · channel · status) | Channel, ship-by, assigned to |
| **Products** | Photo gallery, or the reference's table (Item · Status · Quantity · Reorder level · Price · Stock value · Supplier) | Category, status, supplier, channel |
| **Low stock** | Products at or under reorder level; select → **Create purchase order** | Supplier |
| **Purchase orders** | Ordered / Received, expected dates | Supplier, status |
| **Returns** | Returned orders with reason and refund | Reason, period |
| **Requests** | Order requests from the form waiting for confirmation (when the form is on) | — |

#### 5. Actions and flow
1. **Order comes in** (by hand, form request confirmed, or CSV) → **New**.
2. **Packed** (assigned packer) → **Shipped** (asks for the tracking number; stock lines are written: −quantity) → **Delivered**.
3. **Paid:** marked by hand; a **shipped and paid** order writes **sales income** to Money (once).
4. **Cancel:** puts stock back if it had shipped lines; Money income reversed if written.
5. **Return…:** choose lines, reason, refund amount; **back to stock** (+ lines) or **damaged** (no stock change; an adjustment note); refund recorded in Money as a negative sale.
6. **Restock:** Low stock → **Create purchase order** (supplier and suggested quantities filled) → **Received** (stock + lines; an **expense** in Money).
7. **Adjust:** a manual + / − with a required reason (counted, damaged, gift…).
8. **Overselling:** ordering more than stock warns and marks the line **Backorder**; it ships when stock arrives.

#### 6. The tab's own surfaces
- **S1. Title row:** `▣ Shop`, counts in mono ("6 to pack today · 4 low stock"), **+ Order** (primary), **+ Product**, ⋯: Order form settings · Channels · Categories and locations · Import CSV · Export CSV.
- **S2. View tabs:** `Dashboard · Orders · Products · Low stock · Purchase orders · Returns` (+ Requests when the form is on).
- **S3. Dashboard**
```
┌ To pack today ┐┌ Low stock ──┐┌ This month ────┐┌ Stock value ┐   ┌ Items by category ┐
│ 6 orders      ││ 4 products  ││ ₹1,84,000 sold ││ ₹3,20,000   │   │  (ring, labelled)  │
│ 2 ship by 5pm ││ 1 out       ││ 212 orders     ││ 411 items   │   │                    │
└───────────────┘└─────────────┘└────────────────┘└─────────────┘   └────────────────────┘
Recent orders
┌ #1042 Meera ──┐ ┌ #1041 Dev ───┐ ┌ #1040 Ravi ───┐
│ Nov 16 · ₹2,400│ │ Nov 16 · ₹890 │ │ Nov 15 · ₹1,250│
│ Etsy · New     │ │ Website·Packed│ │ WhatsApp·Shipped│
└────────────────┘ └───────────────┘ └────────────────┘
```
- **S4. Product page** (side panel, one scroll)
```
▣ Hand-thrown mug (blue)                         Status  Low stock ⚠
  SKU        MUG-BLU-01        Category  Kitchen       Supplier  Clayworks
  Price      ₹850              Cost      ₹320          Profit    ₹530 (62%)
  Stock      4   (reorder at 5)                Location  Shelf B2
  Variants   Blue · Green · White   (each with its own stock)
  Channels   Website · Etsy · Instagram
──────────────────────────────
Stock history   Nov 16  −2  order #1042   ·  Nov 10  +20  PO-007 received  ·  Nov 2  −1  damaged (adjusted)
──────────────────────────────
Photos (Asset library) · Comments · Activity
```
- **S5. Order page** (side panel, one scroll)
```

  Channel   Etsy          Payment   Paid (marked by you)     Tracking  —
  Items     Hand-thrown mug (blue) × 2   ₹1,700
            Gift wrap × 1                 ₹100
            Shipping                      ₹600        Total  ₹2,400
  Deliver to  (address, members only)
──────────────────────────────
[ Packed ] [ Shipped → tracking ] [ Delivered ]   [ Cancel ] [ Return… ]
```
- **S6. Purchase order page:** supplier, lines, expected date, **Mark received** (all or partial).
- **S7. Return dialog:** lines, reason, refund amount, back to stock / damaged.
- **S8. Adjust stock dialog:** + / −, reason (required).
- **S9. Public Order form:** shop name and avatar, products (photo, name, price, quantity) or a custom request box, name, email or phone, delivery address (optional), note, Cloudflare check, **Send request**; then the confirmation message and the "Pay by" text.
- **S10. Requests list:** request → **Confirm as order** / **Decline** (with a message to copy).
- **S11. Overview card:** "6 to pack today · 4 low stock".

#### 7. Design spec
- **Type (Section 04):** Instrument Sans for names; **JetBrains Mono for SKUs, quantities, prices, order numbers and totals**, right-aligned in tables; money through the shared formatter (12.2).
- **Colour:** stock In stock = success, Low = warning, Out = danger (always with words); order statuses New = muted Ink, Packed = in-progress status colour, Shipped = Ink, Delivered = success, Cancelled / Returned = muted Ink with words.
- **Charts:** the ring is plain SVG with labels.
- **Badges (Section 10):** precision geometry; no fully round pills.
- **Icons (Lucide):** Store (the tab), Package (products), ShoppingCart (orders), PackageCheck (packed), Truck (shipped), Undo2 (returns), ClipboardList (purchase orders), AlertTriangle (low stock).
- **Contract test:** `tests/unit/inventory-design-contract.test.ts` (task contract rules plus amounts and quantities in mono).

#### 8. Words
- **Tab:** "Shop". **Items:** Product, Variant, Order, Purchase order, Return, Order request.
- **Kept from the references:** In stock, Low stock, Out of stock, Quantity, Reorder level, Stock value, Supplier, Price, Cost, Profit.
- **Ours:** To pack today, Packed, Shipped, Delivered, Ship by, Channel, Tracking number, Backorder, Stock history, Adjust stock, Mark received, Back to stock, Damaged, Order form, Confirm as order.
- Never "Lead", "Owner", "checkout", "payment" as an action (we don't take payments).
- **Empty messages:** Orders: "No orders yet." · Products: "Add your first product, or import a CSV." · Low stock: "Nothing low. Nice."

#### 9. Links to the rest of NetworkBase
- **Money (12.2), Shop setup:** shipped and paid orders → sales income (once); refunds → negative sales; received purchase orders → expenses; profit per product and month.
- **Pipeline:** **Suppliers** preset (23.3); repeat customers can be added to a Clients pipeline (12.3) **[call: optional]**.
- **Asset library (14.3):** product photos; the gallery grid powers the Products view.
- **Content calendar (14.2):** promotions link products; "Low stock" warns when a promoted product is short.
- **My Work:** orders to pack (assignee), purchase orders arriving today.
- **CLI and agents:** `nb orders today`, `nb products low`; agents can draft orders and adjust stock only with a member's access, never confirm form requests **[call]**.

#### 10. People
| Who | Can |
|---|---|
| Owner / admin | Everything, plus the order form, channels, export |
| Member | Manage orders, products, purchase orders, returns, stock adjustments |
| Viewer | See products and orders (customer addresses hidden) |
| Public | Only the Order form, when it's on (no sign-in, per the agreed exception) |
| Organization | Can push the tab; no roll-up |

#### 11. States
- **Loading:** tile and card skeletons; numbers show "—".
- **Error:** the tab error boundary; stock numbers never show partial totals.
- **Live updates:** new orders and stock changes appear for everyone.
- **Two people at once:** two people shipping the same order: the second sees "Already shipped by Asha".
- **Undo:** status moves (with their stock lines), adjustments, receiving a purchase order.

#### 12. Edges
- **Stock never drifts:** the count is always the total of the history lines.
- **Variants:** a product's stock is the sum of its variants'.
- **Deleting a product:** kept on old orders as it was; its history stays.
- **Currencies:** kept separate, as in Money.
- **Order form abuse:** rate limits per address and device, Cloudflare check, moderation queue for flagged requests; repeated declines can block a sender.
- **Customer data:** members only; deleted with the order after 30 days in Trash.
- **Removing the tab:** decision 2. Hide keeps everything and turns the order form off; Delete sends products, orders and history to Trash; Money records stay.

#### 13. Phone
- **To pack today** first, with **Packed** and **Shipped** as large buttons (tracking number field for Shipped).
- **Adjust stock** quickly from a product.
- **Barcode scanning** later **[call]**.

#### 14. Accessibility
- Cards read as "Order 1042, Meera Rao, 2,400 rupees, Etsy, New, ship by November 17"; stock statuses carry words; quantities in tables have column headers; keyboard: **P** packed, **S** shipped on a focused order.

#### 15. Notifications and activity
| Event | Who | Level |
|---|---|---|
| New order or order request | Order handlers | Normal |
| Ship-by is today | Order handlers | Important |
| Low stock | Admins | Normal |
| Out of stock | Admins | Important |
| Purchase order overdue | Admins | Normal |
| Return requested | Order handlers | Normal |

- **Activity:** every order status change, every stock line (who, why), purchase orders, returns, form requests confirmed or declined.

#### 16. Trust and data
- **The order form** is the only place outsiders submit **without an account** (agreed exception): Cloudflare check, rate limits, moderation, confirmation before an order exists. The same exception was later extended to the **Commission request form** (24.2).
- **Customer details** (name, contact, address) are members only, never on public pages, never in chat cards, deleted with the order after Trash's 30 days.
- **No payments taken, no store accounts connected.**
- **Export:** admins only, logged.
- **Limits to track** (values come with decision 6): products, orders per month, order-form requests per day.

#### 17. Reuse vs new
- **Reused:** Money (Shop setup, formatter, income / expense records); the Asset library (photos, gallery grid); Pipeline's CSV importer; Cloudflare checks, rate limits and moderation; the board engine; filter chips and the one-scroll item page; the Overview card pattern.
- **New:** the **Inventory & orders** tab; products with variants; the **stock history**; kind `order`; purchase orders; returns; the Dashboard; the public **Order form** (the first form without sign-in) and the Requests list; links into Money; `nb orders` / `nb products`; a design contract test; the tab switch (B10).

#### 18. How we know it works
- **Usage signal:** the share of shops where stock stays correct (no unexplained adjustments) and orders reach Delivered within their ship-by dates.
- **Checks once built:**
  - the design contract test
  - side-by-side checks against the references (inventory table and views; order cards)
  - unit tests: stock count = total of history lines; variants sum; cancel and return put stock back; backorders
  - shipped and paid orders appear in Money exactly once; refunds reverse correctly
  - the order form refuses abuse (rate limits, Cloudflare, moderation) and never creates an order without confirmation
  - customer details never reach a public page, chat card or export for non-admins
  - phone packing; keyboard-only order handling

- **3. Items:** pipeline items (kind `deal`, shown as "Supplier").
- **5. Flow:** Found → Sampling (log samples as interactions) → Approved → **Active** (appears in products' Supplier field and in Create purchase order).
- **8. Words:** Supplier, Sampling, Approved, Active, Dropped, Minimum order, Lead time.
- **18. How we know it works:** purchase orders use only Active suppliers; lead time feeds the purchase order's suggested expected date.

### 24.2 Pipeline → Commissions preset (preset: layers 2, 3, 5, 8, 18)
```
◇ Pipeline · Commissions ▾     Board · Queue · Directory      Slots open: 2 of 5
Request → Quote sent → Deposit paid → In queue → Sketch → Line art → Color → Final → Delivered   (Declined)
  Meera · Full body · ₹4,500 · deposit ✓ · revisions 1/2 · due Dec 3 · Sketch
```
- **2. Setting it up:** item **Commission**; working stages **Request → Quote sent → Deposit paid → In queue → Sketch → Line art → Color → Final**; **Delivered** (Won type) / **Declined** (Lost type); a **price sheet** (Headshot · Half body · Full body · Custom, plus extras); **slots** (how many at once) **[call]**; revisions allowed per type; terms of service doc; request form on / off.
- **3. Items:** pipeline items (kind `deal`, shown as "Commission") with type, price, extras, reference images (Asset library), **deposit** (a Money invoice), **revisions allowed / used**, deadline, **usage rights** (personal / commercial), queue position.
- **5. Flow:** request (form or by hand) → **Accept** → Quote sent → Deposit paid (invoice marked paid) → In queue (by position) → Sketch → Line art → Color → Final (each step shared in the **Client portal** for **Approve / Request changes**; each change request uses a revision) → **Delivered** (final files, remaining invoice). "Slots open: 2 of 5" can show on the public request form.
- **Commission request form:** the agreed exception (above): no sign-in, Cloudflare, rate limits, moderation, accept before it becomes a commission; shows the price sheet, slots open and the terms.
- **8. Words:** Commission, Request, Quote sent, Deposit paid, In queue, Sketch, Line art, Color, Final, Delivered, Slots, Price sheet, Revisions, Usage rights.
- **18. How we know it works:** the share of commissions reaching Delivered with client approvals; checks that revisions count correctly, slots stop new requests when full, and the request form refuses abuse.

### 25.2 Feedback → Ideas board (preset: layers 2, 3, 5, 8, 18)
```
💡 Ideas      Board · Ranked · Dropped
Idea → Validating → Building → Launched      (Dropped)
  Notion template shop     Impact 4 · Ease 3 · Confidence 2 → 24   Validating  ☑ 5 people asked ☐ landing page ☐ first sale
  Weekend coding course    Impact 3 · Ease 4 · Confidence 4 → 48   Idea
```
- **2. Setting it up:** item **Idea**, **private to the workspace** (never on a public page); statuses **Idea → Validating → Building → Launched / Dropped**; **score [call]** = Impact × Ease × Confidence (each 1–5); a **validation checklist** (talk to 5 people · landing page · first sale; editable).
- **3. Items:** Feedback items (kind `request`, shown as "Idea"), optionally linked to an **Assumptions check** doc (11.8).
- **5. Flow:** capture → score → **Ranked** view (highest first, the Ideapad's "rank & prioritize") → Validating (checklist) → **Start building** (creates a **project** in the Project planner or a **roadmap item**, linked back) → Launched, or Dropped with a reason.
- **8. Words:** Idea, Validating, Building, Launched, Dropped, Impact, Ease, Confidence, Score, Start building.
- **18. How we know it works:** the share of ideas that reach Validating with at least one checklist step done; checks that scores rank correctly and ideas never appear publicly.

### 26.5 Rules that hold everywhere (agreed)
- **Decisions 1–5** (section 9): work items are tasks, records are records; hide by default, delete through Trash; owners and admins add tabs; org tabs locked; wizard suggests with the top one ticked.
- **References** are chosen on rating **and** UI quality at the Anthropic planner's level (section 10).
- **Outside forms need sign-in**, with one agreed exception: the **Order form** (23.2) and **Commission request form** (24.2) accept requests without sign-in, off by default, confirmed before they count.
- **NetworkBase never:** takes payments or moves money; sends email to outside people; posts to social platforms, YouTube, app stores or Steam; hosts podcast audio; syncs with Shopify / Etsy / Amazon; fetches pasted outside links on the server.
- **Agents never:** publish, mark invoices paid, score, vote, take attendance, register people, confirm form requests, or act inside a client portal.
- **Never shown to the public:** contact details, client values, registration answers, 1:1 notes, teacher notes, incident timelines, support tickets, idea boards.

## 27. Blend first: where each workflow lives (agreed 2026-11-16)

**The change.** Most ideas don't need a tab of their own. A workflow can **blend into a default tab** (Tasks, Documents, Files, Updates, Sprints) or, later, become **its own tab**. **Agreed:** the blended versions are designed and built end to end now; **own tabs are parked** (their designs in sections 11–25 stay as reference, not built now).

### 27.1 What decides the home
- **Records** (money, products, stock, deals with private values, registrations, attendance) → **own tab only**, so parked.
- **Work items** (projects, roadmap items, bugs, content, requests) → **blend into Tasks**.
- **Pages** (meetings, decisions, launch checklists, quarterly goals, ideas, light events, templates) → **blend into Documents**. Own tab only for collections people browse as a set.
- **Two limits on Tasks:** every member, viewers included, sees Tasks, so nothing private goes there (money, deal values, support tickets, 1:1s); and each type keeps **its own stages** when filtered to it, while the mixed board maps them to To do / In progress / Completed **[call]** (updated in 28.3: stages map to statuses, not column names).
- **One limit on Documents:** a document can be public, members only or leaders only (`workspace_documents.settings.visibilityOverride`), never private to two people, so **1:1s stay with the parked Meetings tab**.
- **From the code (2026-11-16):** document smart blocks today are `roles`, `contributors`, `files`, `tasks`, `sprints`, `projects` (`src/lib/workspaces/doc-blocks.ts`). Interactive documents need new blocks (27.4).

## 28. The workflow rule, the prototype, and the fixes (agreed 2026-11-16, written 2026-11-17)

This section brings the report in line with what was agreed after section 27: the rule for when a workflow gets its own tab, the clickable prototype, and the rules found by checking the code. **Where 27 and 28 differ, 28 wins.**

### 28.1 The rule: a tab is a job, not a pile of data
- **There is one set of tasks.** Bugs, requests, content pieces, projects, roadmap items, goals and ideas are all task records (decision 1). Nothing is copied between tabs.
- **The Tasks tab has one job: doing the work.**
- **A workflow gets its own tab only when it has a different job** before or around the doing: sorting reports (**Bugs**), taking in asks (**Requests**), deciding what's published and when (**Content**), deciding Now / Next / Later (**Roadmap**). Its items are the same tasks: they **join the Tasks board at one stage** and leave it when the work is done.
- **No different job → it blends** into a default tab as a view, a field, a section or a block.
- **Never on the board:** project, roadmap item, objective, key result, idea, and lesson (`class_lesson`, added in 30.3). They hold or measure work; only **their work tasks** go on the board. Projects show in the Tasks tab's **Projects** view.
- **Own tabs with their own data** (Money, Shop, Pipeline and the rest of the parked list in 28.2) stay parked.
- **Pinned views were considered and dropped:** a filter dressed up as a tab looked like a tab but did nothing a tab should.

### 28.2 Where every workflow lives (replaces 27.2)

| Workflow | Home | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Project planner | **Tasks** · Projects view (Timeline, Active), Group by Project, Part of | Look from 11.3 (Anthropic planner reference) |
| Timeline, Calendar, Matrix | **Tasks** · views | 11.3, 14.2, 11.7 |
| **Bugs** | **Own tab, same tasks** · joins the board at **Fixing** | 13.2; outside reporting parked |
| **Requests** (internal, design) | **Own tab, same tasks** · joins at **Accepted** | 21.3, 24.6; response clock |
| **Content** (Blog, Social) | **Own tab, same tasks** · joins at **Drafting** | 14.2; Podcast and Video setups parked |
| **Roadmap** (+ Game milestones) | **Own tab, same tasks** · never on the board; its work tasks are | 11.5, 22.4 |
| Meetings & decisions (all types except 1:1) | **Documents** · Meetings and Decisions sections | 11.6, 13.6, 17.5, 18.3, 19.4, 20.6, 21.2, 22.3 |
| Launch checklists | **Documents** · Launches section; every step is a task | 11.5, 20.4, 22.4, 25.5 |
| Quarterly goals | **Documents** · Goals section; key results with check-ins | 11.4 |
| Ideas | **Documents** · Ideas section; ranked table | 25.2 |
| Team off-site | **Documents** · Off-site section | 16.2 |
| Document templates, Docs site, Snippets | **Documents** | 26.3, 20.3, 21.4 |
| Asset library | **Files** · Assets view | 14.3, 18.5, 19.5, 19.6, 22.5, 24.3 |
| Changelog, scheduled Updates | **Updates** · views | 13.7, 14.2 |
| Learning path | **Sprints** · Path view | 15.2 |
| **Parked** | Money · Shop · Pipeline (12 presets) · Feedback public page · Support inbox · Listener questions · Incidents and Status page · Event planner (except off-site) · Course planner · Goals & OKRs tab · Meetings tab for 1:1s · Client portal · public Order and Commission forms · Podcast and Video content setups | Designs kept as reference |

### 28.3 How one record walks between tabs
The board's columns belong to the workspace: up to six, renamed freely, each tied to one **status**: `todo`, `in_progress`, `done` or `blocked` (`workspace_workflow_columns`). So **each stage maps to a status, never to a column name**; the card lands in that workspace's column for the status, whatever it is called. The stage is kept in its own field.

| Type | Own tab | Stages only in the own tab | Stage → board status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Task | — | — | To do → todo · In progress → in_progress · In review → in_progress + review requested · Completed → done |
| Bug | Bugs | New, Confirmed; closed as Won't fix, Duplicate or Can't reproduce | Fixing → in_progress · Fixed → done · Verified → done |
| Request | Requests | New; closed as Declined | Accepted → todo · In progress → in_progress · In review → in_progress + review requested · Delivered → done |
| Content | Content | Idea | Drafting → in_progress · Editing → in_progress + review requested · Scheduled → done · Published → done |
| Project, roadmap item, objective, key result, idea | Tasks (Projects view) · Roadmap · Documents | All of them | Never on the board |

- **Two doors, one record:** **New ▾** in Tasks creates the type **at the stage where it joins the board** (someone is starting the work now). The own tab's button creates it at the **first stage**.
- **The walk is visible:** the item page shows "Shows in: Tasks · In progress / Bugs · Fixing" and the stages with two brackets, one for the own tab (all stages) and one for the board.

### 28.4 Rules found in the code (B1–B14)

| # | Rule | Marked |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | Stages map to **statuses**, not column names (28.3). Renamed or added columns keep working. | Agreed |
| B2 | **Blocked** is a status any type can take **without losing its stage**: the card reads "Bug · Fixing · Blocked" and sits in the Blocked column. | [call] |
| B3 | In workspaces that **require review before completion** (`reviewStatus`), the done stages (Fixed, Delivered, Scheduled, Completed) are set **only after approval**. | [call] |
| B4 | **One number for every type** (`NB-142`), from the workspace's existing counter, with the type icon beside it. No BUG- or REQ- numbers. | [call] |
| B5 | When an item joins the board, the person moving it picks the sprint: **"Add to [running sprint]"** is ticked by default; unticked sends it to the Backlog. | [call] |
| B6 | **Removing a workflow** hides its tab and its sections. Items already on the board **stay as plain tasks** with a greyed type mark until done. Nothing is deleted. | [call] |
| B7 | **Moving back off the board** (Fixing → Confirmed) keeps the sprint history: the sprint shows "Moved back to Bugs". | [call] |
| B8 | **Live state lives in records, not in document text.** Ticks, check-ins and scores change records; the document holds smart blocks pointing at them (the existing smart block syntax), so ticking never creates a document version. An agenda is ordinary document text. | [call] |
| B9 | **Ticking follows the task's permission; adding rows follows the document's.** A member can tick their action item in a document only admins edit. | [call] |
| B10 | The **never-on-board** group is named in the rule (28.1). | Agreed |
| B11 | Workflow tabs are **hidden from the public** by default (`publicTabVisibility`). Bugs and Requests can't be made public; the public pages are parked. | [call] |
| B12 | **Organization-added workflows** show a lock and "Added by [organization]" on the tab and in the dialog, and can't be removed in the child workspace (decision 4). | Agreed (decision 4) |
| B13 | The **CLI, MCP and agents** read and move the new types under the same rules: `nb tasks list --type bug`, stage moves that respect B1–B7, and the agent limits from 26.5. | [call] |
| B14 | **Phone tab row:** workflow tabs sit after a divider; **Add workflow moves into ⋯**. | [call] |

**Smaller rules [call]:**
- Unread counts on workflow tabs count only items waiting at the first stage.
- The Changelog's "Improved" comes from completed tasks with the **Improvement** label, or is written by hand.
- Learning-path ticks reuse the existing **"everyone" assignments** (one copy per person).
- Pinned image comments and timestamped video comments share one anchor shape: a spot (x, y) or a moment (seconds).

### 28.5 Documents: sections and live blocks
- **Sections are stored in the document's settings** (`workspace_documents.settings`: section, kind, date) and shown as the rail's existing groups: Pages · Meetings · Decisions · Launches · Goals · Ideas · Off-site.
- **Live blocks:** action items and launch steps (task rows), decisions (links to Decisions documents, numbered D-001…), goals (key results with Check in; some counted live from Tasks or Bugs), ranked ideas (Impact × Ease × Confidence, Start building).
- **Meeting types:** Weekly, Standup, Planning, Retrospective, Kickoff, Client, Board meeting (motions, quorum), Recording session, Shoot day (call sheet), User interview, Incident review, Playtest. 1:1s are parked (documents can't be private to two people).
- **Privacy:** documents keep their existing visibility (public, members only, leaders only). Ideas and goals are never public.

### 28.6 Words
- **Completed**, never "Done", for the finished task status (`TASK_STATUS_LABELS`).
- **NB-142** for every item, never BUG-12 or REQ-21.
- **Shows in**, **Joins Tasks at Fixing**, **Add to Week 47**, **Moved back to Bugs**.
- **Work tasks** (tasks Part of a roadmap item), **Action items**, **Check in**, **Start building**.
- Dialog groups: **Blends into Tasks** · **Own tab · same tasks** · **Blends into Documents / Files / Updates / Sprints** · **Later · parked**.
- Never "Owner" for a person on an item (use **Assigned to**); never "Lead".

### 28.7 The clickable prototype
- **Link:** https://claude.ai/artifact/XzbFeYK9K2BzNFLnkcjkab (private to the user; share from the page's Share menu).
- **What it shows:** the Lantern Labs example workspace with every blended workflow and the four same-data tabs; the record walk between tabs; Documents sections and live blocks; Assets, Changelog, Scheduled, the learning path; the Add workflow dialog with the parked list; and (version 3) the fixes in 28.3–28.4: NB numbers, columns by status with Blocked and a renamed column, sprint choice on joining, roles, organization lock, the Project planner look, the full item page, real forms, all meeting types, first looks, phone width and working buttons.
- **Example only:** data resets on reload; nothing is saved.

### 28.8 Where each design section stands
Each category section (11–25) now starts with a **Status** line: **Tasks**, **Own tab · same tasks**, **Documents**, **Files**, **Updates**, **Sprints** or **Parked**. The own-tab designs in those sections stay the reference for the parked tabs and the source for the blended ones.

| Wave | What |
|---|---|
| **0. Foundation** | Types with a stage field and the stage → status map (B1–B4); **the New module (28.11)**; one-scroll item page; Add workflow dialog with groups, roles and organization lock; filter chips; document sections and live blocks (B8–B9); NetworkBase templates |
| **1. Tasks** | Project planner (Projects view: Timeline, Active; Part of; completion) · Timeline, Calendar and Matrix views |
| **2. Same-data tabs** | Bugs → Requests → Content → Roadmap (with launch checklist documents), each with B5–B7 |
| **3. Documents** | Meetings & decisions (all types), Quarterly goals, Ideas, Off-site, templates, Docs site, Snippets |

- **CLI and MCP** command and tool design for the new types (B13).
- **Overview cards** for the blended workflows.

- **Blend rounds:** section 38 started 2026-11-17 (17 rounds at the inch-by-inch depth); F1, F2 and F3 agreed (Wave 0 complete); T1 agreed (Wave 1 complete); T3 Bugs, T4 Requests and T5 Content agreed; T2, D1–D6 and O1–O3 agreed 2026-11-18 — section 38 complete (all 17 rounds).
- **Next:** the user reviews prototype version 3; then a design doc per wave and `superpowers:writing-plans`. Nothing is built until the user says "implement".

### 28.11 One New module for everything people create (agreed 2026-11-17)
Every item is created through **the existing task create module** (`CreateTaskModal`), extended. Nothing gets a separate form of its own.

**What the module already is:** a 640px dialog built from the shared form parts (`Field`, `SectionDivider`, `QuickChips`, `FORM_*`): title and subtitle, ✕, **"What are you creating?"** underline tabs (Task · Assignment), fixed sections **Basics → Sprint and assignee → Schedule → Subtasks and files**, quick due chips **Today · 1 week · 2 weeks · 4 weeks**, checks before saving, and a muted footer with **Cancel** and **Create task**. Switching tabs carries title, description, sprint and due date across.

```
┌ Create bug ─────────────────────────────────────────── ✕ ┐
│ What are you creating?                                    │
│ Task · Bug · Request · Content · Project · Roadmap item   │ ← only added workflows
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ BASICS              Title · Description                   │
│ BUG DETAILS         Severity · Where · Steps · Expected   │ ← the one section a type adds
│ SPRINT AND ASSIGNEE Sprint · Assigned to · Starts at ▾    │
│ SCHEDULE            Due [Today][1 week][2 weeks][4 weeks] │
│ SUBTASKS AND FILES                                        │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Joins Tasks at Fixing · also shows in Bugs  Cancel  Create bug │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Rules [call]:**
- **Same shell, same section order, same footer** for every type. A type adds **one** section after Basics and renames only what it must (Due → Publish date for content, Need by for requests).
- **"Starts at"** replaces Status for types with their own tab. Its default depends on where the module was opened: from Tasks, the stage where the type joins the board (Fixing, Accepted, Drafting); from the type's own tab, the first stage (New, Idea). Options that put the item on the board say so.
- **Tabs show only what's added,** in a fixed order: Task · Bug · Request · Content · Project · Roadmap item · Assignment (organizations). Opened from a goals or Ideas document, the module shows Key result or Idea.
- **Switching tabs keeps** title, description, assignee and date; type-only fields are kept too, in case the person switches back.
- **The footer says where the item will show** ("Joins Tasks at Fixing · also shows in Bugs").
- **Quick adds stay one line** (action items, launch steps, subtasks, check-ins): type the title, press Enter. **More details** opens the full module with From and Part of filled in.

| Type | Its section | Changes to the shared sections |
|---|---|---|
| Task | — | As today |
| Bug | **Bug details:** severity, where (browser or app), steps to reproduce, expected | Starts at: New · Confirmed · Fixing |
| Request | **Request details:** kind (internal, design), brief | Starts at: New · Accepted; Due → **Need by** |
| Content | **Content details:** channels | Starts at: Idea · Drafting; Due → **Publish date** |
| Project | **Project details:** icon, summary | No sprint; Status (Not started, Planning, In progress); Schedule → **Start and End**; Subtasks → tasks added later via Project |
| Roadmap item | **Roadmap details:** outcome, column (Now, Next, Later) | No sprint, no schedule, no subtasks |
| Key result | **Key result details:** objective, start value, target, lower is better, measured by (check-ins, a roadmap item's work tasks, or open Critical bugs) | No sprint, schedule or subtasks |
| Idea | **Idea details:** impact, ease, confidence (1–5) | No sprint, schedule or subtasks |
| Assignment | As today | As today |

**Other things people create** use the **same dialog shell and footer** with their own fields: New document (a "Start from" section with blank, templates and meeting types), New sprint, upload with asset details. **Gap:** `CreateSprintModal` should be checked against the shell. Posting an update keeps the inline composer in the feed.

## 29. Organizations: Education at the organization level (agreed 2026-11-17)

Sections 11–25 designed workflows for **workspaces**. This section starts the same work for **organizations**, by organization type (`org_type`: Education, Company, Community, Research, Club, Other), **Education first**. Templates come at **both levels**: the organization itself, and the workspaces it pushes them to (locked, decision 4). Everything is free, so these sections have no Free/Pro limits.

An organization shows people inside it **ten tabs**: **Overview · About · Documents · Updates · Sprints · Tasks (Assignments + Review queue) · Files · Projects (its workspaces) · Members · Settings** (`isWorkspaceTabVisibleToViewer` in `src/lib/workspaces/settings-policies.ts`). Visitors see About and the public tabs. *(Corrected 2026-11-17: an earlier draft said organizations had no Documents, Updates, Sprints or Files.)* The analysis is about **how the org-only tabs (Overview, About, Assignments, Review queue, Projects, Members, Settings) work and react** for each type. **Documents, Sprints and Files reuse the workspace analysis** (sections 26–28). They aren't redone, and only education-specific additions are noted.

This section is the organization-level base. **College / University**, **Coaching / Bootcamp** and **School (K–12)** follow, one category at a time.

### 29.1 What was checked
| Finding | What it means |
|---|---|
| **Today an Education org is one class:** roles Teacher / TA / Student, term dates, Unit/Week sprints, review required, a "Course materials" folder (`ORG_TYPE_PROFILES.education` in `src/lib/organizations/type-profile.ts`). Its workspaces are student and team projects. | The class level is already strong. **The school level doesn't exist.** |
| `docs/organization-concept-report.md` §2: **"two levels only. An org cannot be inside another org."** | Section 29.2 reverses this rule (call 1 in 29.6). |
| **Sign-up requires 18 or older** (`src/lib/legal/acceptance.ts`). | Schools with under-18 students can't use NetworkBase today (call 2 in 29.6). |
| **Production (2026-11-17, read-only totals):** 1 education org, 2 members, 4 assignments, 6 file hand-ins. | No real use to learn from yet. The templates come from research. |
| **Notion:** education templates are teacher or student planners (Classroom Manager for Teachers, Teacher OS, Teacher's Planner, Notion Course Manager, University Planner). **None is for running a school or department.** | Notion is the reference at the class level only. The institution level uses patterns from class platforms (Canvas, Google Classroom), never copies of them. |
| The org already pushes **documents, updates, sprints and files** into its workspaces, and already has assignments with file, link or text hand-ins, late rules, an AI policy, versions, a roster, the copy states (not started, submitted, returned, missing, excused), teams, class questions, and a review queue with **Lanes** and **One at a time**. | The analysis starts from what's there, where it falls short, and what templates add. |

### 29.2 Structure: three levels
```
Institution   (school · college · university · academy)        ← new
  └ Class org (an Education org exactly as it is today)
       └ Workspaces (student and team projects)
```
- **Institution** is a new top level. It holds people, the academic calendar, the rules and templates it pushes down, and summary numbers across classes.
- **A class stays exactly as it is.** A teacher can still make a class with no school, then **Join a school** later (the same flow as "Move into an organization" for workspaces).
- **A department is a label, not a level:** a Department label on each class, and a **Head of department** role scoped to it. Three levels, not four. **[call]**
- **Data:** an org whose `parentId` points to an institution. No new table. **[call]**
- **Cost to check before building:**
  - read permissions gain a grandparent (`app_private.nb_project_can_read` and the viewer's parent-org role)
  - the sidebar and profile nest three deep
  - "Part of Northgate" verification (`verified_against`) becomes a real link
- **Privacy:** an institution admin **never reads student work by default**. They see counts and states only; the class's teachers see the work. **[call]**
- **Other types later:** Company → Department → Team may use the same shape. That's decided in the Company round.

### 29.3 The term cycle
| Moment | Institution | Class | Today |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Before term** | Set the academic year and terms; create classes from a template; assign teachers | Plan units and weeks; syllabus; course materials | Partly ("Plan your term", term dates) |
| **Week 1** | Students join classes (code or CSV) | Welcome note, required reading, teams | Yes |
| **Every week** | Watch which classes are behind | Assignments, hand-ins, review, announcements | Yes |
| **Mid-term** | Progress across classes | Mid-term test, feedback round | Partly |
| **Exams** | Exam period on the calendar | Exam assignments, second marker | **Missing** |
| **End of term** | Results released together; classes archived | Final review, verified contribution entries | Partly (archive, verify) |
| **Next term** | Roll the year over | **Start next term:** copy the plan, documents and assignments as drafts, without people or work | **Missing: the biggest template job** |

### 29.4 Each role's week
| Role | Level | What their week needs |
|---|---|---|
| **Institution admin** | Institution | Classes needing attention, people imports, rules, the calendar. Never student work by default |
| **Head of department** | Institution, scoped to a department | Their department's classes: behind plan, review backlog |
| **Teacher** | Class | Plan, assign, review, announce |
| **TA** | Class | Review **their share** of hand-ins (split by team or section) |
| **Student** | Class + workspace | What's due, hand in, read feedback, team project |
| **Parent / guardian** | — | No account. **Parked** (another platform solves this with email summaries) |
| **Outside examiner** | Class | The existing Viewer role, plus second marking |

### 29.5 Each org tab at both levels
| Tab | Institution (new) | Class (today + templates) |
|---|---|---|
| **Overview** | Classes needing attention (behind plan, review backlog, low hand-in rate), term progress, announcements to everyone | Keeps Catch up · Today · How the class is doing · This week. **Get started** follows the template chosen |
| **About** | Public page: programs, departments, public classes, Verified badge, how to join | Course description, teacher, schedule, syllabus summary |
| **Tasks · Assignments** ★ | Pushes **assignment templates and policies** (AI policy, late rule, reminders); **never assigns work itself** | **Assignment templates:** Homework · Lab · Team project · Essay · Presentation · Reading · Quiz/test · Exam · Peer review · Practice (not reviewed). Each one sets the hand-in type, late rule, AI policy, team or individual, review, rubric and reminders. They're created through the one New module (28.11) as tabs under "What are you creating?" |
| **Tasks · Review queue** ★ | Counts only: backlog per class and teacher | Keeps Lanes and One at a time, and adds: **rubric scoring** in the side panel · **comment bank** · **release feedback together** · **split reviews among TAs** · **second marker** for exams |
| **Projects** | Classes grouped by term, department and teacher; **Start next term**; bulk archive | Student workspaces grouped by team. **Workspace templates:** Group project · Lab notebook · Portfolio · Capstone · Thesis |
| **Members** | Staff and student directory, CSV import, roles (Admin, Head of department, Teacher, Student) | Teacher / TA / Student; sections as groups; **Attendance** view (present, late, absent per session) |
| **Settings** | Academic year and terms (pushed down); defaults for AI policy, late rule and review; the **template library** (assignment, workspace and document templates); who can create classes; a cap on student privacy | Inherits them as locked "Set by <institution>" rows (the existing pattern) |
| **Documents · Sprints · Files** | Handbook and policy documents | Reused as they are. Adds a **Syllabus** and **Lesson plan** document, Units/Weeks, and Course materials. **Course planner comes back from parked, blended:** units and weeks in Sprints, lessons as tasks, syllabus in Documents (replaces the 15.2 own tab for organizations) |

### 29.6 Calls (picks agreed 2026-11-17)
1. **Three levels:** reverse "two levels only" for Institution → Class. **Agreed: yes**, with the department as a label, not a level.
2. **Under-18 students:** **keep 18+ for now.** Build for **College / University** and **Coaching / Bootcamp** (adult students). **School (K–12)** is staff-only, and students are parked until a separate legal and safety design is done (parental consent, accounts managed by the school).
3. **Marks:** **a rubric and marks per assignment**, seen only by that student and staff. **No overall grade book, GPA or transcript**: NetworkBase isn't a school records system.
4. **Quizzes:** **no quiz engine.** A quiz is an assignment with a text answer or an outside link.
5. **Plagiarism checks:** **no.** The AI policy and labels already exist.
6. **Attendance:** **yes, light** (Members → Attendance, per session).
7. **Roster sync with school systems:** **no.** CSV import and join codes only.

### 29.7 Next
One category at a time, each with its own Notion and platform template sort and its presets of 29.5:
1. **College / University** (departments, exams, second marker, thesis)
2. **Coaching / Bootcamp** (cohorts, capstone, demo day reusing the Event setup)
3. **School (K–12)**, staff-only per call 2

Nothing is built until the user says "implement".
