### 30.2 W1 · Class home (agreed 2026-11-17)
**Reference:** Classroom Home (Notion, 4.90 / 52), with Syllabus (4.89 / 44) for the syllabus card.

**Today:**
- **About** has the welcome note, the overview card (About / Who it's for / What happens here) and Workspaces. Its rail has Stages, Recent activity, Join / Invite, Owner and admins, and Details (web address, verified, time zone, since).
- **Overview** has Catch up, the pinned announcement, Get started, Today, and How the class is doing. Its rail has This week, Workspaces, People and Activity.

**Agreed changes from an exact copy:**
1. The email row becomes a **Message** button (same-org messages). Teachers' emails are never shown.
2. The course website row is dropped; the web address is already in Details.
3. Announcements stay in **Updates**. The newest pinned one shows on Overview.
4. The class directory goes to Members. Students get a names-only **Classmates** list in the Overview rail.
5. The course schedule goes to W2. About shows only a short **This term** summary.
6. The syllabus is a Documents template, pinned to About as a card.

```
ABOUT (everyone; visitors see the public rows)
┌───────────────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────┐
│ Welcome note (members)                    │ Class details        │
│ Overview card: About · Who it's for ·     │  Course code  CS 301 │
│   What happens here                       │  Meets   Tue Thu     │
│ ┌ Syllabus ─────────────────── Open ┐     │          10:30–12:00 │
│ │ Data Structures · 4 units          │     │  Room    LH-2 · 204  │
│ │ First paragraph of the syllabus…   │     │  Office hours Wed 3–4│
│ └────────────────────────────────────┘     │  Teacher  Dr Rao  ✉  │
│ This term                     Term plan → │  Term  Jan 6–Apr 25  │
│  Unit 1 Arrays      Jan 6–24   ✓          │ Part of Northgate ✓  │
│  Unit 2 Trees       Jan 27–Feb 21 ← now   │ Stages · Activity    │
│  Midterm week       Feb 24–28             │ Join / Your role     │
│ Workspaces                                │ Details              │
└───────────────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────┘

OVERVIEW (members): one line added to Today
  Next class · Thu 10:30 · LH-2 204 · Unit 2 Trees        (or: Cancelled · Thu)
  Office hours today · 3–4 pm
```

**The 18 layers**
1. **Getting it:**
   - Every Education class has a Class home; it isn't an add-on.
   - The institution's template fills in the starting rows and can make rows required.
   - **Teacher's first look:** Get started adds Class details · Syllabus · Term plan · Welcome note · Invite students.
   - **Student's first look:** welcome note → Class details → first announcement.
2. **Setting it up:**
   - **Settings → Class details:** course code, meets (days, times, room or online link), office hours (days, times, place or link), credits (optional), department label.
   - Each row has a **Show to visitors** switch: on for course code, meets and term; off for room and office hours.
3. **Items:**
   - Class details saved on the org (`org_settings` keys, no new table). **[call]**
   - **Sessions** are worked out from meets × term dates − institution breaks. They're stored only once changed (cancelled or moved) or once attendance is taken (W6). **[call]**
   - The syllabus is a Documents template with the role "Syllabus".
   - Announcements are the existing Updates.
   - **Creating:** details are edited in Settings; the syllabus comes from New document → Syllabus; announcements use the existing inline composer (28.11).
4. **Views:**
   - About as sketched.
   - Overview gets **Next class** and **Office hours today** in Today.
   - The workspace header line becomes `Part of CS 301 · Next class Thu 10:30 · 1 assignment due`.
5. **Actions and flow:**
   - Edit details → a **Tell the class** tick (unticked by default) posts one short announcement.
   - **Cancel this class / Move this class** on a single session → Next class shows "Cancelled" or "Moved to Fri 9:00", and the class is notified.
   - End of term → About shows "Ended Apr 25" and is read-only.
6. **Surfaces:**
   - **Class details card:** icon rows, a Message button on the teacher row, Edit for teachers.
   - **Syllabus card:** title, number of units, first paragraph, Open. Teachers see **Add a syllabus** when there's none.
   - **This term:** units from Sprints, with ✓, "← now", and exam weeks from W4.
   - **Next class line:** shows a "your time" second time when the student is in another zone.
7. **Design spec:**
   - Reuse `ProjectOverviewCard`, `RailSection`, `OrgCard`, the Details row style and `nb-meta`.
   - Lucide icons: Hash, CalendarClock, MapPin, Clock, UserRound, CalendarRange, BookOpenText.
   - Add a design contract test.
8. **Words:**
   - Class details · Course code · Meets · Room · Office hours · Term · Next class · Cancelled · Moved to · Syllabus · This term · Classmates · Tell the class.
   - Role names come from the type profile. Never "Instructor", "Lead" or "Owner".
9. **Links:**
   - Updates · Documents (Syllabus) · Sprints (This term → Term plan, W2) · Files (Course materials) · Members (Classmates) · Attendance (W6) · My work (W3) · the workspace header line · search.
   - The CLI and agents can read details; changing them is left to B13.
10. **People:**

    | | Sees | Can do |
    |---|---|---|
    | Institution admin | Details, syllabus, term | Set the template and required rows; can't edit the class |
    | Head of department | The same, for their department's classes | Read only |
    | Teacher | Everything | Edit details, syllabus, sessions; Tell the class |
    | TA | Everything | Cancel or move sessions; not the details **[call]** |
    | Student | Everything except visitor-hidden settings | Message the teacher; open the syllabus |
    | Outside examiner (Viewer) | About, syllabus | Read only |
    | Visitor | Rows marked Show to visitors, the overview card, a public syllabus | Join / Request |

11. **States:**
    - Loading skeletons as today.
    - No details: teachers see **Add class details**; students see nothing.
    - Edits show live, with the existing last-changed footer.
12. **Edges:**
    - No term dates: Meets shows, and Next class asks the teacher to set the term.
    - Times are in the class's zone, plus "your time" when different.
    - Breaks are skipped.
    - Archived class: read-only "Ended".
    - Teacher leaves: the existing succession flow.
    - **Start next term** copies details and the syllabus, not sessions or announcements.
13. **Phone:** the details card moves above the overview card; Next class goes to the top of Overview.
14. **Accessibility:**
    - Details as a description list.
    - Times in `<time datetime>`.
    - "Cancelled" in words as well as colour.
15. **Notifications:**
    - Cancelled or moved class: **Important**, to members.
    - Tell the class: **Normal**.
    - Silent edits: nothing.
16. **Trust and data:**
    - No teacher email is shown.
    - Room and office hours are hidden from visitors by default.
    - Students are 18+ (29.6 call 2).
17. **Reuse vs new:**
    - **Reuse:** overview card, welcome note, Details rail, Stages, pinned announcement, Get started, org documents, direct messages, the "Set by" lock.
    - **New:**
      - the Class details fields
      - a pure session rule (meets × term − breaks + changes)
      - the Syllabus template and a pinned document role
      - the This term card
      - the Next class line
18. **How we know it works:**
    - **Signal:** the share of classes with details and a syllabus by week 2.
    - **Checks:** session-rule unit tests (time-zone shifts, breaks, a moved session); visitor vs member view; Tell the class posting exactly one announcement.

**Organization steps:**
- **Level:** the institution sets the template and required rows; the class fills them in; the student workspace header shows Next class.
- **Term moment:** before term (fill in) → week 1 (students land) → every week (Next class, changes) → end of term (Ended, read-only) → next term (copied).
- **Org tab:** About (main) + Overview (Next class) + Settings (Class details).

**Calls agreed 2026-11-17:**
1. Details stored in `org_settings`.
2. Sessions are worked out, not stored, until changed.
3. A TA can cancel or move a session but not edit details.
4. Names-only Classmates for students; Members stays admins-only.
5. Room and office hours hidden from visitors by default.
6. Tell the class starts unticked.

### 30.3 W2 · Term plan + lessons (agreed 2026-11-17)
**References:**

| Template | Rating | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **Course Schedule** (Notion) | **4.80 / 345** | **Main reference:** the Week · Dates · Topics · Assessments table, a midterm week row, and items typed Lesson / Assignment / Exam. Views: All · By type · Lessons · Assignments · Exams · Calendar |
| Lesson Plans (Notion) | 4.76 / 163 | Lessons grouped by course with a status, and a lesson calendar |
| Teacher Home (Notion) | 4.83 / 183 | Lessons grouped by unit, tagged with standards |
| Course Planner | 4.85 / 324 | A % complete bar on each unit card |

**Today:**
- Units and weeks are sprints (a week is a sprint inside a unit, `parent_sprint_id`).
- Plan your term builds a series; sprint materials (`sprint_materials`); auto-start; class sprints show in student workspaces.
- Org documents can be Required reading, with read counts.
- **The Sprints tab shows one sprint at a time; nothing shows the whole term.**
- No lessons, no outcomes. `tasks.kind` is `task` or `assignment`.

**From 15.2:** the Course planner's lessons (`class_lesson`), the statuses Planned → Ready → Taught, and Before / In / After class move **into the Sprints tab** (29.5). The self-paced Learning path moves to the Coaching / Bootcamp round.

**Agreed changes from an exact copy:**
1. One table inside the Sprints tab, built from units → weeks rather than loose dated items.
2. "Topics" is the week's existing sprint **goal** field, relabelled for classes.
3. "Assessments" lists the assignments due that week (exams get their own chip, W4). Nothing is typed by hand.
4. "Standards" becomes **Outcomes** (CO1, CO2 …): a list on the class, tagged on lessons and assignments, with coverage shown.
5. Unit progress = lessons taught ÷ planned. It's class progress, never a per-student score.
6. No banner or sticker decoration.

```
SPRINTS tab (a class)        [ Term plan ] [ Sprint ] [ Calendar ]          + New ▾
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Spring 2027 · Jan 6 – Apr 25 · Week 6 of 16          Outcomes covered 4 of 5 │
├──────┬───────────────┬──────────────────────┬─────────┬──────────────────────┤
│ Week │ Dates         │ Topics               │ Lessons │ Assessments          │
├──────┴───────────────┴──────────────────────┴─────────┴──────────────────────┤
│ ▾ Unit 1 · Arrays and lists                    ████████ 100%   CO1 CO2       │
│   W1 │ Jan 6–10   │ Arrays, complexity       │ 2 ✓✓    │ Lab 1 · due Jan 10   │
│   W2 │ Jan 13–17  │ Linked lists             │ 2 ✓✓    │ —                    │
│ ▾ Unit 2 · Trees                    ← now      ████░░░░  50%   CO3           │
│   W5 │ Feb 3–7    │ BSTs                     │ 2 ✓·    │ Assignment 2 · Feb 7 │
│   W6 │ Feb 10–14  │ Balancing      ← now     │ 2 ··    │ Quiz 1 · Feb 13      │
│   ── │ Feb 17–21  │ Mid-term break (Northgate)                               │
│   W7 │ Feb 24–28  │ Midterm week                       │ ▣ Midterm · Feb 26   │
│ ▸ Unit 3 · Graphs                              ░░░░░░░░   0%   CO4           │
│ CO5 · not covered by any lesson yet                                          │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
Lesson row (a week expanded):  Tue Feb 11 · 10:30 · Balancing BSTs · Ready · CO3 · 2 materials
```

**The 18 layers**
1. **Getting it:**
   - Every Education class gets the **Term plan** view in Sprints, as its default view.
   - The institution template can bring units, weeks, outcomes and the academic calendar (term, breaks, exam weeks).
   - **Teacher's first look:** Plan your term (it exists) fills units and weeks from the term dates; the hint reads "Add lessons to each week."
   - **Student's first look:** the same table, read-only, with only Ready and Taught lessons.
2. **Setting it up:** **Settings → Term plan**:
   - outcomes list (code + description)
   - default lesson length (from W1's meets)
   - "Students see lessons when: Ready (default) / Always" **[call]**
   - the Topics column label (Topics · Chapters · Themes)
3. **Items:**
   - **Lesson:** a task of kind **`class_lesson`** (one more value in `tasks_kind_check`). It holds:
     - title, unit/week (sprint)
     - session (a date from W1)
     - status Planned → Ready → Taught (or Cancelled)
     - outcomes
     - Before class / In class / After class
     - materials (the existing task files and docs)
     - linked assignments
     - teacher notes (staff only)
   - **Never on the board** (added to 28.1). **[call]**
   - **Outcome:** a short list on the class (`org_settings`), tagged on lessons and assignments.
   - **Topics:** the week's sprint goal.
   - **Creating:**
     - (1) + New ▾ → **Lesson**, as a tab in the one New module (28.11; type section: session, outcomes, Before / In / After)
     - (2) + on a week row
     - (3) clicking a day in Calendar
     - (4) Duplicate a lesson or a whole unit
     - (5) institution template
     - (6) Start next term
     - (7) CLI and agents (B13)
4. **Views:**

   | View | On screen | Drag | Filter |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | **Term plan** (default) | Units → weeks → lessons; Assessments; breaks; outcome coverage | Lessons between weeks | Unit, outcome, type |
   | **Sprint** (today's view) | One week or unit, plus a **Lessons in this week** block | — | As today |
   | **Calendar** | Sessions with their lessons, due dates and exams (the 14.2 Calendar view) | Lessons to another session | Type |
5. **Actions and flow:**
   - Teacher: Planned → **Ready** (students now see Before class) → **Mark taught** after the session (one click; Overview reminds the teacher the next day).
   - Before class materials can be ticked **Required**, using the existing Required reading counts.
   - If W1 cancels or moves a session, its lesson shows **Needs a new session** and offers the next free one. **[call]**
   - Moving a lesson to another week asks whether to **Shift the rest**.
6. **Surfaces:**
   - **Header strip:** term, "Week 6 of 16", Outcomes covered.
   - **Unit rows:** progress bar, outcome chips, collapse.
   - **Week rows:** Topics (edit in place), lesson dots, Assessments chips, institution break rows.
   - **Lesson page:** the one-scroll item page with session, status, outcomes, Before / In / After, materials, linked assignments, and teacher notes ("Only Teachers and TAs see this").
7. **Design spec:**
   - Reuse the sprint left rail, `SprintHeader`, the materials block, `StatusBadge` and the progress bar.
   - Lucide icons: GraduationCap, Target, CalendarDays, CheckCircle2.
   - Add a contract test.
8. **Words:**
   - Term plan · Unit · Week · Topics · Lesson · Planned · Ready · Taught · Cancelled · Outcomes · Outcomes covered · Before class · In class · After class · Teacher notes · Mark taught · Needs a new session · Shift the rest.
   - "Unit" and "Week" follow the renameable sprint words.
9. **Links:**
   - W1: sessions → lessons; About's This term; Next class shows the lesson title.
   - Assignments: the Assessments column; After class.
   - Documents: a **Term plan block** for the Syllabus.
   - Files (materials) · My work (W3) · W4 exam weeks · W6 attendance · search.
10. **People:**

    | | Sees | Can do |
    |---|---|---|
    | Institution admin | Every class's plan (read only), outcome coverage | Academic calendar, template, required outcomes |
    | Head of department | Department classes; **Behind plan** (taught vs. planned by today) | Read only |
    | Teacher | Everything | Everything |
    | TA | Everything, including teacher notes | Mark taught, edit In class and materials; not add or delete lessons or outcomes **[call]** |
    | Student | Ready and Taught lessons, Topics, Assessments, materials | Open materials; required reading |
    | Visitor | Nothing (Sprints isn't public by default) | — |
11. **States:**
    - Skeleton rows while loading.
    - No term dates → "Set the term dates to plan your term".
    - Live updates when lessons are marked taught.
    - The existing last-changed footer.
12. **Edges:**
    - Break weeks show a break row.
    - More lessons than sessions in a week: "3 lessons, 2 sessions".
    - A deleted unit takes its lessons to Trash (30 days).
    - Archived class: read-only.
    - **Start next term:** units and weeks are re-dated; lessons go back to Planned and are matched to sessions in order; outcomes and materials are kept; assignments are copied as drafts.
13. **Phone:** the table becomes a list of units → weeks, with Assessments under each week. Drag becomes "Move to week".
14. **Accessibility:**
    - A real table with row headers.
    - Progress as text ("50%, 1 of 2 taught").
    - A menu option for every drag.
15. **Notifications:**
    - Lesson Ready: nothing (it shows in W3).
    - Required material added: the existing Required reading notice.
    - "Mark yesterday's lesson taught": **Summary**, at most one a day.
    - Lesson needs a new session: **Important**, to the teacher.
16. **Trust and data:**
    - Teacher notes are never sent to students or visitors.
    - Outcome coverage is a class-level number only.
17. **Reuse vs new:**
    - **Reuse:** sprints, Plan your term, sprint materials, Required reading, the item page, the Calendar view, the New module.
    - **New:**
      - the `class_lesson` kind
      - the Term plan view
      - outcomes and their tags
      - lesson ↔ session matching (pure function)
      - Shift the rest
      - Behind plan
18. **How we know it works:**
    - **Signal:** the share of classes with lessons in at least 70% of weeks by week 3.
    - **Checks:**
      - session matching (cancelled and moved sessions, breaks)
      - Start next term re-dating
      - teacher notes never reach students (server test)
      - outcome coverage counts

**Organization steps:**
- **Level:** the institution sets the academic calendar, template and required outcomes, and sees Behind plan. The class holds the plan. Student workspaces show the running Unit and Week in their header (exists).
- **Term moment:** before term (plan) → every week (Ready, Taught) → mid-term (Behind plan) → exams (W4 weeks) → next term (copied and re-dated).
- **Org tab:** Sprints (Term plan) + Settings (Term plan) + About's This term (W1) + Overview (the Mark taught reminder).

**Calls agreed 2026-11-17:**
1. Lessons are `class_lesson` tasks, never on the board.
2. Students see lessons once Ready (setting: Always).
3. Topics reuses the sprint goal.
4. Outcomes are a short list on the class, with coverage on the table.
5. A cancelled or moved session leaves its lesson as Needs a new session; nothing moves on its own.
6. A TA can mark taught and edit In class and materials, but can't add or delete lessons or outcomes.
7. The self-paced Learning path goes to the Coaching / Bootcamp round.
8. The Mark taught reminder is Summary level, at most once a day.


### 30.4 W3 · Student's week (agreed 2026-11-17)
**References:**

| Template | Rating | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **The Best Student Planner** (Fayefilms) | **4.83 / 2,701** | **Main reference:** today's top priorities, my week at a glance (one column per day with schedule, priority and regular tasks), and cards into each area |
| Exam Cram Dashboard | 4.76 / 447 | The exam countdown at the top; a study schedule by subject |

**Today:**
- The **My work drawer** has **Tasks** (due first) and **Requests** tabs.
- Filters: **All · Personal · each org**. Quick filters: **Due soon · Missing · To review**.
- Chips: Late / Missing, team and class context.
- Each class Overview has its own This week rail.
- **Missing:** a week across every class, sessions (W1), Before class prep (W2), the exam countdown, and "my top things today".

**Agreed changes from an exact copy:**
1. It isn't a new page. It's a **Week** view inside the My work drawer.
2. Days run **down the page** (Today, Tomorrow, then weekdays), not as columns.
3. Nothing is typed twice; every row comes from records that already exist.
4. Top priorities become **Pin for today** (at most 3, personal, cleared at the end of the day).
5. Daily routine, habit trackers and decorative cards are dropped.
6. The exam countdown is one strip at the top; exams themselves are W4.

```
MY WORK                          [ Tasks 7 ] [ Requests ]
 [ Week ] [ List ]          All · Personal · CS 301 · MA 210
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ▣ Midterm · CS 301 · Thu Feb 26 · in 9 days              →   │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ PINNED FOR TODAY                                             │
│  ★ Lab 3 · CS 301 · due 23:59                    Hand in     │
├ TODAY · Tue Feb 17 ──────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  ◷ 10:30  CS 301 · Balancing BSTs · LH-2 204                 │
│           Before class · Read ch. 7  Required  ☐             │
│  ▢ Lab 3 · CS 301 · due 23:59 · Not started      Hand in     │
│  ▢ Sprint notes · Heap Viz (your team)                       │
├ TOMORROW · Wed ──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  ◷ 09:00  MA 210 · Eigenvalues · Cancelled                   │
│  ◷ 15:00  Office hours · CS 301                              │
├ THU · FRI · SAT · SUN ───────────── 2 more ─────────── ▸ ────┤
├ MISSING · 1 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  ▢ Lab 1 · CS 301 · was due Jan 10 · Late work until Feb 20  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**The 18 layers**
1. **Getting it:**
   - Anyone who belongs to an Education class sees **Week** in My work, which opens on Week by default. Others open on List as today. **[call]**
   - **First look:** today's class, the welcome reading, and the hint "Your classes, prep and due work, day by day."
   - With no classes, Week isn't shown.
2. **Setting it up (per person):**
   - Week or List as the default
   - week starts Monday or Sunday (profile locale)
   - show cancelled classes
   - Classes can be hidden one at a time with the existing org filter.
3. **Items** (all read from existing records):
   - session rows (W1 sessions with the W2 lesson title, room, Cancelled or Moved)
   - Before class rows (materials from Ready lessons; Required ones tick through Required reading)
   - assignment copy rows (existing states)
   - team project tasks and personal tasks
   - office hours rows
   - the exam strip (W4)
   - **Pin for today:** a per-person list of up to 3 task ids, cleared at the person's midnight. The only new stored data. **[call]**
   - **Creating:** + New adds a personal task through the one New module. Nothing class-related is created here.
4. **Views:**
   - **Week:** Pinned → Today → Tomorrow → rest of the week (collapsed) → Missing.
   - **List:** today's view, unchanged.
   - Both keep the org filter, search and quick filters.
5. **Actions and flow:**
   - **Hand in** opens the existing hand-in.
   - Tick a Before class item to mark it read.
   - Pin or Unpin from a row's ⋯ menu.
   - A session opens its lesson; the exam strip opens the exam.
   - Rows clear by themselves when done, handed in or excused.
6. **Surfaces:**
   - **Exam strip:** the nearest exam within 14 days ("in 9 days" → "Tomorrow" → "Today"). **[call]**
   - **Day headers:** date, plus a dot when something is due.
   - **Session rows:** the class's time plus "your time".
   - **Missing:** only copies that still accept late work ("Late work until …").
   - **Empty day:** "Nothing scheduled."
7. **Design spec:**
   - Reuse the drawer, its tab bar, row and chip styles.
   - Day headers in the mono uppercase rail heading style.
   - Lucide icons: Clock, BookOpen, FileUp, Star, Timer.
   - Add a contract test.
8. **Words:** Week · List · Pinned for today · Today · Tomorrow · Before class · Required · Hand in · Missing · Late work until · Nothing scheduled · in 9 days · Pin for today. **Completed**, never "Done".
9. **Links:** W1 sessions and office hours · W2 lessons and Before class · Assignments · W4 exam strip · team workspaces · Required reading · the Needs you badge (unchanged count rule).
10. **People:**
    - **Student:** their own week.
    - **Teacher / TA:** the same Week with **teaching rows**: their sessions, lessons still Planned in the next 7 days, reviews waiting. **[call]**
    - **Admins:** their own week only. **Nobody sees another person's week.**
11. **States:**
    - Skeleton day groups while loading.
    - Live flips: a cancelled class, a returned hand-in.
    - The drawer's existing error and retry.
12. **Edges:**
    - At most 8 rows a day, then "+3 more".
    - A class with no term dates shows assignments only.
    - Mixed time zones are sorted by the person's time.
    - Excused copies are hidden; ended classes drop out.
    - A completed pinned task stays with a tick until midnight.
13. **Phone:** full-screen drawer; the exam strip sticks under the tabs; ⋯ menus instead of swipes.
14. **Accessibility:**
    - Each day is a labelled list ("Tuesday, February 17, 4 items").
    - Times in `<time>`.
    - Cancelled and Missing in words, not only colour.
    - Keyboard pin.
15. **Notifications:** none new. The week gathers what existing notices already cover.
16. **Trust and data:**
    - Built only from rows the viewer can already read.
    - Teacher notes never show.
    - Pins are private and kept for one day.
17. **Reuse vs new:**
    - **Reuse:** the My work drawer, `listMyCopies`, copy states, quick filters, the org filter, Required reading, W1 sessions, W2 lessons.
    - **New:**
      - the Week grouping (pure function: items → days)
      - session and Before class row types
      - the exam strip
      - Pin for today
      - teaching rows
18. **How we know it works:**
    - **Signal:** the share of students opening Week at least 3 days a week in week 3 of term.
    - **Checks:**
      - day grouping across time zones and week starts
      - rows clearing on hand-in or excuse
      - a teacher never sees students' personal tasks (server test)
      - pins clearing at midnight

**Organization steps:**
- **Level:** across every class, plus team workspaces and personal tasks. The institution contributes only its calendar.
- **Term moment:** week 1 → every week (main use) → exams (countdown) → end of term (the class drops out).
- **Org tab:** none. It lives in the My work drawer; each row opens the class's Sprints, Assignments or About.

**Calls agreed 2026-11-17:**
1. A Week view in the My work drawer, the default for people in a class.
2. Days run down the page.
3. Pin for today (at most 3, private, cleared at midnight) is the only new stored data.
4. Routine, habits and decorative cards are left out.
5. The exam strip covers the nearest exam within 14 days.
6. Teachers and TAs get teaching rows.
7. No new notifications.


### 30.5 W4 · Exams (agreed 2026-11-17)
**References:**

| Template | Rating | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **Exam Cram Dashboard** | **4.76 / 447** | **Main reference (student side):** exam countdown, a study schedule with a calendar, a subject mastery tracker. **Dropped:** "score you need on the final" (call 3), the Pomodoro timer, decoration |
| Exam Planner | 4.76 / 330 | Study sessions mapped out until the exam |
| Course Schedule (Notion) | 4.80 / 345 | The midterm exam week row; exams as their own type |
| Class platforms (patterns only) | — | Release results together, second (moderated) marking, extra time |

**Today:**
- Assignments already carry most of an exam:
  - hand-in type (none, file, link, text)
  - late rule (`none`)
  - scheduled publishing (`publishAt`)
  - reviewers (`reviewers[]`)
  - AI policy and note
  - copy states (missing, excused)
  - Extend and Excuse
  - reminders
- **Missing:**
  - an Exam type
  - an exam window
  - a paper locked until it opens
  - room and seats
  - exam weeks
  - clash checks
  - second marking
  - held results
  - make-up exams
  - extra time

**Agreed changes from an exact copy:**
1. An exam is an **assignment of type Exam**, with its own tab in the one New module.
2. The countdown is W3's exam strip, plus an Exams row on the Term plan.
3. Subject mastery becomes **What's in it**: the units and outcomes covered (W2), each linking to its lessons. Personal revised ticks are left out.
4. The study schedule is left out; students plan revision as personal tasks in their Week.

**Formats:**

| Format | Hand-in | Window | Paper |
|---|---|---|---|
| **In person** (default) | None; staff enter marks | Date, time, length, room | Not on NetworkBase |
| **Timed online** | File or text | Opens → closes; late rule forced to Not accepted | Attached, locked until it opens |
| **Take-home** | File, link or text | Start and due | Visible from the start |

There's no personal per-student countdown timer: the window is the same for everyone except for extra time. **[call]**

```
NEW MODULE · tab "Exam"            (Basics → Exam details → Schedule → Subtasks and files)
 Exam details
  Format        (•) In person  ( ) Timed online  ( ) Take-home
  Covers        Unit 1 · Unit 2            Outcomes CO1 CO2 CO3   (from W2)
  Room          LH-2 · 204                 Seats  "by roll number"
  Out of        50 marks
  Marking       [✓] Second marker  Dr Iyer      [✓] Hold results until released
 Schedule
  Thu Feb 26 · 10:00 · 2 h          ⚠ 3 students also have MA 210 Midterm at 10:00

STUDENT · exam page
 Midterm · CS 301 · Thu Feb 26 · 10:00–12:00 · LH-2 204 · in 9 days
 What's in it   Unit 1 Arrays (6 lessons) · Unit 2 Trees (4 lessons) · CO1 CO2 CO3
 Paper          Opens Thu 10:00                     (timed online)
 Rules          No AI agents · Late work not accepted

REVIEW QUEUE · exam
 Marking 38 of 60 · Second marking 10 of 12 · 2 need agreement     [ Release results ]
```

**The 18 layers**
1. **Getting it:**
   - The Exam type is in every Education class's New module.
   - The institution's academic calendar sets **exam weeks**, shown on the Term plan with **+ Add exam**.
2. **Setting it up:**
   - **Class: Settings → Exams:**
     - default format
     - Hold results until released (on)
     - second marking and its default marker
     - **No classes during exam weeks** (on; sessions are skipped) **[call]**
   - **Institution:** exam weeks; second marking can be required (locked "Set by").
3. **Items:**
   - **Exam:** an assignment master with `type: exam`. Stored in the existing settings: format, window (opens, closes, length), room and seats note, covers (units, outcomes), out of, second marker, hold results.
   - **Copies:** one per student.
   - **Extra time:** per-student minutes on the class, seen only by staff and that student; it moves only that student's close. **[call]**
   - **Make-up for…:** from the roster, a new exam for chosen students with its own date. **[call]**
   - **Creating:** New module → Exam · + Add exam on an exam week · Duplicate · Start next term (draft) · institution template.
4. **Views:**
   - Assignments: Exam chip and filter.
   - Term plan: exam chip and shaded exam weeks.
   - Calendar.
   - The student exam page.
   - The review queue (marking, second marking, release).
   - **Institution: Exams view** (read only): every exam in the exam weeks by day, room and class, with clashes.
5. **Actions and flow:**
   - **Schedule** → students see date, room and What's in it; the paper stays locked.
   - **Clash check** on save: students with another exam in an overlapping window. It warns but doesn't block. **[call]**
   - **On the day:** a timed paper unlocks at opening; hand-in closes at closing + extra time.
   - **Absent:** Missing → Excuse → Make-up for…
   - **Marking:** first reviewer → **second marker** (all copies, or a 10% sample) → **Needs agreement** when the marks differ by more than 10% of the total, until one final mark is saved. **[call]**
   - **Results:** with Hold on, returned copies stay hidden from students until **Release results**, then all show at once with one notice.
6. **Surfaces:**
   - the Exam details section in the New module
   - the student exam page (header, What's in it, Paper, Rules)
   - the marking strip with Release results
   - the institution Exams view (day columns, clash rows "3 students")
7. **Design spec:**
   - Reuse the New module, assignment pages, the review queue (Lanes / One at a time), `StatusBadge` and roster actions.
   - Lucide icons: FileCheck2, Lock, Users2, Megaphone, AlertTriangle.
   - Add a contract test.
8. **Words:**
   - Exam · In person · Timed online · Take-home · Covers · What's in it · Paper · Opens · Out of · Second marker · Needs agreement · Hold results until released · Release results · Make-up for · Extra time · Exam weeks · Clash.
   - Never "grade" or "GPA".
9. **Links:**
   - W2: exam weeks, Covers, Assessments.
   - W3: exam strip.
   - W1: no classes in exam weeks.
   - W7: rubric and marks.
   - Review queue · roster · Files (the locked paper) · search.
10. **People:**

    | | Sees | Can do |
    |---|---|---|
    | Institution admin | Exams view, clashes, marking progress as counts | Exam weeks; require second marking. Never sees marks |
    | Head of department | The same, for their department | Read only |
    | Teacher | Everything | Create, schedule, mark, second marking, release |
    | TA | The exam, the paper after it opens, copies they review | Mark assigned copies; not release or change the window **[call]** |
    | Second marker (a Teacher, or an outside examiner as Viewer) | Assigned copies and the first mark | Enter the second mark |
    | Student | Their exam page; their result after release | Hand in (timed, take-home) |
11. **States:**
    - Before: "Paper opens Thu 10:00".
    - During: "Closes in 42 min".
    - After: "Closed".
    - Release runs as one step with progress.
12. **Edges:**
    - Extra time past the close: only that student can still hand in.
    - The 15-minute late allowance **doesn't apply to exams** unless the teacher sets it. **[call]**
    - Time changed after publishing: Tell students (ticked).
    - A deleted exam goes to Trash.
    - Start next term copies it as a draft on the matching exam week.
13. **Phone:**
    - The exam page fits one screen.
    - Hand-in works from the phone.
    - The institution Exams view becomes a list by day.
14. **Accessibility:**
    - The timer is announced every 10 minutes.
    - The locked paper is labelled with its time.
    - Extra time as text.
15. **Notifications:**
    - Exam scheduled: **Important**.
    - Day before: existing reminder.
    - Paper opened: **Normal**.
    - Time changed: **Important**.
    - Results released: **Important**, one per student.
    - Needs agreement: **Normal**, to both markers.
16. **Trust and data:**
    - Marks are seen only by the student and staff.
    - Extra time is private to staff and that student, and never shown to TAs who don't mark that student. **[call]**
    - The paper is locked on the server.
    - The institution sees counts only.
17. **Reuse vs new:**
    - **Reuse:** assignments, copies, `publishAt`, reviewers, late rules, Excuse, Extend, reminders, the review queue, the New module, W2 exam weeks.
    - **New:**
      - the exam type and settings
      - the locked paper
      - the close with extra time
      - the clash check (pure function)
      - second marking with Needs agreement
      - hold and release
      - Make-up for…
      - the institution Exams view
18. **How we know it works:**
    - **Signal:** the share of exams released within 14 days.
    - **Checks:**
      - the paper is never sent before opening
      - the close with extra time
      - clashes across classes
      - held results stay hidden until release
      - the institution never receives marks

**Organization steps:**
- **Level:**
  - Institution: exam weeks, required second marking, the Exams view, clashes, progress counts.
  - Class: exams, marking, release.
  - Student: the exam page and the W3 strip.
- **Term moment:** before term (exam weeks) → mid-term → exams (main use) → end of term (release) → next term (copied as drafts).
- **Org tab:** Assignments (Exam type) · Review queue · Sprints (exam weeks) · Overview (marking progress) · Settings (Exams) · institution Assignments → Exams view.

**Calls agreed 2026-11-17:**
1. Three formats, with no per-student countdown timer.
2. No classes during exam weeks, on by default.
3. Extra time is private to staff and that student, and moves only their close.
4. Make-up for… creates a new exam for chosen students.
5. Clash check warns, doesn't block.
6. Second marking: all or a 10% sample; Needs agreement above a 10% difference.
7. Hold results until released, on by default.
8. A TA marks assigned copies; can't release or change the window.
9. The 15-minute late allowance doesn't apply to exams unless set.


### 30.6 W5 · Thesis workspace (agreed 2026-11-17)
**References:**

| Template | Rating | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **PhDiaries Academia Dashboard** | **4.91 / 350** | **Main reference:** serif look, a home with to-dos, deadlines, project status and notes; a side menu (Thesis planning · Literature · Finances · Supervisions · Outputs · Data management); chapters with status, word target and words written; literature with authors, date, key issues and summary; outputs from Not started → In progress → Submitted → Peer review → Published |
| Thesis Planning (Notion) | 4.74 / 299 | A timeline from ideation → proposal → faculty mentor → research → chapter drafts (Done / Current / Upcoming / Overdue); sources linked to steps |

**Today:**
- `each_child` assignments (one copy per student workspace, reviewed in the org queue) are exactly thesis milestones.
- Org templates for new workspaces; inherited admins.
- Document sections and live blocks (28.5), meeting types with action items, the Tasks Timeline view, Files folders.
- **Missing:**
  - a Thesis template
  - automatic word counts
  - a literature list
  - a Supervision meeting type
  - outputs
  - a supervisor on each workspace
  - a coordinator overview

**Agreed changes from an exact copy:**
1. Words written are **counted from the chapter documents**.
2. **Milestones are the class's each-child assignments**; the timeline shows them as fixed markers.
3. Finances and funding applications are **parked** (like Money).
4. Journal, Academic CV and Professional development are dropped.
5. The mini calendar and day counter become the **Next milestone** line.
6. **No new tab**: everything blends into the workspace's Overview, Documents, Tasks, Files and Sprints.

**Levels:**
```
Institution  Northgate University
  └ Class org  "CSE Final-year projects 2027"   ← the coordinator (Teacher), supervisors (TAs)
       └ Workspace "Graph neural nets for traffic" (Thesis template)   ← one per student
```
A thesis course is a class whose workspaces use the Thesis template.

```
THESIS WORKSPACE · Overview
┌────────────────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────┐
│ Graph neural nets for traffic   (title)    │ Next milestone          │
│ Research questions                          │  Draft · due Mar 30     │
│  1. Can GNNs beat …   2. …                  │  in 23 days             │
│ ┌ Writing progress ─────── 18,400 / 40,000 ┐│ Supervisor              │
│ │ 1 Introduction     Completed  3,100/4,000 ││  Dr Iyer  ✉             │
│ │ 2 Literature rev.  Drafted    8,200/8,000 ││ Last supervision        │
│ │ 3 Method           In progress 7,100/10k  ││  Mar 2 · 2 action items │
│ │ 4 Results          Not started    0/12k   ││ Outputs                 │
│ └──────────────────────────────────────────┘│  IEEE ITS paper · Peer  │
│ Milestones ●Proposal ✓ ●Lit review ✓ ●Draft │  review                 │
└────────────────────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────┘

DOCUMENTS rail:  Chapters · Literature · Supervisions · Pages
CLASS (coordinator) · Projects tab
 Student      Title                    Supervisor  Milestone       Words      Last supervision
 A. Rao       Graph neural nets…       Dr Iyer     Draft · due 30  18.4k/40k  Mar 2
 K. Shah      Low-power sensors…       Dr Menon    Lit review ⚠    2.1k/40k   Jan 11 · 45 days ⚠
```

**The 18 layers**
1. **Getting it:**
   - The Thesis template is chosen when the class creates student workspaces (From an org template), or by a student where students may create workspaces.
   - The institution can offer it to every department.
   - **Student's first look:** title, "Add your research questions", an empty Writing progress, and the first milestone.
2. **Setting it up:**
   - **Class:**
     - thesis word target
     - default chapters (Introduction · Literature review · Method · Results · Discussion · Conclusion)
     - milestones (each-child assignments)
     - "Supervisor reviews milestones" (on)
     - "Flag when no supervision for … days" (30)
   - **Student:** rename, add or remove chapters and set targets. **[call]**
3. **Items:**
   - **Chapter:** a document in the Chapters section (settings: number, word target, status Not started → In progress → Drafted → Completed). Words are counted from the Markdown, leaving out code, comments and the reference list. **[call]**
   - **Source:** a row in the Literature record list (title, authors, year, link or DOI, key issues, summary, a PDF from Files), shown through a live block (B8). BibTeX paste-in and export are worked out in the browser; nothing is fetched from a DOI on the server (14.3).
   - **Supervision:** a meeting document of a new 13th meeting type, **Supervision** (agenda, notes, action items).
   - **Output:** a task labelled **Publication** or **Talk**; In review = submitted or in peer review; Completed = published. **[call]**
   - **Milestone:** the class's each-child copy.
   - **Supervisor:** a label on the existing admin role in the workspace, with an optional Co-supervisor. **[call]**
   - **Creating:** New document → Chapter · + Add source / Paste BibTeX · New document → Meeting → Supervision · New module → Task with the Publication label. Milestones come from the class.
4. **Views:**
   - **Workspace Overview:** title, research questions, Writing progress, milestones row; rail with Next milestone, Supervisor, Last supervision, Outputs.
   - **Documents:** Chapters, Literature, Supervisions sections.
   - **Literature:** table · by key issue · by year.
   - **Tasks Timeline:** with milestones as fixed markers.
   - **Class Projects:** the coordinator's table.
5. **Actions and flow:**
   - Writing updates the counts on save.
   - Hand in a milestone by attaching chapter documents ("submit with a doc" freezes a version).
   - The supervisor reviews in the class queue, which shows only their students (`reviewers` = the workspace's supervisor). **[call]**
   - Supervision action items become the student's tasks.
   - **Viva:** the last milestone, a Supervision-type meeting with outside examiners (Viewer); marks (W7) with a second marker (W4).
6. **Surfaces:**
   - **Writing progress block:** bars, totals, red above 110% of target.
   - **Milestones row:** ✓, now, Overdue.
   - **Literature table:** tag chips.
   - **Coordinator table:** "no supervision in 45 days" ⚠, "milestone overdue" ⚠, and Supervisor load in the rail.
7. **Design spec:**
   - Reuse Overview cards, documents rail sections, meeting templates, task labels, the Timeline view and the review queue.
   - Chapter titles in Instrument Serif.
   - Lucide icons: BookMarked, Library, MessagesSquare, Award, Flag.
   - Add a contract test.
8. **Words:**
   - Thesis · Research questions · Chapter · Word target · Words · Writing progress · Not started · In progress · Drafted · Completed · Literature · Source · Key issues · Supervision · Supervisor · Co-supervisor · Milestone · Outputs · Publication · Talk · Viva.
   - Supervisor is a label, never "Owner" or "Lead".
9. **Links:**
   - class assignments and review queue
   - W4 (viva second marker)
   - W7 (marks)
   - Files (PDFs; Data and Ethics folders in the template)
   - document versions
   - My work (milestones in W3)
   - search
   - **Publish to profile** after the final milestone (the case-study pattern), off by default **[call]**
10. **People:**

    | | Sees | Can do |
    |---|---|---|
    | Institution admin | Counts per department (on track, overdue, no supervision) | Offer the template; never reads thesis text |
    | Coordinator (class Teacher) | The Projects table and progress numbers; thesis text only if also the supervisor **[call]** | Milestones, flags, assign supervisors |
    | Supervisor | Their students' workspaces in full | Review milestones, comment, run supervisions |
    | Student | Their workspace | Everything in it |
    | Outside examiner (Viewer) | The final version and the viva meeting | Viva marks |
    | Visitor | Nothing (private by default) | — |
11. **States:**
    - Empty Writing progress offers "Add your chapters".
    - Counts update after each save.
    - The coordinator table loads progressively.
12. **Edges:**
    - Supervisor leaves → "No supervisor" ⚠ and reassignment; history kept.
    - Extend and Excuse on milestones.
    - "Move to next year's class" (move into org).
    - Co-written chapters count per document.
    - Literature over 500 rows is paged.
13. **Phone:** cards stack; literature becomes cards; writing is best on desktop.
14. **Accessibility:**
    - Bars with text ("8,200 of 8,000 words").
    - The milestones row as a list.
    - BibTeX errors reported per entry.
15. **Notifications:**
    - Milestone reminders (existing).
    - **No supervision in 30 days:** **Normal**, once, to the student and supervisor.
    - Action items and returned milestones use the existing notices.
16. **Trust and data:**
    - Thesis text is private to the student, supervisors and examiners.
    - The coordinator and institution see numbers only.
    - PDFs follow the Files terms.
    - Never public unless the student uses Publish to profile.
17. **Reuse vs new:**
    - **Reuse:** each-child assignments, org templates, documents and versions, meetings and action items, task labels, the Timeline view, the review queue, Files, Extend and Excuse, move into an org.
    - **New:**
      - the Thesis template
      - chapter settings and word count (pure function)
      - the Literature record list with BibTeX
      - the Supervision meeting type
      - the Supervisor label
      - supervisor-routed review
      - the coordinator table and flags
18. **How we know it works:**
    - **Signal:** the share of theses with a supervision every 30 days.
    - **Checks:**
      - word count rules
      - the coordinator can't read thesis text unless they're the supervisor (server test)
      - review routing
      - BibTeX round trip

**Organization steps:**
- **Level:**
  - Institution: offers the template and sees counts.
  - Class: milestones, supervisors, the Projects table.
  - Workspace: the thesis.
- **Term moment:** before term (topics, supervisors) → every week (writing, supervisions) → milestone dates → end of year (viva, final) → next year (unfinished theses move).
- **Org tab:** class Projects · Assignments (milestones) · Review queue (by supervisor) · Settings (thesis rules) · inside the workspace: Overview, Documents, Tasks, Files.

**Calls agreed 2026-11-17:**
1. Students edit chapters and targets.
2. Word count leaves out code, comments and references.
3. Outputs are Publication or Talk tasks.
4. Supervisor is a label on the admin role, with an optional co-supervisor.
5. Milestone reviews go to that workspace's supervisor.
6. The coordinator sees numbers, not text, unless also the supervisor.
7. Publish to profile is off by default.
8. Finances and funding are parked; Journal and CV are dropped.
9. The topic pool is parked (could reuse open seats and applications later).


### 30.7 W6 · Attendance (agreed 2026-11-17)
**Reference:** Student Attendance Tracker (Notion4Teachers, **4.79 / 53**; 3 desktop screens):
- a student list with class, attendance score with a % bar, and the date range
- a student page with **Status today** (one-click Present / Absent / Reset), the score, notes and records
- navigation: Students · Records · Notes · Set date

**Today:**
- **Members** in a class: the roster, filters, Behind and Outside people, the member drawer. It's staff-only.
- W1 sessions.
- Excuse on assignments.
- **Missing:** attendance records, %, a minimum, absence notes, a register export.

**Agreed changes from an exact copy:**
1. "Set date" is gone; attendance is taken for a **session** (W1).
2. Present / Absent / Reset becomes **Present · Late · Absent · Excused**.
3. Student notes go to the existing member drawer.
4. The video strip is dropped; one line of hint instead.
5. A student sees only their own %.

```
MEMBERS tab (class)          [ Roster ] [ Attendance ]
 Attendance · Spring 2027 · minimum 75% (Set by Northgate)          Export register
 ┌ Today · Tue Feb 17 · 10:30 · CS 301 · Balancing BSTs ────────── Take attendance ┐
 Student          Feb 3  Feb 5  Feb 10 Feb 12  Feb 17   Attendance
 A. Rao            ●      ●      ●      L       ·       100%  ████████
 K. Shah           ●      ✕      ✕      ●       ·        50%  ████░░░░  Below 75% ⚠
 M. Das            ●      E      ●      ●       ·       100%  ████████
 ● Present  L Late  ✕ Absent  E Excused  · not taken

TAKE ATTENDANCE (sheet, phone-first)
 Tue Feb 17 · 10:30 · 42 students            [ Mark all present ]
 A. Rao     (Present) Late  Absent  Excused
 K. Shah     Present  Late (Absent) Excused   "Notified: fever" 
 …                                           [ Save · 40 present, 1 late, 1 absent ]

STUDENT · class Overview rail
 Your attendance  86%  · minimum 75% · you can miss 3 more classes
```

**The 18 layers**
1. **Getting it:**
   - Every Education class has an **Attendance** view in Members.
   - It's on by default where the institution sets a minimum; otherwise the teacher turns it on. **[call]**
   - **Teacher's first look:** the empty grid, plus **Take attendance** on today's session (Overview's Next class, the Term plan).
2. **Setting it up:**
   - **Class: Settings → Attendance:**
     - on or off
     - Late counts as present (on) **[call]**
     - late after (10 min)
     - students can send an absence note (on)
     - **Check-in code** (off) **[call]**
   - **Institution:** a minimum % (e.g. 75%), locked as "Set by"; whether check-in codes are allowed.
3. **Items:**
   - **Attendance record:** session × student → Present / Late / Absent / Excused, with an optional note, who marked it and when. A new small table; the session is stored on first use (W1 call 2).
   - **Absence note:** a student's line, text only (no file upload, because medical papers are sensitive). **[call]**
   - **Creating:** Take attendance · Check-in code (students tap **I'm here**) · edit a grid cell · CSV import.
4. **Views:**
   - **Grid** (student × session): sortable by %, with Below minimum and section (W8) filters.
   - **Take attendance sheet.**
   - The **student's own line** in the class Overview rail and in their member card.
5. **Actions and flow:**
   - **Take attendance** opens the sheet unmarked → **Mark all present** → change the exceptions → **Save**. **[call]**
   - **Check-in code:** 4 digits valid for **10 minutes**; entering it marks Present (or Late after the late time); the teacher reviews before saving.
   - Absence notes show as "Notified: …"; the teacher decides on Excused.
   - **Changing a record:** staff can change one within **7 days**; after that only a Teacher can, and the change is logged. **[call]**
   - **Export register:** a CSV for the term.
6. **Surfaces:**
   - **The grid:** sticky names, compact session columns, % bar, Below 75% ⚠.
   - **The sheet:** four large segmented buttons per student, a live count, absence notes inline.
   - **The student's line:** %, the minimum, and "you can miss N more classes" (from the sessions left). **[call]**
7. **Design spec:**
   - Reuse the Members frame, roster filters, member drawer, `StatusBadge` and the progress bar.
   - Mono letters in cells, with the state as text.
   - Lucide icons: CheckCircle2, Clock, XCircle, ShieldCheck, KeyRound.
   - Add a contract test.
8. **Words:** Attendance · Take attendance · Mark all present · Present · Late · Absent · Excused · Not taken · Check-in code · I'm here · Absence note · Notified · Minimum · Below minimum · You can miss N more classes · Export register.
9. **Links:**
   - W1 (sessions; cancelled sessions aren't counted)
   - W2 (from the lesson)
   - W3 (the absence note from Week)
   - W4 (no sessions in exam weeks)
   - W8 (sections)
   - the member drawer
   - Settings locks
   - the account export
10. **People:**

    | | Sees | Can do |
    |---|---|---|
    | Institution admin | Counts per class (average %, number below minimum), no names **[call]** | Set the minimum; allow check-in codes |
    | Head of department | The same, for their department | Read only |
    | Teacher | Everything | Take, edit, export, settings |
    | TA | Everything (their section once W8 exists) | Take attendance; edit within 7 days |
    | Student | Their own records and % | Absence note; I'm here |
    | Visitor | Nothing | — |
11. **States:**
    - Not taken shows "·".
    - Two devices: the last save per student wins, with "Updated by …".
    - On a poor connection the sheet keeps the marks and retries.
12. **Edges:**
    - Mid-term joiners are counted from their join date.
    - Leavers' records stay with the class.
    - Moved sessions keep their records.
    - A cancelled session with records asks "Keep or clear these records?"
    - Excused counts as neither present nor absent.
    - No sessions held yet shows "—".
13. **Phone:** the sheet is built for phones first (large targets, sticky Save); the grid scrolls sideways with names pinned.
14. **Accessibility:**
    - States as words as well as colour.
    - A radio group per student.
    - A real table with a summary row.
15. **Notifications:**
    - Dropping below the minimum: **Important** to the student, once per crossing; **Summary** to the teacher.
    - Absence note: **Normal** to the teacher.
    - Nothing per session to students. **[call]**
16. **Trust and data:**
    - Attendance is personal data: staff and the student only; included in the account export and removed with the account.
    - Absence notes are private.
    - Codes expire after 10 minutes, one count per account.
    - The institution sees counts only.
17. **Reuse vs new:**
    - **Reuse:** the Members tab, roster filters, member drawer, W1 sessions, settings locks, CSV import patterns, the account export.
    - **New:**
      - the attendance record table
      - the % rule (pure function)
      - the Take attendance sheet
      - the check-in code
      - absence notes
      - the register export
      - institution counts
18. **How we know it works:**
    - **Signal:** the share of held sessions with attendance taken.
    - **Checks:**
      - % rules (excused, late, joiners, cancelled)
      - the 7-day rule
      - code expiry and one count per account
      - no student receives another's records (server test)
      - the institution receives no names

**Organization steps:**
- **Level:** Institution: minimum and counts. Class: records, grid, register. Student: their own %.
- **Term moment:** week 1 (on) → every session → mid-term (below-minimum warnings) → exams (no sessions) → end of term (export, archive).
- **Org tab:** Members (Attendance) · Overview (Take attendance; the student's line) · Sprints (from the lesson) · Settings (Attendance).

**Calls agreed 2026-11-17:**
1. On by default where the institution sets a minimum.
2. Late counts as present.
3. Check-in code is optional and off by default.
4. Absence notes are text only.
5. The sheet opens unmarked with Mark all present.
6. 7-day edit window, then Teacher-only and logged.
7. "You can miss N more classes" for students.
8. The institution sees counts only.
9. Only crossing the minimum notifies the student.
10. Excused counts as neither present nor absent.


### 30.8 W7 · Marks and rubric (agreed 2026-11-17)
**References:**

| Template / pattern | Rating | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **Student Grade Tracker** (Notion4Teachers) | **4.83 / 12** | **Main reference:** a Grades list (name, topic, student, date completed, score, total, % ring), views All / By topic, quick-add buttons. A Topics list with weights adding to 100%. **Dropped:** weights (a weighted total is a grade book, call 3) |
| Class platforms (patterns only) | — | A rubric grid (criteria × levels with points), click to score, a comment bank, marks hidden until released |

**Today:**
- The review queue: Lanes / One at a time, file viewer with versions, steps, discussion.
- **Approve** (optionally with a note).
- **Return** with a reason and Fix by, plus recent reasons.
- Keyboard keys, private feedback, team copies.
- **Missing:** marks, rubrics, a comment bank, marks the student can see, a marks export.

**Agreed changes from an exact copy:**
1. Marks live on each assignment ("Out of 50"). **No topic weights, no totals across assignments, no averages, no letter grades** (call 3).
2. "By student" becomes a staff-only **Marks** list in the member drawer, with no total row.
3. Score and % ring become "38 / 50 · 76%".
4. Quick-add buttons become marking inside the review queue.

```
NEW MODULE · Assignment (or Exam) → Marking
  Marking      ( ) Not marked   (•) Out of [50]   ( ) Rubric  [Lab rubric v2 ▾]  Edit

RUBRIC (class or institution library)
 Criterion        Excellent 10   Good 7   Fair 4   Missing 0
 Correctness      All cases …    Most …   Some …   —
 Code quality     …              …        …        —
 Report           …              …        …        —            Out of 30

REVIEW QUEUE · One at a time
┌ work (files, versions) ───────────────────┬ Marking ───────────────────────┐
│                                           │ Correctness  [10] 7  4  0   1–4│
│                                           │ Code quality  10 [7] 4  0      │
│                                           │ Report        10  7 [4] 0      │
│                                           │ ✎ "Explain the edge case…"     │
│                                           │ Total 21 / 30 · 70%            │
│                                           │ Comment bank: Good tests · Cite │
│                                           │ [ Return ]   [ Approve · 21 ▾ ] │
└───────────────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────┘

STUDENT · copy page (after Approve, or after Release when held)
 Lab 3 · 21 / 30 · 70% · Approved by Dr Rao
 Correctness Excellent · Code quality Good · Report Fair  "Explain the edge case…"
 Ask about this mark →
```

**The 18 layers**
1. **Getting it:**
   - Every Education class has **Marking** in the New module's Assignment and Exam sections.
   - The institution can share rubrics (copied, or locked as "Set by").
   - "Not marked" is the default for Homework and Practice; "Out of" for Lab, Exam and Project. **[call]**
2. **Setting it up:**
   - **Class: Settings → Marking:**
     - rubric library (new, duplicate, archive)
     - comment bank (seeded from recent reasons)
     - "Show marks when approved" (on) vs. Hold until released (on by default only for exams)
   - **Institution:** shared rubrics; whether marks may be exported.
3. **Items:**
   - **Marking setting** on the assignment master: none · out of N · rubric id.
   - **Rubric:** criteria and levels (points, descriptions) on the class or institution, **frozen onto the assignment when published**. **[call]**
   - **Mark** on each copy: total, per-criterion level, criterion comments, marker and time, plus W4's second mark. A new small table.
   - **Comment:** a saved line, for each teacher and shared across the class.
   - **Team copies:** one mark for every member, with an optional **Adjust for one person** (with a reason). **[call]**
   - **Peer review:** each student reviews 2 copies with the same rubric, names hidden both ways; feedback, not marks. **[call]**
4. **Views:**
   - the Marking panel in One at a time
   - Lanes: a Marked / Not marked chip and the total
   - the assignment roster: a **Marks column** and Export marks
   - the member drawer (staff): a **Marks** list with no total
   - the student copy page: result, levels, comments
5. **Actions and flow:**
   - Click a level per criterion (keys 1–4) or type a number → comments from the bank → **Approve** saves the mark.
   - **Return** keeps marks as a **hidden draft**; the teacher re-marks after the resubmission. **[call]**
   - **Held results** show at Release (W4).
   - **Ask about this mark** uses the private feedback thread; no formal regrade process. **[call]**
   - **Late:** the chip shows; no automatic deduction. **[call]**
6. **Surfaces:**
   - **Rubric editor:** drag to reorder, points total, "Used by 3 assignments".
   - **Marking panel:** sticky, live total, comment chips, "Marked 24 of 60".
   - **Marks column:** the number, "—", Returned or Excused.
   - **Export:** CSV per assignment or all assignments, with no totals column.
7. **Design spec:**
   - Reuse `ReviewDecision`, One at a time, roster columns, the member drawer, the New module and `StatusBadge`.
   - Levels as segmented buttons.
   - Lucide icons: ClipboardCheck, Table2, MessageSquareQuote, Download.
   - Add a contract test.
8. **Words:**
   - Marking · Not marked · Out of · Rubric · Criterion · Level · Points · Total · Comment bank · Marked 24 of 60 · Adjust for one person · Ask about this mark · Export marks · Peer review.
   - Never "grade", "GPA", "gradebook" or "score average".
9. **Links:**
   - W4 (second marking, held results)
   - W5 (milestones, viva)
   - W8 (TAs mark their section)
   - the review queue, roster, member drawer, private feedback
   - Files
   - the account export
   - CLI and agents read their own marks; **AI agents never set or change marks**. **[call]**
10. **People:**

    | | Sees | Can do |
    |---|---|---|
    | Institution admin | Counts (marked vs. not marked per class) | Shared rubrics, export permission; never sees marks |
    | Head of department | The same | Read only |
    | Teacher | All marks | Mark, edit rubrics, export, adjust |
    | TA | Marks of copies they review | Mark; not edit shared rubrics or export the whole class **[call]** |
    | Student | Their own marks and feedback | Ask about this mark; peer review |
    | Visitor | Nothing | — |
11. **States:**
    - Draft marks are saved as you click.
    - "Being marked by …" makes a copy read-only for the second person.
    - The live total updates as levels are picked.
12. **Edges:**
    - Rubric edits don't change old marks ("Rubric changed" note).
    - Each mark keeps its own out-of.
    - Excused copies have no mark.
    - Resubmissions are marked again, with history kept.
    - Marks go to Trash with their assignment.
    - Start next term copies rubrics, not marks.
13. **Phone:** the marking panel goes under the work with big buttons; the student result is one card.
14. **Accessibility:**
    - A radio group per criterion.
    - Keys 1–4.
    - The total is announced as it changes.
15. **Notifications:**
    - Mark visible (Approve or Release): **Important**, one per copy, "Lab 3 was marked", **without the mark**. **[call]**
    - Ask about this mark: the existing private feedback notice.
16. **Trust and data:**
    - Marks are seen only by the student and the staff who review them; the institution sees counts.
    - The export is logged.
    - Peer review hides names both ways.
    - Agents can't write marks.
    - Marks are in the student's account export.
17. **Reuse vs new:**
    - **Reuse:** the review queue, `ReviewDecision`, recent reasons, private feedback, roster, member drawer, the New module, team copies, W4 hold and release.
    - **New:**
      - the rubric record and editor
      - the marks table
      - the marking panel
      - the comment bank
      - the Marks column and export
      - the member Marks list
      - peer review
18. **How we know it works:**
    - **Signal:** the median time from hand-in to a mark the student can see.
    - **Checks:**
      - returned drafts are never visible
      - held marks stay hidden until release
      - rubrics freeze on publish
      - team marks plus adjustments
      - peer review hides names
      - agents are refused when writing marks (server test)
      - the institution receives no marks

**Organization steps:**
- **Level:** Institution: shared rubrics and counts. Class: rubrics, marking, export. Student: their own marks.
- **Term moment:** before term (rubrics) → every week (marking) → exams (W4) → end of term (export) → next term (rubrics copied).
- **Org tab:** Review queue (Marking panel) · Assignments (Marking setting, Marks column) · Members (drawer Marks) · Settings (Marking).

**Calls agreed 2026-11-17:**
1. Marking defaults by assignment template.
2. Rubrics freeze when published.
3. A team mark goes to every member, with Adjust for one person.
4. Peer review is feedback, not marks, with names hidden.
5. Return keeps a hidden draft.
6. Ask about this mark, with no formal regrade process.
7. No automatic late deduction.
8. AI agents never set or change marks.
9. A TA marks their own copies only.
10. The marked notice doesn't include the mark.


### 30.9 W8 · Sections and TAs (agreed 2026-11-17)
**Reference:** University TA Section template (**5.0 / 5**, built by a computer science TA):
- a section home with the current section (term, code, Tue + Thu 10:30–11:20, room) and the TA's office hours
- a welcome note
- general information, recordings, important links, and section news

**Today:**
- Class roles Teacher / TA / Student.
- Team assignments (Team A / B / C); units with seats inside child workspaces.
- Announcements with an audience (role or workspace).
- Reviewers on each assignment.
- **Missing:** a group of students inside the class with its own TA, times and room.

**Agreed changes from an exact copy:**
1. The section home becomes a **Your section** card on the class About and Overview.
2. Section news becomes class announcements with the audience "Section B".
3. Recordings and links become section materials (files and documents tagged with the section).
4. Motivational videos are dropped.

The default word is **Section** (renameable to Batch, Lab group or Tutorial), always kept separate from **Team**. **[call]**

```
MEMBERS tab (class)      [ Roster ] [ Sections ] [ Attendance ]
 Sections · 3 · 120 students                          + New section   Split students…
┌ Section A · Lab ─────────────┬ Section B · Lab ─────────────┬ Section C · Lab ──────────┐
│ Wed 14:00–16:00 · Lab 3      │ Thu 14:00–16:00 · Lab 3      │ Fri 09:00–11:00 · Lab 2   │
│ TA Priya · 40 students       │ TA Arjun · 41 students       │ TA Meera · 39 students    │
│ To review 12 · Attendance 91%│ To review 3 · 88%            │ To review 20 ⚠ · 79%      │
└──────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┘
 Review load   Priya 12 · Arjun 3 · Meera 20 ⚠                         [ Rebalance… ]

STUDENT · class About / Overview
 Your section   B · Lab · Thu 14:00–16:00 · Lab 3
                TA Arjun ✉ · office hours Mon 12–1
```

**The 18 layers**
1. **Getting it:**
   - A **Sections** view in Members for every Education class; classes without sections work as today.
   - **Teacher's first look:** an explainer plus **+ New section** and **Split students…**
   - **Student:** a Your section card once placed.
2. **Setting it up (Class: Settings → Sections):**
   - the word
   - **TAs work only with their section** (on: their reviews and attendance; they still see every name) **[call]**
   - **Students pick their own section** with a seat limit (off) **[call]**
3. **Items:**
   - **Section:** a small record on the class: name, kind (Lab, Tutorial, Lecture group), TAs, students, meets (the W1 pattern), room, office hours. A new small table with membership.
   - **One section per student per kind.** **[call]**
   - **Creating:**
     - + New section
     - **Split students…** (evenly, randomly, by roll number range or surname range, with a preview)
     - CSV with a section column
     - student self-pick
     - institution template
     - Start next term (sections without students)
4. **Views:**
   - **Sections cards:** time, TA, number of students, To review, Attendance %, and a Review load line.
   - **Roster:** a section filter and column.
   - **Attendance:** a section filter and section sessions.
   - **Review queue:** Mine follows section routing.
   - The student's card.
5. **Actions and flow:**
   - A new assignment target, **Sections**. **[call]**
   - **Review routing:** a copy's reviewers = its student's section TAs, unless the assignment names reviewers. **[call]**
   - **Rebalance…** moves copies not yet reviewed between TAs, with a preview.
   - **Section sessions** come from the section's meets.
   - **Lab lessons** (W2) are for all sections (each on its own session) or for one. **[call]**
   - **Moving a student:** unmarked copies follow the new TA; marked ones stay. **[call]**
   - **Announcements:** the audience picker gains sections.
6. **Surfaces:**
   - **Section card:** Open, Edit, ⋯ (Move students, Remove).
   - **Split dialog:** method, preview table, Apply.
   - **Review load:** ⚠ above **1.5× the average**. **[call]**
   - **Your section card:** section, times, room, TA with Message, office hours.
7. **Design spec:**
   - Reuse `RailSection` cards, roster filters, the audience picker, assignment target fields, Mine, and the W1 meets fields.
   - Lucide icons: Users, UserCog, Shuffle, Scale.
   - Add a contract test.
8. **Words:**
   - Section (or the class's word) · Your section · Split students · Rebalance · Review load · Students pick their own section · Seats left · TA.
   - Never "Team" for a section or "Lead" for a TA.
9. **Links:**
   - W1 (section meets; Next class)
   - W2 (lessons for all sections or one)
   - W3 (section sessions in Week)
   - W4 (exam rooms by section)
   - W6 (attendance by section)
   - W7 (marking by section TA)
   - announcements, assignment targets, the review queue, the roster
10. **People:**

    | | Sees | Can do |
    |---|---|---|
    | Institution admin | Counts (number of sections, students per section) | Template sections |
    | Teacher | Everything | Make, split, rebalance, assign TAs |
    | TA | Every name; their section's work, attendance and reviews (setting on) | Work within their section; post to it |
    | Student | Their own section, its TA, and section classmates' names only | Pick a section if turned on |
    | Visitor | Nothing | — |
11. **States:**
    - No sections: the explainer.
    - The split preview before any change.
    - Live counts.
12. **Edges:**
    - "Not in a section · 4" with a prompt.
    - TA leaves: "No TA" ⚠ and reviews fall back to the Teacher.
    - Deleting a section with students asks "Move them to…".
    - Seat limits stop picks at 0.
    - Section session clashes give a warning.
    - Start next term copies sections without students.
13. **Phone:** cards stack; the split dialog is one column; the student's card sits at the top of Overview.
14. **Accessibility:**
    - Cards are a list with counts in their labels.
    - Moving a student has a menu.
    - The preview is a table.
15. **Notifications:**
    - Placed in or moved to a section: **Normal**.
    - Made a section TA: **Normal**.
    - Review load over the limit: **Summary** to the Teacher.
    - Section announcements use the existing levels.
16. **Trust and data:**
    - Students see only their own section's names.
    - Section-only TA access is enforced on the server for marks and attendance.
    - Section membership is in the account export.
17. **Reuse vs new:**
    - **Reuse:** roles, roster, the audience model, assignment targets, reviewers and Mine, W1 meets, W6, W7, the open-seats idea.
    - **New:**
      - the section table and membership
      - the Sections view
      - Split students (pure function)
      - the Sections target
      - section review routing
      - Rebalance
      - the section audience
      - the Your section card
18. **How we know it works:**
    - **Signal:** the share of copies reviewed by their section's TA within 7 days.
    - **Checks:**
      - routing on moves
      - section-only TA access (server test)
      - split rules
      - seat limits
      - the section audience

**Organization steps:**
- **Level:** Institution: section templates and counts. Class: sections, TAs, routing. Student: their section card.
- **Term moment:** before term (make, assign TAs) → week 1 (split or pick) → every week (section sessions, routed reviews) → mid-term (rebalance) → exams (rooms by section) → next term (copied, empty).
- **Org tab:** Members (Sections, roster column) · Review queue (routing, Rebalance) · Assignments (Sections target) · Updates (section audience) · About and Overview (Your section) · Settings (Sections).

**Calls agreed 2026-11-17:**
1. The word is Section (renameable), never Team.
2. TAs work only with their section by default, and still see every name.
3. Student self-pick is off by default, with a seat limit.
4. One section per student per kind.
5. A Sections assignment target.
6. Reviews go to the student's section TA unless named.
7. A moved student's unmarked copies follow the new TA.
8. Lab lessons for all sections or one.
9. Review load warning above 1.5× the average.

| W1 | Class home | Classroom Home 4.90 / 52 | About · Overview · Settings | Class (institution template) |
| W2 | Term plan + lessons | Course Schedule 4.80 / 345 | Sprints (Term plan view) | Class (institution calendar) |
| W3 | Student's week | Best Student Planner 4.83 / 2,701 | My work drawer (Week view) | Across classes |

**New stored things across W1–W8:**

**New shared rules (pure functions):**

**Words added:** Class details · Next class · Term plan · Lesson · Taught · Outcomes · Week · Pin for today · Exam · Release results · Supervisor · Chapter · Attendance · Rubric · Marks · Section.

**Never:** grade, GPA, gradebook, Lead, Owner.

**Build order inside this category:**
1. **W1 + W2:** class details and sessions underpin everything.
2. **W8:** sections change routing and sessions.
3. **W6, W7, W4:** each needs sessions and sections.
4. **W3:** gathers the rest.
5. **W5.**

All of it waits for the three-level structure (29.2) and the 28.9 Wave 0 foundation.

## 31. Organization category: Coaching / Bootcamp (complete 2026-11-17)

This section uses the same combined method as section 30. It's for coding and design bootcamps, cohort courses, test-prep academies (IELTS, GRE, CAT, certifications), online academies with self-paced paths, and mentorship programs.

**Flag:** JEE and NEET coaching students are mostly under 18. Call 2 in 29.6 keeps them out until the School round's safety design.
