### 31.2 C1 · Cohorts and programs (agreed 2026-11-17)
**References:**

| Template | Rating | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **Course Tracker** (desbyseb) | **4.84 / 164** | The program plan: a calm board with Overview · Status · Timeline · Archive |
| **Course Creation Hub** | **4.89 / 75** | The cohort home (learner side): Home · Lessons · Assignments · Schedule · Library · FAQs · Office hours; a welcome video |
| Mentorship Cohort HQ | 5.0 / 4 | Cohorts with start, end, status and theme; a 5-step launch checklist |
| Course & Program Builder | 4.92 / 53 | A program as 7+ modules (decoration dropped) |

**Today:**
- `duplicateOrg`: a new title and start date, every date shifted, a choice of what to copy (about, docs, files, sprints, assignments, channels, admins).
- Join with a code, approval, Max members.
- Verified contribution entries.
- The type profile ("a type sets words and starting values, never power").
- W1–W8 and the institution level (29.2).
- **Missing:**
  - programs
  - a program and cohort list
  - cohort words
  - completion
  - moving a learner to a later cohort

**Agreed changes from an exact copy:**
1. A **program** is a saved class template in the institution's template library (29.5). A **cohort** is a class org started from it.
2. **Start a cohort** is the existing duplicate, run from the program with a start date.
3. The cohort home reuses W1. Lessons and Schedule → Sprints Term plan · Assignments → Tasks · Library → Files · **FAQs → a pinned FAQs document** · Office hours → Class details.
4. The welcome video is a **link card** on About (no autoplay; NetworkBase never hosts video).
5. The launch checklist becomes the existing Get started card.

```
Institution   Lantern Academy               (kind: Coaching / Bootcamp)
  ├ Program   Full-stack Web · 12 weeks      (a saved class template)
  └ Class org Full-stack Web · Cohort 12 · Jan 13 – Apr 4     ← a run of the program
       └ Workspaces: each learner's capstone and projects
```
Without an institution, a cohort uses **Start next cohort** on itself (the same duplicate).

```
INSTITUTION · Projects tab        [ Programs ] [ Cohorts ] [ Timeline ]
 Program                 Weeks  Status   Cohorts  Next start   Seats
 Full-stack Web          12     Active   12       Apr 21       18 / 30
 Data Analytics          10     Active    7       May 5         4 / 25
 UX Design (2025)        8      Retired   5       —            —

 Timeline (one bar per cohort, by program)
 Full-stack  ███ C11 ███  ███████ C12 ███████   ░░░░ C13 (upcoming) ░░░░
 Data        ██████ C7 ██████            ░░░░ C8 ░░░░

PROGRAM page
 Full-stack Web · 12 weeks · 4 modules · outcomes CO1–CO5 · from Cohort 12
 Modules  1 HTML & CSS (2 wk) · 2 JavaScript (3 wk) · 3 React (4 wk) · 4 Capstone (3 wk)
 [ Start a cohort ]   Update from a cohort…   Retire

START A COHORT (dialog)
 Name   Full-stack Web · Cohort 13      Starts  Apr 21  → ends Jul 11 (12 weeks)
 Seats  30        Join  (•) Approval  ( ) Code only
 Copy   ✓ Plan and lessons  ✓ Assignments (as drafts)  ✓ Rubrics  ✓ Documents  ✓ Materials
        ✓ Sections (empty)  ☐ Staff     Staff  Instructor Asha · Mentors Ravi, Lin
```

**The 18 layers**
1. **Getting it:**
   - The institution kind **Coaching / Bootcamp** sets its starting values. **[call]**
   - **Admin's first look:** "Make your first program from a cohort you've run, or start one from scratch."
   - **Learner's first look:** the cohort About with the welcome video card and FAQs.
2. **Setting it up:**
   - **Kind starting values** (renameable):
     - roles **Instructor · Mentor · Learner** **[call]**
     - **Module / Week**
     - attendance off, no exam weeks
     - join by approval with Seats
   - **Program settings:** name, length in weeks, modules and outcomes (from its source cohort), default seats, what new cohorts copy, the completion rule.
3. **Items:**
   - **Program:** a template library entry with a **frozen snapshot** of a class plan (modules and weeks, lessons, assignment drafts, rubrics, documents, materials, empty sections, settings), its length, status (Draft · Active · Retired) and source cohort.
   - **Cohort:** a class org with a program link (one field).
   - **Completion:** Completed / Not completed on each learner at the end.
   - **Creating:** Save as program · New program · Start a cohort · Start next cohort.
4. **Views:**
   - **Institution Projects:**
     - **Programs**
     - **Cohorts** (by program; Upcoming · Running · Finished; seats)
     - **Timeline** (the 11.3 S14 Portfolio timeline, one bar per cohort) **[call]**
   - **Program page.**
   - **Cohort:** a class as in W1–W8.
5. **Actions and flow:**
   - **Start a cohort:** name, start (the end is worked out), seats, join method, what to copy, staff → `duplicateOrg` with shifted dates.
   - **Update from a cohort…:** replaces the snapshot after a list of what changed. **Running cohorts never change on their own.** **[call]**
   - **Completion** at the end date: all required assignments Approved **and** attendance at or above the minimum (if on); an instructor override with a reason. **[call]**
   - **Completed** → a verified profile entry ("Completed Full-stack Web · Cohort 12 · Verified by Lantern Academy"). No PDF certificates. **[call]**
   - **Move to a later cohort:** finished work stays in the old cohort; open copies there are Excused. **[call]**
   - **Retire:** no new cohorts; old ones stay.
6. **Surfaces:**
   - the Programs table
   - the Start a cohort dialog (the New module shell: Basics → Copy → Staff → Seats)
   - the cohort timeline
   - a Completed chip on the member card and roster
   - "Completion 24 of 28" on the cohort Overview after it ends
7. **Design spec:**
   - Reuse the projects list, the Portfolio timeline, the New module shell, the duplicate dialog's checkboxes, `StatusBadge` and the profile contribution entry.
   - Lucide icons: Layers, Users, PlayCircle, BadgeCheck.
   - Add a contract test.
8. **Words:**
   - Program · Cohort · Start a cohort · Start next cohort · Update from a cohort · Retire · Seats · Upcoming · Running · Finished · Module · Instructor · Mentor · Learner · Completed · Not completed · Move to a later cohort.
   - Never "Lead" or "Owner".
9. **Links:**
   - W1 (cohort home, video card, FAQs)
   - W2 (plan copied and re-dated)
   - W6 (completion rule)
   - W7 (required assignments, rubrics)
   - W8 (batches)
   - C2, C4, C5
   - profile entries, join and seats, search
10. **People:**

    | | Sees | Can do |
    |---|---|---|
    | Institution admin | Programs, cohorts, seats, completion counts | Make and retire programs, start cohorts, Update from a cohort |
    | Program lead (an admin scoped like a Head of department) | Their programs and cohorts | The same, for theirs |
    | Instructor (Teacher) | Their cohort | Everything in the class; **Save as program** needs admin approval when there's an institution **[call]** |
    | Mentor (TA) | Their cohort | As TA |
    | Learner | Their cohort and completion | Join; request to move to a later cohort |
    | Visitor | The program's public About and upcoming cohorts with seats left | Request to join |
11. **States:**
    - Start a cohort runs in the background ("Setting up Cohort 13…" → "Ready").
    - Live seat counts.
12. **Edges:**
    - A program keeps its snapshot if its source cohort is deleted.
    - Parallel cohorts are normal.
    - A full cohort offers the next one.
    - A learner may be in cohorts of different programs at once.
    - Changing the length re-dates only future cohorts.
    - Start a cohort **never copies learners, marks or attendance**.
13. **Phone:** programs become cards; the timeline scrolls sideways; the dialog is one column.
14. **Accessibility:**
    - A table alternative to the timeline.
    - Completion as a word.
    - A labelled checkbox group for copy options.
15. **Notifications:**
    - Cohort ready: **Normal**, to staff.
    - Cohort starts: the existing sprint-start notice.
    - Completed: **Important**, to the learner.
    - Moved to a later cohort: **Important**.
    - Seats full: **Summary** to admins.
16. **Trust and data:**
    - Programs hold no learner data.
    - Completion is seen by the learner and staff; the institution sees counts.
    - The profile entry shows only with "Show on my profile".
17. **Reuse vs new:**
    - **Reuse:** `duplicateOrg`, the template library, type profile words, join and seats, the Portfolio timeline, contribution entries, W1–W8.
    - **New:**
      - the institution kind and its values
      - the Program record
      - the cohort ↔ program link
      - the Programs and Cohorts views
      - Update from a cohort
      - the completion rule
      - Move to a later cohort
18. **How we know it works:**
    - **Signal:** the share of cohorts started from a program after the first three.
    - **Checks:**
      - date shifting
      - no learner data copied (server test)
      - running cohorts don't change on update
      - completion rule cases
      - deferral excuses open copies

**Organization steps:**
- **Level:** Institution: programs, cohort list and timeline, seats, completion counts. Class: the cohort. Learner: completion and profile entry.
- **Term moment:** no fixed term. Before a cohort → running (W1–W8) → cohort end (completion) → next cohort.
- **Org tab:** institution Projects (Programs, Cohorts, Timeline) · Settings (template library, kind values) · cohort About (video, FAQs) · Members (Completed chip).

**Calls agreed 2026-11-17:**
1. The kind Coaching / Bootcamp sets starting values only.
2. Instructor · Mentor · Learner with Module / Week, all renameable.
3. A program is a frozen snapshot in the template library.
4. Update from a cohort after a list of changes; running cohorts never change on their own.
5. Completion: required assignments Approved + attendance at or above the minimum, with an override.
6. Completion becomes a verified profile entry, with no PDF.
7. Move to a later cohort keeps finished work and excuses open copies.
8. The cohort timeline reuses the Portfolio timeline.
9. An instructor's Save as program needs admin approval.

### 31.3 C2 · Learning path (agreed 2026-11-17)
**References** (a second scan of 14 searches found 114 templates, 50 of them rated; 7 studied from their screenshots):

| Template | Rating | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **Python Roadmap** | **4.89 / 151** | **Main reference for the learner:** "Your Progress" with Beginner · Intermediate · Advanced levels, each with a % and its chapters, above a Course Index |
| **Data Engineering Roadmap** | **4.90 / 195** | Numbered phases (#0 Exploration → #1 Foundations → #2 Core → #3 Get hired), each listing its skills and projects; Phases and Table views |
| **AI/ML Learning Roadmap** | 4.89 / 61 | A "Track your progress" table: Phase · Status · **Timeline (Weeks 1–4, 5–12 …)** · Notes |
| **Online Course Tracker** | 4.86 / 36 | Learning-path cards with a % ring; **In progress · Next up · Later**; a courses board grouped by path with status and %; quick actions |
| personal curriculum | 4.87 / 389 | A weekly check-in list above course cards. **Dropped:** it's a personal plan, which belongs in a Learning workspace (15), not a class |
| Course Creation Hub | 4.89 / 75 | Home · Lessons · Assignments · Library · FAQs (W1 already has these) |
| Master the Topic: Online Course Site | 4.94 / 32 | A public course page: description, **Enroll now**, and FAQs (format, prerequisites, how long, certificate, support, access after finishing) |

**Today:**
- Sprints nest (units → weeks) and carry materials, but **every sprint needs a start and end date** and runs Planning → Active → Completed.
- W2 adds lessons (`class_lesson`); 15.2 planned Draft → Published and **Mark done** for self-paced lessons.
- "Everyone" assignments make one copy per learner when published. **Late joiners** get copies of open assignments that aren't past due (`createCopiesForNewMember`). Every copy has a **fixed due date**.
- The My work drawer lists copies across classes; Required reading has read counts; C1 has the completion rule and the verified profile entry.
- **Missing:**
  - a structure without dates
  - a learner's own "done" on a lesson
  - order and unlocking
  - due dates counted from each learner's start
  - each learner's %, pace and drop-off

**Agreed changes from an exact copy:**
1. The path belongs to the **class**; learners don't build their own (a personal curriculum is a Learning workspace).
2. Levels and phases become **Phase → Module → Step**: the two sprint levels, plus lessons and assignments inside a module.
3. "Weeks 1–4" becomes an optional **Suggested pace**, counted from each learner's start date.
4. Checkboxes become **Mark done** on lessons. Assignments count when handed in (or when Approved, if review is on).
5. In progress · Next up · Later becomes the **Learning** group in My work, across every path a learner is on.
6. The Course Index becomes the **outline**, which an admin can show on the public About page.
7. Covers, priorities, banners and stickers are dropped.

```

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────┐
│ Your progress  ███████░░░░░ 58% · 14 of 24 steps             │ Up next              │

**The 18 layers**
1. **Getting it:**
   - **Settings → Pacing:** Scheduled (W2's Term plan) or **Self-paced** (the Path). It's one choice per class; a class can't mix both. **[call]**
   - Coaching / Bootcamp institutions offer Self-paced as the starting value for new classes; Education stays Scheduled.
   - **Instructor's first look:** an empty Path with "Add your first phase", plus **Import outline** (paste a list of headings).
   - **Learner's first look:** the Path with Module 1 open and **Start**.
2. **Setting it up (Class: Settings → Path):**
   - the words (Phase, Module, Step; renameable like the sprint words)
   - **Order:** Open (default), or modules unlock in order **[call]**
   - **Suggested pace:** off, or weeks per module
   - **Stuck after:** 14 days without a step done
   - **Reminder to learners when stuck:** off **[call]**
   - **Show the outline publicly:** off
3. **Items:**
   - **Phase and Module:** sprints with **no dates** (the dates become optional only in self-paced classes); the Planning → Active → Completed cycle is hidden for them. **[call]**
   - **Step:** a lesson (`class_lesson`, Draft → Published, with a length in minutes) or an assignment, placed in a module by position. Any step can be **Optional**.
   - **Progress:** a new small table, step × learner → done at. It's one row per finished lesson, never a copy of the lesson for each learner. **[call]**
   - **Assignment copies** in a self-paced class are made **when the learner opens the module**, with an optional due date counted from then ("Due 7 days after you start"). **[call]**
   - **Requires:** a module can name the module that must be finished first ("Finish Module 5 first").
   - **Creating:**
     - + New ▾ → Phase, Module, Lesson or Assignment (the one New module, 28.11)
     - + on a module row
     - Import outline
     - Duplicate a module or phase
     - a C1 program snapshot
     - CLI and agents (B13)
4. **Views:**

   | View | Who | On screen |
   |---|---|---|
   | **Path** (learners) | Learner | Their %, pace, phases → modules → steps with ✓ / ◐ / ○ / 🔒, Up next, Due, Help |
   | **Edit path** | Staff | The same tree with drag, Draft steps, and the drop-off line |
   | **Progress** (Members) | Staff | Learner × module grid, %, pace, filters |
   | **Learning** (My work) | Learner | In progress · Next up across classes |
   | **Outline** (public About) | Visitor | Phase, module and step titles and lengths, nothing else |
5. **Actions and flow:**
   - **Continue** opens the next step that isn't done → read → **Mark done** → the next step.
   - **A step counts as done when:** the learner marks a lesson done · an assignment is handed in (review off) or Approved (review on) · an Excused assignment is left out of the count. **[call]**
   - **Progress %** = required steps done ÷ required steps; optional steps never count.
   - **Pace:** with Suggested pace on, each module has a target week counted from the learner's start; the learner is On pace or Behind pace. Nothing is ever locked or marked late by pace. **[call]**
   - **Changing the path:** a step added to a module a learner has already finished shows as **New** and doesn't lower their %; moving a step keeps its ✓. **[call]**
   - **Finishing:** every required step done → **Completed** (C1 call 5 without attendance) → the verified profile entry (C1 call 6).
6. **Surfaces:**
   - **Header:** the % bar, "14 of 24 steps", pace, start date.
   - **Phase rows:** % and a ✓ when finished; collapsed when finished.
   - **Module rows:** "2 of 6", ← you are here, 🔒 with its reason.
   - **Step rows:** type, title, length, Mark done or the assignment state, Optional, New.
   - **Rail:** Up next with Continue, Due (copies with dates), Help (the mentor from W8 or the instructor).
   - **Drop-off line** (staff): how many learners reached each module, with ⚠ on the biggest drop.
7. **Design spec:**
   - Reuse the sprint left rail, the W2 table frame, `StatusBadge`, the progress bar, the item page, the W6 grid and the My work drawer.
   - Lucide icons: Route, Lock, CircleCheck, CircleDashed, PlayCircle.
   - Add a contract test.
8. **Words:**
   - Path · Phase · Module · Step · Lesson · Optional · Start · Continue · Mark done · Done · Up next · You are here · Locked · Finish … first · Suggested pace · On pace · Behind pace · Stuck · Not started · New · Progress · Learning.
   - Never "score", "streak", "points", "rank" or "leaderboard". **[call]**
9. **Links:**
   - C1 (a self-paced program is one class that stays open, with no cohorts; completion and the profile entry)
   - W1 (FAQs, the video card, the outline on About)
   - W2 (`class_lesson`, materials, Required reading)
   - W3 (the Learning group in My work)
   - W7 (rubric marks on path assignments)
   - W8 (a mentor's own learners in Progress)
   - C3 (mock tests as path steps), C4 (the capstone as the last phase)
   - the review queue, search, the account export
10. **People:**

    | | Sees | Can do |
    |---|---|---|
    | Institution admin | Counts: learners, % finished, drop-off by module | Offer self-paced programs |
    | Program lead | The same, for their programs | The same |
    | Instructor (Teacher) | Everything, with names | Build and edit the path, publish steps, settings |
    | Mentor (TA) | The Progress grid (their section once W8 is on) | Review assignments, message learners; not edit the path **[call]** |
    | Learner | Their own path and progress | Mark done, hand in, Continue |
    | Visitor | The outline, if it's public | Join or Request to join |
11. **States:**
    - Not started: the Path with Start.
    - Steps in Draft are hidden from learners.
    - Progress updates at once after Mark done; the staff grid refreshes live.
    - A finished path shows "Completed Nov 30" with the profile entry offer.
12. **Edges:**
    - A learner who leaves and comes back keeps their ✓s (progress isn't deleted when copies are).
    - A deleted step goes to Trash with its progress rows; % is worked out again.
    - Reordering never re-locks a module someone has already opened.
    - Pacing can switch only before the first learner joins.
    - Paths over 200 steps load one phase at a time.
    - A learner on several paths sees each in My work.
13. **Phone:** the Path is one column with a sticky **Continue** button; the rail moves to the top; the grid scrolls sideways with names pinned.
14. **Accessibility:**
    - Progress as text ("58%, 14 of 24 steps").
    - Locked modules say why.
    - The tree is a list of lists; the grid is a real table.
    - Mark done is a button with its step's name in its label.
15. **Notifications:**
    - Step marked done: nothing.
    - Module unlocked: nothing (it shows in the Path).
    - Relative due dates use the existing due reminders.
    - **Stuck:** **Summary** to staff, once a week.
    - Reminder to a stuck learner (when turned on): **Normal**, at most once per stuck spell.
    - **New steps** in a module the learner finished: **Summary**.
    - **Completed:** **Important** (C1).
16. **Trust and data:**
    - Progress is personal: the learner and staff only; in the account export; removed with the account.
    - The institution sees counts.
    - The public outline shows titles and lengths only, never content.
    - **AI agents can read a learner's path and progress but can't mark steps done.** **[call]**
17. **Reuse vs new:**
    - **Reuse:** sprint nesting and materials, `class_lesson`, assignment copies and the review queue, the late-joiner copy code, the My work drawer, the W6 grid, the C1 completion rule and profile entry, the public About.
    - **New:**
      - the Pacing setting
      - undated sprints
      - the progress table
      - the Path, Edit path and Progress views
      - copies made when a module is opened, with relative due dates
      - the unlock, % and pace rules (pure functions)
      - the drop-off line
      - the public outline
      - the Learning group in My work
18. **How we know it works:**
    - **Signal:** the share of learners who finish Module 1 within 14 days of joining.
    - **Checks:**
      - the % rule (optional, excused, New steps)
      - the unlock rule
      - relative due dates
      - no copy before a module is opened
      - undated sprints are skipped by auto-start
      - agents are refused when marking done (server test)
      - visitors never get step content (server test)

**Organization steps:**
- **Level:**
  - Institution (the academy): self-paced programs, counts and drop-off.
  - Class (the path): its structure, the Progress grid.
  - Learner: their Path, Continue and Learning.
  - Learner workspaces are only needed for project work (C4).
- **Term moment:** no term. Join any time → Module 1 → every week (steps and hand-ins) → stuck or behind → finished (Completed, profile entry) → the path changes (New steps).
- **Org tab:**
  - Sprints (Path, Edit path)
  - Members (Progress)
  - Overview (the learner's Continue card; the staff's Stuck and Behind card)
  - Assignments (relative due dates, made on opening)
  - Review queue (unchanged)
  - About (the outline)
  - Settings (Pacing, Path)

**Calls agreed 2026-11-17:**
1. Pacing is one setting per class: Scheduled or Self-paced, never mixed.
2. Phases and modules are sprints with no dates in self-paced classes.
3. A lesson done is one progress row, not a copy for each learner.
4. Assignment copies are made when the learner opens the module, with a due date counted from then.
5. Modules are open by default; locking in order is a setting.
6. A step counts as done when marked done, handed in (no review) or Approved (review on); Excused is left out.
7. Suggested pace only shows On pace or Behind pace; it never locks anything or marks it late.
8. New steps never lower a learner's %.
9. Reminders to stuck learners are off by default.
10. Mentors see progress and review, but don't edit the path.
11. No streaks, points or leaderboards.
12. AI agents can't mark steps done.

### 31.4 C3 · Mock tests and skills (agreed 2026-11-17)
**References** (22 searches found 163 templates, 79 of them rated; 8 studied from their screenshots; personal planners left to W3):

| Template | Rating | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **IELTS Study Planner** | **4.88 / 132** | **Main reference for scores:** a goal per skill (Overall · Listening · Reading · Writing · Speaking); a score table per skill (date, test, band, number correct with a ring, parts 1–4); a Calendar view |
| **Test Revision Planner** | 4.76 / 377 | A month calendar of tests with subject chips and a Revising status |
| **NEET 2026 Master Dashboard** | 4.76 / 124 | Ideal score, a days-to-go countdown, the syllabus per subject (Class 11 · Class 12). **Dropped:** ideal rank, the study streak, the seconds counter |
| **SAT Question Error Tracker** | 4.87 / 47 | A testing record (mock calendar, all tests, scores) beside a mistake database (date, source, section) |
| **ERROR LOG** | 4.78 / 41 | Source · question · marked · correct answer · reason tags (time management, calculation error, anxiety, concept gap, vocabulary) · remarks |
| NEET Preparation 2026 | 4.91 / 11 | Syllabus status per subject · Mock tests · Doubts · "Score needed" |
| IELTS Exam Preparation | 4.94 / 31 | The four skills, a score calculator and an exam-day checklist |
| JEE Preparation Dashboard | 4.79 / 42 | A weekly task tracker by subject (W3 covers it) |

**Today:**
- Assignments, hand-ins, the review queue, private feedback.
- **W4 (agreed):** the Exam type, held results and Release.
- **W7 (agreed):** marks out of N, rubrics, and **no totals, averages or grades across assignments** (29.6 call 3).
- W2 outcomes (a topic list on the class); C2 progress.
- **Missing:**
  - section scores inside one mock
  - a series of mocks with the same layout
  - fast marks entry for paper mocks
  - targets
  - the learner's real exam date
  - an error log
  - a syllabus tracker

**Agreed changes from an exact copy:**
1. Each learner's own score sheet becomes the class's **mock series**. Staff enter marks once; every learner sees only their own.
2. One table per skill becomes the **sections of one Score layout**; one mock holds every section.
3. Averages under the table become **Latest, Best and a trend line** (no average across mocks, call 3).
4. "Ideal rank" becomes a **target score**; there are no ranks.
5. Streaks, the seconds counter, quotes and playlists are dropped; **days to go** stays.
6. Error-log tags become a short fixed **reason** list (renameable).
7. Syllabus toggles become the class's **topic list**, with each learner's own stages.

**The 18 layers**
1. **Getting it:**
   - Every class in a Coaching / Bootcamp institution can have **mock series**; Education classes can turn them on too.
   - **Instructor's first look:** + New ▾ → **Mock**, which asks for a Score layout (from the library or new).
   - **Learner's first look:** My prep asks for **My exam** (name, date or "not booked", target), then shows the empty Scores.
2. **Setting it up:**
   - **Institution: Settings → Score layouts:**
     - **sections:** name, maximum, and an optional marking scheme (e.g. +4 / −1 / 0)
     - an optional **raw → scaled table** per section (e.g. 30 of 40 → 7.0)
     - the **overall rule** within one mock: Sum · Average rounded to 0.5 · None **[call]**
     - **Presets** bring sections and maxima only (IELTS Academic, IELTS General, TOEFL iBT, Digital SAT, GRE, JEE Main, NEET, Custom). Conversion tables are entered by the institution. **[call]**
   - **Class: Settings → Mocks:**
     - reasons for mistakes
     - the topic list (W2 outcomes, called **Topics** here) and syllabus stages (Concept · Practice · Revised)
     - "Results stay held until Release" (on)
3. **Items:**
   - **Mock:** a W4 Exam with a **Score layout**, frozen when published (like a rubric, W7 call 2). Its **series** is a label that groups mocks with the same layout. **[call]**
   - **Section mark:** stored with the W7 mark as per-section values (raw and scaled), with the overall worked out from the rule.
   - **Target:** set by the learner per section and overall; staff can suggest one. **[call]**
   - **My exam:** the learner's real exam (name, date, target), with an optional **reported result** after it. **[call]**
   - **Mistake:** a learner's private row: mock, question, section, topic, reason, note, Fixed. **[call]**
   - **Syllabus stage:** topic × learner × stage, ticked by the learner. **[call]**
   - **Creating:**
     - + New ▾ → Mock (the one New module, 28.11)
     - Duplicate a mock
     - **Plan a series** (n mocks, every n weeks, from the W4 pattern)
     - CSV import of marks
     - a C1 program snapshot
4. **Views:**

   | View | Who | On screen |
   |---|---|---|
   | **My prep** (class) | Learner | My exam and days to go; Scores · Syllabus · Mistakes |
   | **Scores** (Members) | Staff | Learner × mock grid, targets, "Below target in", the mark spread for one mock |
   | **Enter marks** (review queue) | Staff | Learner × section entry sheet for paper mocks |
   | **Series** (Assignments) | Staff | The series' mocks with dates, Held or Released, marked counts |
   | **Real exams** (a Members column) | Staff | Each learner's exam date, sortable |
5. **Actions and flow:**
   - **Paper mock:** sit in class → **Enter marks** (type a section mark, or Correct / Wrong / Unattempted when there's a marking scheme) → Save → **Release** (W4).
   - **Online mock:** W4 Timed online → hand in → the W7 marking panel shows the sections.
   - Absent learners stay **Missing** or **Excused**, never zero.
   - **After release, the learner:** sees the marks → logs mistakes from the mock → **Ask about this mark** (W7).
   - **Weak topics:** sections or topics below the learner's own target in two of their last three mocks.
   - **Retakes** are kept and marked "Retake"; the trend uses first attempts.
6. **Surfaces:**
   - **My exam strip:** days to go (days only), target, Edit.
   - **The scores table:** a section per row, Latest, Best, a **Gap** in words, a small trend line.
   - **Syllabus:** topics by subject with stage ticks and "12 of 40 revised".
   - **Mistakes:** a table with reason chips and counts by reason ("Time 9 · Concept 6").
   - **Staff grid:** colour only alongside words; the spread is shown in bands, not as an ordered list.
7. **Design spec:**
   - Reuse the W6 grid, the W7 marking panel, the W4 exam settings, the roster columns, `StatusBadge` and the progress bar.
   - Lucide icons: ClipboardList, Target, LineChart, Bug, ListChecks, CalendarClock.
   - Add a contract test.
8. **Words:**
   - Mock · Series · Score layout · Section · Marking scheme · Scaled · Overall · Target · Gap · On target · Below target · Latest · Best · Trend · My prep · My exam · Days to go · Weak topics · Mistake · Reason · Fixed · Syllabus · Concept · Practice · Revised · Enter marks · Retake.
   - Never "rank", "percentile", "leaderboard", "streak", "grade" or "average". **[call]**
9. **Links:**
   - W4 (the Exam type, hold and Release, clash check, extra time)
   - W7 (marks, the marking panel, Ask about this mark, agents never set marks)
   - W2 (topics are outcomes) · W3 (the exam strip shows real exams too) · W6 (attendance at paper mocks) · W8 (sections enter their own marks)
   - C1 (score layouts travel in program snapshots) · C2 (mocks as path steps) · C5 (shared mistakes go to the mentor)
   - Documents: an **Exam day** checklist template
10. **People:**

    | | Sees | Can do |
    |---|---|---|
    | Institution admin | Counts: mocks held, learners on target, reported results | Score layouts and conversion tables |
    | Program lead | The same, for their programs | The same |
    | Instructor (Teacher) | Every learner's scores, targets, exam dates, syllabus counts | Make series, enter marks, release, suggest targets |
    | Mentor (TA) | Their section's scores; mistakes a learner shared | Enter marks for their section |
    | Learner | Only their own scores, syllabus and mistakes | Set targets and My exam; log mistakes; share them |
    | Visitor | Nothing | — |
11. **States:**
    - No mocks yet: "Your first mock is on Nov 24."
    - Held marks show "Results on release".
    - The entry sheet saves each cell as it's typed, with "Saved".
    - Conversion shows the scaled value next to each raw mark.
12. **Edges:**
    - A value missing from the conversion table shows the raw mark with ⚠ to staff.
    - A layout change after publishing affects only new mocks.
    - Learners who join mid-series start their trend from their first mock.
    - A learner with no target sees no Gap column.
    - A real exam date in the past asks "How did it go?" once.
    - Start a cohort (C1) copies series, layouts and topics, never marks, targets or mistakes.
13. **Phone:** My prep is one column with a section per card; the entry sheet works one learner at a time; the staff grid scrolls sideways with names pinned.
14. **Accessibility:**
    - The trend has a table alternative.
    - The gap is in words ("0.5 below target").
    - The entry sheet is a real table that works by keyboard (Tab, Enter).
    - Colours always come with words.
15. **Notifications:**
    - Results released: **Important**, "Mock 4 results are out", without the marks (W7 call 10).
    - Real exam in 7 days: **Normal**, with the Exam day checklist.
    - Below target in the same section for 3 mocks: **Summary** to the mentor or instructor.
    - Mistake shared: **Normal** to the mentor.
16. **Trust and data:**
    - Scores are personal: the learner and staff only; the institution sees counts.
    - **Mistakes and syllabus ticks are private to the learner**; staff see syllabus counts only.
    - Reported results are self-reported and labelled that way.
    - Everything is in the account export.
    - **JEE and NEET learners are mostly under 18.** Until there's an under-18 policy (29.6 call 2), these classes serve learners aged 18 and over only. **[call]**
    - AI agents can read a learner's own scores and add mistakes to their log when the learner asks; they never set marks (W7). **[call]**
17. **Reuse vs new:**
    - **Reuse:** W4 exams and Release, W7 marks and the marking panel, the review queue, W2 topics, the W6 grid, roster columns, private feedback, C1 snapshots.
    - **New:**
      - score layouts and conversion tables
      - per-section marks and the overall rule (pure function)
      - the series label and Plan a series
      - the Enter marks sheet
      - targets and My exam
      - the My prep page
      - the mistake log
      - syllabus stages
      - Weak topics (pure function)
      - the Scores grid
18. **How we know it works:**
    - **Signal:** the share of learners whose last mock before their real exam meets their target.
    - **Checks:**
      - conversion and the overall rules (sum, average rounded to 0.5, marking schemes)
      - layouts freeze on publish
      - held marks stay hidden
      - a learner never receives another learner's scores (server test)
      - mistakes never reach staff unless shared (server test)
      - retakes are left out of the trend
      - no zero for Missing

**Organization steps:**
- **Level:**
  - Institution: score layouts, conversion tables, counts.
  - Class (the batch): series, Enter marks, the Scores grid.
  - Learner: My prep.
- **Term moment:** joining (My exam, targets) → diagnostic mock → a mock every one or two weeks → after each mock (release, mistakes, weak topics) → the last two weeks (Exam day checklist) → the real exam → the reported result.
- **Org tab:**
  - Tasks (Assignments: Mock and Series; Review queue: Enter marks)
  - Members (Scores, the Exam date column)
  - Overview (the learner's My prep card; the staff's "Below target" card)
  - Settings (Score layouts, Mocks)
  - Documents (Exam day checklist)

**Calls agreed 2026-11-17:**
1. A mock is a W4 Exam with a Score layout; a series is a label grouping mocks with the same layout.
2. The overall is worked out inside one mock (Sum, Average rounded to 0.5, or None); nothing is totalled or averaged across mocks.
3. Presets bring sections and maxima only; institutions enter their own conversion tables.
4. Learners see Latest, Best and a trend, never an average.
5. No ranks, percentiles or leaderboards; learners never see others' scores, and staff see the spread in bands.
6. Targets are set by the learner; staff can suggest one.
7. My exam and the reported result are entered by the learner and optional.
8. Mistakes are private, with Share with mentor.
9. Syllabus ticks are the learner's own; staff see counts.
10. JEE and NEET classes serve learners aged 18 and over until there's an under-18 policy.
11. AI agents can log mistakes for the learner but never set marks.

### 31.5 C5 · Mentors (agreed 2026-11-17)
**References** (16 searches found 111 templates, 34 of them rated; 7 studied from their screenshots):

| Template | Rating | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **1x1 Meeting** | **4.91 / 44** | **Main reference for the check-in:** one running page, the newest date on top. Each date has Opening & check-in ("anything you stumbled over?", highlights and concerns), each person's Updates, Specific asks, and Feedback & recognition; a Feedback & improvement section at the top |
| **1:1 meeting docs** | 4.89 / 70 | One running doc per pair with a date and Complete tick; each person's Priorities and To discuss |
| 1:1 Notes | 4.78 / 237 | Notes per person with dates |
| **Mentor/Mentee Dashboard** | 4.80 / 10 | **Our commitment:** dates, cadence ("every other week, about 1 hour, 6 times"), who does what (the mentee reaches out and sends the agenda; the mentor listens and coaches); a meetings database |
| **Mentor/Mentee Success Tracker** | 4.88 / 16 | Pre-session prep; objectives |
| **Mentorship Cohort HQ** | 5.0 / 4 | A 5-step launch checklist (copy, rename the cohort, add people, **match partners**, send the kickoff); Admin HQ with Cohorts · People · Sessions · Feedback |
| Mentee Page | 4.94 / 47 | A study to-do list with subject trackers (C2 and C3 cover it) |

**Today:**
- **W8 (agreed):** sections with TAs, one per student per kind, Rebalance, review load, section-only TAs.
- **C1:** the Mentor role word (on TA). **C2:** the Help card names the mentor. **C3:** shared mistakes go to the mentor.
- **Direct messages** exist (messaging). The chat canvas has meeting templates (notes, status, retro, brief, decision, incident), but **no 1:1**.
- **11.6 (designed):** meeting types, with 1:1s private even from admins. **W5:** the Supervision type, whose action items become tasks.
- **11.4 (designed):** objectives.
- **Missing:**
  - matching mentors to learners
  - a running check-in page per pair
  - prep before a check-in
  - booking
  - a check on each pair's rhythm
  - mentor feedback
  - access for outside mentors

**Agreed changes from an exact copy:**
1. Cohort HQ's Cohorts and People are already C1 and the roster; **Match partners** becomes a mentor group (a W8 section kind).
2. The running 1:1 page becomes a **Check-in** document per pair (the 11.6 1:1 type, named Check-in for coaching).
3. "Our commitment" becomes a **Plan** card set by the program (cadence, number of check-ins, length, who prepares).
4. Pre-session prep becomes the learner's **Prep** part, filled before each check-in.
5. AI meeting notes and transcripts are dropped (NB doesn't record calls).
6. Cohort HQ's Feedback becomes a one-tap **Was this useful?** after each check-in.

**The 18 layers**
1. **Getting it:**
   - Every Coaching / Bootcamp cohort can turn on **Mentoring** (Settings); Education classes can too.
   - **Instructor's first look:** Members → Mentors with "Invite mentors" and **Match mentors…**, and the launch steps from C1's Start a cohort (invite → match → kickoff message).
   - **Mentor's first look:** **My mentees** cards and the Mentor guide (Required reading for mentors).
   - **Learner's first look:** the My mentor card with Book a time.
2. **Setting it up (Class: Settings → Mentoring):**
   - **Plan:** every n weeks, length, number of check-ins, who prepares (learner)
   - **Rhythm warning:** after 21 days without a check-in
   - **Was this useful?** on (answers show after 5)
   - **Mentors book through:** NB time slots, or "arrange yourselves" (no booking)
   - The institution can supply the Mentor guide and the Check-in template.
3. **Items:**
   - **Mentor group:** a W8 section of kind **Mentor group** with its mentor(s); one per learner (W8 call 4). **[call]**
   - **Check-in document:** one running meeting document per pair, newest date first. Each date has Prep (the learner, before), Notes (both), Action items (they become the learner's tasks, W5 pattern) and Objectives (a status line). **[call]**
   - **Objective:** up to 3 per learner, the 11.4 objective item, owned by the learner, kept to the pair; status On track · At risk · Done. **[call]**
   - **Time slot:** a mentor's weekly times; a booking makes the next dated entry. **[call]**
   - **Useful answer:** Very · Somewhat · Not really, with an optional note.
   - **Concern:** a private note from a mentor or learner to the instructor.
4. **Views:**

   | View | Who | On screen |
   |---|---|---|
   | **Mentors** (Members) | Staff | Mentor cards: learners, rhythm, objectives by status, Useful counts; pairs off rhythm |
   | **My mentees** (Overview, mentors) | Mentor | A card per learner: last and next check-in, prep, objectives, C2 % and C3 gap (their section only) |
   | **My mentor** (Overview, learners) | Learner | Mentor, plan, next check-in or Book, prep, objectives |
   | **Check-in** (Documents) | The pair | The running document |
5. **Actions and flow:**
   - **Match mentors…:** staff assign; the dialog suggests matches balanced by load, with optional fields (track, time zone, language) from the learner's join answers. There's no automatic matching. **[call]**
   - **Kickoff:** one message to each pair, with the plan and the first booking link.
   - **Before:** the learner fills Prep (reminded the day before) → the mentor sees ✓ Prep done.
   - **During and after:** notes, action items → tasks, objective statuses → **Was this useful?** for the learner.
   - **Change mentor:** a learner can ask privately; staff move them (W8 moving rules), and the old document stays with the learner, read-only to the old mentor. **[call]**
   - **Raise a concern:** a mentor or learner sends a private note to the instructor; it's logged. **[call]**
   - **Closing check-in:** the last one in the plan asks for a short reflection; the mentor can add a **mentor's note** to the learner's completion entry (C1), shown only after the learner approves. **[call]**
6. **Surfaces:**
   - **Mentor cards:** rhythm ("on rhythm 5 · 1 ⚠"), objectives by status, Useful counts.
   - **Plan line:** "every 2 weeks · 30 min · 4 of 6".
   - **Booking:** the mentor's free slots for the next 2 weeks, a .ics file after booking.
   - **Prep form:** three short fields (Since last time · Stuck on · Asks) with shared C3 mistakes offered as Asks.
7. **Design spec:**
   - Reuse the W8 section cards and Rebalance, the meeting document template, task creation from action items, the objective item, Overview cards, direct messages and Required reading.
   - Lucide icons: HeartHandshake, CalendarCheck, NotebookPen, Target, Flag.
   - Add a contract test.
8. **Words:**
   - Mentor · Mentor group · Mentoring · Plan · Check-in · Prep · Since last time · Stuck on · Asks · Action items · Objective · On track · At risk · Done · On rhythm · Book a time · My mentor · My mentees · Was this useful? · Raise a concern · Change mentor · Mentor's note · Mentor only.
   - Never "coach rating", "score" or "Lead".
9. **Links:**
   - W8 (sections, Rebalance, load) · C1 (launch steps, mentor pool across cohorts, the completion entry)
   - C2 (the Help card, progress on My mentees) · C3 (shared mistakes as Asks, the gap on My mentees) · C4 (the mentor as a capstone reviewer)
   - 11.6 meetings · 11.4 objectives · direct messages · the Calendar view (14.2)
10. **People:**

    | | Sees | Can do |
    |---|---|---|
    | Institution admin | Counts: pairs, on rhythm, Useful per program | Mentor guide, Check-in template |
    | Program lead | Mentor cards for their programs, Useful counts per mentor | Invite and match; read concerns for their programs |
    | Instructor (Teacher) | Mentor cards, rhythm, objective statuses, concerns; **never check-in notes** unless shared **[call]** | Match, Rebalance, change mentors, settings |
    | Mentor (TA) | Their mentees only, their check-ins, their own Useful totals after 5 answers | Run check-ins, set slots, action items, raise a concern |
    | Outside mentor (**Mentor only**) | The same, with no review queue, marks or roster | The same **[call]** |
    | Learner | Their own check-ins, objectives, mentor | Book, prep, answer Useful, change mentor, raise a concern |
    | Visitor | Nothing | — |
11. **States:**
    - Not matched: "Your mentor will be shared soon."
    - No slots: "Message Arjun to arrange a time."
    - Prep due, Prep done.
    - A finished plan: "6 of 6 · finished".
12. **Edges:**
    - A mentor leaves: "No mentor" ⚠ and matching again; documents stay with the learner.
    - A learner moves to a later cohort (C1): they keep the document; a new pair starts.
    - Booking clashes with a session (W1) or an exam (W4) give a warning.
    - Several mentors on one group share the document.
    - Time zones show for both people.
    - Start a cohort never copies documents or answers.
13. **Phone:** cards stack; Prep and booking are one column; the document shows the newest date open.
14. **Accessibility:**
    - Rhythm and status as words.
    - Slots as a list of buttons with full dates.
    - The document is plain headings with dates.
15. **Notifications:**
    - Matched: **Important** to the learner, **Normal** to the mentor.
    - Booked or moved: **Normal** to both; a reminder 1 hour before.
    - Prep reminder: **Normal**, the day before.
    - Off rhythm: **Normal** once to the pair; **Summary** to staff.
    - Concern raised: **Important** to the instructor.
    - Useful answers: nothing.
16. **Trust and data:**
    - **Check-in notes are private to the pair**, like 11.6 1:1s; the learner can Share an entry with the instructor.
    - Concerns are the one exception and are logged.
    - Useful answers are never shown per session or under 5.
    - Outside mentors see only their mentees.
    - Everything is in the account export.
    - AI agents can draft Prep for the learner on request, but never answer Useful or raise concerns.
17. **Reuse vs new:**
    - **Reuse:** W8 sections and Rebalance, the TA role, direct messages, meeting documents and action items, objectives, Overview cards, Required reading, the C1 completion entry.
    - **New:**
      - the Mentor group kind
      - Match mentors with suggestions (pure function)
      - the Check-in type and running document
      - the Plan card
      - slots and booking with .ics
      - the rhythm rule
      - Was this useful?
      - Mentor only access
      - Raise a concern
      - the mentor's note
18. **How we know it works:**
    - **Signal:** the share of learners with a check-in in every 21-day window.
    - **Checks:**
      - notes never reach staff unless shared (server test)
      - Mentor only access (server test)
      - Useful hidden under 5 answers
      - booking clashes
      - the rhythm rule
      - a moved learner keeps their document

**Organization steps:**
- **Level:**
  - Institution: the mentor pool across cohorts, the guide, counts.
  - Cohort: mentor groups, matching, rhythm.
  - The pair: the Check-in document.
- **Term moment:** before the cohort (invite mentors, guide) → week 1 (match, kickoff, objectives) → every n weeks (prep, check-in, action items) → mid-cohort (rhythm, Rebalance, change mentor) → the end (closing check-in, mentor's note) → next cohort (the mentor pool).
- **Org tab:**
  - Members (Mentors; mentor groups in Sections)
  - Overview (My mentor; My mentees; the staff rhythm card)
  - Documents (Check-in documents, Mentor guide)
  - Tasks (action items)
  - Settings (Mentoring)

**Calls agreed 2026-11-17:**
1. A mentor group is a W8 section kind; one per learner.
2. Staff match with suggestions; no automatic matching.
3. One running Check-in document per pair, newest first; action items become the learner's tasks.
4. Check-in notes are private to the pair; staff see rhythm and objective statuses unless an entry is shared.
5. Raise a concern is the one route to the instructor, and it's logged.
6. Up to 3 objectives per learner, kept to the pair.
7. Booking uses NB time slots and a .ics file; no calendar sync.
8. Outside mentors join as Mentor only.
9. Was this useful? shows only as counts after 5 answers; never per session.
10. Change mentor keeps the document with the learner.
11. The mentor's note on the completion entry shows only after the learner approves.
12. Peer buddies are parked.

### 31.6 C4 · Capstone and demo day (agreed 2026-11-17)
**References** (18 searches found 152 templates, 54 of them rated; 7 studied from their screenshots):

| Template | Rating | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **Case Study Gallery** | **4.85 / 86** | **Main reference for the showcase:** a welcome line, contact, then a gallery of projects (cover, title) with tabs by topic |
| Portfolio | 4.84 / 805 | Skills chips above "My work" cards with filters (C1's profile entry covers the person's side) |
| **Final Year Capstone Project Tracker** | 4.63 / 16 | **Main reference for the project:** Project overview (title, supervisor, start–end, status), **Success metrics**, journals (Research · Meeting notes · Feedback and evaluation), quick actions |
| **Hackathon Project Planner** | 4.88 / 40 | A team gallery with each person's **role** (UI/UX, Back-end, Front-end); planning steps (1. Exploring the problem …) |
| **Hackathon Event Page** | 4.80 / 15 | Place · date · in person / online cards, then the agenda by day with time slots (registration → opening → team formation → … → awards) |
| Startup Pitch Deck | 4.87 / 61 | A one-page pitch: a headline, four points, a picture (the showcase card's shape) |
| Final Year Project | 4.75 / 12 | Milestones, tasks, notes and meetings (W5 covers it) |

**Today:**
- **Built:**
  - each-child assignments (one copy per class workspace, reviewed in the class queue)
  - team assignments
  - org templates for new workspaces
  - profile contribution entries (draft, published, hidden, Completed)
  - workspace visibility under the org's cap
- **Agreed:**
  - W5 (milestones, the coordinator table, supervisor routing)
  - W7 (rubrics, team mark + Adjust for one person)
  - C1 (completion, the profile entry)
  - C2 (the capstone as the last phase)
  - C5 (mentors, the mentor's note)
- **Section 16** designed demo-day pieces (agenda slots, judges, criteria, awards), but the Event planner tab is **parked** (27).
- **Missing:**
  - team workspaces from a capstone template
  - a project brief with success metrics
  - a showcase card and gallery
  - a run of show for one afternoon
  - judges from outside
  - awards without a leaderboard

**Agreed changes from an exact copy:**
1. The capstone tracker becomes a **Capstone workspace template**: brief, success metrics, team roles, milestones, journals as document sections.
2. Supervisor becomes the team's **mentor** (C5).
3. The case-study gallery becomes the cohort's **Showcase**: one card per project.
4. The hackathon agenda becomes a **Run of show**: one slot per team, made from the teams.
5. Section 16's weighted scores and leaderboard are dropped: judges give **feedback**, and awards are **picked**, not ranked.
6. Registration, budget and the checklist stay with the parked Event planner.

**The 18 layers**
1. **Getting it:**
   - **Settings → Capstone** in Coaching / Bootcamp cohorts; Education classes can use it too (W5 covers theses).
   - **Instructor's first look:** "Set up the capstone" → brief source, team size, milestones, demo day date.
   - **Learner's first look:** "Join or form a team" (or their team, if set), then the brief.
   - **Judge's first look:** the demo-day page with their judging list.
2. **Setting it up (Cohort: Settings → Capstone):**
   - **Teams:** set by staff, or formed by learners with a **size limit** (2–4) and a **lock date** **[call]**
   - **Briefs:** the learner's own, or from the instructor's **brief list** **[call]**
   - **Milestones:** Proposal → MVP → Final → Demo (each-child assignments, renameable)
   - **Demo day:** date, time, place or link, minutes per team, **awards** (names, off by default)
   - **Showcase:** members only (default) or public **[call]**
   - The institution supplies the Capstone template and can keep a **Demo days** archive across cohorts.
3. **Items:**
   - **Team workspace:** one per team, made from the Capstone template; its members are the team; staff inherited (as today). **[call]**
   - **Brief:** the workspace's About fields: problem, who it's for, **success metrics** (up to 5), and the track.
   - **Role:** a short label for each member on the team ("Front-end").
   - **Milestone:** an each-child copy reviewed by the team's mentor (W5 call 5, C5), with W7 marks (team mark + Adjust for one person).
   - **Showcase card:** cover, title, one line, links (demo, code, video), track, members with roles. Draft → **Ready**, handed in with the Final milestone. **[call]**
   - **Run of show:** a list of slots (time, team or a named slot, length) on the cohort, made from the teams.
   - **Judge:** an outside person invited for one demo day, with the **Judge** role (a Viewer kind). **[call]**
   - **Judge feedback:** the demo-day criteria (a W7 rubric, 1–5) and a note to the team, plus award picks.
   - **Award:** a name and its winners, announced by staff.
4. **Views:**

   | View | Who | On screen |
   |---|---|---|
   | **Projects** (cohort) | Staff, mentors | The W5 coordinator table: team, brief, mentor, milestone, Showcase status, last check-in |
   | **Team Overview** (workspace) | The team | Brief, team and roles, milestones, next milestone, the showcase card |
   | **Showcase** (cohort About) | Members; visitors where public | Demo day details, cards by track, awards once announced |
   | **Run of show** (Overview card on the day) | Staff, teams | Slots with ← now, Next team, Skip |
   | **Judging** | Judges | One team at a time: links, criteria, note, picks |
   | **Demo days** (institution) | Admins; visitors where public | Past showcases by cohort |
5. **Actions and flow:**
   - **Kickoff:** briefs → teams (formed or set; "Looking for a team" ⚠ before the lock date) → **Create team workspaces** from the template.
   - **Build:** mentor check-ins (C5), tasks and sprints inside the workspace, milestones handed in and reviewed.
   - **Before demo day:** showcase cards Ready → the Run of show is made (Shuffle, drag) → judges invited.
   - **On the day:** Next team / Skip; judges give feedback and picks.
   - **After:** staff see picks → **Announce awards** (winners marked on the Showcase; an Update is optional) → teams see judge notes.
   - **After the cohort:**
     - each member can **Publish to profile** (the project joins their Completed entry, with the mentor's note if approved)
     - the team can **Take the workspace** out of the organization; the organization keeps milestones and marks **[call]**
6. **Surfaces:**
   - **Projects table:** Showcase status chips (—, Draft, Ready), overdue ⚠, "Looking for a team".
   - **Team Overview:** brief, success metrics as a checklist, role chips, milestones row.
   - **Showcase cards:** cover, title, one line, team names (only those who agreed when public), track chip, award badge.
   - **Run of show:** large "now" row, timer per slot.
   - **Judging sheet:** big 1–5 controls, note, picks, Save and next.
7. **Design spec:**
   - Reuse the W5 coordinator table, each-child assignments, the review queue, W7 rubrics, the org template, the Overview cards, the gallery grid view (14.3) and the profile entry.
   - Lucide icons: Rocket, Presentation, GalleryHorizontal, Award, Gavel.
   - Add a contract test.
8. **Words:**
   - Capstone · Brief · Success metrics · Team · Role · Looking for a team · Teams lock · Milestone · Proposal · MVP · Final · Demo · Showcase · Showcase card · Ready · Demo day · Run of show · Now · Next team · Skip · Judge · Feedback · Award · Picks · Announce awards · Take the workspace.
   - Never "leaderboard", "rank", "score", "winner board" or "Lead".
9. **Links:**
   - W5 (the pattern: template, milestones, routing, coordinator table) · W7 (rubrics, team marks)
   - C1 (completion; the program snapshot keeps the capstone set-up) · C2 (the capstone as the last phase) · C5 (mentors review and meet)
   - section 16 (agenda and judging pieces, ready to move into the Event planner when it's un-parked)
   - profile entries · the public About · the Update composer
10. **People:**

    | | Sees | Can do |
    |---|---|---|
    | Institution admin | Counts; the Demo days archive | Capstone template; the archive's visibility |
    | Program lead | Their cohorts' Projects tables and showcases | The same as an instructor for their programs |
    | Instructor (Teacher) | Everything | Set up, teams, briefs, run of show, invite judges, announce awards |
    | Mentor (TA) | Their teams' workspaces and milestones | Review milestones; can't judge their own teams **[call]** |
    | Learner | Their team workspace; the cohort Showcase | Form teams, build, fill the card, agree to public, publish to profile, take the workspace |
    | Judge | That demo day's showcase and judging list; nothing else | Feedback and picks until awards are announced |
    | Visitor | Public showcase cards only | — |
11. **States:**
    - Teams forming: counts and "Looking for a team".
    - The showcase hides cards until Ready.
    - Judging closes when awards are announced.
    - An archived cohort keeps its showcase read-only.
12. **Edges:**
    - A member leaves: the workspace stays with the team; their entry shows Left.
    - A team below the minimum size before the lock date: ⚠ to staff.
    - A team without a mentor: "No mentor" ⚠ (C5).
    - A missed slot: Skip, with a later slot offered.
    - A judge who is linked to a team (mentor, member) is blocked from that team.
    - A late Final: Late chip; the card can still be Ready.
    - Start a cohort copies the capstone set-up and brief list, never teams, workspaces or cards.
13. **Phone:**
    - The Run of show works on a phone (Next team is a big button).
    - Judging works one team per screen.
    - Showcase cards stack.
14. **Accessibility:**
    - Cards have text alternatives for covers.
    - The run of show is a list with times.
    - 1–5 controls are radio groups.
    - Award badges are words.
15. **Notifications:**
    - Team set or joined: **Normal**.
    - Teams lock tomorrow, still looking: **Important** to that learner.
    - Asked to agree to a public showcase: **Important** to each member.
    - Invited as a judge: **Important** (the existing invite link, then in-app).
    - Your slot is next: **Normal**.
    - Awards announced: **Important** to winning teams; others get nothing.
    - Judge notes ready: **Normal** to the team.
16. **Trust and data:**
    - Workspaces are private by default (the org cap applies).
    - A public showcase card shows only when every member agreed, and only the names of members who agreed.
    - Judges see only that day's cards and links; judge notes go to the team and staff only.
    - No guest registration; demo day is shared by link (registration waits for the Event planner). **[call]**
    - AI agents can help fill the showcase card on a member's request; they never give judge feedback or picks.
17. **Reuse vs new:**
    - **Reuse:**
      - each-child assignments and the review queue
      - the W5 coordinator table and routing
      - W7 rubrics and team marks
      - org templates and the gallery grid
      - profile entries
      - the public About and the Update composer
      - section 16's agenda and judging designs
    - **New:**
      - the Capstone template and setting
      - team forming with a lock date
      - the brief list
      - the showcase card and Showcase
      - the Run of show
      - the Judge role (Viewer kind) and judging sheet
      - award picks and Announce awards
      - Take the workspace
      - the Demo days archive
18. **How we know it works:**
    - **Signal:** the share of teams with a Ready showcase card by demo day.
    - **Checks:**
      - a project goes public only when every member agreed (server test)
      - judges see only their demo day (server test)
      - judges can't judge their own teams
      - teams lock on the date
      - Take the workspace keeps the org's milestones and marks
      - Start a cohort copies no teams or cards

**Organization steps:**
- **Level:**
  - Institution: the Capstone template, the Demo days archive, counts.
  - Cohort: teams, milestones, Showcase, Run of show, judges, awards.
  - Team workspace: the project.
- **Term moment:** capstone kickoff (briefs, teams) → Proposal → build (check-ins, sprints) → MVP → Final with the showcase card → demo day → awards → after the cohort (profile, take the workspace).
- **Org tab:**
  - Projects (team workspaces)
  - Tasks (milestones; Review queue by mentor)
  - Sprints or Path (the capstone phase)
  - About (Showcase, demo day details)
  - Overview (Demo day card, Run of show)
  - Settings (Capstone)

**Calls agreed 2026-11-17:**
1. One workspace per team from the Capstone template; milestones are each-child assignments.
2. Teams are set by staff or formed by learners, with a size limit and a lock date.
3. Briefs come from the learner or the instructor's brief list; outside partner briefs are parked.
4. Demo day is part of the cohort (Showcase + Run of show), not the parked Event planner.
5. One showcase card per project, Ready with the Final milestone.
6. The showcase is members-only by default; a project goes public only when every member agrees.
7. Outside judges join with a Judge role for one demo day; their scores are feedback, never marks.
8. Awards are optional and picked by judges, then announced by staff; no leaderboard or totals.
9. Mentors can't judge their own teams.
10. No guest registration; demo day is shared by link.
11. After the cohort, a team can take its workspace out of the organization; the organization keeps milestones and marks.

**Never:** rank, percentile, leaderboard, streak, points, grade, average, Lead, Owner.

**Flags carried forward:**
- **Under 18:** JEE and NEET classes serve learners aged 18 and over until there's an under-18 policy (29.6 call 2, 31.4 call 10).
- **Sprint dates:** C2 needs sprint dates to be optional in self-paced classes (one migration; auto-start, the timeline and insights skip undated sprints).
- **Event planner:** demo day blends into the cohort (31.6 call 4); registration and budgets wait for the parked tab.

**Build order inside this category:**
1. **C1:** programs and cohorts need the institution level (29.2) and reuse `duplicateOrg`.
2. **C2:** undated sprints and progress (after W2's `class_lesson`).
3. **C5:** mentor groups (after W8 sections).
4. **C3:** mocks (after W4 exams and W7 marks).
5. **C4:** the capstone (after W5, W7 and C5).

All of it waits for the three-level structure (29.2), the 28.9 Wave 0 foundation and College / University's W1, W2 and W8.

## 32. Organization category: School (K–12) (complete 2026-11-17)

This section uses the same combined method as sections 30 and 31. **Students are parked** (29.6 call 2: sign-up stays 18+), so a school on NetworkBase is its **staff**: teachers, teaching assistants, heads of department, school leaders and office staff.

### 32.1 Every School template, sorted
**How:**
- 48 searches (teacher, teacher planner, lesson plan, lesson planner, classroom, school, elementary, middle school, high school, K-12, curriculum map, unit plan, substitute teacher, sub plans, parent communication, parent-teacher conference, behavior tracker, IEP, special education, report card, gradebook, school administration, principal, staff meeting, school calendar, timetable, field trip, PTA, professional development, teacher observation, school department, homeroom, school newsletter, duty roster, teacher dashboard, teaching portfolio, school management, staff directory, school events, teacher evaluation, school improvement plan, academic calendar, curriculum planner, scheme of work, teacher binder, school year planner, student records, class roster) returned **330 templates**.
- Every rating and review count was read; 14 staff-side templates were studied from their screenshots.
- **The most-rated "school" templates are student planners** (Dark academia dashboard 4.81 / 757, Neapolitan planner 4.85 / 545, School / College Agenda 4.83 / 504). They're left out because students are parked.

**The top 10 (staff side)**

| # | Template | Rating / reviews | Level | Moment | Roles | Lands in |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Teacher home | 4.83 / 183 | Team | Every week | Teacher | S2 (already used by W2) |
| 2 | Lesson plans (Notion) | 4.76 / 163 | Team | Every week | Teacher | S2 |
| 3 | Teacher Lesson Planner | 4.89 / 122 | Teacher | Every week | Teacher | S2: Subjects · Lessons · Calendar |
| 4 | Teacher Class Manager | 4.90 / 97 | Teacher | Each term | Teacher | S4: classes and timetable (its student list is parked) |
| 5 | Lesson Plan Organizer | 4.84 / 92 | Team | Every week | Teacher | S2: days until the lesson, grade, Draft → Ready → Planned, objectives · materials · activities |
| 6 | Classroom home | 4.90 / 52 | Class | — | Students | Parked here (W1 for adult classes) |
| 7 | Teacher Curriculum Map | 4.84 / 37 | Team | Before the year | Head of department | S2: the year's map |
| 8 | Teacher Productivity Hub | 4.87 / 23 | Teacher | Every week | Teacher | S2 board by subject; S3 task and admin tracker (its student records are parked) |
| 9 | Teacher Curriculum Planner | 4.91 / 22 | Team | The whole year | Head of department | S2: course → unit → lesson, % of the unit taught |
| 10 | K-8 Substitute Teacher Homepage | 4.83 / 18 | School | An absence | Cover teacher | S4: cover |

**Worth taking parts from:**
- **School Calendar** (4.87 / 15): the school year as a month calendar; each item has a type (meeting, deadline, event), an **audience** (parents, students, staff), a place and a status; views School year · Upcoming · By type → S1.
- **Staff 1:1 Meeting Notes** (4.75 / 4) and **Professional Development tracker** (5.0 / 6) → S5.
- **Staff Directory** (4.78 / 27) → Members (exists).
- **Timetable** (4.70 / 188) → S4.

**Left out:**
- Student planners and dashboards (students are parked).
- **Parent Communication Log** (4.89 / 9): its rows are records about children (student, guardian, reason such as behaviour). Parked with the other student records.
- Gradebooks (29.6 call 3).

**Features taken from the screenshots:**
- **#3, #4, #7 (one maker):** side navigation Subjects · Lessons · Calendar; All classes · Timetable · Lesson plans; Subjects · Curriculum map.
- **#5:** a lesson table with subject, date, **days until the lesson**, grade, status (Draft, Ready, Planned), objectives, materials, activities; views by status, grade and objective.
- **#8:** a lesson board with a column per subject; cards with date, grade, objective, activity, status; Weekly overview and a Task & admin tracker.
- **#9:** courses grouped, units with **% of the unit taught**, lessons linked to their unit.
- **#10:** a card per grade (Kindergarten to 7th) holding that grade's notes and links for the cover teacher.
- **School Calendar:** events with an audience chip, and Needs action, Scheduled and Completed statuses.

**What's different about a staff-only school:**
1. **The org tabs serve staff work.** Assignments go to **teachers** ("Hand in your Unit 3 plan by Friday"), and the **Review queue is where a head of department reviews them**. Students never get copies.
2. **The middle level is a teaching team, not a class.** A department (Science) or a grade team (Grade 5) holds the shared map and plans; the classes it teaches are a short list of names with no students in them. **[call]**
3. **No student names in structured records.** Class lists hold class names and sizes only; attendance, marks, behaviour, SEN/IEP plans, parent contact logs, report cards and trip consent are parked with the under-18 design. **[call]**

**Covered by W1–W8 and C1–C5 (reused for teams):**
- the term plan, units, weeks and lessons (W2)
- the academic calendar at the institution (W1, W2)
- rubrics as feedback (W7)
- sections become class names (W8)
- running meeting documents (C5)

**Missing:**
- a school year calendar with audiences and events
- a shared curriculum map across grades and subjects
- staff hand-ins and reviews
- a staff timetable, cover and duty rota
- staff meetings, development and lesson observations

**Workflows, in order:**
- **S1** School year and calendar
- **S2** Curriculum map and lesson plans
- **S3** Staff hand-ins and reviews
- **S4** Timetable, cover and duties
- **S5** Staff meetings and growth

**Parked:**
- student accounts and every student record (see 3 above)
- parent accounts
- district or trust levels above one school
- trip consent forms

### 32.2 S1 · School year and calendar (agreed 2026-11-17)
**References** (10 more calendar searches found 94 templates; 4 studied from their screenshots):

| Template | Rating | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **Events Calendar** (Notion) | **4.80 / 504** | **Main reference for the look:** a calm month grid; each card has a title, a person, a type chip and a place; Calendar · All events · Gallery |
| **School Calendar** | 4.87 / 15 | **Main reference for the fields:** each item has a type (meeting, deadline, event), an **audience** (parents, students, staff), a place and a status (Needs action, Scheduled, Completed); views School year · Upcoming · By type |
| Event Calendar | 4.91 / 53 | A table of events: type, date range, organizer, place, status; views **Organized by me** and **Going to** |
| Calendar July 2026 – June 2027 | 4.58 / 12 | **The school year as one page:** months stacked from July to June |

**Today:**
- **Built:**
  - each org has **term start and end** and a **time zone**
  - announcements have an **audience** (roles or child workspaces) and notice levels
  - sprints nest and can **show in child workspaces**
  - `duplicateOrg` shifts dates
- **Agreed:**
  - W1 sessions skip institution breaks
  - W2 shows break rows and exam weeks on the Term plan
  - W4 exam weeks
  - a Calendar view in Sprints (14.2)
- **Missing:**
  - the school year itself (terms, holidays, staff days)
  - school events with audiences
  - one calendar every team sees
  - a public calendar for families
  - moving the year on to the next one

**Agreed changes from an exact copy:**
1. The calendar lives at the **school** and shows in every team; teams add their own events on top.
2. The "Parents" and "Students" audiences become **Show publicly** (families read the public calendar; there are no parent or student accounts).
3. "Needs action" becomes the event's **checklist** (a few prep items with owners).
4. Organized by me and Going to become **Mine** and **For me** filters.
5. Analytics, prices and participants are dropped.

```
SCHOOL (institution) · Sprints       [ Year ] [ Month ] [ Upcoming ]        + Event   Import…

 Year view (Sep → Aug, a row per month)
 SEP ░░▓▓▓▓▓░░▓▓▓▓▓░░▓▓▓▓▓░░▓▓▓▓▓░░▓   ▓ school day  ▒ staff day  ░ weekend  █ holiday  E exams
