```
 Fri Oct 10 · Staff day, no classes · Half-term in 9 days · Parents' evening Tue (you're in the audience)
```

**The 18 layers**
1. **Getting it:**
   - A School institution starts with **Set up the school year**: year name, start and end, terms, then holidays (typed in, or Import… from a CSV or .ics file).
   - **School admin's first look:** the empty Year view with that one button.
   - **Teacher's first look:** their team's Calendar with the school's year in grey and "This week at school" on Overview.
2. **Setting it up (School: Settings → School year):**
   - the words (Term · Semester · Quarter; Holiday · Break · Vacation; Staff day · INSET · PD day)
   - the week start (Monday or Sunday) and the time zone (exists)
   - event types (Meeting · Deadline · Event · Parents' evening · Trip · Assessment; renameable)
   - who adds school events (School admins; heads of department optional)
   - the public calendar (off)
3. **Items:**
   - **School year and terms:** terms are **school sprints** that show in every team (the existing show-in-children), with weeks inside; teams' term start and end follow them, shown as "Set by". **[call]**
   - **Day type:** a date range marked **Holiday · Staff day · Half day · Exam week** (school days are the rest). Days that aren't school days stop W1 sessions and S4 cover and duties. **[call]**
   - **Event:** an `event` item (section 16's kind, without its registration or budget) with title, date and time or range, type, **audience**, place, owner, status (Planned · Confirmed · Done · Cancelled), notes and a short checklist. Never on the board. **[call]**
   - **Audience:** Everyone · some teams · some roles (the announcement audience model). **[call]**
   - **Repeat:** weekly or every n weeks, skipping holidays and staff days. **[call]**
   - **Creating:**
     - + Event
     - click a day
     - Import… (CSV or .ics, with a preview)
     - duplicate an event
     - Start next year
     - CLI and agents (B13)
4. **Views:**

   | View | Where | On screen |
   |---|---|---|
   | **Year** | School Sprints | Months as rows from the year's start; day types as coloured cells with words on hover; terms marked |
   | **Month** | School and team Sprints | The Events Calendar grid; school items grey in teams |
   | **Upcoming** | School and team Sprints | A table: date, event, type, audience, place, owner, status; filters Mine, For me, type |
   | **This week at school** | Overview | Day types, events for me, the next holiday countdown |
   | **Public calendar** | School About | Public events and holidays only |
5. **Actions and flow:**
   - **Set up the school year** → terms → holidays and staff days → repeating events (staff briefing every Monday) → one-off events.
   - Each event can carry a checklist; items with an owner and date show in that person's My work.
   - **S3 deadlines** (staff hand-ins) appear on the calendar on their own; they're not typed twice.
   - **Changing term dates** warns "12 lessons in 3 teams need new sessions" (W2 call 5); nothing moves on its own.
   - **Start next year:** a new year with terms typed or imported; events that repeat or sit in a term week ("Week 3 of Term 1, Tue") are copied to the same place; one-off dated events are offered as a list to tick. **[call]**
   - **Subscribe:** each person gets a private .ics link for their own calendar (school plus team plus their events); it can be reset. **[call]**
6. **Surfaces:**
   - **Year strip:** a legend with words, "Term 1 · Week 6 of 15", the next holiday.
   - **Event card:** time, type chip, audience, place, 🌐 when public, checklist count ("2 of 4").
   - **Event page:** the one-scroll item page with audience, place, checklist and notes.
   - **Import preview:** rows matched to day types or events, with errors per row.
7. **Design spec:**
   - Reuse the Calendar view (14.2), the sprint rail, the item page, the announcement audience picker, `StatusBadge` and Overview cards.
   - Mono for dates; day-type colours always with words.
   - Lucide icons: CalendarRange, CalendarDays, PartyPopper, Coffee, Globe, Repeat.
   - Add a contract test.
8. **Words:**
   - School year · Term · Week · Holiday · Staff day · Half day · Exam week · Event · Deadline · Parents' evening · Trip · Audience · Everyone · For me · Mine · Show publicly · Subscribe · Set up the school year · Start next year · This week at school · Set by.
   - Never "Lead" or "Owner" (the event owner shows as "Organised by").
9. **Links:**
   - W1 sessions and W2 Term plan (holidays and staff days stop sessions; Week numbers)
   - W3 My work (events and checklist items for me)
   - W4 exam weeks
   - S2 (the year map's weeks), S3 (deadlines), S4 (no cover or duties on non-school days), S5 (meeting series)
   - announcements (an event can post one), the public About, search
10. **People:**

    | | Sees | Can do |
    |---|---|---|
    | School admin | Everything | The school year, day types, school events, the public calendar |
    | School leader | Everything | School events |
    | Head of department | Everything for them; their team | Team events; school events if allowed; "Show to the school" for a team event **[call]** |
    | Teacher, teaching assistant | Events for them, plus Show all | Team events if the team allows |
    | Office staff | Everything | School events, imports |
    | Visitor | Public events and holidays | Subscribe to the public feed |
11. **States:**
    - No year yet: Set up the school year.
    - Out of term: "Summer holiday · back Sep 2".
    - A cancelled event stays struck through, with the reason.
    - Import shows a preview before anything is saved.
12. **Edges:**
    - An event on a holiday gives a warning, but it's allowed.
    - Overlapping terms are refused.
    - A half day keeps sessions before its cut-off time.
    - Daylight-saving changes use the school's time zone.
    - Deleting a term with lessons asks where they go.
    - Several schools (trusts and districts) are parked.
13. **Phone:** Upcoming is the default on phones; the Year view becomes one month at a time; This week at school sits at the top of Overview.
14. **Accessibility:**
    - Day types as words as well as colour.
    - The Year view has a table alternative.
    - Events are a list per day for screen readers.
15. **Notifications:**
    - **Next week at school:** a **Summary** each Friday (or the last school day) with your events and day types. **[call]**
    - An event for you changed or cancelled within 48 hours: **Important**.
    - A checklist item given to you: **Normal**.
    - Nothing for each new event.
16. **Trust and data:**
    - No student data (32.1 point 3).
    - Public events show title, date, time and place only.
    - The public .ics feed carries only public items; personal .ics links are secret and can be reset.
    - Imports never fetch a URL from the server; the file is uploaded.
17. **Reuse vs new:**
    - **Reuse:** sprints with show-in-children, term dates and time zone on orgs, the announcement audience model, the Calendar view (14.2), the item page, Overview cards, `duplicateOrg` date shifting, the public About.
    - **New:**
      - the School year setup
      - day types (a small date-range table)
      - the `event` kind without its parked parts
      - repeat rules that skip non-school days (pure function)
      - the Year and Upcoming views
      - CSV and .ics import
      - personal and public .ics feeds
      - Start next year by week of term (pure function)
      - This week at school
18. **How we know it works:**
    - **Signal:** the share of schools with the whole year (terms and holidays) entered before the first day of term.
    - **Checks:**
      - repeats skip holidays and staff days
      - term changes warn and don't move lessons
      - week-of-term copying
      - audience filtering (server test)
      - the public feed holds only public items (server test)
      - import errors per row

**Organization steps:**
- **Level:**
  - School: the year, terms, day types, school events, the public calendar.
  - Team: its own events on top; the school's in grey.
  - Person: For me, This week at school, their .ics link.
- **Term moment:** summer (set up the year, import holidays) → first day of term → every week (Friday Summary, briefings) → each term's events (parents' evenings, exams) → end of year → Start next year.
- **Org tab:**
  - school Sprints (Year, Month, Upcoming)
  - team Sprints (Calendar)
  - Overview (This week at school)
  - About (public calendar)
  - Updates (an event can post an announcement)
  - Settings (School year)

**Calls agreed 2026-11-17:**
1. Terms are school sprints shown in every team; teams follow them ("Set by").
2. Holidays, staff days, half days and exam weeks are date ranges; non-school days stop sessions, cover and duties.
3. Events are `event` items without registration or budget, never on the board.
4. Audiences use the announcement model: everyone, teams or roles.
5. Repeating events skip holidays and staff days.
6. Start next year copies repeating and term-week events; one-off events are ticked from a list.
7. A personal .ics link per person, plus an optional public feed of public items; no live sync, only file import.
8. Public events are opt-in per event, shown on the school's About.
9. A head of department's team event shows to the whole school only when marked.
10. A Friday Summary instead of a notice per event; Important only for changes within 48 hours.

### 32.3 S2 · Curriculum map and lesson plans (agreed 2026-11-17)
**References** (from the 32.1 sort; 6 screens studied):

| Template | Rating | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **Teacher Curriculum Map** | **4.84 / 37** | **Main reference for the map:** a Map view with a **column per subject and a row per week**; each topic card has a status and three questions: *What skill should students learn? How will they show it? What activities will they do?* A Subjects table with "2 of 2 topics planned" and **% planned** |
| **Teacher Lesson Planner** | 4.89 / 122 | A page per subject: Lessons (status, name, date, **class**), views All · By class · Archive, and a month/week calendar |
| **Lesson Plan Organizer** | 4.84 / 92 | Lesson fields: subject, date, **days until the lesson**, grade, Draft → Ready, objectives · materials · activities |
| Teacher Curriculum Planner | 4.91 / 22 | Course → unit → lesson, with **% of the unit taught** |
| The Integrated Educator | 4.71 / 7 | Unit documents (Unit 1–6) beside the lessons calendar; aligned to standards |
| Teacher home · Lesson plans (Notion) | 4.83 / 183 · 4.76 / 163 | Already the W2 references (lessons by unit, status, standards) |

**Today:**
- **Built:** child workspaces under an org (creation rules, visibility caps); sprints nest and show in children; sprint materials; Required reading.
- **Agreed:**
  - **W2:** the Term plan (units → weeks → lessons), `class_lesson` with Planned → Ready → Taught, Before / In / After, teacher notes, outcomes and coverage, Shift the rest, Start next term
  - **S1:** school weeks and holidays
- **Missing:**
  - a map across several grades or subjects at once
  - one plan taught to several classes by several teachers
  - standards at the school
  - assessments without student copies
  - "how far each class has got"

**Agreed changes from an exact copy:**
1. **Subjects become course workspaces** (one per grade × subject, e.g. "Grade 6 Science") under the team. The map is the team's view across them.
2. The topic card's three questions become the **unit's** fields: Skill (outcomes and standards) · Evidence (the assessment) · Activities.
3. "% planned" stays as **Planned**; W2's "% taught" becomes **Taught per class**.
4. "Class" on a lesson becomes **per-class Taught ticks**: one plan, taught to 6A, 6B and 6C.
5. Video help strips and decoration are dropped.

**Levels:**
```
School  Northgate Primary          ← the school year (S1), standards, the lesson template
  └ Team org  "Science department"  ← heads of department, teachers; the Year map
       ├ Course workspace "Grade 6 Science"   ← units, lessons, classes 6A 6B 6C
       ├ Course workspace "Grade 7 Science"
       └ Course workspace "Grade 8 Science"
(A grade team works the same way: "Grade 5 team" → "Grade 5 English", "Grade 5 Maths" …)
```

```
TEAM · Science department · Sprints → [ Year map ] [ Calendar ]        Standards covered 41 of 48
           Term 1                                   │ ░ │ Term 2
           W1  W2  W3  W4  W5  W6  W7  W8  W9  W10  │half│ W1  W2 …
 Grade 6   ■ Cells ■■■■■■■ │■ Forces ■■■■■■ │A│      │    │ ■ Light ■■ …     Planned 92% · Taught 6A 7/10 6B 6/10 ⚠
 Grade 7   ■ Particles ■■■■■■■■ │■ Energy ■■■■│A│    │    │ …                Planned 70%
 Grade 8   ■ Atoms ■■■■■ │□ Reactions (draft) □□□□□ │    │ …                Planned 45% ⚠
 A = assessment week   ░ = holiday (Set by Northgate)

COURSE WORKSPACE · Grade 6 Science · Sprints → Term plan (W2)
 ▾ Unit 2 · Forces                     Skill: SC6.3, SC6.4 · Evidence: Forces test · Activities: 3
   W6 │ Balanced forces   Lesson · Ready      Taught 6A ✓ Oct 7 · 6B ✓ Oct 8 · 6C ·
   W7 │ Friction lab      Activity · Draft ⚠ in 2 days
   W8 │ Forces test       Assessment · Ready
```

**The 18 layers**
1. **Getting it:**
   - Every team org in a School gets a **Year map** in Sprints; every course workspace gets W2's **Term plan**.
   - **Head of department's first look:** "Add your courses" (one per grade or subject), each made from the school's **Course template**.
   - **Teacher's first look:** their courses, with the Term plan open on this week.
2. **Setting it up:**
   - **School: Settings → Teaching:**
     - **standards** (import from CSV: code, description, grade, subject)
     - the **lesson template** sections (default Objective · Starter · Main · Plenary · Support and stretch; or I do · We do · You do) **[call]**
     - plans need a review before Ready (off) **[call]**
     - the public curriculum overview (off)
   - **Team:** courses, the classes each course teaches (names from S4), the map's rows (grades or subjects).
3. **Items:**
   - **Course workspace:** a child workspace of the team, one per grade × subject. **[call]**
   - **Unit:** a sprint in the course (W2) with **Skill** (outcomes and standards), **Evidence** (its assessment) and **Activities**.
   - **Lesson:** W2's `class_lesson` with a **type**: Lesson · Assessment · Activity. An assessment is a planned lesson, never an assignment with student copies. **[call]**
   - **Taught:** a small record per lesson × class (date, by whom). **Ready is shared; Taught is per class.** **[call]**
   - **Class note:** an optional line per lesson × class ("6B: run the lab in two parts"), with no student names.
   - **Standard:** a row in the school's list, tagged on units and lessons. **[call]**
   - **Creating:**
     - + Course (from the Course template)
     - + New ▾ → Unit, Lesson, Assessment, Activity
     - drag on the map to make a unit across weeks
     - Duplicate a unit into another course
     - Start next year
     - CLI and agents (B13)
4. **Views:**

   | View | Where | On screen |
   |---|---|---|
   | **Year map** | Team Sprints | Rows = courses, columns = school weeks (S1); units as bars; assessment weeks; holidays; Planned %, Taught per class, Standards covered |
   | **Term plan** | Course Sprints | W2's table with lesson type, per-class Taught ticks, days until the lesson |
   | **Calendar** | Course and team Sprints | Lessons on school days with S1 events |
   | **Standards** | Team Sprints | Each standard → the units and lessons that cover it; "not covered yet" |
   | **My lessons this week** | My work (W3) | The teacher's lessons across courses: Draft ⚠, Ready, Taught |
   | **Curriculum overview** | School About (public, opt-in) | Unit titles per grade and term only |
5. **Actions and flow:**
   - **Before the year:** the head of department sketches units on the map → teachers fill lessons → (if on) **Request review** → Ready.
   - **Each week:** teachers open My lessons → finish Draft lessons ("in 2 days" ⚠) → after teaching, **Mark taught** for their class.
   - **Pacing:** **Behind the map** per class = lessons planned by today − taught by today, shown to the head and leaders. **[call]**
   - **Share across courses:** Duplicate a unit or lesson into another course.
   - **Start next year:** course workspaces are copied into the new year (S1 call 6, by week of term); lessons go back to Planned; Taught ticks and class notes aren't copied. **[call]**
6. **Surfaces:**
   - **Map bars:** unit name, Draft (outline) or Ready (filled), the assessment marker, standards count on hover.
   - **Row summary:** Planned %, Taught per class with ⚠ when two or more lessons behind.
   - **Lesson row:** type chip, status, days until it, per-class ticks.
   - **Lesson page:** W2's page with the school's template sections, standards, materials, class notes.
7. **Design spec:**
   - Reuse the W2 Term plan and lesson page, the sprint rail, the Calendar view (14.2), child workspace creation, Duplicate, `StatusBadge` and the progress bar.
   - The map is a new grid view of sprints across child workspaces; bars use the sprint colours.
   - Lucide icons: Map, BookOpen, Target, ClipboardCheck, Shapes.
   - Add a contract test.
8. **Words:**
   - Year map · Course · Unit · Skill · Evidence · Activities · Lesson · Assessment · Activity · Draft · Ready · Taught · Mark taught · Planned · Behind the map · Standards · Standards covered · Not covered yet · Class note · Lesson template · Curriculum overview.
   - Never "Lead"; no student words in staff-only schools (no "hand in", "submissions" or "grades" here).
9. **Links:**
   - S1 (weeks, holidays, assessment weeks) · S3 (Request review on units and lessons; plans due) · S4 (classes and the timetable; a cover teacher opens the lesson) · S5 (department meetings review the map)
   - W2 (all lesson parts) · W3 (My lessons) · Files (materials) · search
10. **People:**

    | | Sees | Can do |
    |---|---|---|
    | School leader | Every team's map, Planned and Behind the map | Standards, the lesson template, the public overview |
    | Head of department | Their team's map and every course | Make courses, sketch units, review, see pacing |
    | Teacher | Their team's map; courses they're in | Plan lessons, mark taught for their classes, class notes |
    | Teaching assistant | Ready lessons for their classes | Read, add materials if allowed |
    | Office staff | Nothing by default | — |
    | Visitor | The curriculum overview, if public | — |
11. **States:**
    - No courses: "Add your courses."
    - Map rows load one course at a time.
    - Draft lessons in the next 3 school days show ⚠.
    - A finished year is read-only.
12. **Edges:**
    - A class taught by two teachers: either can tick Taught.
    - A lesson moved to another week keeps its ticks.
    - A holiday added mid-term warns "4 lessons need new days" (S1).
    - A standard removed from the list stays on old lessons, marked "retired".
    - A course with no classes still plans; Taught is hidden.
13. **Phone:** the map becomes a list per course with its units in order; the Term plan is W2's phone list; Mark taught is a big button per class.
14. **Accessibility:**
    - The map has a table alternative (course × term → units).
    - Planned and Taught as text.
    - Drag on the map has a menu ("Move to week…").
15. **Notifications:**
    - Lesson still Draft 2 school days before: **Normal**, to the teacher, once.
    - Review requested or done: S3's notices.
    - Behind the map by 3 or more lessons: in the head's weekly **Summary**.
    - Nothing to the whole team for each lesson change.
16. **Trust and data:**
    - Plans and class notes hold no student names (32.1 point 3); the lesson template's "Support and stretch" is about groups, not named children.
    - The public overview shows unit titles only.
    - Imports are uploaded files; nothing is fetched.
17. **Reuse vs new:**
    - **Reuse:** W2 entirely, child workspaces, sprints shown in children, Duplicate, the Calendar view, My work, Files.
    - **New:**
      - the Course template
      - the Year map view across child workspaces
      - lesson types
      - per-class Taught ticks and class notes
      - the school standards list and coverage
      - the lesson template setting
      - Behind the map (pure function)
      - the public curriculum overview
18. **How we know it works:**
    - **Signal:** the share of lessons that are Ready at least one school day before they're taught.
    - **Checks:**
      - per-class Taught and Behind the map
      - Start next year copying (no ticks, no notes)
      - standards coverage counts
      - the public overview shows titles only (server test)
      - holidays push lessons only with a warning

**Organization steps:**
- **Level:**
  - School: standards, the lesson template, the public overview, every team's pacing.
  - Team: the Year map, courses, review.
  - Course workspace: units and lessons.
  - Teacher: My lessons this week.
- **Term moment:** summer (map and units) → the week before (lessons Ready) → every week (teach, Mark taught) → half-term (Behind the map, adjust) → end of year → Start next year.
- **Org tab:**
  - team Sprints (Year map, Standards)
  - course Sprints (Term plan)
  - Projects (the team's courses)
  - Overview (this week's Draft lessons; the head's pacing card)
  - Settings (Teaching, at the school)

**Calls agreed 2026-11-17:**
1. School → team org → course workspaces; the plan lives in the course workspace.
2. The Year map is the team's view across its courses, by school week.
3. Lessons have a type (Lesson · Assessment · Activity); assessments never make student copies.
4. Ready is shared; Taught is ticked per class.
5. Standards are a school list imported from CSV, tagged on units and lessons.
6. The school sets the lesson template's sections; teams can add their own.
7. Review before Ready is off by default and uses S3's queue when on.
8. Behind the map is per class, for heads and leaders, with no ranking of teachers.
9. The public curriculum overview is opt-in and shows unit titles only.
10. Start next year copies courses by week of term, without Taught ticks or class notes.

### 32.4 S3 · Staff hand-ins and reviews (agreed 2026-11-17)
**References** (12 more searches on approvals and deadlines found 117 templates; few are rated, and 3 were studied from their screenshots):

| Template | Rating | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **Async Doc Reviews** (Notion) | **5.0 / 5** | **Main reference for the review:** a docs table with Reviewed by and a status (Proposed · Accepted · Rejected); views All docs · By type · **By author** · By status |
| **Deadline & Test Tracker** | 4.83 / 54 | **Main reference for deadlines:** due date, **days left or "36 days overdue"**, subject, a done tick; cards per area |
| Teacher Productivity Hub | 4.87 / 23 | A Task & admin tracker beside the lesson board |
| Team Hub | 4.75 / 8 | Team members above a timeline of work |

**Today (built):**
- Assignments target **everyone, a role, people, teams, each child workspace** or chosen children, with publish times, late rules and **reviewers**.
- Hand-ins keep **versions** with files, a link, text and a note.
- The **Review queue** (Lanes · One at a time) has Approve, Approve with a note, Return with a reason and Fix by, recent reasons, keys and private feedback.
- My work lists every copy; Required reading has read counts.
- **Missing:**
  - handing in something that lives in NB (a unit, a lesson, a document)
  - a second approver
  - repeating deadlines by school week
  - a deadline clash check
  - policy sign-off
  - staff-friendly words

**Agreed changes from an exact copy:**
1. Proposed · Accepted · Rejected become the existing **Waiting for review · Approved · Returned**.
2. By author becomes **By person** (heads only) and **By team** (leaders, as counts).
3. "36 days overdue" becomes **Overdue** for the person and their reviewer only; there's no public overdue list.
4. Subject and area cards become the **team** and **course** the hand-in belongs to.

```
TEAM · Science department · Tasks → [ Assignments ] [ Review queue ]            + Hand-in ▾
 Hand-in                     For            Due          Handed in  Waiting  Approved  Returned
 Unit 3 plan                 Each course    Oct 10 (Fri)  2 of 3      1        1         0
 Lab safety sign-off         Everyone       Sep 12        12 of 12    —        12        —
 Year 8 test for checking    Grade 8 course Nov 21        0 of 1      —        —         —
 Due date check: "3 other staff deadlines for Science teachers in Week 6"

REVIEW QUEUE · One at a time (head of department)
┌ Grade 6 Science · Unit 3 Forces (handed in Oct 9, version 2) ┬ Decision ──────────────┐
│ Skill SC6.3 SC6.4 · Evidence: Forces test · 8 lessons        │ ✎ "Add a practical…"    │
│ (the frozen unit, read-only, with comments)                  │ [ Return ]  [ Approve ▾ ]│
│                                                              │  ☑ Mark its lessons Ready│
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────┘

SCHOOL · Tasks → Deadlines (leaders)       Week 6: Science 3 · English 1 · Maths 2  ⚠ heavy week
 Trip risk assessment · Grade 5 zoo trip     Head of Grade 5 ✓ → Visits coordinator (waiting)
```

**The 18 layers**
1. **Getting it:**
   - In a School, the Tasks tab's + New ▾ says **Hand-in**, with templates from the school's library.
   - **Head of department's first look:** an empty Assignments list with "Ask for unit plans" (the Unit plan template set to **each course**).
   - **Teacher's first look:** My work with "Due this week".
2. **Setting it up:**
   - **School: Settings → Hand-ins:**
     - the **hand-in templates**: Unit plan · Scheme of work · Assessment paper for checking · Trip risk assessment · Policy sign-off · Training record · Cover work (S4)
     - **quiet weeks** (S1 weeks where no new staff deadline should fall, e.g. report or exam weeks) **[call]**
     - who sees counts across teams (leaders)
   - **Per hand-in:**
     - who it's for
     - what to hand in
     - due date or **repeat by school week** ("Week 5 of every half-term") **[call]**
     - reviewers
     - "Then approved by" **[call]**
3. **Items:**
   - **Hand-in:** the existing assignment, aimed at staff. In a staff-only school, **each child** means each course workspace.
   - **New hand-in type, NB item:** a unit, lesson or document from the person's course; handing it in **freezes a read-only version** (beside file, link and text). **[call]**
   - **Reviewers:** the team's heads of department by default; school-wide hand-ins name their reviewers.
   - **Second approver:** an optional "Then approved by" step after the first Approve; at most two steps. **[call]**
   - **Sign-off:** a Required reading document with an **I've read this** button that keeps the date; it's a hand-in with nothing to upload. **[call]**
   - **Creating:**
     - + Hand-in (from a template or blank)
     - Duplicate
     - repeat by school week
     - Start next year (repeating hand-ins move on; one-offs are offered as a list)
4. **Views:**

   | View | Who | On screen |
   |---|---|---|
   | **Assignments** (team Tasks) | Heads | Hand-ins with counts: handed in, waiting, approved, returned |
   | **By person** | Heads | Each teacher's hand-ins and states for their team |
   | **Review queue** | Reviewers | Lanes and One at a time (existing), with frozen NB items shown in place |
   | **Deadlines** (school Tasks) | Leaders | Staff deadlines by week, as counts per team, with heavy weeks ⚠ |
   | **My work** | Everyone | Their hand-ins: Due, Overdue, Returned (Fix by) |
   | **Calendar** (S1) | Everyone | Deadlines on their days |
5. **Actions and flow:**
   - **Ask:** pick a template → who it's for → due date (the **clash check** lists other staff deadlines that week for the same people and warns in quiet weeks; it never blocks) → publish. **[call]**
   - **Hand in:** from My work or from the unit itself (**Hand in this unit**) → the version freezes.
   - **Review:** Approve (optionally **Mark its lessons Ready**, linking S2 call 7) · Approve with a note · Return with a reason and Fix by.
   - **Second step:** the second approver gets it only after the first Approve; a Return at either step goes back to the person.
   - **Sign-off:** open the document → I've read this → done.
6. **Surfaces:**
   - **Counts row** on each hand-in.
   - **Due chip:** "in 3 days", "today", "Overdue" (only for the person and reviewers).
   - **Decision panel:** the existing ReviewDecision, plus the Ready tick for units.
   - **Step line:** "Head of Grade 5 ✓ → Visits coordinator (waiting)".
   - **Heavy week ⚠** in Deadlines.
7. **Design spec:**
   - Reuse the assignment master and copies, the New module (28.11), the Review queue, `ReviewDecision`, Required reading, My work and the S1 Calendar.
   - Lucide icons: Inbox, FileCheck2, Stamp, CalendarClock, ShieldCheck.
   - Add a contract test.
8. **Words:**
   - Hand-in · Hand in this unit · Due · Overdue · Waiting for review · Approved · Returned · Fix by · Then approved by · Sign-off · I've read this · Quiet week · Heavy week · By person · Deadlines.
   - In staff-only schools, **"Overdue" replaces "Missing" and "Late"**; never "Lead". **[call]**
9. **Links:**
   - S1 (school weeks, quiet weeks, the calendar) · S2 (units and lessons handed in; Ready on approval) · S4 (cover work as a hand-in) · S5 (development records)
   - Required reading · private feedback · My work · document versions
10. **People:**

    | | Sees | Can do |
    |---|---|---|
    | School leader | Counts per team; the hand-ins they review | Ask school-wide; templates; quiet weeks |
    | Head of department | Their team's hand-ins and states by person | Ask, review, approve |
    | Teacher | Their own hand-ins | Hand in, see feedback, fix and hand in again |
    | Teaching assistant | Their own hand-ins (e.g. sign-offs) | The same |
    | Office staff | Hand-ins they're asked to review (e.g. training records) | Review |
    | Visitor | Nothing | — |
11. **States:**
    - Draft (not published), Scheduled, Open, Closed (existing).
    - Each copy: Due · Handed in · Waiting for review · Approved · Returned · Overdue · Excused.
    - A frozen version stays readable after the unit changes ("Changed since handed in").
12. **Edges:**
    - A teacher on leave: **Excuse** (existing) with the Away reason.
    - A teacher joining mid-year gets open hand-ins that aren't past due (existing late-joiner rule).
    - A course with two teachers: one hand-in for the course; either can hand in.
    - The second approver leaving: "No approver" ⚠ to the asker.
    - A repeating hand-in that lands on a holiday moves to the last school day before it.
13. **Phone:** sign-offs and approvals work on a phone; frozen units show as the W2 phone list.
14. **Accessibility:**
    - States as words.
    - The clash check is read out as a list.
    - Steps as text ("step 1 of 2 approved").
15. **Notifications:**
    - The existing assignment notices (published, due soon, returned, approved).
    - Waiting for your review: in the reviewer's daily **Summary**, not one per hand-in.
    - Your step is next (second approver): **Normal**.
    - Overdue: one **Normal** reminder to the person, never to the team.
16. **Trust and data:**
    - Hand-ins are seen only by the person, their reviewers and the asker; leaders see counts.
    - Training records and other personal files follow the same rule.
    - **No student data:** report comments, data drops and pupil lists aren't hand-in templates (32.1 point 3).
    - Staff records (background checks, contracts, pay) are parked.
    - AI agents can draft a unit or a sign-off note for the person, but never approve or return.
17. **Reuse vs new:**
    - **Reuse:** assignments and copies, every target mode, reviewers, the Review queue and `ReviewDecision`, versions, Excuse and Away, late joiners, Required reading, My work.
    - **New:**
      - the NB item hand-in type with frozen versions
      - the second approver step
      - repeat by school week (pure function)
      - the clash check and quiet weeks (pure function)
      - I've read this
      - the Deadlines view
      - staff words in staff-only schools
      - the hand-in template library
18. **How we know it works:**
    - **Signal:** the median time from hand-in to a decision.
    - **Checks:**
      - frozen versions don't change with the unit
      - the second step only after the first Approve
      - leaders receive counts, not names (server test)
      - repeats skip holidays
      - the clash check counts the right people
      - "Missing" never shows in a staff-only school

**Organization steps:**
- **Level:**
  - School: templates, quiet weeks, school-wide hand-ins, counts.
  - Team: hand-ins for its people and courses, reviews by heads.
  - Person: My work.
- **Term moment:** before the year (templates, repeating hand-ins) → every half-term (unit plans) → trips (risk assessments) → policy changes (sign-offs) → exam season (papers for checking) → end of year (schemes of work) → Start next year.
- **Org tab:**
  - Tasks (Assignments, Review queue, Deadlines) — the centre of S3
  - Sprints (the S1 calendar shows deadlines)
  - Documents (sign-offs)
  - Overview (Due this week; Waiting for your review)
  - Settings (Hand-ins)

**Calls agreed 2026-11-17:**
1. Staff hand-ins are the existing assignments; "each child" means each course.
2. A new hand-in type hands in a unit, lesson or document and freezes its version.
3. An optional second approver, at most two steps.
4. Approving a unit can mark its lessons Ready.
5. Hand-ins can repeat by school week.
6. The clash check warns about busy weeks and quiet weeks, and never blocks.
7. Sign-off is Required reading with I've read this.
8. States are seen by the person and their reviewers; leaders see counts; there's no public overdue list.
9. "Overdue" replaces "Missing" and "Late" for staff.

### 32.5 S4 · Timetable, cover and duties (agreed 2026-11-17)
**References** (14 more searches on timetables, cover and rotas found 121 templates; 5 studied from their screenshots):

| Template | Rating | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **Quick Class Schedule** | **4.87 / 231** | **Main reference for a person's week:** a column per day; each card has the course, time, teacher, room and a type chip |
| My Class Schedule | 4.82 / 743 | Calm day columns with coloured blocks (title and time) |
| **Timetable** | 4.70 / 188 | **Main reference for the school grid:** periods down the side (08:30–09:30 …) × days across, with **Break** and **Lunch** rows |
| Employee Shift Scheduling | 4.58 / 12 | Ongoing shifts (who, time range), a monthly overview, Alerts; Schedules · Employees · Settings |
| **K-8 Substitute Teacher Homepage** | 4.83 / 18 | **Main reference for cover:** a card per grade holding that class's notes and links for the cover teacher |

**Today:**
- **Built:**
  - **Away** (`org_member_away`): a person's absence with start, end, reason and who recorded it; it already excuses their hand-ins.
  - Org roles, Members, the member drawer.
- **Agreed:**
  - W1 meets → sessions (for adult classes)
  - S1 school days, holidays and staff days
  - S2 courses, classes as names, lessons
  - S3 the Cover work hand-in template
- **Missing:**
  - the school day's periods
  - a timetable of who teaches which class where
  - cover for an absence
  - a duty rota
  - "your day" for each person

**Agreed changes from an exact copy:**
1. A personal schedule becomes **My timetable**, worked out from the school timetable; nobody types their own.
2. The periods grid becomes the **school's day pattern** with break and lunch rows, used everywhere.
3. Shifts become **duties** (place × time × person) and **cover slots**.
4. The substitute homepage becomes a **Cover info** page per class, plus the planned lesson (S2) opened automatically.
5. Phone numbers and emergency contacts on shifts are dropped (staff contact details stay in profiles).

```
SCHOOL · Sprints → Timetable        By [ Teacher ▾ ]  Week A │ B                 Import…
            Mon            Tue            Wed           Thu           Fri
 P1 08:30   6A Science     8C Science     —             6B Science    7A Science
            Lab 2          Lab 2                        Lab 2         Lab 1
 Break 09:30 ───────────────────────── Duty: Playground (Mon) ─────────────────────
 P2 09:50   —              6A Science     7B Science    …

SCHOOL · Members → [ Roster ] [ Away and cover ] [ Duties ]        Today · Tue Oct 14
 Away today  Ms Rao (all day) · Mr Das (P3–P4)
 Cover       P1 8C Science Lab 2   Mr Khan ✓ (free, Science, 2 covers this term)
             P3 6B Maths Rm 14     ⚠ open   Suggest: Ms Iyer (free, 1) · Mr Bose (free, 3)
             Break Playground duty Ms Sen ✓
 Filled 5 of 6

TEACHER · Overview → Your day (Tue)
 P1 Cover 8C Science · Lab 2 → lesson "Friction lab" (Ready) · cover note
 P2 6A Science · Lab 2 · "Balanced forces"
 Lunch  Duty: Lunch hall
```

**The 18 layers**
1. **Getting it:**
   - A School gets **Timetable** in Sprints and **Away and cover** and **Duties** in Members.
   - **Office's first look:** Set up the school day (periods) → Import the timetable (CSV from the school's timetabling system) → Duties.
   - **Teacher's first look:** **Your day** on Overview and My timetable.
2. **Setting it up (School: Settings → Timetable):**
   - **day patterns:** periods with times, plus break and lunch; more than one pattern if days differ (short Fridays) **[call]**
   - **rotation:** one week, or Week A / Week B
   - **rooms:** a simple list
   - **cover managers:** who arranges cover (a label on admins or office staff)
   - duty places (Playground, Gate, Lunch hall, Bus bay)
3. **Items:**
   - **Class:** a name (6A), its grade and an optional size, on the team; no students (32.1 point 3). **[call]**
   - **Period:** name and times in a day pattern.
   - **Timetable slot:** day × period (× week A/B) → class, course workspace, teacher(s), room. NB doesn't build timetables: slots are **imported from CSV** or typed. **[call]**
   - **Change:** a one-off "today only" change to a slot (room swap, cancelled lesson).
   - **Absence:** the existing **Away** record, now with periods (whole day or P3–P4); the reason is seen only by cover managers and leaders. **[call]**
   - **Cover slot:** a timetable slot or duty hit by an absence, with the cover person and a cover note.
   - **Duty:** place × day × time (break, lunch, before or after school) × person, repeating with the rotation.
   - **Cover info:** one document per class with routines, where things are and what to do in an emergency; never student names or medical details. **[call]**
4. **Views:**

   | View | Where | On screen |
   |---|---|---|
   | **Timetable** | School Sprints | The periods grid by teacher, class or room; Week A / B |
   | **My timetable** | Person (Overview link, My work) | Day columns with cards: course, class, room |
   | **Your day** | Overview | Today's lessons, covers and duties in order, with each lesson's plan |
   | **Away and cover** | School Members | Today's absences, cover slots filled or open with suggestions; any date |
   | **Duties** | School Members | Places × days grid with people; swaps |
   | **Free now** | School Members | Who's free this period (for cover managers) |
5. **Actions and flow:**
   - **Report an absence:** the person (or the office) adds Away with days or periods → its slots and duties become **open cover slots**.
   - **Arrange cover:** for each open slot the manager sees **suggestions**: free that period → same department → fewest covers this term. The manager picks; nothing is assigned on its own. **[call]**
   - **The cover lesson:** the cover person opens the slot → the class's **planned lesson** for that day (S2) and the **cover note** the absent teacher left (or the S3 Cover work hand-in). If the lesson isn't Ready, the head of department gets ⚠. **[call]**
   - **Duty swap:** a person asks a colleague to swap → the colleague accepts → done; the manager is told, with no approval step. **[call]**
   - **Today only** changes for room swaps and cancellations; non-school days (S1) have no slots or duties.
   - **Sessions:** a course's sessions come from its timetable slots × school days, so S2 lessons know their dates. **[call]**
6. **Surfaces:**
   - **Cover board:** "Filled 5 of 6", open slots first, suggestion chips with reasons ("free, Science, 2 covers").
   - **Your day:** a list in time order with the lesson title and a Ready or Draft chip.
   - **Duty grid:** places down the side, days across, names in cells, Week A / B tabs.
   - **Cover info page:** headings for Routines · Where things are · Emergencies.
7. **Design spec:**
   - Reuse Away, the Members frame, the W6 grid pattern, the W2 lesson page, Overview cards, the S1 calendar and CSV import patterns.
   - Mono for times; day columns follow the Quick Class Schedule cards in NB parts.
   - Lucide icons: Clock, Grid3x3, UserX, Repeat2, ShieldAlert, MapPin.
   - Add a contract test.
8. **Words:**
   - Timetable · Period · Break · Lunch · Day pattern · Week A · Week B · Room · Class · Your day · My timetable · Away · Cover · Cover slot · Open · Filled · Cover note · Cover info · Free now · Duty · Swap · Today only.
   - Never "substitute" as a role name (it's **Cover**, renameable to Supply or Substitute); never "Lead".
9. **Links:**
   - S1 (school days; staff days have no slots) · S2 (courses, classes, the planned lesson; sessions) · S3 (the Cover work hand-in) · S5 (meetings on the timetable, e.g. department time)
   - Away (excuses hand-ins as today) · My work (W3 Week shows covers and duties) · the member drawer
10. **People:**

    | | Sees | Can do |
    |---|---|---|
    | Cover manager | Everything, including absence reasons | Set up periods and duties, import, arrange cover |
    | School leader | Everything, including reasons | The same |
    | Head of department | Their team's timetable and cover; not reasons | Leave cover notes for their teachers' classes |
    | Teacher, teaching assistant | The whole timetable; their day; their own covers count | Report their absence, leave a cover note, ask for a duty swap |
    | Cover only (outside supply staff) | Their cover slots, each lesson's plan and cover info | Read; leave a short note for the class teacher **[call]** |
    | Visitor | Nothing | — |
11. **States:**
    - No periods yet: Set up the school day.
    - An open cover slot within 30 minutes turns red.
    - Filled, Open, Cancelled (the lesson won't run).
    - An import preview shows clashes before saving.
12. **Edges:**
    - **Clashes** (one teacher or room in two places) are shown on import and edit, but not blocked.
    - Two teachers on one slot: either can cover the other.
    - A half day (S1) drops periods after its cut-off.
    - An absence added after cover was arranged keeps the arrangement and flags it.
    - A teacher leaving mid-year: their slots show "No teacher" ⚠.
    - Start next year: periods, rooms, duty places and cover info are copied; the timetable is imported fresh.
13. **Phone:** Your day is the phone's home card; the cover board works one slot per row with a big Assign; the grid becomes one day at a time.
14. **Accessibility:**
    - The timetable is a real table with period and day headers.
    - States as words (Open, Filled).
    - Suggestions read with their reasons.
15. **Notifications:**
    - Cover given to you: **Important**, at once, with room and lesson.
    - A duty swap asked of you: **Normal**; accepted: **Normal** to the asker.
    - Your day changed (cover, room, cancelled): **Normal** at 07:00 or at once if it's today; nothing on ordinary days. **[call]**
    - An open cover slot 30 minutes before: **Important** to cover managers.
16. **Trust and data:**
    - No student data: classes are names; cover info holds no names or medical details.
    - Absence reasons are private to cover managers and leaders.
    - Cover counts are seen by the manager and the person, **never as a ranking**. **[call]**
    - Cover only accounts see nothing outside their slots (server test).
    - Imports are uploaded files; no live link to the timetabling system.
17. **Reuse vs new:**
    - **Reuse:** Away, Members and the member drawer, the W6 grid, S1 school days, S2 lessons, the S3 Cover work template, Overview cards, My work.
    - **New:**
      - day patterns, periods and rooms
      - classes as names
      - timetable slots, today-only changes and CSV import
      - absences by period
      - cover slots and suggestions (pure function)
      - duties and swaps
      - Cover info pages
      - Your day and My timetable
      - the Cover only role
      - sessions from slots (pure function)
18. **How we know it works:**
    - **Signal:** the share of cover slots filled at least 30 minutes before the period.
    - **Checks:**
      - suggestions never offer someone busy that period
      - no slots or duties on non-school days
      - Week A / B rotation
      - absence reasons stay private (server test)
      - Cover only access (server test)
      - swaps need the other person's yes
      - import clash detection

**Organization steps:**
- **Level:**
  - School: periods, rooms, the timetable, absences, cover, duties.
  - Team: its classes and slots; cover notes for its classes.
  - Person: Your day, My timetable, their covers and duties.
- **Term moment:** summer (periods, import the timetable, duties) → first day (Your day) → every morning (absences, cover by 08:00) → each break and lunch (duties) → timetable changes at term start → Start next year.
- **Org tab:**
  - school Sprints (Timetable)
  - school Members (Away and cover, Duties, Free now)
  - Overview (Your day; the cover board for managers)
  - Documents (Cover info per class)
  - Settings (Timetable)

**Calls agreed 2026-11-17:**
1. Classes are names with an optional size; no students.
2. The school day is periods in one or more day patterns, with an optional Week A / B.
3. NB doesn't build timetables: slots are imported from CSV or typed, with today-only changes.
4. A course's sessions come from its timetable slots × school days.
5. Absences reuse Away, by day or period; reasons are private to cover managers and leaders.
6. Cover suggestions: free that period → same department → fewest covers; the manager picks.
7. The cover lesson opens the class's planned lesson and the cover note; not Ready warns the head.
8. Outside supply staff join as Cover only.
9. Duty swaps need the other person's yes, not a manager's approval.
10. Cover info pages never hold student names or medical details.
11. Notices only when your day changes; Important for cover given to you.
12. Cover counts are never shown as a ranking.

### 32.6 S5 · Staff meetings and growth (agreed 2026-11-17)
**References** (13 more searches on meetings, reviews and development found 124 templates; 4 studied from their screenshots, plus 2 from earlier rounds):

| Template | Rating | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **Meeting notes** (Notion) | **4.85 / 367** | **Main reference for meetings:** one list of all meetings, each tagged by type, with who was there and the date; List · By meeting type |
| **Team Meeting Notes** | 5.0 / 21 | Upcoming meetings · **By team / department** · **Decision log** · **Action tracker**; status, date, team, length |
| **Performance Review** (Notion) | **4.82 / 22** | **Main reference for the year review:** For · Reviewer · Date, then Targets from the last review → Self-reflection (what's going well, what isn't) → Manager feedback → Development plan → Action points |
| Career pack | 4.89 / 91 | 1 on 1 · Performance reviews · **Achievement log** |
| 1x1 Meeting · Staff 1:1 Meeting Notes | 4.91 / 44 · 4.75 / 4 | The running 1:1 page (already C5's Check-in) |
| Professional Development tracker | 5.0 / 6 | Training ideas and a record of what was done |

**Today:**
- **Built:** announcements with audiences and levels; Required reading; chat canvas meeting templates (notes, status, retro, decision); org roles.
- **Agreed:**
  - 11.6 meeting types with action items, decisions, and 1:1s private even from admins
  - 11.4 objectives
  - C5 the running Check-in document, Raise a concern
  - S1 staff days and repeating events; S4 timetable slots
- **Missing:**
  - school meeting types
  - who manages whom
  - staff goals and a year review
  - lesson observations as feedback
  - a development log

**Agreed changes from an exact copy:**
1. Manager feedback's skill headings become the school's own **review headings** (renameable); there are **no ratings**.
2. "Reviewer" becomes the person's **line manager** (a label).
3. Achievement log becomes the **Development log** (training, reading, observations given and received).
4. Decision log and Action tracker are the existing 11.6 decisions and action items.

```
SCHOOL · Documents → Meetings      [ All ] [ By team ] [ Decisions ] [ Actions ]      + Meeting ▾
 Mon 08:15  Briefing                    All staff        notices only (Updates)
 Tue 15:30  Science department meeting  Science · 8      Agenda ✓ · 3 actions · 1 decision
 Thu 16:00  Line management · Ms Rao ↔ Mr Khan  (private)

PERSON · My growth (Overview link)                              Year 2026–27
 Goals (with Ms Rao)   ● Practical work in Grade 7 (on track) ● Coach a new colleague (at risk)
 Observations          Oct 14 · P3 6A Science · by Ms Rao · focus: Questioning
                       Strengths "Wait time…" · Next step "Hinge question before the lab"
 Development log       Sep 2 Staff day: Retrieval practice (3 h) ✓ · Reading: Rosenshine …
 Year review           Due Jun 20 · Self-reflection (draft)

SCHOOL · Members → Growth (leaders, counts only)
 Science  goals set 8 of 8 · mid-year check-ins 6 · observations 11 · development hours 64
```

**The 18 layers**
1. **Getting it:**
   - A School gets **school meeting types** in the New module and **My growth** for every staff member.
   - **School admin's first look:** set **Reports to** for each person (or import a CSV), then the review headings and observation focus list.
   - **Teacher's first look:** My growth with "Set up to 3 goals with Ms Rao".
2. **Setting it up (School: Settings → Staff growth):**
   - **Reports to** for each person (the line manager) **[call]**
   - review headings (default What's going well · What to work on · Development plan)
   - **observation focus list** (e.g. Questioning, Behaviour routines, Feedback, Practical work; renameable)
   - **notice for observations** (2 school days by default) **[call]**
   - the year review window (e.g. Jun 1–30)
3. **Items:**
   - **Meeting:** an 11.6 meeting document with a **school type**: Department meeting · Leadership meeting · Line management (C5's running Check-in) · Training session. Agendas, notes, **decisions** and **action items** (they become tasks). **[call]**
   - **Briefing:** daily or weekly notices are **announcements** with an audience (exists), not meeting documents; a meeting is made only when people meet. **[call]**
   - **Goal:** an 11.4 objective, up to 3 per person per year, kept to the person and their line manager. **[call]**
   - **Year review:** a document per person per year from the review template; self-reflection first, then the line manager's part, then the development plan. **No ratings, scores or pay outcomes.** **[call]**
   - **Observation:** observer, observed, a timetable slot (S4), a focus, **Strengths** and **One next step**; feedback only. **[call]**
   - **Development entry:** a training session, reading, course or visit with date, hours and a reflection; an optional certificate through S3's Training record.
4. **Views:**

   | View | Where | On screen |
   |---|---|---|
   | **Meetings** | Documents (school and team) | All · By team · Decisions · Actions |
   | **My growth** | Person (Overview link) | Goals, observations, development log, year review |
   | **My people** | Line managers | Each report's goals, last 1:1, observations, review state |
   | **Growth** | School Members (leaders) | Counts per team: goals set, check-ins, observations, development hours, reviews done |
   | **Calendar** | S1 | Meetings and training sessions on their days |
5. **Actions and flow:**
   - **Meetings:** + Meeting → type → audience → agenda (from the type's template) → notes, decisions, actions → actions become tasks in My work.
   - **Department time:** a repeating meeting in the team, shown on S1 and on the S4 timetable.
   - **Goals:** the person drafts → talks it through in Line management → both mark it agreed → check-ins update the status.
   - **Observation:** book it on a timetable slot with notice → the observed teacher sees the focus → after the lesson, Strengths and One next step → **the observed teacher reads it first**, then it goes to their line manager. A **peer observation** can be marked "Just between us". **[call]**
   - **Training:** a training session on an S1 staff day → people tick **I attended** → it lands in their development log with its hours.
   - **Year review:** in the window, the person writes the self-reflection → the line manager adds theirs → both agree the development plan → the next year's goals start from it.
6. **Surfaces:**
   - **Meeting list rows:** type chip, team, agenda, action and decision counts.
   - **My growth:** four cards, a year switcher.
   - **Observation form:** focus, Strengths, One next step; no score fields.
   - **Growth counts** per team for leaders.
7. **Design spec:**
   - Reuse the 11.6 meeting documents, C5's Check-in, 11.4 objectives, announcements, the S1 Calendar, S4 slots, the S3 Training record and Overview cards.
   - Lucide icons: Users, Sprout, Eye, NotebookPen, Target.
   - Add a contract test.
8. **Words:**
   - Meeting · Department meeting · Leadership meeting · Line management · Training session · Briefing · Reports to · Goal · Year review · What's going well · What to work on · Development plan · Observation · Focus · Strengths · One next step · Peer observation · Just between us · Development log · I attended · My growth · My people.
   - **Never** "grade", "rating", "score", "Outstanding", "Requires improvement", "performance" as a label on a person, or "Lead".
9. **Links:**
   - S1 (staff days, repeating meetings) · S2 (the department meeting reviews the Year map) · S3 (Training record; actions with due dates) · S4 (observation slots; department time)
   - C5 (the running 1:1) · 11.4 objectives · 11.6 meetings · announcements · My work
10. **People:**

    | | Sees | Can do |
    |---|---|---|
    | School leader | Counts per team; full detail only for people who report to them | Settings; meetings; observe |
    | Line manager | Their reports' goals, 1:1s, observations, reviews | Agree goals, write their part of reviews, observe |
    | Teacher, teaching assistant, office staff | Their own growth; meetings they're in | Draft goals, self-reflect, log development, observe peers |
    | Observer (any staff) | Observations they wrote | Write Strengths and One next step |
    | Visitor | Nothing | — |
11. **States:**
    - Goals: Draft · Agreed · On track · At risk · Done.
    - Year review: Not started · Self-reflection · Line manager · Agreed.
    - Observations: Booked · Written · Read.
12. **Edges:**
    - A line manager changes mid-year: goals and reviews move with the person; old 1:1s stay readable to the person only.
    - Someone with two line managers (part-time roles): both see, and either can agree.
    - An observation on a slot that's later covered (S4) is cancelled with a notice.
    - A person who leaves keeps nothing in the school; their growth record stays with the school for the year, then is removed.
13. **Phone:** meeting notes, I attended, and reading observations work on a phone; writing a year review is best on a desktop.
14. **Accessibility:**
    - Cards and states as words.
    - The observation form has plain labelled fields.
    - Counts as a table for leaders.
15. **Notifications:**
    - Invited to a meeting: **Normal**; agenda posted: in the meeting's own notice.
    - Observation booked on your lesson: **Important**, with the notice period.
    - Observation written: **Normal** to the observed teacher.
    - Year review window opens: **Normal**, once.
    - Actions due: the existing task notices.
16. **Trust and data:**
    - Growth records are personal: the person and their line manager; leaders see counts. **[call]**
    - 1:1 notes stay private to the pair (11.6, C5).
    - Formal appraisal decisions, capability processes and pay are **parked** (HR records).
    - **Learning walks** (unannounced visits) are recorded only as counts, with no notes about a named teacher.
    - AI agents can draft a self-reflection or meeting notes for the person, but never write a line manager's part or an observation.
17. **Reuse vs new:**
    - **Reuse:** 11.6 meetings with decisions and actions, C5 Check-in, 11.4 objectives, announcements, S1 events and repeats, S4 slots, S3 Training record, My work.
    - **New:**
      - school meeting types
      - Reports to
      - My growth, My people and Growth counts
      - the year review template and states
      - observations with notice, focus and Just between us
      - the development log and I attended
18. **How we know it works:**
    - **Signal:** the share of staff with agreed goals and a check-in by the end of Term 1.
    - **Checks:**
      - growth records reach only the person and their line manager (server test)
      - leaders receive counts only
      - "Just between us" never reaches the line manager
      - observations need notice
      - no score fields anywhere in growth

**Organization steps:**
- **Level:**
  - School: settings, meeting types, training sessions, counts.
  - Team: department meetings, decisions and actions.
  - Pair: line management 1:1s, goals, reviews.
  - Person: My growth.
- **Term moment:** before the year (Reports to, focus list) → staff days (training sessions) → Term 1 (goals agreed) → every few weeks (line management) → through the year (observations, department meetings) → summer term (year review) → next year (goals from the plan).
- **Org tab:**
  - Documents (Meetings)
  - Updates (Briefing notices)
  - Members (Growth counts; My people)
  - Overview (My growth link; meetings today)
  - Sprints (meetings and training on the calendar)
  - Settings (Staff growth)

**Calls agreed 2026-11-17:**
1. Meetings are 11.6 meeting documents with school types; line management uses C5's Check-in.
2. Briefings are announcements, not meeting documents.
3. Reports to is a label per person, set by school admins.
4. Up to 3 goals per person per year, kept to the person and their line manager.
5. The year review has no ratings, scores or pay outcomes.
6. Observations are feedback (Strengths and One next step), booked with notice; the observed teacher reads first.
7. A peer observation can be kept between the two teachers.
8. Growth records are seen by the person and their line manager; leaders see counts.
9. Formal appraisal, capability and pay are parked; learning walks are counts only.


### 32.7 School (K–12): the whole picture (complete 2026-11-17)

| # | Workflow | Main reference | Home | Level |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | School year and calendar | Events Calendar 4.80 / 504 · School Calendar 4.87 / 15 | School Sprints (Year, Month, Upcoming) · Overview | School |
| S2 | Curriculum map and lesson plans | Teacher Curriculum Map 4.84 / 37 · Lesson Plan Organizer 4.84 / 92 | Team Sprints (Year map) · course Sprints (Term plan) | Team + course workspace |
| S3 | Staff hand-ins and reviews | Async Doc Reviews 5.0 / 5 · Deadline & Test Tracker 4.83 / 54 | Tasks (Assignments, Review queue, Deadlines) | School + team |
| S4 | Timetable, cover and duties | Quick Class Schedule 4.87 / 231 · Timetable 4.70 / 188 | School Sprints (Timetable) · Members (Away and cover, Duties) · Your day | School + person |
| S5 | Staff meetings and growth | Meeting notes 4.85 / 367 · Performance Review 4.82 / 22 | Documents (Meetings) · My growth · Members (Growth) | School + pair |

**The shape of a staff-only school:**
- School → team org (department or grade team) → course workspaces.
- **Tasks serve staff:** assignments are staff hand-ins, the Review queue is for heads of department.
- **No student records** anywhere (32.1 point 3).

**New stored things across S1–S5:**
- day types, the `event` kind without its parked parts, repeat rules
- the Course template, lesson types, per-class Taught ticks and class notes, the standards list
- the NB-item hand-in type, the second approver, repeating hand-ins, quiet weeks, I've read this
- day patterns, periods, rooms, classes as names, timetable slots, absences by period, cover slots, duties, Cover info
- school meeting types, Reports to, the year review, observations, the development log

**New shared rules (pure functions):**
- repeats that skip non-school days, Start next year by week of term (S1)
- Behind the map (S2)
- repeat by school week, the clash check (S3)
- sessions from slots, cover suggestions (S4)

**Words added:** School year · Holiday · Staff day · Event · Audience · Year map · Course · Assessment · Taught · Standards · Hand-in · Overdue · Then approved by · Sign-off · Period · Week A / B · Away · Cover · Duty · Your day · Reports to · Goal · Year review · Observation · One next step · Development log.

**Never:** grade, rating, score, ranking, Missing or Late for staff, Lead, Owner.

**Parked, carried forward:**
- students and parents, and every student record (attendance, marks, behaviour, SEN, parent logs, reports, consent)
- trusts and districts above one school
- staff HR records (background checks, contracts, pay, formal appraisal)
- building timetables (NB imports them)
- registration and budgets for events (the Event planner)

**Build order inside this category:**
1. **S1:** the school year underpins everything.
2. **S2:** courses and lessons (after W2).
3. **S3:** hand-ins (the most reuse; after S2's units).
4. **S4:** the timetable and cover (sessions feed S2's dates).
5. **S5.**

All of it waits for the three-level structure (29.2) and the 28.9 Wave 0 foundation.

**Next category:** Company, then Community, Research, Club and Other.
