## 34. Organization type: Community (complete 2026-11-17)

This section uses the combined method from sections 29–33.

**What a Community org is today:**
- The `community` type sets the roles Owner · Admin · Member · Viewer, **instant join**, **public**, the word **Season**, and **Code of conduct** as the starter document.
- Its example is a meetup ("Bangalore Rust meetup": monthly talks, beginner workspaces, hack nights, "Say hi in #general").
- **Built and ready for communities:**
  - the public About and Discover
  - join codes and member caps
  - chat channels (#general, members can make channels)
  - announcements and member posts with likes
  - **trust and safety** (reports, cases, appeals, the console, blocking)
  - child workspaces and profiles

### 34.1 Every Community template, sorted
**How:**
- 30 searches (community, community hub, community management, community dashboard, member directory, meetup, community events, community guidelines, code of conduct, Discord, forum, ambassador program, community newsletter, open source community, alumni, community onboarding, moderation, member onboarding, creator community, local chapter, chapters, community content, membership, online community, study group, networking, speaker, event speakers, community resources, community feedback) returned **175 templates, only 46 rated**, and most of those are off-topic (sales forms, personal networking logs).
- Notion's own **Communities** category has **89 templates, nearly all unrated**; its best-rated is Membership Directory (4.59 / 27).
- **Ratings can't choose the references here**, so this category is judged on **UI and fit** (section 10's second test). Adjacent rated templates and platform patterns (meetup, forum and member-community products, patterns only, as in W7) fill the gaps.
- 9 templates were studied from their screenshots.

**The 10 to work from**

| # | Template | Rating / reviews | Level | Moment | Roles | Lands in |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Membership Directory | 4.59 / 27 | Community | Always | Members | M2: each member edits their own card; tier, organisation, title, status; views Active · Newest · Company directory |
| 2 | Community Member Directory | unrated (Communities) | Community | Always | Organisers | M2: cards with status (New · Active), interests, **contributions**, stage (Onboarding · Mentor); views Directory · Member status · Analytics |
| 3 | Community Engagement Tracker | unrated (Communities) | Community | Every week | Organisers | M4: activity cards (**Monthly reflection thread** · **Member showcase** · Release announcement · **Founder AMA**) with type and status; Engagement calendar |
| 4 | Community Events Calendar | unrated (Communities) | Community | Each event | Organisers | M3: events with format (**in person · online · hybrid**), host, access level, venue, link, status; an event-mix chart |
| 5 | Community Event (Notion) | 4.70 / 10 | Event | Each event | Visitors | M3: a public event page — welcome, **When**, **Tickets**, **Where** with a map |
| 6 | Community Guidelines | 5.0 / 4 | Community | Joining | Everyone | M1: Values · Policies · Rules · **Enforcement policy**, with an outline |
| 7 | Community Manager OS | 5.0 / 2 | Community | Every day | Organisers | M4: daily and weekly tasks, active and inactive members, upcoming lives (its payments are parked) |
| 8 | Community Sign-Up Form 101 | 4.67 / 3 | Community | Joining | Visitors | M1: join questions |
| 9 | Study Group | 4.83 / 6 | Small group | Every week | Members | M5: a small group inside the community |
| 10 | Mastermind Member Onboarding Checklist | unrated | Community | Joining | Organisers | M1: welcome message, access, profile, first session |

**Worth taking parts from:**
- Public Roadmap with forms (4.71 / 45) → the Feedback page (13.3, parked) for communities that build products together.
- Volunteer Sign-Up & Hours Log → section 17 (non-profit volunteers).
- Simple Club Dashboard (4.50 / 6) → the Club round.

**Left out:**
- Paid community, membership billing and revenue templates (Money is parked).
- Personal networking logs and job trackers.
- Gym and fitness member systems (paid memberships).

**Features taken from the screenshots:**
- **#1:** each member keeps their own card; status Active / Pending.
- **#2:** a contributions count and a member stage on each card.
- **#3:** recurring community rituals as cards (threads, showcases, AMAs) with a type and a live/planned status.
- **#4:** format, access level and host on every event.
- **#5:** When · Tickets · Where as three blocks on a public page.
- **#6:** guidelines in four parts ending with how they're enforced.

**What's different about a Community org:**
1. **Visitors matter most.** People find it in Discover, read About, join instantly; most members read more than they post, and organisers are volunteers.
2. **Three levels, middle optional:** Community → **chapters** (local or topic groups, as child orgs) → project workspaces (beginner projects, open-source work). **[call]**
3. **Safety is built in.** Public, instant join and chat need the code of conduct agreed on joining and the trust and safety tools already built.
4. **The Tasks tab becomes challenges.** Assignments to everyone with **optional** participation (a monthly challenge, a hack night); hand-ins become **showcases** (C4's Showcase), and the Review queue picks **featured** entries, never marks. **[call]**
5. **No money:** paid tiers, billing and sponsors stay parked.

**Covered elsewhere:**
- moderation (trust and safety, built)
- announcements and posts (built)
- K1's handbook pattern (for guidelines and FAQs)
- K2's directory pattern (for members)
- S1's calendar (for events)
- C4's Showcase (for challenge entries)

**Missing:**
- a welcoming front door with guidelines agreed on joining
- a member directory with interests and contributions
- events with RSVPs
- recurring rituals and challenges
- chapters

**Workflows, in order:**
- **M1** Community home, guidelines and joining
- **M2** Members and roles
- **M3** Events and meetups
- **M4** Rituals, challenges and showcases
- **M5** Chapters and small groups

**Parked:**
- paid memberships, tiers and billing (Money)
- sponsors (Pipeline)
- imports from Discord, Slack or Meetup
- under-18 members (sign-up stays 18+)

### 34.2 M1 · Community home, guidelines and joining (agreed 2026-11-17)
**References** (judged on UI and fit, 34.1; 5 screens studied; platform patterns noted as patterns only):

| Template / pattern | Rating | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **Community Guidelines** | 5.0 / 4 | **Main reference for the rules:** Values · Policies · Rules · **Enforcement policy**, with an outline beside the page |
| **Community Event** (Notion) | 4.70 / 10 | **Main reference for the public look:** a welcome paragraph, then **When** · **Tickets** · **Where** as three calm blocks |
| Community Sign-Up Form 101 | 4.67 / 3 | "Join our community!" with a few questions (name, links, occupation); Responses · My members |
| Mastermind Member Onboarding Checklist | unrated | Welcome message · access · profile · first session, with a done / in progress / not started chart |
| Company home (Notion) | 4.78 / 260 | K1's two-column home, reused |
| Meetup-style group page (pattern) | — | About, organisers, member count, **next event** first, photos of past events |
| Forum "welcome" pattern (pattern) | — | A pinned welcome and rules that new people agree to before posting |

**Today (built):**
- the public **About** (About · Who it's for · What happens here), a welcome note, **Code of conduct** as the starter document
- **instant join** and approval, join codes, member caps, Discover
- chat channels ("Say hi in #general")
- announcements and member posts; Required reading with re-read
- **trust and safety:** reports, cases, appeals, the console, blocking
- **Missing:**
  - agreeing to the rules before joining
  - join questions
  - a welcome checklist
  - a front door that shows what's next
  - rules that reports can point to
  - first-day spam limits

**Agreed changes from an exact copy:**
1. Guidelines become the **Code of conduct** document in four parts (Values · Rules · How we keep it safe · Contact), with **numbered rules**.
2. Tickets become **Join** (and, for events, M3's RSVP); Where becomes the community's place (city or "Online").
3. The sign-up form becomes **up to 3 join questions**; email and LinkedIn are never asked (the profile has links).
4. The onboarding chart is dropped; new members get a **short checklist** on Overview.
5. Photos come from past events and showcases (M3, M4), not uploads on About.

```
VISITOR · Community About (public)
┌ Bangalore Rust meetup ───────────────────────────────┬ Next event (M3) ─────────────┐
│ Rust developers in Bangalore, beginners welcome       │ Hack night · Thu Dec 4 · 19:00│
│ What happens here: monthly talks, hack nights,        │ HSR Layout · 32 going          │
│ beginner workspaces                                   │ Organisers: Asha · Dev          │
│ 412 members · Season 3 · Online + Bangalore           │ [ Join the community ]          │
├ Our guidelines (summary) ─────────────────────────────┤ Recent showcases (M4)          │
│ 1 Be kind · 2 No spam or selling · 3 Credit others …  │ ▢ ▢ ▢                           │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────┘

JOIN (instant)
 1. Read the Code of conduct (summary, full link)       ☑ I agree to the Code of conduct
 2. What brings you here? [ ……… ]   (optional)   ☐ Show my answer on my member card
                                                           [ Join ]

NEW MEMBER · Overview → Getting started (14 days)
 ☑ Agree to the Code of conduct   ☐ Say hi in #introductions   ☐ Add your interests (M2)
 ☐ Pick an event (M3)             ☐ Look at this month's challenge (M4)
```

**The 18 layers**
1. **Getting it:**
   - Every Community org's About is its **front door** for visitors and its Overview is the home for members.
   - **Organiser's first look:** "Write your Code of conduct" (starter, already made) and "Add join questions".
   - **Visitor's first look:** About with the next event, the guidelines summary and Join.
   - **New member's first look:** Getting started on Overview.
2. **Setting it up (Community: Settings → Joining):**
   - **Agree to the Code of conduct before joining** (on) **[call]**
   - **join questions:** up to 3, optional in instant join, required in approval mode **[call]**
   - the **Getting started** list (up to 5 items; organisers edit it)
   - a **welcome post** in a channel when someone joins (off) **[call]**
   - **First-day limits:** for the first 24 hours a new member can't start direct messages with members they haven't talked to (on for instant join) **[call]**
3. **Items:**
   - **Code of conduct:** the starter document in four parts with **numbered rules**; a short summary of the rules is shown on About and in Join. **[call]**
   - **Agreement:** the member, the Code of conduct version and the date (K1's I've read this pattern); a new version asks again on the next visit.
   - **Join answer:** stored on the membership; seen by organisers, and on the member's card only if they tick **Show on my card**.
   - **Getting started item:** a fixed link (introductions channel, interests, an event, a challenge, the guidelines), ticked when done.
4. **Views:**

   | View | Who | On screen |
   |---|---|---|
   | **About** | Visitors and members | Name, who it's for, what happens here, members count, place, season, organisers, next event, guidelines summary, recent showcases, Join |
   | **Overview** | Members | Getting started (new members), What's happening (next event, the open challenge, new showcases, pinned announcement), **Where to talk** (channels with their purpose) |
   | **Join** | Visitors | The rules summary, I agree, the join questions |
   | **New members** | Organisers | Who joined this week, their answers, Getting started progress |
5. **Actions and flow:**
   - **Join:** read the summary → I agree → answer (or skip) → Join → Getting started.
   - **Approval mode:** the answers go to organisers → Approve or Decline with a reason (exists).
   - **Change the rules:** edit → Publish with re-read (exists) → members agree again on their next visit; reading isn't blocked, but posting waits for the new agreement. **[call]**
   - **Report:** the existing report flow asks **which rule** (from the numbered list); moderator actions name the rule. **[call]**
   - Getting started disappears when done, or after 14 days.
6. **Surfaces:**
   - **About right column:** next event, organisers, Join.
   - **Rules summary:** numbered one-liners with "Read the full Code of conduct".
   - **Where to talk:** channel name, a line on what it's for, members in it.
   - **New members card** (organisers): name, joined, answer, items done.
7. **Design spec:**
   - Reuse the About tab, Overview cards, the join button and approval flow, Required reading and re-read, channels, the report flow and `RailSection`.
   - Lucide icons: DoorOpen, ScrollText, Hand, MessagesSquare, ShieldCheck.
   - Add a contract test.
8. **Words:**
   - Join the community · Code of conduct · I agree · Rules · How we keep it safe · Join questions · Show on my card · Getting started · Where to talk · What's happening · Organisers · New members · Welcome.
   - Never "Lead"; never "ban" in member-facing text (the trust and safety words apply).
9. **Links:**
   - M2 (interests and cards) · M3 (next event) · M4 (challenges and showcases) · M5 (chapters on About)
   - trust and safety (rules in reports and actions) · Discover · channels · K1's handbook pattern
10. **People:**

    | | Sees | Can do |
    |---|---|---|
    | Owner and admins (organisers) | Everything; join answers | Code of conduct, questions, Getting started, approvals |
    | Moderator (M2) | Reports with rule numbers; join answers | Act on reports |
    | Member | About, Overview, the Code of conduct | Agree, tick Getting started, report |
    | Visitor | About (fields switched to Show to visitors), the rules summary | Join |
11. **States:**
    - Visitor · Joining · New member (14 days) · Member · Needs to agree to the new version.
    - A full community (member cap) shows "Full" with Request to join when approval is on.
12. **Edges:**
    - Someone blocked by an organiser can't see Join (exists).
    - A member who doesn't agree to a new version keeps reading; their posts wait.
    - Leaving and rejoining asks to agree again.
    - Join questions changed later don't touch old answers.
    - A private community shows About only to people with the link or code.
13. **Phone:** About is one column with Join pinned at the bottom; Join is a short sheet; Getting started is the first card.
14. **Accessibility:**
    - Rules are an ordered list.
    - The agree box is a real checkbox with its label.
    - Getting started counts as text.
15. **Notifications:**
    - Welcome on joining: **Normal**, with Getting started.
    - New members: in organisers' daily **Summary**.
    - A new Code of conduct version: the existing re-read notice.
    - No reminders to post or join in, ever. **[call]**
16. **Trust and data:**
    - The member list is never public; visitors see a count and the organisers.
    - Join answers are private unless shown on the card.
    - Agreements are kept with their version and date.
    - First-day limits slow spam without blocking replies.
    - AI agents can draft the Code of conduct and welcome text, but never agree for someone.
17. **Reuse vs new:**
    - **Reuse:** About, Overview cards, instant join and approval, member caps, Required reading and re-read, channels, reports and moderator actions, Discover.
    - **New:**
      - agreement before joining, with versions
      - join questions and Show on my card
      - Getting started
      - the welcome post
      - first-day message limits
      - numbered rules linked to reports
      - Where to talk
      - the About front door layout
18. **How we know it works:**
    - **Signal:** the share of new members who do at least two Getting started items within 14 days.
    - **Checks:**
      - no join without agreeing (server test)
      - posting waits for a new version's agreement
      - join answers stay private unless shown
      - first-day limits apply only to new conversations
      - reports carry the rule number

**Organization steps:**
- **Level:**
  - Community: About, the Code of conduct, joining, Getting started.
  - Chapter (M5): its own About under the community's rules.
  - Member: agreement, answers, their checklist.
- **Moment:** found in Discover → reads About → agrees and joins → first 14 days (Getting started) → every visit (What's happening) → rules change (agree again).
- **Org tab:**
  - About (front door)
  - Overview (home)
  - Documents (Code of conduct)
  - Members (New members)
  - Settings (Joining)
  - chat (introductions, Where to talk)

**Calls agreed 2026-11-17:**
1. Joining needs agreement to the Code of conduct, recorded with its version.
2. Up to 3 join questions: optional for instant join, required for approval.
3. The Code of conduct has numbered rules; reports and moderator actions name the rule.
4. A new version is agreed on the next visit; reading continues, posting waits.
5. A welcome post in a channel is off by default.
6. New members can't start new direct messages for their first 24 hours (instant-join communities).
7. Getting started is a short organiser-edited list for 14 days; no reminders to post.
8. The member list is never public; visitors see the count and the organisers.

### 34.3 M2 · Members and roles (agreed 2026-11-17)
**References** (judged on UI and fit; studied in 34.1):

| Template / pattern | Rating | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **Membership Directory** | **4.59 / 27** | **Main reference for cards:** each member keeps their own card (tier, organisation, title, status); views Active · Newest · Company directory |
| **Community Member Directory** | unrated | **Main reference for organisers:** status (New · Active), interests, a **contributions** count, a stage (Onboarding · Mentor); views Directory · Member status · Analytics |
| K2 Directory (33.3) | — | Our own design: search by name or skill, Message, no email or phone |
| Forum and chat-community patterns | — | **Moderators** with limited powers; helper badges; earned trust levels (**not taken**) |

**Today (built):**
- org roles owner · admin · member · guest · visitor in one permission matrix
- profiles with interests and skills
- the Members tab, but **admins only**
- moderation for admins: standing, reports (reporters never named; unanswered reports pass to NetworkBase at a deadline), blocked people
- likes on posts, direct messages, blocking
- **Missing:**
  - a directory members can use
  - moderators who aren't admins
  - event hosts and helpers
  - pausing someone's posting
  - contributions on a card
  - organisers' view of new and quiet members

**Agreed changes from an exact copy:**
1. Tiers are dropped (no paid membership).
2. Status (New · Active · Quiet) is **for organisers only**, never on cards.
3. The contributions number becomes **plain counts** (posts, showcases, events hosted), never a score.
4. "Mentor" stage becomes the **Helper** label.
5. Earned trust levels aren't taken: roles are given by people, not by activity counts.

```
MEMBER · Members → Directory (members only)          Search people or interests…   Interest ▾  Place ▾
┌ (photo) Priya ─────────────────┬ (photo) Dev  · Helper ─────────┬ (photo) Mei ──────────────────┐
│ Bangalore · joined Season 2    │ Online · joined Season 1       │ Bangalore · joined Season 3   │
│ Interests: async, embedded     │ Ask me about: borrow checker   │ Here for: "first Rust job"    │
│ 12 posts · 2 showcases          │ Hosted 4 events · 31 posts     │ New                            │
│ [ Message ]                    │ [ Message ]                    │ [ Message ]                    │
└────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────┘

ORGANISERS · Members → People      New 23 · Active 140 · Quiet 249         Roles: Organisers 2 · Moderators 3 · Hosts 5 · Helpers 8
MODERATOR · Moderation → Reports    #2 No spam · "selling courses" in #general   [ Hide ] [ Pause posting 24 h ▾ ] [ Pass to organisers ]
```

**The 18 layers**
1. **Getting it:**
   - In a Community org, **Members becomes the Directory for every member**; organisers keep the People tools in the same tab. **[call]**
   - **Organiser's first look:** People with New / Active / Quiet counts and "Give someone a role".
   - **Member's first look:** the Directory with their own card first and "Add your interests".
2. **Setting it up (Community: Settings → Members):**
   - directory fields (interests, Ask me about, place, Here for, joined, contribution counts)
   - **Quiet after** (60 days without posting, an RSVP or attending)
   - the **Helper** label's wording ("Ask me for help", renameable)
   - how long **Pause posting** can last (24 hours · 7 days)
3. **Items:**
   - **Member card:** profile photo, name, interests and skills (as Ask me about), place (city or Online), **Here for** (their join answer, only if shown, M1), joined (by Season), contribution counts.
   - **Show me in the directory:** on by default; a member can turn it off. **[call]**
   - **Contribution counts:** posts, showcases (M4) and events hosted (M3), worked out, never ranked; a member can hide them. **[call]**
   - **Member status:** New (first 30 days) · Active · Quiet, worked out; organisers only. **[call]**
   - **Roles and labels:**
     - **Moderator:** a new community grant, described in Actions **[call]**
     - **Host:** a label that gives M3's event tools for the events they host **[call]**
     - **Helper:** a visible badge with a short line; no extra powers
   - **Pause posting:** a time-limited block on posting and new messages in this community, with the rule number (M1) and an end time.
4. **Views:**

   | View | Who | On screen |
   |---|---|---|
   | **Directory** | Members | Cards or a list; search by name or interest; filters for interest, place, role |
   | **People** | Organisers | Everyone, with status, roles, joined, join answers; New this week |
   | **Roles** | Organisers | Who holds each role and label |
   | **Moderation** | Moderators and organisers | The existing reports, plus Hide, Pause posting and Pass to organisers |
   | **Activity log** | Organisers | Every moderator action with its rule and who did it |
5. **Actions and flow:**
   - **Find people:** search an interest → cards → Message (M1's first-day limit and blocks apply).
   - **Give a role:** People → a member → Moderator, Host or Helper → they're told.
   - **Moderate:**
     - a report arrives naming a rule
     - the moderator can **Hide** the post or message, **Pause posting** (24 hours or 7 days) or **Pass to organisers**
     - removing and blocking stay with organisers (built) **[call]**
   - Every moderator action is logged with its rule; the member is told which rule and when the pause ends.
   - **Appeals** use the existing trust and safety appeals.
   - **Quiet members** are never removed automatically. **[call]**
6. **Surfaces:**
   - **Card:** role badges (Organiser, Moderator, Host, Helper) as words.
   - **People row:** status chip, roles, joined, join answer.
   - **Moderation row:** rule number, excerpt, reporter count (never names), actions.
   - **Pause notice to the member:** the rule, the end time, Appeal.
7. **Design spec:**
   - Reuse the K2 directory, `PersonCardContent`, the Members frame, the moderation section, trust and safety appeals, blocking and `StatusBadge`.
   - Lucide icons: Users, Shield, Mic, LifeBuoy, PauseCircle.
   - Add a contract test.
8. **Words:**
   - Directory · Interests · Ask me about · Here for · Joined Season 2 · Organiser · Moderator · Host · Helper · New · Active · Quiet · Pause posting · Hide · Pass to organisers · Show me in the directory.
   - Never "ban", "kick", "mute" (member-facing), "trust level", "karma", "points" or "Lead".
9. **Links:**
   - M1 (join answers, rules, first-day limits) · M3 (Hosts run events; events hosted count) · M4 (showcases count) · M5 (chapter organisers and moderators)
   - K2 (the directory pattern) · trust and safety (reports, appeals, blocking) · messages · profiles
10. **People:**

    | | Sees | Can do |
    |---|---|---|
    | Owner | Everything | Everything, including organisers |
    | Organiser (admin) | People, statuses, join answers, the log | Give roles, remove and block, settings |
    | Moderator | Reports and the content reported; the directory | Hide, Pause posting, Pass to organisers |
    | Host | The directory; their events' RSVPs (M3) | Run their events |
    | Helper | The directory | As a member |
    | Member | The directory (people who show themselves) | Edit their card, Message, report |
    | Guest / Viewer | Names only, if allowed | — |
    | Visitor | The count and organisers (M1) | — |
11. **States:**
    - Card: New badge for 30 days (to everyone, so others can welcome them); status otherwise for organisers only.
    - Paused until a time, then back automatically.
    - A role being removed shows on the log.
12. **Edges:**
    - A moderator can't act on their own reports or on organisers.
    - A paused member can still read and appeal.
    - Hidden from the directory still shows on their own posts.
    - Someone in several chapters (M5) has one card with chapter chips.
    - A member who leaves disappears from the directory; their posts stay as "Former member".
13. **Phone:** the directory is a list with search; moderation works one report per screen with large buttons.
14. **Accessibility:**
    - Role badges and status as words.
    - Pause ends shown as full dates and times.
    - Cards as a list with names as headings.
15. **Notifications:**
    - Given a role: **Normal**.
    - Your posting is paused: **Important**, with the rule, the end time and Appeal.
    - A report for moderators: in their daily **Summary**, or **Normal** at once when the community turns on fast handling.
    - New members: organisers' Summary (M1).
16. **Trust and data:**
    - The directory is members-only, and members can hide.
    - Status and join answers are for organisers.
    - Reporters are never named (built).
    - Every moderator action is logged with its rule, and appeals go to trust and safety.
    - AI agents never moderate, give roles or pause anyone.
17. **Reuse vs new:**
    - **Reuse:** the K2 directory, profiles' interests and skills, the Members frame, the moderation section and reports, trust and safety appeals, blocking, messages.
    - **New:**
      - the Directory for every Community member
      - Show me in the directory
      - contribution counts
      - member status (pure function)
      - the Moderator grant in the permission matrix
      - Host and Helper labels
      - Pause posting and Hide for moderators
      - the moderator activity log
18. **How we know it works:**
    - **Signal:** the share of reports handled by the community (not passed to NetworkBase) within the deadline.
    - **Checks:**
      - moderators can't remove, block or change settings (server test)
      - status never reaches members (server test)
      - hidden members stay out of the directory
      - pauses end on time
      - every action is logged with a rule

**Organization steps:**
- **Level:**
  - Community: the directory, roles, moderation.
  - Chapter (M5): its own organisers and moderators, under the community's rules.
  - Member: their card and visibility.
- **Moment:** joining (card, interests) → every visit (find people) → reports (moderate) → each Season (organisers review roles and quiet counts).
- **Org tab:**
  - Members (Directory, People, Roles)
  - Settings (Members, Moderation)
  - Overview (New members for organisers)
  - chat (moderation of channels)

**Calls agreed 2026-11-17:**
1. Every Community member sees the Directory.
2. Members appear in the directory by default and can hide themselves.
3. Contribution counts are plain, never ranked, and can be hidden; no points or trust levels.
4. New · Active · Quiet status is for organisers only.
5. Moderator is a new role grant: hide, pause posting and pass on; never remove, block or change settings.
6. Host and Helper are labels; Host gets event tools for their own events.
7. Removing and blocking stay with organisers; every moderator action names a rule and is logged.
8. Quiet members are never removed automatically.

### 34.4 M3 · Events and meetups (agreed 2026-11-17)
**References** (studied in 16, 32.2 and 34.1):

| Template / pattern | Rating | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **Events Calendar** (Notion) | **4.80 / 504** | The calm month grid (already S1's look) |
| **Community Event** (Notion) | 4.70 / 10 | **Main reference for the event page:** welcome, **When**, **Tickets**, **Where** as three blocks |
| **Community Events Calendar** | unrated | **Main reference for the fields:** format (in person · online · hybrid), host, **access level**, venue, link, status; an event-mix chart |
| Conference Event Page (Notion) · Event Registration Form | 4.8 / 30 · 5.0 / 21 | Section 16's agenda of time slots and sign-up fields |
| Meetup-style pattern | — | **Going / Not going**, a place limit with a **waitlist**, the list of who's going, hosts, a call for talks |

**Today:**
- **Built:** assignments to everyone with hand-ins and the **Review queue**; announcements; Files; chat channels.
- **Designed:**
  - S1's `event` item (without registration or budget), repeat rules, calendar views and public events
  - **16's Event planner** (registrations with roles, capacity, waitlist, check-in, run of show) — **parked**
  - C4's Run of show
  - M2's Host label
- **Missing for meetups:**
  - going / not going
  - a place limit with a waitlist
  - online links kept for attendees
  - talks proposed by members
  - attendance
  - slides and photos afterwards

**The RSVP decision:** take **only the RSVP slice** of 16's registrations (Going · Can't go, a place limit, a waitlist) and put it on S1's `event` item. Registration questions, roles, approvals, tickets and budgets **stay parked** with the Event planner. **[call]**

**Agreed changes from an exact copy:**
1. "Tickets" becomes **RSVP** (free); paid tickets are parked (Money).
2. The map embed becomes an address with **Open in maps** (nothing is fetched from map services).
3. Access level becomes **Who can come**: members, a chapter (M5), or "members and the public page" (visitors see it and join to RSVP).
4. The event-mix chart is dropped; a Past events list keeps the history.
5. Speakers come from a **Call for talks** that reuses assignments and the Review queue.

```
COMMUNITY · Sprints → Events     [ Upcoming ] [ Calendar ] [ Past ]                     + Event
 Thu Dec 4 · 19:00  Hack night            In person · HSR Layout     32 going · 8 places left   Host: Dev
 Sat Dec 13 · 11:00 Rust 101 (online)     Online                     54 going                   Host: Priya
 First Thursday · monthly talks (repeats, S1)

EVENT PAGE (public when allowed)
┌ Hack night ───────────────────────────────────┬ When  Thu Dec 4 · 19:00–21:30 ┐
│ Bring a laptop and a half-finished project…   │ Where HSR Layout, 2nd floor   │
│ Run of show: 19:00 Hello · 19:15 Lightning    │       Open in maps            │
│ talks (3) · 20:00 Hacking · 21:15 Show & tell │ 32 going · 8 places left      │
│ Talks: "Async in 5 min" (Mei) · …             │ [ Going ] [ Can't go ]        │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────┘
 (online events: the link shows only to people who are Going)

TASKS · Call for talks: Hack night (Dec 4)        Optional · closes Nov 27
 Review queue: "Async in 5 min" (Mei)   [ Accept → Run of show slot ]  [ Not this time ]
```

**The 18 layers**
1. **Getting it:**
   - Community orgs show **Events** in Sprints (Upcoming · Calendar · Past) and the next event on About and Overview (M1).
   - **Organiser's first look:** + Event, with "Make it repeat" (first Thursday).
   - **Host's first look:** their events with RSVPs and the run of show.
   - **Member's first look:** Upcoming with Going buttons.
2. **Setting it up:**
   - **Per event:**
     - title, description, when, format (in person · online · hybrid), place or link
     - host(s) (M2 Hosts)
     - **who can come**
     - **place limit** (optional) with **waitlist** (on when there's a limit)
     - **show on the public page** (on for public communities) **[call]**
   - **Community: Settings → Events:**
     - default reminders (the day before; 1 hour before)
     - whether members can propose events (off; organisers and hosts create)
3. **Items:**
   - **Event:** S1's `event` item, with format, hosts, who can come, place limit and a run of show (C4's slots).
   - **RSVP:** member × event → Going · Can't go · Waitlisted, with the time. **RSVPs need membership**; visitors join (instantly) first. **[call]**
   - **Waitlist:** first come; when someone cancels, the next person moves to Going and is told. **[call]**
   - **Online link:** shown only to people who are Going. **[call]**
   - **Check-in:** optional, a host ticks names from the Going list; it counts toward "events attended" (M2). No QR codes. **[call]**
   - **Call for talks:** an **assignment to everyone, optional**, with a text hand-in (title, a line, length); proposals go to the **Review queue**; **Accept** puts the talk in a run-of-show slot. **[call]**
   - **After the event:** slides and recordings (Files, attached to the event) and an optional recap post (Update).
4. **Views:**

   | View | Who | On screen |
   |---|---|---|
   | **Upcoming** | Members | Date, title, format, place, going and places left, host, Going |
   | **Calendar** | Members | S1's month grid |
   | **Past** | Members | Events with slides, recordings and recaps |
   | **Event page** | Members; visitors when public | When · Where · RSVP · run of show · talks · who's going (members only) |
   | **Host view** | Hosts and organisers | Going, waitlist, check-in, run of show, the call for talks |
   | **My events** | Members | Events they're going to, in My work and S1's calendar |
5. **Actions and flow:**
   - **Plan:** + Event → details → (optional) Call for talks → Publish → members are told by the event's channel post or announcement (the organiser's choice).
   - **RSVP:** Going → reminders → (online) the link appears → attend → (optional) checked in.
   - **Can't go after Going:** frees the place; the waitlist moves up.
   - **Talks:** members propose → hosts Accept or say Not this time (with a kind default line) → accepted talks appear on the event page.
   - **After:** attach slides or a recording → optional recap Update → it shows in Past and on About (M1).
   - **Cancel or move an event:** everyone Going is told at once (Important).
6. **Surfaces:**
   - **Event card:** date block, title, format chip, place, going count, places left, host avatar, Going button.
   - **Event page right column:** When, Where with Open in maps, RSVP buttons, going count.
   - **Who's going:** avatars and names, members only; people can **RSVP privately** (counted, not named). **[call]**
   - **Host view:** a checklist-style Going list for check-in.
7. **Design spec:**
   - Reuse S1's event item, Calendar and repeat rules, C4's Run of show, assignments and the Review queue, Files, Updates, chat posts and `StatusBadge`.
   - Lucide icons: CalendarDays, MapPin, Video, Users, Mic, CheckCheck.
   - Add a contract test.
8. **Words:**
   - Events · Upcoming · Past · Going · Can't go · Waitlist · Places left · Who can come · In person · Online · Hybrid · Open in maps · Host · Run of show · Call for talks · Propose a talk · Accept · Not this time · Checked in · Slides · Recording · Recap.
   - Never "Lead", "tickets" (until paid events exist) or "no-show".
9. **Links:**
   - M1 (next event on About; Getting started "Pick an event") · M2 (Hosts; events attended and hosted counts) · M4 (show & tell becomes a showcase) · M5 (chapter events)
   - S1 (event item, calendar, repeats, public events) · 16 (parked: the rest of registration) · C4 (Run of show) · assignments and the Review queue · Files · Updates · chat
10. **People:**

    | | Sees | Can do |
    |---|---|---|
    | Organiser | Everything | Create, edit, cancel any event; settings |
    | Host | Their events' RSVPs, waitlist, proposals | Edit their events, check in, accept talks |
    | Member | Events they can come to; who's going (except private RSVPs) | RSVP, propose talks |
    | Visitor | Public event pages: when, where (in person), going count | Join, then RSVP |
11. **States:**
    - Event: Draft · Published · Full (waitlist open) · Happening now · Ended · Cancelled.
    - RSVP: Going · Waitlisted · Can't go · Checked in.
12. **Edges:**
    - **No penalties** for people who don't turn up. **[call]**
    - Lowering the place limit below Going keeps everyone already Going; it only stops new places.
    - A moved event asks everyone Going to confirm again.
    - A paused member (M2) can't RSVP until the pause ends.
    - An event on a past date can't be RSVP'd.
    - A host who leaves: organisers become hosts.
13. **Phone:** Upcoming is the phone home card; Going is one tap; check-in is a big list of names to tick.
14. **Accessibility:**
    - Dates and times in full with the time zone.
    - RSVP buttons as a pair with the current choice announced.
    - Place counts as text.
15. **Notifications:**
    - New event: through the organiser's chosen channel post or announcement, not a separate notice.
    - Reminders to Going: **Normal**, the day before and 1 hour before.
    - Moved up from the waitlist: **Important**.
    - Event moved or cancelled: **Important** to everyone Going.
    - Talk accepted or not: **Normal**.
16. **Trust and data:**
    - RSVPs need membership, so the Code of conduct (M1) covers every attendee.
    - Online links go only to people who are Going.
    - Private RSVPs are counted, never named.
    - Addresses are typed by organisers; nothing is fetched from map services.
    - AI agents can draft events and recaps, but never RSVP for someone.
17. **Reuse vs new:**
    - **Reuse:** S1's event item, calendar and repeats; C4's Run of show; assignments and the Review queue; Files; Updates; chat; M2's Host label.
    - **New:**
      - RSVP, place limit and waitlist (the slice taken from 16)
      - format and who can come
      - links only for Going
      - private RSVP
      - host check-in
      - Call for talks on assignments
      - the event page and the Past list
18. **How we know it works:**
    - **Signal:** the share of Going RSVPs that are checked in (where hosts check in).
    - **Checks:**
      - the waitlist moves up in order
      - online links never reach anyone not Going (server test)
      - visitors can't RSVP without joining
      - private RSVPs are never named
      - an accepted talk lands in a run-of-show slot

**Organization steps:**
- **Level:**
  - Community: events, calls for talks, the Past list.
  - Chapter (M5): its own events, shown in the community's calendar.
  - Member: RSVPs, proposals, My events.
- **Moment:** plan (event, call for talks) → publish → RSVPs and reminders → the day (check-in, run of show) → after (slides, recap) → the next in the series.
- **Org tab:**
  - Sprints (Events: Upcoming, Calendar, Past)
  - About and Overview (next event)
  - Tasks (Call for talks; Review queue)
  - Files (slides, recordings)
  - Updates (recaps)
  - chat (event posts)

**Calls agreed 2026-11-17:**
1. Only the RSVP slice of 16's registration is taken (Going · Can't go, place limit, waitlist); the rest stays parked.
2. RSVPs need membership; visitors join first.
3. The waitlist is first come, and moves up on its own.
4. Online links show only to people who are Going.
5. Events in public communities show on the public page by default; each can be turned off.
6. Check-in is a host ticking names; no QR codes.
7. A Call for talks is an optional assignment reviewed in the Review queue; Accept puts it in a slot.
8. Members can RSVP privately (counted, not named).
9. No penalties for not turning up.

### 34.5 M4 · Rituals, challenges and showcases (agreed 2026-11-17)
**References** (20 searches, 138 templates; 4 screens studied):

| Template / pattern | Rating | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **Software Projects Showcase / Portfolio** | **4.90 / 96** | **Main reference for the Showcase:** a gallery of cover cards (title, dates, status chip, tags); views All · New |
| **Manage a Challenge Community** | 5.0 / 3 | **Main reference for the shape:** three spaces (Admin centre · Monitoring and archive · Community space) and a **Current challenge** block on the home |
| **Community Engagement Tracker** (34.1 #3) | unrated | **Main reference for rituals:** cards for Monthly reflection thread · Member showcase · Founder AMA, each with a type and a status; an engagement calendar |
| 30 Days Challenge · 30-Day Challenge tracker | 4.89 / 19 · 4.74 / 23 | A challenge as **a prompt per day** (the check-off grid is not taken) |
| Game Jam Planner | 4.69 / 26 | A theme and a timetable (start, idea, first version, hand in, end), as in 22's game jam |
| 75 Hard trackers (the top-rated results) | 4.90 / 301 | **Left out:** personal fitness, built on streaks and "start again from day 1" |

**Today:**
- **Built:**
  - assignments to everyone with file, link or text hand-ins, but every copy turns **Missing** after its due date
  - the **Review queue**
  - Updates with likes, comments, comment likes and pinning
  - chat channels and Files
- **Designed:**
  - C4's **Showcase** card (cover, title, one line, links) and its "public only if every member agrees" rule
  - 14.2's **scheduled Updates**, S1's repeat rules, M3's events (show & tell)
  - 22's theme reveal (peer rating stays there); 16's judging (parked)
  - M1's Getting started item "Look at this month's challenge"; M2's showcase count
- **Missing:**
  - taking part by choice, without anything turning Missing
  - prompts that open on a date
  - a gallery of entries
  - featured picks
  - repeating community threads and AMAs

**Agreed changes from an exact copy:**
1. The three spaces become tabs we have: the challenge lives in **Tasks**, featured picks in the **Review queue**, the current challenge on **Overview**, and the Showcase on **About**.
2. The daily check-off grid is dropped: there are **no streaks**, no "start again" and no points.
3. The portfolio's status chip and "Future projects" view are dropped; the Showcase shows only finished entries.
4. The engagement calendar becomes rituals on S1's calendar and M3's Upcoming list; the analytics become plain counts for organisers.
5. Judging and leaderboards (16, 22) are not taken: organisers **feature** entries with a line on why, never a score or a rank.

```
MEMBER · Tasks → Challenges
┌ November: Build a CLI in a weekend ─────────────────────── Open · closes Sun Nov 30 ┐
│ Prompt: make a tool you'd use every day. Any size counts.                           │
│ 86 joined · 41 entries                                    [ Join the challenge ]    │
│ Prompts: Day 1 Pick a problem ✓ · Day 2 First version (opens Sat) · Day 3 Polish …  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

ENTRY (hand in)   Title · one line · cover · link or files    ☐ Show on the public Showcase
                                                                            [ Hand in ]

ORGANISERS · Review queue → Challenge entries
 "tz-now" (Mei)   [ Feature ▸ why we love it: "tiny and useful" ]  [ Not now ]

VISITOR / MEMBER · About → Showcase       Featured ✦ first, then newest     Challenge ▾  Season ▾
 ▢ tz-now · Mei ✦ Featured    ▢ cargo-tidy · Dev    ▢ Hack night demo: rustlings-tui · Priya

ORGANISERS · Sprints → Rituals
 Weekly wins          Thread · every Friday 17:00 · #general     Host: Asha    Next Fri Nov 21
 Ask me anything      Thread · monthly, questions open 3 days    Host: Dev     Dec 10
 Show & tell          Event (M3) · first Thursday                Host: Priya   Dec 4
```

**The 18 layers**
1. **Getting it:**
   - Community orgs show **Challenges** in Tasks, the **Showcase** on About and **Rituals** in Sprints next to Events.
   - **Organiser's first look:** "Start a challenge" and "Add a ritual" (Weekly wins and Ask me anything are ready to use).
   - **Member's first look:** the current challenge on Overview with Join, and the Showcase.
   - **Visitor's first look:** the public part of the Showcase on About (M1's front door).
2. **Setting it up:**
   - **Per challenge:**
     - title, prompt, opens and closes
     - prompts by day (optional, each with an **Opens on** date)
     - entry type (file, link or text, with a cover)
     - solo or teams (assignment teams, up to a set size)
     - the AI policy (built; Labelled by default)
     - who can Feature (organisers; hosts if allowed)
   - **Per ritual:**
     - name, type (**Thread** or **Event**), repeat (S1), host, where it posts (Updates or a channel)
     - the prompt text
     - for Ask me anything, when questions open
   - **Community: Settings → Showcase:** whether entries can go on the public page (on in public communities; each maker still decides).
3. **Items:**
   - **Challenge:** an **assignment to everyone marked Optional**. Copies are made only when someone presses **Join**, and an optional copy is **never Missing or Overdue**. **[call]**
   - **Prompt:** a step with an Opens on date; its text stays hidden on the server until then (like W4's locked paper). **[call]**
   - **Entry:** the hand-in plus a title, a line and a cover (C4's Showcase card). Members see it once handed in; likes and comments are the built ones.
   - **Featured:** an organiser's pick from the Review queue, with a short **"Why we love it"** line. There are no marks, scores, votes or ranks. **[call]**
   - **Public Showcase:** an entry shows on the public page only when its maker ticks it; a team entry needs every member. **[call]**
   - **Ritual:** a repeating item. A **Thread** ritual is a **scheduled Update** (14.2) with the prompt, posted **as the community with the host named**; replies are comments. An **Event** ritual is an M3 event series. **[call]**
   - **Ask me anything:** a Thread ritual whose post opens for questions ahead of time. Likes on questions help the host choose, and the host answers in replies at the set time. Hosts must be members. **[call]**
4. **Views:**

   | View | Who | On screen |
   |---|---|---|
   | **Challenges** (Tasks) | Members | The current challenge, prompts by day, Join, my entry; past challenges |
   | **Challenge page** | Members | Prompt, dates, joined and entry counts, prompts, the entries gallery |
   | **Showcase** (About) | Members; visitors for public entries | **Featured first, then newest**; filters for challenge, Season, tag; never sorted by likes **[call]** |
   | **Review queue → Challenge entries** | Organisers (hosts if allowed) | New entries with Feature and Not now |
   | **Rituals** (Sprints) | Organisers manage; members see them in Upcoming | Name, type, repeat, host, next date, where it posts |
   | **Season recap** | Organisers | Counts: joined, entries, featured, replies to rituals; no names ranked |
5. **Actions and flow:**
   - **Challenge:** Start a challenge → prompts → Publish (announced in a post) → members **Join** → prompts open on their days → **Hand in** → organisers Feature → Close → the challenge moves to Past with its entries.
   - **Join late:** anyone can join until the challenge closes; earlier prompts are already open.
   - **Leave a challenge:** removes the copy; an entry already handed in stays unless its maker deletes it.
   - **Ritual:** Add a ritual → it posts on its schedule → members reply → the host can pin a good reply.
   - **Ask me anything:** the post opens for questions → members ask and like → at the time, the host answers → the post closes for new questions.
   - **Add to my profile:** a maker can add an entry to their profile's contribution stories (24). **[call]**
6. **Surfaces:**
   - **Current challenge card** (Overview): title, closes, joined count, Join or "Your entry".
   - **Entry card:** cover, title, maker (or team), challenge, ✦ Featured with its line.
   - **Prompt row:** day, title, Opens on or ✓ for done by me (private to me).
   - **Ritual row:** type icon, repeat in words, host, next date.
7. **Design spec:**
   - Reuse assignments and copies, the Review queue, C4's Showcase card, scheduled Updates, Updates' likes, comments and pinning, S1's repeats, M3's events, `StatusBadge`.
   - The gallery grid from 14.3.
   - Lucide icons: Flag, Images, Sparkles, Repeat, MessageCircleQuestion.
   - Add a contract test.
8. **Words:**
   - Challenge · Join the challenge · Prompt · Opens on · Entry · Hand in · Showcase · Featured · Why we love it · Not now · Ritual · Thread · Weekly wins · Ask me anything · Show & tell · Took part · Add to my profile · Show on the public Showcase.
   - Never "winner", "leaderboard", "rank", "streak", "points", "badge", "Missing", "Overdue" or "Lead".
9. **Links:**
   - M1 (Getting started "Look at this month's challenge"; the Showcase on About) · M2 (showcase and took-part counts; moderators can hide entries) · M3 (show & tell events become rituals; demos become entries) · M5 (chapter challenges and rituals)
   - assignments and the Review queue · C4 (Showcase) · 14.2 (scheduled Updates) · 14.3 (gallery) · S1 (repeats) · 24 (profile stories) · 22 (game jam, for theme reveals)
10. **People:**

    | | Sees | Can do |
    |---|---|---|
    | Organiser | Everything; counts | Start challenges, add rituals, Feature, close |
    | Host | Their rituals; entries if allowed to Feature | Run their rituals, answer an AMA, Feature if allowed |
    | Moderator (M2) | Entries and replies | Hide them, with a rule |
    | Member | Challenges, entries, rituals | Join, hand in, like, comment, ask |
    | Visitor | Public Showcase entries | Join the community |
11. **States:**
    - Challenge: Draft · Announced · Open · Closed.
    - Entry: Joined · Handed in · Featured · Hidden (M2).
    - Ritual: Active · Paused · Ended. Rituals pause in Season breaks.
    - Ask me anything: Taking questions · Answering · Closed.
12. **Edges:**
    - An optional copy never turns Missing; leaving it alone is fine.
    - A deleted entry leaves the Showcase and loses Featured.
    - A paused member (M2) can't hand in until the pause ends.
    - A private community has no public Showcase at all.
    - A team entry leaves the public Showcase if any member unticks it.
    - A ritual with no host left goes to Paused, and organisers are told.
13. **Phone:** the current challenge is the first card after Getting started; Hand in takes a photo or a link; the Showcase is one column.
14. **Accessibility:**
    - Covers need alt text (asked on hand-in).
    - Featured is shown as a word, not only ✦.
    - Prompt dates are in full.
15. **Notifications:**
    - A new challenge or ritual post: no notice; it shows in the members' **Summary** and on Overview.
    - A prompt opens: **Normal**, only to people who joined; daily challenges send one daily line, not one per prompt. **[call]**
    - "Closes tomorrow": **Normal**, once, only to people who joined and haven't handed in.
    - Your entry is featured: **Normal**.
    - An AMA starts answering: **Normal** to people who asked.
    - No other reminders to take part (M1).
16. **Trust and data:**
    - Entries go public only with the maker's yes (every member for a team).
    - Prompts stay on the server until they open.
    - Entries follow the community's Code of conduct; reports name a rule (M1).
    - AI-made entries follow the challenge's AI policy; AI agents never Feature and never hand in for someone.
17. **Reuse vs new:**
    - **Reuse:** assignments, copies and teams; the Review queue; C4's Showcase card; scheduled Updates; likes, comments and pinning; S1's repeats; M3's events; 14.3's gallery; 24's profile stories.
    - **New:**
      - the Optional assignment (join-only copies, never Missing)
      - prompts with Opens on
      - Featured with Why we love it
      - the Showcase view and public tick
      - rituals (Thread and Event) posting as the community
      - Ask me anything
      - the Season recap counts
18. **How we know it works:**
    - **Signal:** the share of members who join at least one challenge or reply to a ritual in a Season.
    - **Checks:**
      - optional copies never become Missing (pure-function test on `copyState`)
      - prompt text never reaches anyone before Opens on (server test)
      - nothing reaches the public Showcase without the maker's tick
      - the Showcase never sorts by likes
      - ritual posts go out on schedule and stop when Paused

**Organization steps:**
- **Level:**
  - Community: challenges, rituals, the Showcase.
  - Chapter (M5): its own challenges and rituals; its entries can show in the community's Showcase.
  - Member: joins, entries, replies, their profile.
- **Moment:** a Season starts (rituals resume, the first challenge) → each week (threads) → each month (a challenge, an AMA) → the challenge closes (Featured) → the Season ends (recap).
- **Org tab:**
  - Tasks (Challenges; Review queue)
  - About (Showcase)
  - Overview (current challenge, New in the Showcase)
  - Sprints (Rituals beside Events)
  - Updates (ritual threads)
  - Settings (Showcase)

**Calls agreed 2026-11-17:**
1. A challenge is an Optional assignment: copies only for people who Join, and never Missing or Overdue.
2. Prompts open on dates and stay hidden until then.
3. No streaks, points, badges or "start again".
4. Featured is a human pick with a "Why we love it" line; no marks, votes, scores or ranks.
5. The public Showcase needs the maker's yes (every member for a team entry).
6. The Showcase shows Featured first, then newest; never sorted by likes.
7. Rituals are Threads (scheduled Updates posted as the community with the host named) or Events (M3).
8. Ask me anything collects questions ahead; hosts must be members.
9. Entries can go on the maker's profile with their yes.
10. Prompt notices go only to people who joined; daily challenges send one daily line.

### 34.6 M5 · Chapters and small groups (agreed 2026-11-17)
**References** (20 searches, 143 templates, 44 rated; few templates are about chapters, so small-group templates and the 29.2 structure carry this one; 5 screens studied):

| Template / pattern | Rating | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **Book Club** | **4.93 / 15** | **Main reference for a group's home:** Our story · Vision & mission · Attendance · Ideas, then a **Meeting list** (table or gallery) and shared lists (books for sharing, recommendations, requests) |
| **Book Club Organizer** | 4.84 / 19 | A home split **For members** (voting, each member's notes, past reads) and **For the host** (Host planner) |
| **Study Group** | 4.83 / 6 | **Main reference for small-group rhythm:** Share · Collaborate · Schedule, group guidelines ("our commitment"), New meeting · New discussion topic, and a **sessions held** count |
| **Church Community** | 5.0 / 3 | A month strip of every group's events, with pinned Attendance, Events and Statistics |
| **Group Availability Finder** | 5.0 / 1 | **Main reference for finding a time:** proposed slots, each person ticks the ones they can make, with replies counted and availability by day |
| 29.2 three levels · Meetup-style networks (pattern) | — | One parent, local chapters under it, each with its own organisers under the parent's rules |

**Today:**
- **Built:**
  - child workspaces under an org (`parentId`), with the org's visibility cap ("Set by" locked rows)
  - member caps and join modes (instant or approval)
  - ownership succession to the longest-serving active member
  - `duplicateOrg`
  - org chat, Updates, Files, Documents
  - trust and safety reports with a deadline that passes to NetworkBase
- **Designed:**
  - 29.2's three levels (an org under an org)
  - C1's frozen Program snapshot used as a template
  - W8 sections
  - 11.6 meeting docs, C5's Check-in doc, S1's calendar, M1–M4
- **Missing:**
  - chapters with their own organisers
  - a kit for starting a chapter
  - the community's rules reaching every chapter
  - reports routed chapter first
  - small groups people can find and ask to join
  - finding a time together
  - a view of chapter health for community organisers

**Agreed changes from an exact copy:**
1. The book club's voting and the availability finder become one **Poll** (choose a time, or choose an option such as the next book); results are counts.
2. Each member's notes page becomes the group's 11.6 meeting notes, with private notes only where 11.6 already allows.
3. The Statistics card becomes **chapter health counts** for community organisers, never a ranking of chapters.
4. The "sessions held" counter stays as a plain count; no streaks or goals for attendance.
5. Church-specific databases (giving, ministries) are left out; the month strip becomes S1's calendar with chapter events.

```
COMMUNITY · Projects → Chapters                                         + Start a chapter   Proposals 2
 Bangalore          Local · 212 members · 3 organisers · next event Dec 4         Active
 Pune               Local · 64 members · 1 organiser   · last event Aug 30        Needs a co-organiser
 Embedded Rust      Topic · 88 members · 2 organisers  · next event Dec 13        Active
 Chennai            Local · 19 members · 1 organiser   · nothing since May        Dormant (organisers only)

COMMUNITY · Projects → Groups (small groups)                 Chapter ▾  Kind ▾  Open to join ▾
 Rustlings study group   Study group · 7 of 10 · Tuesdays 20:00 · Bangalore   [ Join ]
 Async book club         Book club · 10 of 10 · monthly · Online              Full
 Founders circle         Accountability · 6 of 8 · Fridays · Online          [ Ask to join ]

GROUP (workspace) · Overview     Our commitment · Next session Tue · 4 sessions held
 Poll: "When should we meet in December?"   Tue 20:00 ▮▮▮▮▮ 5 · Wed 19:00 ▮▮ 2 · Sat 11:00 ▮▮▮ 3   [ Pick Tue ]
```

**The 18 layers**
1. **Getting it:**
   - A Community org shows **Chapters** and **Groups** in Projects (the workspace list).
   - **Community organiser's first look:** "Start a chapter" with the **Chapter kit**, and Proposals.
   - **Chapter organiser's first look:** their chapter's Overview with Getting started for organisers (first event, co-organiser, local About).
   - **Member's first look:** "Pick your chapter" in Getting started (M1), and Groups to join.
2. **Setting it up:**
   - **Community: Settings → Chapters:**
     - who can propose a chapter (members; organisers approve) **[call]**
     - the **Chapter kit**: a frozen snapshot of a chapter (About sections, starter documents, a first event, rituals, Getting started), as C1's Program **[call]**
     - kinds: **Local** (a city) and **Topic**
     - **Dormant after** (180 days with no events or posts)
   - **Per chapter:** name, kind, place or topic, organisers, join mode (instant or approval, never looser than the community), its own About text.
   - **Per small group:** name, kind (**Study group · Book club · Accountability circle · Mastermind · Other**), purpose, when it meets, size cap (**12** by default), join mode (**Open · Ask · Invite only**), the chapter it belongs to (optional). **[call]**
3. **Items:**
   - **Chapter:** an **org under the community** (29.2's shape, `parentId`), with its own organisers, moderators and hosts (M2). **[call]**
   - **Small group:** a **workspace** from a Small group template (home, Our commitment document, meeting notes, a shared list). It sits under the community or a chapter; there is no fourth level. **[call]**
   - **Locked rules:** the community's Code of conduct, safety settings and visibility cap show in each chapter as "Set by <community>". Chapters can add local notes but never loosen them. **[call]**
   - **Proposal:** a member's request to start a chapter (name, kind, place or topic, why, a co-organiser), approved or declined with a reason.
   - **Poll:** a question with **times** or **options**, ticks by members, closing at a time. Results are counts, and the host confirms a pick, which can create the meeting or event. **[call]**
   - **Chapter health:** members, events in the last 90 days, organisers, open reports. These are counts for community organisers, never a ranking. **[call]**
4. **Views:**

   | View | Who | On screen |
   |---|---|---|
   | **Chapters** (community Projects) | Members; organisers see health | Name, kind, place or topic, members, next event; organisers also see organisers, last activity, flags |
   | **Proposals** | Community organisers | Proposed chapters with Approve or Decline |
   | **Groups** (Projects at community and chapter) | Members | Name, kind, size and cap, when it meets, chapter, Join · Ask to join · Full |
   | **Chapter Overview** | Chapter members | M1's home for the chapter: next event, current challenge, Where to talk, Getting started |
   | **Group Overview** | Group members | Our commitment, next session, sessions held, open poll, the shared list |
   | **Calendar** (community) | Members | S1's calendar with every chapter's public events (M3), filterable by chapter |
5. **Actions and flow:**
   - **Start a chapter:** a member proposes → community organisers Approve → the chapter is made from the Chapter kit with the proposer and co-organiser as organisers → it shows in Chapters and in Getting started for nearby members.
   - **Join a chapter:** only community members can; joining the community never joins a chapter for you. Getting started suggests chapters by the place typed on the member card (M2), with no location lookup. **[call]**
   - **Start a small group:** any member (setting) → template → it's listed in Groups → people Join or Ask.
   - **Poll:** propose up to 5 times or options → members tick → it closes → the host picks → (times) a meeting or M3 event is made.
   - **Reports:** go to the chapter's moderators first, then the community's organisers, then NetworkBase at the existing deadline. **[call]**
   - **Organisers leave:** a chapter with one organiser shows **Needs a co-organiser**; when the last one leaves, community organisers take over, instead of the built rule that hands it to the longest-serving member. **[call]**
   - **Dormant and closing:** a chapter with nothing for 180 days is marked **Dormant** for organisers; it's **never closed automatically**. Closing a chapter archives it, and its members stay in the community. **[call]**
6. **Surfaces:**
   - **Chapter row:** kind chip, place or topic, members, next event; flags as words (Needs a co-organiser, Dormant) for organisers only.
   - **Group card:** kind, "7 of 10", when it meets, chapter, the join button by mode.
   - **Poll card:** options as rows with counts and bars, who ticked (group members only), Close and Pick.
   - **"Set by <community>"** rows in chapter settings (built pattern).
7. **Design spec:**
   - Reuse the org frame for chapters, the Projects list (`OrgWorkspacesTab`), workspace templates, `duplicateOrg` and C1's snapshot, locked "Set by" rows, join modes and member caps, 11.6 meeting docs, S1's calendar, M3's events, `StatusBadge`.
   - Lucide icons: MapPin, Hash, UsersRound, Vote, CalendarCheck.
   - Add a contract test.
8. **Words:**
   - Chapter · Local · Topic · Start a chapter · Propose a chapter · Chapter kit · Co-organiser · Needs a co-organiser · Dormant · Group · Study group · Book club · Accountability circle · Mastermind · Our commitment · Sessions held · Open · Ask to join · Invite only · Poll · Pick · Set by.
   - Never "branch", "franchise", "Lead", "inactive chapter" (member-facing) or ranking words.
9. **Links:**
   - M1 (Pick your chapter; chapter About under the community's rules) · M2 (chapter organisers and moderators; one card with chapter chips) · M3 (chapter events in the community calendar) · M4 (chapter challenges; entries in the community Showcase)
   - 29.2 (three levels) · C1 (snapshot kit) · W8 (sections, if a chapter needs groups inside a class-like structure) · 11.6 (meetings) · C5 (Check-in) · trust and safety
10. **People:**

    | | Sees | Can do |
    |---|---|---|
    | Community organiser | All chapters, health counts, proposals; small groups' names and sizes only | Approve chapters, edit the kit, take over a chapter, close it |
    | Chapter organiser | Their chapter in full | Run the chapter: events, rituals, roles, groups under it |
    | Group host | Their group | Edit, polls, sessions, accept Ask requests |
    | Member | Chapters and groups listed; content of the ones they're in | Join, propose, start a group, tick polls |
    | Visitor | Public chapter About pages (M1 rules) | Join the community first |
11. **States:**
    - Chapter: Proposed · Active · Needs a co-organiser · Dormant (organisers only) · Closed.
    - Group: Open · Full · Invite only · Archived.
    - Poll: Open · Closed · Picked.
12. **Edges:**
    - A member in several chapters has one card with chapter chips (M2).
    - Blocks (built) carry across the whole community and its chapters.
    - A paused member (M2) is paused in every chapter.
    - A community made private makes every chapter private (the cap).
    - Moving a group to another chapter keeps its members and content.
    - A chapter can't be moved to another community.
13. **Phone:** Chapters and Groups are lists; ticking a poll is one tap per option; the group home leads with the next session.
14. **Accessibility:**
    - Poll counts as text beside the bars.
    - Flags as words.
    - Group sizes as "7 of 10".
15. **Notifications:**
    - Your proposal is approved or declined: **Normal**.
    - A poll opens: **Normal** to the group; closes and picked: **Normal**.
    - Ask to join: the group host's **Summary**.
    - Needs a co-organiser and Dormant: community organisers' **Summary**.
    - A report passed up from a chapter: **Normal** to community organisers.
16. **Trust and data:**
    - The community's rules are locked in every chapter.
    - Reports always have a next stop (chapter → community → NetworkBase).
    - Small groups' content is private to the group; community organisers see names and sizes only.
    - Places are typed, never looked up from devices.
    - AI agents can draft a chapter's About and poll options, but never approve chapters or tick polls.
17. **Reuse vs new:**
    - **Reuse:** child orgs (29.2) and child workspaces, `duplicateOrg` and the snapshot kit, "Set by" locks, join modes and caps, succession, 11.6 meetings, S1's calendar, M1–M4, trust and safety.
    - **New:**
      - chapter kinds (Local, Topic) and proposals
      - the Chapter kit setting
      - small group templates and the Groups view
      - Open · Ask · Invite only for groups
      - the Poll item
      - the report chain through chapters
      - chapter health counts and the Dormant and Needs a co-organiser flags (pure functions)
18. **How we know it works:**
    - **Signal:** the share of chapters with at least one event in the last 90 days.
    - **Checks:**
      - a chapter can't loosen a locked community rule (server test)
      - joining a chapter without community membership is refused
      - a report in a chapter reaches community organisers at its deadline
      - small-group content never reaches community organisers who aren't in the group
      - Dormant never closes a chapter

**Organization steps:**
- **Level:**
  - Community: the kit, proposals, rules, health counts, the shared calendar and Showcase.
  - Chapter: its own events, rituals, challenges, roles and groups, under the community's rules.
  - Group (workspace): sessions, polls, notes, its shared list.
  - Member: chapters joined, groups, polls.
- **Moment:** a member proposes → approved → kit → first event → regular rhythm (M3, M4) → organisers change (co-organiser) → quiet (Dormant) → revived or closed.
- **Org tab:**
  - Projects (Chapters, Groups, Proposals)
  - Settings (Chapters, Chapter kit)
  - Overview (chapter and group homes)
  - Sprints (the shared calendar)
  - Members (chapter chips)

**Calls agreed 2026-11-17:**
1. Chapters are orgs under the community (29.2); small groups are workspaces; there's no fourth level.
2. Members propose chapters; community organisers approve; new chapters start from the community's Chapter kit.
3. The community's Code of conduct, safety settings and visibility cap are locked in every chapter.
4. Joining a chapter needs community membership; joining the community never auto-joins a chapter; suggestions use the typed place only.
5. Reports go chapter moderators → community organisers → NetworkBase at the deadline.
6. One organiser left shows Needs a co-organiser; when the last leaves, community organisers take over.
7. Dormant after 180 days is an organisers-only label; chapters are never closed automatically, and closing keeps people in the community.
8. Small groups are listed to the community (name, kind, size, when, join mode); their content is private to the group.
9. Small groups have a size cap (12 by default) and Open · Ask · Invite only.
10. One Poll item (times or options) with counts, and the host confirms the pick; no calendar sync.
11. Chapter health is counts for community organisers, never a ranking.

### 34.7 Community: the whole picture (complete 2026-11-17)

| # | Workflow | Main reference | Home | Level |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | Community home, guidelines and joining | Community Guidelines 5.0 / 4 · Community Event 4.70 / 10 | About (front door) · Overview · Documents (Code of conduct) · Settings → Joining | Community + chapters |
| M2 | Members and roles | Membership Directory 4.59 / 27 · Community Member Directory | Members (Directory, People, Roles) · Moderation | Community |
| M3 | Events and meetups | Events Calendar 4.80 / 504 · Community Event 4.70 / 10 | Sprints (Events) · Tasks (Call for talks) | Community + chapters |
| M4 | Rituals, challenges and showcases | Software Projects Showcase 4.90 / 96 · Manage a Challenge Community 5.0 / 3 | Tasks (Challenges) · About (Showcase) · Sprints (Rituals) | Community + chapters |
| M5 | Chapters and small groups | Book Club 4.93 / 15 · Study Group 4.83 / 6 · Group Availability Finder | Projects (Chapters, Groups, Proposals) · Settings (Chapter kit) | Community → chapter → group |

**The shape of a Community org:**
- Community → chapters (orgs, optional) → workspaces (projects and small groups).
- Visitors find it in Discover and read About; members mostly read; organisers are volunteers.
- Tasks become optional: challenges and calls for talks. The Review queue picks Featured entries and accepts talks; it never marks.
- Safety comes first: agreement to the Code of conduct on joining, numbered rules in every report, moderators with limited powers, and the community's rules locked in every chapter.

**New stored things across M1–M5:**
- Code of conduct agreements with versions, join questions and answers, Getting started, first-day message limits
- Show me in the directory, the Moderator grant, Host and Helper labels, Pause posting, the moderator log
- RSVPs, place limits and waitlists on S1's event item, format and who can come, private RSVPs, check-in
- the Optional assignment, prompts with Opens on, Featured with a line, the public Showcase tick, rituals (Thread and Event), Ask me anything
- chapter kinds and proposals, the Chapter kit, small group templates with join modes, the Poll item

**New shared rules (pure functions):**
- member status New · Active · Quiet (M2)
- waitlist move-up (M3)
- optional copies never Missing in `copyState` (M4)
- the report chain through chapters, and the Dormant and Needs a co-organiser flags (M5)

**Words added:** Join the community · Code of conduct · I agree · Getting started · Where to talk · Directory · Ask me about · Here for · Moderator · Host · Helper · Pause posting · Going · Can't go · Waitlist · Places left · Call for talks · Challenge · Prompt · Entry · Showcase · Featured · Why we love it · Ritual · Ask me anything · Chapter · Chapter kit · Co-organiser · Dormant · Group · Our commitment · Poll.

**Never:** Lead, ban or kick (member-facing), karma, points, streaks, badges, trust levels, leaderboard, rank, winner, no-show, tickets (until paid events exist).

**Parked, carried forward:**
- paid memberships, tiers, billing and paid tickets (Money)
- sponsors (Pipeline)
- imports from Discord, Slack or Meetup
- under-18 members (sign-up stays 18+)
- the rest of the Event planner's registration (16)
- calendar sync and location lookups

**Build order inside this category:**
1. **M1:** the front door, the Code of conduct and safe joining.
2. **M2:** the directory and moderators (needed before a community grows).
3. **M3:** events with RSVPs (after S1's event item).
4. **M4:** challenges, rituals and the Showcase (after 14.2's scheduled Updates and C4's Showcase card).
5. **M5:** chapters and small groups (after the three-level structure).

All of it waits for the three-level structure (29.2) and the 28.9 Wave 0 foundation.

**Next type:** Research, then Club and Other.
