**The 18 layers**
1. **Getting it:**
   - After "What do you call it?", Other shows **Pick a starting kit** with six cards; the word typed suggests one.
   - **Creator's first look after creating:** the kit's Getting started (for example "Write your mission", "Add volunteer roles", "Set the event date").
   - **Member's first look:** the tabs the kit switched on, with M1's welcome.
2. **Setting it up:**
   - **Kits (fixed, defined as data in one file):** **[call]**
     - **Nonprofit:** Director · Coordinator · Volunteer · Viewer; approval; private with a public About; time word **Year**; starters Mission and values (X4) and Volunteer handbook (K1); on: X2 volunteers, X4 programs, 17.5 Board meetings, M3 events.
     - **Event team:** Organiser · Coordinator · Team member · Viewer; approval; private with a public event page; time word **Phase**; **an end date is required** (X3); on: X3, X2, M3 (one event), C4's run of show, 11.6 meetings. **[call]**
     - **Association or committee:** Chair · Officer · Member · Viewer; approval; time word **Year**; on: L1 renewal, L2 positions and handover, L3 meetings, minutes and constitution, M3 events.
     - **Public-sector team:** Owner · Manager · Member · Viewer; approval; private; time word **Quarter**; on: K1 handbook, K2 directory, K3 goals and projects, K5 requests.
     - **Faith or interest community:** Owner · Organiser · Member · Viewer; instant; public or private; time word **Season**; on: M1, M2, M3, M5 small groups.
     - **Blank:** today's neutral defaults.
   - **Settings → Workflows:** what's on, and **Add from a kit**.
3. **Items:**
   - **Kit:** role names, join mode, visibility, time word, starter documents, Getting started items, the workflows switched on (installed into default tabs, decision 8), and section names. It sets **defaults only**; everything stays editable. **[call]**
   - **Suggestion:** a fixed word list checked in the browser (nonprofit, NGO, charity → Nonprofit; event, hackathon, festival, conference → Event team; committee, association, society, PTA, hostel, residents, alumni → Association; government, council, department, public → Public-sector team; church, temple, mosque, faith, fellowship → Faith community); no match → Blank. **No AI and nothing sent anywhere; the person always chooses.** **[call]**
   - **Org's own template:** any running org can be saved with C1's snapshot (**Start another like this**), separate from the built-in kits. **[call]**
4. **Views:**

   | View | Who | On screen |
   |---|---|---|
   | **Pick a starting kit** (creation) | Creator | Six cards with role names and what's on; a preview of tabs and first look |
   | **Settings → Workflows** | Owner and admins | Workflows on, with Turn off; Add from a kit |
   | **Getting started** (Overview) | Owner first, then members | The kit's first steps |
5. **Actions and flow:**
   - **Create:** Other → type a name for it → a kit is suggested → pick (or Blank) → the wizard's later phases fill with the kit's defaults → untouched fields follow the kit if it changes (dirty-field rule) → create.
   - **Later:** Settings → Workflows → **Add from a kit** adds a workflow into its default tab; **Turn off** hides it and **keeps its data**; turning it on again brings everything back. **[call]**
   - **Change type later:** Settings → General (built) keeps working; the kit doesn't lock anything.
   - **Save as a template:** Start another like this (C1) for orgs that repeat, such as next year's event.
6. **Surfaces:**
   - **Kit card:** name, role names in small text, three lines of what's on, a Suggested chip.
   - **Preview:** the tab bar and the first Getting started items.
   - **Workflow row** in Settings: name, where it lives (tab), On or Off, "has data" when off.
7. **Design spec:**
   - Reuse the type cards' layout, the wizard's dirty-field rule, `savedTypeSettings`, decision 8's installer, M1's Getting started, C1's snapshot.
   - Kits live as data in one file beside `type-profile.ts`.
   - Lucide icons: Package, Sparkles, Settings2, Plus.
   - Add a contract test (each kit's parts exist and are switched on).
8. **Words:**
   - What do you call it? · Pick a starting kit · Suggested · Nonprofit · Event team · Association or committee · Public-sector team · Faith or interest community · Blank · Everything can be changed later · Workflows · Add from a kit · Turn off · Start another like this.
   - Never "Lead", "premium kit" or "template store".
9. **Links:**
   - X2 (volunteers) · X3 (fixed-time teams) · X4 (programs)
   - Every section a kit borrows from: 17, 33 (K1–K5), 34 (M1–M5), 36 (L1–L3), C4, 16 · decision 8 · 28.11 · C1
10. **People:**

    | | Sees | Can do |
    |---|---|---|
    | Creator | Kits | Pick one or Blank |
    | Owner and admins | Settings → Workflows | Add from a kit, turn workflows off and on, save as a template |
    | Member | The tabs that are on | Use them |
11. **States:**
    - Org: created from a kit (remembered for help text only) · Blank.
    - Workflow: On · Off (data kept).
12. **Edges:**
    - Changing the label later doesn't change the kit or switch anything.
    - A workflow added twice is refused; it's already on.
    - Turning off a workflow with open items warns with the count, then hides them; nothing is deleted.
    - A kit part that needs another (X3 needs an end date; L2 needs L1's Season) brings it along.
    - Youth-facing kits don't exist; every kit is 18+ like the rest of NetworkBase.
13. **Phone:** kit cards stack; the preview is a short list.
14. **Accessibility:**
    - Kit cards are radio buttons with full labels.
    - Suggested is a word, not only a chip colour.
15. **Notifications:** none; creating and changing workflows notify no one.
16. **Trust and data:**
    - The label is matched in the browser; nothing is sent to AI or outside services.
    - Turning parts off never deletes data.
    - AI agents can explain kits, but never create orgs or turn workflows on or off for someone.
17. **Reuse vs new:**
    - **Reuse:** the type step and dirty-field rule, `savedTypeSettings`, decision 8's installer, every designed workflow, C1's snapshot.
    - **New:**
      - the six kits as data
      - the word-list suggestion
      - the kit step and preview
      - Settings → Workflows with Add from a kit and Turn off (data kept)
18. **How we know it works:**
    - **Signal:** the share of new Other orgs created from a kit rather than Blank.
    - **Checks:**
      - each kit's workflows exist and switch on (contract test)
      - turning a workflow off keeps its data, and on brings it back
      - the suggestion runs without any network call
      - untouched fields follow a changed kit; edited ones stay

**Organization steps:**
- **Level:** the org (kits shape it); workspaces inherit nothing new from the kit beyond what each workflow already does.
- **Moment:** creation (pick a kit) → first week (Getting started) → as needs grow (Add from a kit) → repeats (Start another like this).
- **Org tab:**
  - Settings (Workflows)
  - Overview (Getting started)
  - whichever tabs the kit's workflows live in

**Calls agreed 2026-11-17:**
1. Other gets a Pick a starting kit step with six kits: Nonprofit, Event team, Association or committee, Public-sector team, Faith or interest community, Blank.
2. Kits are fixed data built only from designed workflows; they set defaults, and everything stays editable.
3. The typed label suggests a kit from a fixed word list in the browser; no AI, nothing sent; the person chooses.
4. The Event team kit needs an end date (X3).
5. Settings → Workflows can add parts from any kit later; turning a part off hides it and keeps its data.
6. An org can be saved as its own template with C1's snapshot, separate from the kits.
7. No youth-facing kits; all kits are 18+.

### 37.3 X2 · Volunteers and shifts (agreed 2026-11-17)
**References** (37.1, plus 11 searches for shifts, rotas, rosters, availability and volunteer hours: 79 templates, 17 rated; 4 more screens studied):

| Template / pattern | Rating | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **Volunteer Activity Log** | **4.75 / 16** | **Main reference for hours:** activities with volunteer, **check-in and check-out time**, hours worked out, **Start now / End now** buttons, a total |
| Volunteer Activity Tracker · Volunteer Hours Tracker | 4.83 / 12 · 4.64 / 11 | Hours per activity with "what I learned"; hours kept for **applications** |
| **Volunteer Event Sign Up** | 5.0 / 2 | **Main reference for the public side:** a public page of opportunities and a sign-up with an agreement, beside a private page for organisers |
| **Volunteer & Community Event Operations Tracker** | unrated | **Main reference for coordinators:** a roster with skills, **availability**, orientation, reliability, next event; **coverage gaps** before the event, not at check-in |
| Employee Shift Scheduling · Event Staff Schedule | 4.58 / 12 · 5.0 / 4 | Ongoing shifts, a monthly calendar, alerts; time-off requests |
| 17.4 (Community / volunteer setup) | — | Shifts with filled counts, sign-up, check-in, hours, a reminder the day before, "still short 2 days before" (its "top volunteer" line is not taken) |

**Today:**
- **Built:** membership and approval joins, Away, profiles with verified contribution entries, Messages.
- **Designed:**
  - S1's calendar items and repeat rules
  - **M3's RSVP slice** (place limit, waitlist that moves up, host check-in)
  - S4's swaps that need a colleague's yes
  - R4's training sign-off
  - M1's versioned agreement
  - M2's organiser-only status
  - 17.4's volunteer shifts on the parked Event planner
- **Missing:**
  - volunteer roles and shifts at the org level without the Event planner
  - regulars on a weekly rota
  - coverage gaps for coordinators
  - hours that volunteers can trust and use
  - a public "Volunteer with us" list

**Agreed changes from an exact copy:**
1. Email, phone and emergency-contact columns are not taken; contact is **Message** (K2).
2. "Reliability" scores become nothing; coordinators see attended and missed counts only, never a score.
3. The "top volunteer" line from 17.4 is dropped.
4. The signed waiver becomes **M1's versioned agreement**; legal waivers with signatures are parked.
5. Start now / End now become a **self check-in** inside the shift's time window.

```
PUBLIC · About → Volunteer with us                                         [ Join to volunteer ]
 Sat Dec 6 · 08:00–11:00  Sorting (Food bank, Indiranagar)   6 of 8 places   Training: none
 Sat Dec 6 · 11:00–14:00  Delivery                           3 of 6 places   Training: Safe driving

COORDINATOR · Volunteers → Shifts          [ Week ] [ Month ] [ Coverage ]                    + Shift
 Sat Dec 6  Sorting   6/8  ✓ regulars 4   │  Delivery   3/6  ⚠ short 3 (2 days to go)
 Sun Dec 7  Kitchen   5/5  Full · waitlist 2

VOLUNTEER · My shifts       Sat 08:00 Sorting  [ Check in ] (opens at 07:45)   · Regular: every Saturday
                            My hours: 42 this year   [ Add hours (needs confirming) ]   [ Add to my profile ]
```

**The 18 layers**
1. **Getting it:**
   - Orgs with the Volunteers part (Nonprofit and Event team kits, or added from a kit) show **Volunteers** with Shifts, Roles, People and Hours; About shows **Volunteer with us**.
   - **Coordinator's first look:** "Add volunteer roles", "Add your first shift", "Make it repeat".
   - **Volunteer's first look:** My shifts and open shifts that fit their roles.
   - **Visitor's first look:** Volunteer with us with Join.
2. **Setting it up (Settings → Volunteers):**
   - **Roles:** name, what it involves, **training needed** (R4's sign-off) **[call]**
   - default shift length, check-in window (15 minutes before to 30 after)
   - the **volunteer agreement** (M1's versioned agreement) **[call]**
   - who coordinates (admins, or a Coordinator position)
3. **Items:**
   - **Shift:** an S1 calendar item with **role, place, time and places needed**; sign-up uses **M3's RSVP slice** (place limit, a waitlist that moves up on its own). **[call]**
   - **Sign-up:** needs **membership**; in approval orgs a visitor's join request carries the shift they picked and they're placed once approved. **[call]**
   - **Regular:** a volunteer signed up for every repeat of a shift until they stop; S1's repeat rules make the shifts. **[call]**
   - **Swap:** asks a named volunteer, who must say yes (S4); people **Away** can't be placed. **[call]**
   - **Check-in:** a coordinator ticks names, or the volunteer taps **Check in** inside the window. **[call]**
   - **Hours:** from checked-in shifts (shift length); **hours added by hand need a coordinator's confirmation**. **[call]**
   - **Availability:** each volunteer's typed weekly times and roles, used for suggestions.
   - **Involvement:** New · Regular · Occasional, worked out, **coordinators only** (M2's status rule).
4. **Views:**

   | View | Who | On screen |
   |---|---|---|
   | **Volunteer with us** (About) | Everyone | Open shifts by date with role, place, places left, training; Join |
   | **Shifts** (Week · Month) | Coordinators, volunteers | Shifts with filled counts, regulars, waitlist |
   | **Coverage** | Coordinators | Shifts short of people in the next 14 days, ordered by how soon |
   | **People** | Coordinators | Volunteers with roles, trainings, availability, involvement, attended and missed counts, Message |
   | **My shifts** | Each volunteer | Upcoming, check-in, regular shifts, swaps |
   | **Hours** | The volunteer (own); coordinators (all) | Hours by month and role, confirmations waiting |
5. **Actions and flow:**
   - **Join and agree:** Join (or request) → the volunteer agreement → pick roles → trainings if needed (R4) → sign up.
   - **Fill shifts:** sign up or become a Regular → reminder the day before → check in → hours recorded.
   - **Can't make it:** Can't go frees the place; the waitlist moves up; or **Swap** with a named volunteer.
   - **Coverage:** a shift still short **2 days before** tells the coordinator (17.4); the coordinator can **Ask** suitable volunteers (by role and availability) with one message each.
   - **Hours:** confirmed by check-in, or added and confirmed; **Add to my profile** makes a verified entry ("42 hours volunteering with Food bank, 2026") with the volunteer's yes. **[call]**
6. **Surfaces:**
   - **Shift row:** time, role, place, "6 of 8", regulars count, Short as a word when short.
   - **Check in** button live only in the window.
   - **Hours card:** this year, by role, waiting confirmation.
   - **Person row** (coordinators): roles, trainings ✓, availability, involvement, attended and missed as counts.
7. **Design spec:**
   - Reuse S1's items and repeats, M3's RSVP slice and check-in, S4's swap, R4's sign-off, M1's agreement, M2's status rule, verified entries, Messages, `StatusBadge`.
   - Lucide icons: HandHeart, CalendarClock, Repeat, Clock, UserCheck.
   - Add a contract test.
8. **Words:**
   - Volunteer · Volunteer with us · Role · Shift · Places · Sign up · Can't go · Waitlist · Regular · Swap · Check in · Hours · Add hours · Confirm · Coverage · Short · Availability · New · Regular · Occasional · Volunteer agreement.
   - Never "Lead", "no-show", "reliability score", "top volunteer" or "staff" for volunteers.
9. **Links:**
   - X1 (kits switch it on) · X3 (event teams' volunteers) · X4 (hours as a program measure)
   - S1 · M3 · S4 · R4 · M1 · M2 · 17.4 (superseded at org level by this) · verified entries
10. **People:**

    | | Sees | Can do |
    |---|---|---|
    | Coordinator (admin) | Every shift, person, hours | Roles, shifts, coverage asks, check-in, confirm hours |
    | Volunteer (member) | Open shifts for their roles, their shifts and hours | Sign up, be a Regular, swap, check in, add hours, add to profile |
    | Visitor | Volunteer with us | Join |
11. **States:**
    - Shift: Open · Full (waitlist) · Short · Happening now · Done · Cancelled.
    - Sign-up: Going · Waitlisted · Can't go · Checked in · Missed.
    - Hours: Confirmed · Waiting confirmation.
12. **Edges:**
    - **No scores, ranks or "top volunteer"**; missed shifts are a count for coordinators only and are never shown to others. **[call]**
    - A cancelled shift tells everyone Going at once (Important).
    - A Regular who misses 3 in a row is asked once whether to stay a Regular; nothing changes without their answer.
    - A role needing training hides its shifts' Sign up until the volunteer is trained.
    - Contact is **Message only**; phone, email and emergency contacts aren't stored (parked with legal waivers). **[call]**
13. **Phone:** My shifts first; Check in is one tap; Coverage is a short list with Ask.
14. **Accessibility:**
    - Places as text ("6 of 8").
    - Shift times in full with the time zone.
    - Short and Full as words.
15. **Notifications:**
    - Reminder the day before a shift: **Normal**.
    - Moved up from the waitlist: **Important**.
    - Shift changed or cancelled: **Important**.
    - Swap asked or answered: **Normal**.
    - Short 2 days before: **Normal** to coordinators.
    - Hours waiting confirmation: coordinators' **Summary**.
16. **Trust and data:**
    - Hours are seen only by the volunteer and coordinators.
    - No phone, email or emergency contacts are stored.
    - Involvement and missed counts are coordinators only.
    - Verified hours on profiles need the volunteer's yes.
    - AI agents can draft shift descriptions and coverage messages, but never sign people up, check them in or confirm hours.
17. **Reuse vs new:**
    - **Reuse:** S1's items and repeats, M3's RSVP slice and check-in, S4's swaps, R4's trainings, M1's agreement, M2's status rule, verified entries, Messages, Away.
    - **New:**
      - volunteer roles with trainings
      - shifts with roles and places at the org level
      - Regulars
      - self check-in in a window
      - hours with confirmation
      - Coverage and Ask
      - Volunteer with us on About
18. **How we know it works:**
    - **Signal:** the share of shifts fully filled the day before.
    - **Checks:**
      - hours equal checked-in shift time plus confirmed additions
      - a volunteer sees only their own hours (server test)
      - untrained volunteers can't sign up for shifts needing training
      - the waitlist moves up in order
      - Away volunteers are never placed

**Organization steps:**
- **Level:**
  - Org: roles, shifts, coverage, hours, the public list.
  - Chapter (M5) or event team (X3): their own shifts, counted in the org's hours.
  - Volunteer: sign-ups, regular shifts, hours, profile entry.
- **Moment:** join and agree → trainings → sign up or become a Regular → each shift (reminder, check-in, hours) → the year's hours → profile.
- **Org tab:**
  - Sprints (Shifts, Coverage)
  - Members (People, Hours)
  - About (Volunteer with us)
  - Settings (Volunteers)

**Calls agreed 2026-11-17:**
1. Volunteer roles live at the org level, each with optional training (R4) before sign-up.
2. A shift is an S1 calendar item with role, place, time and places; sign-up uses M3's RSVP slice with a waitlist.
3. Signing up needs membership; in approval orgs the join request carries the chosen shift.
4. Regulars are signed up for every repeat until they stop.
5. Swaps need the other volunteer's yes; Away people can't be placed.
6. Check-in is a coordinator's tick or a self check-in inside the shift's window.
7. Hours come from checked-in shifts; hand-added hours need a coordinator's confirmation.
8. A volunteer agreement uses M1's versioned agreement; legal waivers and emergency contacts are parked.
9. Hours are seen only by the volunteer and coordinators; no scores, ranks or "top volunteer".
10. Volunteers can add verified hours to their profile with their yes.
11. Contact is Message only.

### 37.4 X3 · Teams for a fixed time (agreed 2026-11-17)
**References** (37.1, plus 14 searches for event planning, countdowns, task forces, campaigns, wrap-ups and post-mortems: 126 templates, 34 rated; 4 more screens studied; wedding and party planners are personal and left out):

| Template / pattern | Rating | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **Event Planning** | **4.97 / 39** | **Main reference for the work:** tasks on a board (To do · In progress · Done · Blocked) with date and supplier, plus Calendar · Events · Categories · Vendor list views |
| **Countdown Tracker** | 4.92 / 40 | **Main reference for the home line:** "days until" and "days since" for the dates that matter; Active and Past |
| **Festival Organizer System** | 5.0 / 1 | **Run the festival** (Start here · Festivals · Action centre), **Open priorities** with area and priority, an active calendar, areas such as programming, partners, team and crew |
| **Retrospective** (Notion) · **Post-mortem** · Pre-mortem | 4.82 / 100 · 4.83 / 6 · 5.0 / 5 | **Main reference for the wrap-up:** Summary · Impact · what caused problems · what we'll do next time, with owners |
| Event Manager · Marketing Campaign Brief | 4.77 / 22 · 4.88 / 41 | Event details, participants and schedule; a campaign's goal, audience and deadline |

**Today:**
- **Built:**
  - `archiveOrg` / `unarchiveOrg` (read-only archive)
  - **`duplicateOrg`** with ticked parts (About, documents, files, sprints, assignments, channels, admins) and dates moved by the new start (`shiftBy`)
  - child workspaces, verified contribution entries
- **Designed:**
  - 18.2's **dates worked out backwards** from a publish date (offsets admins can change; hand-set dates stay)
  - S1's calendar, C4's run of show, M3's event page, RSVPs and check-in
  - X2's shifts, W8's sections, L4's "registration with a typed reference"
  - 11.6's Retrospective, X4's impact report
  - 29.2's three levels
- **Missing:**
  - an org that knows its key date and its end
  - a plan built backwards from the key date
  - a clean wrap-up and close
  - running it again next year with last year's lessons

**Agreed changes from an exact copy:**
1. Costs and the vendor list's money columns are dropped (Money parked); suppliers appear only as names on **booking** tasks.
2. The festival's tickets, artist contracts and sponsor tracking are parked (Money, Pipeline).
3. Countdowns are one line on Overview, not a separate hub.
4. The post-mortem's "work ticket" column becomes action items as tasks for next time (11.6).

```
EVENT TEAM · Overview            Bengaluru Book Fest 2027 · 23 days to go (Sat Feb 13) · ends Mar 15
 Workstreams  Venue (Asha) · Program (Dev) · Volunteers (Mei) · Comms (Ravi)
 This week (worked back from Feb 13):  confirm stalls (−21) · volunteer briefing (−14) · print map (−10)
 Bookings     Venue ✓ ref MG-2231 · Sound ✓ ref 88 · Permit ⏳ applied Jan 10

DAY OF (Feb 13)   Run of show · Shifts (X2) · Check-in (M3) · Issues today: 2 open
WRAP-UP (after)   ☑ Thank volunteers  ☐ Collect photos  ☐ Debrief (Retrospective)  ☐ Report (X4)   [ Close the team ]
NEXT YEAR         [ Run it again ] → Book Fest 2028, dates moved to Feb 12 2028, last debrief pinned
```

**The 18 layers**
1. **Getting it:**
   - Orgs with a **key date** (the Event team kit, or added in Settings) show a countdown on Overview, a backwards plan, Bookings, a Day-of view and a Wrap-up.
   - **Organiser's first look:** "Set the key date", "Add workstreams", "Pick a plan" (Event · Campaign · Task force starters).
   - **Team member's first look:** their workstream's tasks this week.
2. **Setting it up (Settings → Dates):**
   - **Key date** (the event day, launch or deadline) and **end date** (30 days after the key date by default). **[call]**
   - **Plan starter:** Event (−8 weeks to +2 weeks), Campaign, Task force, or Blank; each a list of phases and tasks with **offsets from the key date**.
   - **Workstreams:** W8 sections with an owner each. **[call]**
3. **Items:**
   - **Key date and end date:** stored on the org; any org can add them later. **[call]**
   - **Countdown line:** "23 days to go", then on the day "Today", then "Wrap-up: 12 days left". **[call]**
   - **Offset items:** phases (sprints) and tasks with "N days before / after the key date"; **moving the key date moves them**, and **dates set by hand stay** (18.2's rule). **[call]**
   - **Booking:** a task labelled Booking (venue, sound, permit, catering) with a supplier name and a **typed reference**; NetworkBase never books or pays. **[call]**
   - **Day of:** C4's **run of show**, X2's **shifts**, M3's **check-in**, and an **Issues today** list (tasks labelled Issue, shown only on the day). **[call]**
   - **Wrap-up:** a checklist (thank volunteers, collect files and photos, **Debrief**, optional **Report** (X4)), then **Close the team**.
   - **Debrief:** 11.6's Retrospective with the post-mortem's headings (Summary · What went well · What went wrong · Next time); its "Next time" items become tasks in the next run.
   - **Close:** the built **archive** (read-only); members can add a verified **"Organising team, Book Fest 2027"** entry with their yes. **[call]**
4. **Views:**

   | View | Who | On screen |
   |---|---|---|
   | **Overview** | Members | Countdown, workstreams, this week (worked back), bookings, open issues |
   | **Plan** (Tasks Timeline) | Members | Phases and tasks against the key date, with the offsets shown |
   | **Bookings** | Organisers, workstream owners | Each booking, supplier, reference, status |
   | **Day of** | Team | Run of show, shifts, check-in, Issues today |
   | **Wrap-up** | Organisers | The checklist and Close the team |
   | **Past runs** | Organisers | Earlier runs of this team, with debriefs |
5. **Actions and flow:**
   - **Plan:** set the key date → pick a plan starter → tasks land with worked-out dates → owners adjust; hand-set dates stay put.
   - **Move the date:** change the key date → a preview of every date that moves → confirm.
   - **Run:** weekly work by workstream → bookings ticked with references → the day (run of show, shifts, issues).
   - **Wrap up:** the checklist → Debrief → optional report → at the end date the owner is asked **Close the team?** (and reminded once a week); **it never closes on its own**. **[call]**
   - **Run it again:** **duplicateOrg** (built) with the parts ticked, dates moved to the new key date (`shiftBy`), and the last debrief **pinned on Overview**. **[call]**
   - **Under a parent:** a fixed-time team can be an org under a club, company or community (29.2); closed, it shows as **Closed** in the parent's Projects. **[call]**
6. **Surfaces:**
   - **Countdown line** with the key date in full.
   - **Offset chip** on a task: "−14 days" beside its date.
   - **Booking row:** what, supplier, reference, status.
   - **Close card:** what's left on the wrap-up list, then Close.
7. **Design spec:**
   - Reuse 18.2's backwards dates, the Tasks Timeline, S1's calendar, W8's sections, C4's run of show, X2's shifts, M3's check-in, 11.6's Retrospective, the built archive and `duplicateOrg`, verified entries, `StatusBadge`.
   - Lucide icons: Hourglass, CalendarRange, ClipboardList, PartyPopper, Archive, Copy.
   - Add a contract test.
8. **Words:**
   - Key date · End date · Days to go · Today · Wrap-up · Workstream · Plan · Before · After · Booking · Reference · Day of · Issues today · Debrief · Next time · Close the team · Closed · Run it again · Past runs.
   - Never "Lead", "deadline missed" in red banners, or "budget" (until Money).
9. **Links:**
   - X1 (the Event team kit asks for the key date) · X2 (shifts) · X4 (the report)
   - 18.2 (backwards dates) · C4 (run of show) · M3 (event page, check-in) · L4 (typed references) · 11.6 · 29.2 · the built archive and duplicate
10. **People:**

    | | Sees | Can do |
    |---|---|---|
    | Organiser (owner, admins) | Everything | Dates, plan, bookings, wrap-up, close, run it again |
    | Workstream owner | Their workstream, bookings | Plan and tick their tasks and bookings |
    | Team member | The plan, day of | Work their tasks |
    | Volunteer (X2) | Their shifts and the run of show | Shifts |
    | Parent org admins | The team in Projects with its status | — |
11. **States:**
    - Team: Planning · This week (final 7 days) · Today · Wrap-up · Closed.
    - Booking: To book · Applied · Confirmed (with reference) · Cancelled.
12. **Edges:**
    - A key date moved after it passed asks for a reason and keeps the original in the debrief.
    - Tasks set by hand never move with the key date.
    - A closed team can be reopened by its owner (built unarchive).
    - Running it again copies no members, messages or work (built rule); people are invited again.
    - Teams without a key date are ordinary orgs; nothing here appears.
13. **Phone:** Overview leads with the countdown and this week; Day of is the phone home on the day; issues are added in one line.
14. **Accessibility:**
    - Countdown as text with the date in full.
    - Offsets as words ("14 days before").
    - Booking states as words.
15. **Notifications:**
    - Your workstream's tasks for the week: the members' weekly **Summary**.
    - Booking still not confirmed 14 days before: **Normal** to its owner.
    - Key date moved: **Important** to the team.
    - Close the team?: **Normal** to the owner at the end date, then weekly once.
16. **Trust and data:**
    - Booking references are typed; nothing is booked or paid by NetworkBase.
    - Closing archives read-only; nothing is deleted.
    - Running it again copies no people or personal work.
    - AI agents can draft plans, bookings lists and debriefs, but never move the key date, close the team or run it again.
17. **Reuse vs new:**
    - **Reuse:** backwards dates (18.2), Timeline, S1, W8 sections, C4, X2, M3, 11.6's Retrospective, archive, `duplicateOrg` and `shiftBy`, verified entries.
    - **New:**
      - key and end dates on an org
      - the countdown line
      - plan starters with offsets from the key date
      - the Booking label with references
      - the Day of view with Issues today
      - the wrap-up checklist and Close prompt
      - the pinned debrief on Run it again
18. **How we know it works:**
    - **Signal:** the share of fixed-time teams that finish their debrief before closing.
    - **Checks:**
      - moving the key date moves offset items and never hand-set ones
      - the team never archives on its own
      - Run it again copies no members or work, and pins the debrief
      - a closed child team shows as Closed in its parent

**Organization steps:**
- **Level:**
  - Parent org (optional): sees the team and its status.
  - Team org: dates, plan, bookings, day of, wrap-up.
  - Workstream (section): its tasks and bookings.
  - Member: their tasks, shifts, profile entry.
- **Moment:** set up (key date, plan) → weeks before (workstreams, bookings) → final week → the day → wrap-up → close → next year (run it again).
- **Org tab:**
  - Overview (countdown, this week, issues)
  - Tasks (plan, bookings, issues)
  - Sprints (phases, the day)
  - Documents (debrief, report)
  - Settings (Dates)

**Calls agreed 2026-11-17:**
1. A fixed-time team has a key date and an end date (30 days after by default); any org can add them.
2. Overview counts down to the key date, then counts the wrap-up.
3. The plan works backwards from the key date; moving it moves offset items, and hand-set dates stay.
4. Workstreams are W8 sections with an owner.
5. Bookings are tasks with a typed reference; NetworkBase never books or pays.
6. The Day of view brings together the run of show, shifts, check-in and Issues today.
7. Wrap-up ends in a Debrief and Close, which archives read-only; members can add a verified Organising team entry.
8. The team never closes on its own; the owner is asked at the end date.
9. Run it again duplicates the team with dates moved and the last debrief pinned.
10. A fixed-time team can sit under a parent org and shows there as Closed when done.

### 37.5 X4 · Programs and impact (agreed 2026-11-17)
**References** (37.1, plus 12 searches for impact reports, logic models, theories of change, program evaluation, annual plans, KPIs and mission statements: 107 templates, 20 rated; 4 more screens studied):

| Template / pattern | Rating | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **Nonprofit Operations Hub** | 5.0 / 7 | **Main reference for the program list:** programs as bars on a timeline with type, status and a line of what each measures |
| **KPIs Tracker** | 4.89 / 19 | **Main reference for measures:** each measure with status, goal, average and a result line (✓ or ✗), plus **logs** by month with current value against the goal |
| **NGO Annual Planning Starter** | 5.0 / 1 | **Goals** for the year → **initiatives** that support them, with area, status, priority, owner |
| **Non-Profit Mission Statement Worksheet** | 4.82 / 11 | A mission statement's ten tests, then sections to reflect, draft and refine together |
| **Impact-driven campaign one-pager** | 4.75 / 4 | **Main reference for starting a program:** what we want to change · the desired reality · why now · how it fits the mission |
| Notion's Annual Planning Exercise · 17.6 / 17.7 | 4.73 / 122 · — | Yearly planning across teams; our Impact goals and Impact report designs |

**Today:**
- **Built:** child workspaces, Updates (public or members), Documents, Files.
- **Designed:**
  - **11.4's goals** (objectives, key results, check-ins, Measured by)
  - **K3's** company goals in the D3 document, projects that **Support** a goal, Goals and Timeline views, project status updates
  - S14's workspace start and end dates
  - **17.6's Impact goals** (volunteer hours, people served) and **17.7's Impact report** (letter, numbers, stories, finances, donors)
  - X2's confirmed hours
  - K1's About labels (Mission, Values)
- **Missing:**
  - programs as the org's main units of work
  - a brief that starts a program
  - measures tied to programs and confirmed before they're published
  - an impact report that works without Money
  - consent for people named in stories

**Agreed changes from an exact copy:**
1. "Average" and pass/fail marks become **progress against a target** with the trend; no red crosses on people's work.
2. Beneficiary and donor databases are left out (parked); **people served is a typed number**.
3. The mission worksheet's ten tests become the Mission and values document's guidance text.
4. The annual planning starter becomes **K3's goals document with a Year period**.
5. 17.7's finance and donor sections are hidden until Money and Donors exist.

```
ORG · Projects → Programs          [ Timeline ] [ By goal ] [ List ]                       + Program
 Reading circles     Ongoing · since 2024 · Owner Asha     Children's literacy goal   Sessions 46/50 · Volunteer hrs 312
 Winter food drive   Dec 1 – Jan 31 · Owner Dev            Food security goal         Families served 180 / 250 (typed)
 Digital skills      Planned · starts Feb                   Livelihoods goal          —

PROGRAM (workspace) · Reading circles     Brief ▸  What we want to change · Desired reality · Why now · Fits our mission
 Measures   Sessions held 46 / 50 (from meetings)  ·  Volunteer hours 312 (from X2)  ·  Children reading weekly 64% (typed, confirmed)
 Check-in   Mar 31: "Two new circles in Whitefield" · numbers waiting confirmation (2)

ORG · Impact report 2026 (draft)   Letter · Numbers (confirmed only) · Stories (2, consent ✓) · [Finances: when Money is on]
                                   [ Save as PDF ]  [ Post as public Update ]
```

**The 18 layers**
1. **Getting it:**
   - Orgs with the Programs part (Nonprofit kit, or added from a kit) show **Projects → Programs**, an **Impact goals** setup and the **Impact report** document.
   - **Director's first look:** "Write your mission", "Set this year's impact goals", "Start a program".
   - **Program owner's first look:** the program's measures and the next check-in.
2. **Setting it up:**
   - **Settings → Programs:** the year (period), check-in rhythm (monthly), who confirms numbers (admins).
   - **Per program:** brief, owner, dates (or Ongoing), the goal it supports, up to 5 measures with targets, public or not.
3. **Items:**
   - **Program:** a **workspace marked Program** with aim, who it serves (in words), place, dates (S14) or Ongoing, an owner; listed in Projects → Programs. **[call]**
   - **Program brief:** a document template (what we want to change · the desired reality · why now · how it fits our mission · who it's for · how we'll know); making a program from it fills the program's aim. **[call]**
   - **Measure:** an 11.4 key result under the org's **impact goal**, with a target, owned by the program. **[call]**
   - **Measured by:** **volunteer hours** (X2, confirmed), **sessions held** (meetings or events tagged to the program), or **a typed number**. **People served is always a typed count; no records of individual people.** **[call]**
   - **Confirmation:** numbers typed by program owners wait for an admin's **Confirm** before they appear in a report or on About; every change keeps its history. **[call]**
   - **Year plan:** **K3's goals document with a Year period**: impact goals → the programs that support them. **[call]**
   - **Mission and values:** a document template with the worksheet's guidance; the mission shows on About (K1's labels). **[call]**
   - **Story:** a program Update marked **Story**; a person named or shown in it needs **their yes recorded** (a tick with who gave it and when). **[call]**
   - **Impact report:** 17.7's document built from a letter, **confirmed** numbers (the goals block), stories and thanks; its finance and donor parts appear only when Money and Donors exist. **Save as PDF**, **Post as public Update**. **[call]**
4. **Views:**

   | View | Who | On screen |
   |---|---|---|
   | **Programs → Timeline** | Members | Programs as bars with status, goal and a measures line |
   | **By goal** | Members | Impact goals with their programs and progress |
   | **List** | Admins | Owner, dates, measures, numbers waiting confirmation |
   | **Program Overview** | Program members | Brief, measures, last check-in, stories |
   | **Confirm numbers** | Admins | Typed numbers waiting, with who typed them and when |
   | **About → Our programs** | Visitors (opt-in) | Mission, public programs, confirmed headline numbers, the latest report |
5. **Actions and flow:**
   - **Start:** + Program → the brief → goal and measures → the workspace is made (from the Program template) → volunteers' shifts can be tagged to it (X2).
   - **Run:** sessions and shifts count on their own → owners type the other numbers on check-in days → admins confirm.
   - **Year:** set impact goals in the year plan → programs support them → year end: the Impact report draft fills itself with confirmed numbers → letter and stories → Save as PDF or post.
   - **Close a program:** status Closed with a closing note; its measures stay in history; a time-boxed program can use X3's wrap-up.
6. **Surfaces:**
   - **Program bar:** name, dates or Ongoing, owner, goal chip, the measures line.
   - **Measure row:** name, source (hours, sessions, typed), value of target, trend, "waiting confirmation" as words.
   - **Story card:** headline, photo, consent ✓ with who and when.
7. **Design spec:**
   - Reuse 11.4's goals and check-ins, K3's goals document, Supports, Goals and Timeline views, S14's dates, X2's hours, meetings and events tagging, Updates, 17.7's report, `StatusBadge`.
   - Lucide icons: HeartHandshake, Target, LineChart, BookOpenText, FileText.
   - Add a contract test.
8. **Words:**
   - Program · Ongoing · Program brief · What we want to change · Desired reality · Why now · Impact goal · Measure · Target · Sessions held · Volunteer hours · People served · Confirm · Waiting confirmation · Year plan · Mission and values · Story · Consent · Impact report.
   - Never "beneficiary record", "case", "Lead" or "KPI fail".
9. **Links:**
   - X1 (the Nonprofit kit) · X2 (hours, tagged shifts) · X3 (time-boxed programs' wrap-up)
   - 11.4 · K3 · S14 · 17.6 · 17.7 · K1 (About labels) · Updates
10. **People:**

    | | Sees | Can do |
    |---|---|---|
    | Director / admins | Everything | Goals, confirm numbers, the report, what's public |
    | Program owner | Their program | Brief, measures, check-ins, stories |
    | Member / volunteer | Programs they're in; public programs | Work, shifts, suggest stories |
    | Visitor | Opted-in programs, confirmed numbers, posted reports | — |
11. **States:**
    - Program: Planned · Running · Paused · Closed (Ongoing has no end date).
    - Number: Waiting confirmation · Confirmed.
    - Story: Draft · Consent recorded · Published.
12. **Edges:**
    - A number changed after confirmation goes back to Waiting and the old value stays in history.
    - A story whose consent is withdrawn is unpublished at once.
    - Programs never hold names, ages or addresses of the people they serve.
    - A program supporting no goal shows "Not linked" to admins only (K3).
    - Reports show only confirmed numbers; unconfirmed ones show as "not yet confirmed" in the draft.
13. **Phone:** Programs is a list; check-ins are a short form; the report is read-only on phones.
14. **Accessibility:**
    - Measures as text with value and target.
    - The timeline is also a list.
    - Consent shown as words.
15. **Notifications:**
    - Check-in day: **Normal** to program owners.
    - Numbers waiting confirmation: admins' **Summary**.
    - Report draft ready at year end: **Normal** to admins.
    - Story consent asked: **Normal** to the person named (if a member); outside people give consent offline and the owner records who and when.
16. **Trust and data:**
    - No records of individual people served.
    - Published numbers are confirmed and keep their history.
    - People in stories appear only with recorded consent.
    - Programs and numbers are private unless shown on About.
    - AI agents can draft briefs, letters and stories, but never confirm numbers or record consent.
17. **Reuse vs new:**
    - **Reuse:** 11.4's goals, K3's goals document and views, S14's dates, X2's hours, tagging meetings and events, Updates, 17.6, 17.7.
    - **New:**
      - the Program workspace mark and the Programs views
      - the Program brief template
      - measures sourced from sessions and hours
      - number confirmation with history
      - Story updates with consent
      - the Mission and values template
      - the impact report without Money
18. **How we know it works:**
    - **Signal:** the share of programs with confirmed numbers for the last check-in.
    - **Checks:**
      - only confirmed numbers reach reports and About (server test)
      - no field for an individual served person exists on programs
      - a story without consent can't be published
      - volunteer hours in measures equal X2's confirmed hours for the program

**Organization steps:**
- **Level:**
  - Org: mission, year plan, impact goals, confirmation, the report.
  - Program (workspace): brief, measures, check-ins, stories.
  - Volunteer: hours and sessions that count toward programs.
- **Moment:** founding (mission) → year start (goals, programs) → each month (check-ins, confirmation) → year end (impact report) → next year.
- **Org tab:**
  - Projects (Programs)
  - Documents (Mission and values, Year plan, Impact report, Program briefs)
  - Updates (stories, the posted report)
  - About (Our programs)
  - Settings (Programs)

**Calls agreed 2026-11-17:**
1. A program is a workspace marked Program, listed in Projects → Programs with a timeline.
2. A Program brief starts each program.
3. Each program has up to 5 measures, as 11.4 key results under the org's impact goals.
4. Measures come from volunteer hours, sessions held or typed numbers; people served is a typed count, never records of people.
5. Typed numbers need an admin's confirmation before reports or About; history is kept.
6. The year plan is K3's goals document with a Year period.
7. The mission lives in a Mission and values document and on About.
8. Stories name or show people only with their recorded yes.
9. The Impact report uses confirmed numbers, stories and a letter; finance and donor parts wait for Money.
10. Programs and numbers are private unless shown on About.

## 38. Blend rounds, end to end (complete 2026-11-18)

Section 27.4 named 15 rounds that "need a new end-to-end design"; none was written. Section 28 then changed four of them (Bugs, Requests, Content, Roadmap) into **own tabs over the same tasks** and added the **New module** (28.11) to Wave 0. This section designs every one of them inch by inch, in build order, so each can go straight to a plan when the user says "implement".

### 38.1 The rounds, the order and the depth

**What the code has today (checked 2026-11-17):**
- **Tasks** (`tasks`): `kind` is only `task` or `assignment`; `status` todo · in_progress · done · blocked; `reviewStatus`; `workflowColumnId`; `sprintId`; `priority`; `taskNumber` (NB-n); `labels[]`; `dueDate`; **no start date, no type, no stage, no parent ("Part of")**. Subtasks live in their own helpers (`task-subtasks.ts`).
- **Board columns** (`workspace_workflow_columns`): up to six per workspace, each tied to one status.
- **Documents** (`workspace_documents`): `settings` holds `editPolicy`, `visibilityOverride`, `externalImages`, `projectBlocks`; **no section, kind or date yet**; versions in `workspace_document_versions`.
- **Smart blocks** (`doc-blocks.ts`): `roles`, `contributors`, `files`, `tasks`, `sprints`, `projects` only.
- **Tabs** (`WorkspaceLayout`): a fixed `TABS` list filtered by role and `publicTabVisibility`; **no per-workspace list of added workflows**.
- **Create** (`CreateTaskModal`): Task · Assignment tabs.

**The depth for every round (the inch-by-inch standard) [call]:**
1. **What it is and the references:** the chosen Notion reference from the category section, checked again against prototype v4.
2. **The 18 layers** (section 10), rewritten for the blended home.
3. **Step-by-step walkthroughs:** every journey click by click, for each role (owner, admin, member, viewer, outside viewer, a child workspace under an organization lock), on desktop and phone: first use (empty state), everyday use, and the edge journeys.
4. **Screen spec:** every screen, panel and dialog: regions, the existing components reused (by file), every field (label, type, default, validation, error text), every button (when it's enabled, what it does, undo), and empty, loading and error states.
5. **Data:** columns and tables to add (with migration names), JSON shapes, indexes, the permission rows, and what's worked out versus stored.
6. **Server:** each action (name, zod input, checks, side effects: activity, notifications, realtime broadcasts, caches), idempotency and rate limits.
7. **Rules as pure functions,** each with its test cases written out.
8. **Everything around it:** Overview cards, notifications (who hears what, at which level), CLI commands and MCP tools (B13), agents, search, public visibility, the organization lock.
9. **Rollout:** existing data, the flag, how it switches on for current workspaces.
10. **Tests:** unit, contract, end-to-end journeys and the browser check list.
11. **Calls** for the user, marked **[call]**.

This closes three items from 28.10 as the rounds go: **Overview cards**, **notifications per type**, and **CLI and MCP** for the new types.

**Size:** each round runs about 400–800 lines, presented in chat and added on "yes", one at a time, like sections 29–37.

**Not in these rounds (still parked, 28.2):** Money, Shop, Pipeline and its presets, the public Feedback page, Support inbox, Incidents and Status page, the Event planner (except off-site), the Course planner, the Goals tab, Podcast and Video setups, the Client portal, 1:1s.

### 38.2 F1 · Types, stages and Add workflow (agreed 2026-11-17)

F1 is the floor every other round stands on: a task can have a **type** and a **stage**, a stage decides the **status** and whether the item is **on the board**, and a workspace keeps a list of the **workflows it added**, which the tab row, the dialog and the organization lock read. F1 adds no workflow people can use by itself; each later round registers its own.

#### 1. What it is and the references
| Reference | Rating / source | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **Prototype v4** (28.7) | The user's reviewed look | The Add workflow dialog with groups, a one-line "Adds to Tasks: …" per row, roles, the organization lock, the tab row divider |
| Notion's **+ Add a view** menu | Pattern | A short grouped list with an icon and one line each; the choice is applied in place |
| Linear's **workflow states** | Pattern | Many named states, each belonging to one of a few fixed categories; boards and reports read the category, people see the state name |
| 28.1–28.4 | Agreed | The rule "a tab is a job", the stage → status table, B1–B14 |

**Agreed changes from an exact copy:** the categories are our four statuses (To do · In progress · Blocked · Completed), not new ones; stage names are fixed per type in this release; no per-workspace custom types.

#### 2. The 18 layers
1. **Getting it:** owners and admins see **+ Add workflow** at the end of the tab row (desktop) or in ⋯ (phone, B14), in Settings → Workflows, and in the create wizard's Settings step (decision 5). Members never see the button.
2. **Setting it up:** adding is one click per workflow; nothing else to fill in. Each workflow's own round decides its starting fields, views and examples.
3. **Items:** every work item is a task row (decision 1) with an **item type** (Task · Bug · Request · Content · Project · Roadmap item · Objective · Key result · Idea · Lesson) and a **stage** from that type's list.
4. **Views:** the Tasks tab gains a **Type** filter chip; cards show the type icon and stage; own tabs (Bugs, Requests, Content, Roadmap) arrive in their rounds.
5. **Actions and flow:** stages move an item; a stage decides its status and whether it's on the board (28.3); joining the board asks which sprint (B5); leaving it records "Moved back" (B7); Blocked keeps the stage (B2); done stages wait for review where review is on (B3).
6. **Surfaces:** the tab row, the Add workflow dialog, the Remove dialog, the Join-board sheet, the type mark on cards and item pages, Settings → Workflows, the wizard section, the organization's Workflows settings.
7. **Design spec:** existing shared parts only (dialog shell, `Field`, `SectionDivider`, `QuickChips`, `StatusBadge`, the tab row); Lucide icons per type (below); a contract test.
8. **Words:** Add workflow · Remove workflow · Added · Added by [organization] · Blends into Tasks · Own tab · same tasks · Blends into Documents / Files / Updates / Sprints · Later · parked · Type · Stage · Shows in · Joins Tasks at Fixing · Add to Week 47 · Moved back to Bugs · Hide · Completed (never "Done").
9. **Links:** Tasks, the board, sprints and sprint history, review, My Work, search, CLI, MCP, agents, organizations, the wizard.
10. **People:** owners and admins add and remove (decision 3); members use what's added; viewers read; the public sees no workflow tab (B11); organization admins push workflows into child workspaces, which show a lock (decision 4, B12).
11. **States:** dialog loading, empty search, everything added, error with retry; live updates when another admin adds or removes; two admins adding at once (the second sees "Already added").
12. **Edges:** removing a workflow (hide only, below); re-adding it; items whose type was removed; a workspace leaving an organization keeps pushed workflows as its own.
13. **Phone:** workflow tabs after a divider; Add workflow in ⋯; the dialog is a full-height sheet.
14. **Accessibility:** the dialog is a labelled list of buttons; stage menus are real menus; every drag has a "Move to…" menu.
15. **Notifications:** adding or removing a workflow notifies no one; it goes into the workspace activity. Stage moves follow the existing task notifications.
16. **Trust and data:** the same task permissions; only owners and admins change the workflow list; nothing public.
17. **Reuse vs new:** below (part 8).
18. **How we know it works:** below (part 10).

#### 3. Step-by-step walkthroughs

**W1 · An admin adds Bugs (desktop, first time)**
1. Asha (admin) opens the workspace; the tab row ends with **+ Add workflow** (a ghost button with a Plus icon).
2. She clicks it; the **Add workflow** dialog opens (640 px), focus on the search box.
3. The dialog shows groups in a fixed order: **Blends into Tasks** · **Own tab · same tasks** · **Blends into Documents** · **Blends into Files** · **Blends into Updates** · **Blends into Sprints** · **Later · parked**. Only workflows whose round is built appear outside "Later · parked".
4. Under **Own tab · same tasks** she sees **Bugs** with the line "Adds a Bugs tab. Bugs join Tasks at Fixing." and an **Add** button.
5. She clicks **Add**. The row turns to **Added ✓** with a **Remove** link; a toast says "Bugs added" with **Undo** (10 seconds).
6. Behind the dialog the tab row now shows a divider and **Bugs** after the default tabs.
7. She closes the dialog (✕, Esc or clicking outside); focus returns to **+ Add workflow**.
8. She opens **Bugs**: the empty state from round T3 ("No bugs yet · New bug").

**W2 · Undo right after adding**
1. Within 10 seconds Asha clicks **Undo** in the toast.
2. If no item of that type was created yet, the workflow row is deleted and the tab disappears; the toast says "Bugs removed".
3. If an item was already created, Undo is replaced by "Can't undo: 1 bug was added. Remove from Settings → Workflows."

**W3 · A member opens the workspace after Bugs was added**
1. Dev (member) sees the divider and **Bugs** in the tab row; no **+ Add workflow** button.
2. Live: if Dev had the workspace open when Asha added it, the tab appears without a reload (workspace settings broadcast).
3. Dev's Tasks board is unchanged until bugs join it.

**W4 · A bug walks onto the board and off again**
1. Mei creates a bug in **Bugs** (round F3's New module); it starts at the first stage, **New**, not on the board.
2. Mei moves it to **Confirmed** (stage menu on the item page or in the Bugs list); still not on the board.
3. Mei moves it to **Fixing**; the **Join-board sheet** opens: "Bug joins Tasks at Fixing" with **Add to Week 47** ticked (the running sprint) and **Move** button.
4. She keeps the tick and clicks **Move**: status becomes In progress, the card appears in the In progress column of Week 47 with the bug icon, **NB-142** and the chip **Bug · Fixing**.
5. If she unticks, the bug goes to the Backlog with status In progress.
6. Later Mei moves it back to **Confirmed**: the card leaves the board; Week 47's history shows "NB-142 moved back to Bugs" (B7); status returns to To do; its sprint is cleared.

**W5 · Dragging a bug card on the board**
1. Karan drags NB-142 from In progress to **Blocked**: status Blocked; the chip reads **Bug · Fixing · Blocked** (B2).
2. He drags it to **Completed** in a workspace without required review: stage becomes **Fixed**, status Completed.
3. In a workspace **with** required review: the card goes to In review (review requested); the stage stays **Fixing** until a reviewer approves, then becomes **Fixed** (B3).
4. Dragging a Completed card back to In progress sets the stage back to **Fixing** (the join stage).

**W6 · Filtering Tasks by type**
1. Tasks shows a **Type** chip in the filter row only when more than one type exists in the workspace.
2. Clicking it opens a menu: All types · Task · Bug · Request · Content (only types that have items on the board).
3. Picking **Bug** filters the board and list; the chip reads "Type: Bug" with an ✕ to clear.

**W7 · Removing a workflow (hide)**
1. Asha opens **+ Add workflow** (or Settings → Workflows) and clicks **Remove** on Bugs.
2. The **Remove Bugs?** dialog shows what it holds: "24 bugs · 6 open · 3 on the board".
3. It explains: "The Bugs tab and the bug stages are hidden. The 3 bugs on the board stay there as plain tasks until they're completed. Nothing is deleted; add Bugs again to bring everything back."
4. She clicks **Hide Bugs**. The tab disappears for everyone; bugs not on the board stop showing anywhere except search results marked "Hidden workflow"; the 3 on the board show a greyed bug mark.
5. Adding Bugs again later restores the tab, every bug and its stage.

**W8 · An organization pushes a workflow**
1. The org admin opens the organization's **Settings → Workflows for workspaces** and clicks **Add to every workspace** on Bugs.
2. A confirm line says "Adds Bugs to 14 workspaces in this organization. They can't remove it."
3. In each child workspace the tab appears with a small lock; the dialog row reads **Added by Northgate CS** with Remove greyed and a tooltip "Only Northgate CS can remove it".
4. A child that had already added Bugs itself keeps one tab; its row shows "Added by Northgate CS" and its own row is kept underneath in case the org removes it later.
5. When the org removes it, the W7 dialog appears for the org admin with totals across workspaces; children that had added it themselves keep it.

**W9 · Creating a workspace from the wizard**
1. On the wizard's Settings step, the section **Workflows** lists the category's suggestions from section 6 that are built, with only the top one ticked (decision 5); e.g. Open source: **Bugs** ticked, Roadmap and Requests unticked.
2. Under an organization, pushed workflows show as locked rows "Set by Northgate CS".
3. Creating the workspace adds the ticked workflows in the same transaction.

**W10 · Phone**
1. The tab row scrolls; after the default tabs comes a thin divider, then Bugs and other workflow tabs.
2. **+ Add workflow** lives in the ⋯ menu at the end of the row (owners and admins only).
3. The dialog opens as a full-height sheet with the same groups; Add buttons are 44 px tall.
4. Stage moves use the item page's **Stage** menu; the Join-board sheet is a bottom sheet.

**W11 · Viewer and the public**
1. A viewer sees workflow tabs and reads items; stage menus are read-only.
2. A visitor to a public workspace never sees workflow tabs (B11); direct links to `?tab=bugs` fall back to the landing tab.

**W12 · An agent through MCP**
1. The agent calls `networkbase_task_list` with `type: "bug", stage: "confirmed"` and gets the list.
2. It calls `networkbase_task_move` with `stage: "fixing"`; the server applies the same rules; with no sprint given, the bug joins the running sprint (the default tick), and the activity shows "via agent".
3. It can't add or remove workflows; the tool list has no such tool.

#### 4. Screen spec
**S1 · Tab row (`WorkspaceLayout`)**
- Default tabs as today (Overview · About · Documents · Updates · Sprints · Tasks · Files · Workspaces · Members · Settings).
- After Tasks' group, a 1 px divider, then added own tabs in a fixed order: **Bugs · Requests · Content · Roadmap**, each with its Lucide icon (Bug, Inbox, PenLine, Map).
- A locked tab shows a 12 px Lock icon after the label; hover: "Added by [organization]".
- **+ Add workflow** (owners and admins, desktop): ghost button with Plus, label hidden below 1100 px (icon with tooltip).
- Keyboard: tabs keep the existing arrow-key roving focus; the button is the last stop.

**S2 · Add workflow dialog**
- Shell: the shared 640 px dialog; title "Add workflow"; subtitle "Workflows add views, stages or tabs. Everyone in the workspace uses them."; ✕.
- Search box: placeholder "Search workflows"; filters by name and line; empty result: "No workflow matches '[text]'".
- Group headers (`SectionDivider` style) in the order of W1 step 3; a group with nothing shows nothing.
- **Row:** 20 px icon · name (`nb-ui-label`) · one line "Adds to Tasks: Projects view, Timeline" or "Adds a Bugs tab. Bugs join Tasks at Fixing." · right side: **Add** (secondary button) / **Added ✓** + **Remove** (link) / **Added by [org]** with a lock (Remove disabled).
- **Later · parked** rows: greyed, no button, line "Coming later".
- Footer: none (each row acts on its own).
- States: loading (6 skeleton rows), error ("Couldn't load workflows" + Try again), everything added ("Every available workflow is added").
- Members who reach it by link see the list read-only with "Only owners and admins can add workflows."

**S3 · Remove dialog**
- Title "Remove [workflow]?"; counts line (items, open, on the board); the explanation from W7 step 3; buttons **Cancel** · **Hide [workflow]** (primary, destructive tone not used: nothing is lost).
- Blend workflows (e.g. Project planner) say what disappears: "The Projects and Timeline views are hidden. Projects keep their tasks."

**S4 · Join-board sheet**
- Title "[Type] joins Tasks at [stage]"; checkbox **Add to [running sprint name]** (ticked; hidden when no sprint is running, then text "Goes to the Backlog"); buttons **Cancel** · **Move**.
- Remembered per person per workspace for 24 hours ("Don't ask again today" is not offered; the tick is remembered instead).

**S5 · Type mark on cards and rows (`TaskCard`)**
- Before NB-n: the type icon (Task shows none, to keep today's cards unchanged).
- A stage chip when the type has stages other than the four statuses: "Bug · Fixing"; with Blocked: "Bug · Fixing · Blocked".
- Hidden workflow: icon at 40 % opacity, tooltip "Bugs is hidden in this workspace".

**S6 · Type filter (`TaskFilters`)**
- A chip after the existing scope menu; menu items with icons and counts; keyboard-reachable; clears with ✕.

**S7 · Item page header (`TaskDetailPanel`)**
- Under the title: "Shows in: **Tasks · In progress** / **Bugs · Fixing**" (links); a **Stage** menu listing the type's stages with two brackets: "Bugs" (all stages) and "On the board" (the stages that join).
- For Task type nothing changes.

**S8 · Settings → Workflows** (new section after "Stages and workflow")
- The same rows as S2 for added workflows, plus "Added by Asha · Nov 17" under each; **Add workflow** button opens S2.

**S9 · Wizard → Workflows** (`Phase4Settings`, a new `LaunchSection` after "Journey stages")
- Checkboxes with the row line; top suggestion ticked; locked rows "Set by [org]".

**S10 · Organization → Settings → Workflows for workspaces**
- Rows with **Add to every workspace** / **Pushed to 14 workspaces** + **Remove from workspaces**.

#### 5. Data
**Migration `0101_workflow_types.sql`:**
- `tasks.item_type text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'task'` with a check over the registry's ids (`task, bug, request, content, project, roadmap_item, objective, key_result, idea, class_lesson`).
- `tasks.stage text NULL`: null for `task` (its stage is its status); otherwise a key from the type's stage list (checked in the server, not in SQL, so new stages need no migration).
- `tasks.type_fields jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'`: each type's own fields (severity, steps…), validated by the type's zod schema in its round.
- `tasks.on_board boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true`: written by the server from the stage on every change; off-board items have `workflow_column_id NULL`.
- Indexes: `tasks_workspace_type_stage_idx (workspace_id, item_type, stage) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`; the board's existing query adds `AND on_board`.
- **New table `workspace_workflows`:** `id uuid`, `workspace_id uuid → workspaces (cascade)`, `workflow text`, `push_to_children boolean default false` (true only on an organization's rows), `added_by uuid → profiles (set null)`, `added_at timestamptz`, `hidden_at timestamptz null`, `hidden_by uuid null`; unique `(workspace_id, workflow)`.
- **Flag:** `workspaces.workflows_enabled boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false` (like `branches_enabled`).
- Sprint history: `workspace_sprint_events.event_type` gains `joined_from_workflow` and `moved_back` (text column, no migration needed beyond the server).

**Worked out, never stored:** a child's effective workflows (own rows ∪ parent rows with `push_to_children`, minus hidden); whether a stage is on the board; the status for a stage.

**In code (new):**
- `src/lib/workflows/types.ts`: one entry per type: id, label, Lucide icon, stages `[{ key, label, status, onBoard, closing? }]`, `joinStage`, `firstStage`, `doneStage`.
- `src/lib/workflows/catalog.ts`: one entry per workflow: id, name, group, line, the types and views it adds, `built` (false until its round ships), section 6 suggestions, `parked`.

**The F1 stage table (from 28.3; later rounds may add closing stages):**

| Type | Stages (own tab) | On the board | Status for each stage |
|---|---|---|---|
| Task | — | always | its status |
| Bug | New · Confirmed · Fixing · Fixed · Verified · closed: Won't fix · Duplicate · Can't reproduce | Fixing, Fixed, Verified | New, Confirmed → todo (off board) · Fixing → in_progress · Fixed, Verified → done · closed → done (off board) |
| Request | New · Accepted · In progress · In review · Delivered · closed: Declined | Accepted → Delivered | New → todo (off) · Accepted → todo · In progress, In review → in_progress (In review requests review) · Delivered → done · Declined → done (off) |
| Content | Idea · Drafting · Editing · Scheduled · Published | Drafting → Published | Idea → todo (off) · Drafting, Editing → in_progress · Scheduled, Published → done |
| Project, Roadmap item, Objective, Key result, Idea, Lesson | defined in T1, T2, D3, D4, 30.3 | never | worked out from their work, never on the board |

**Permissions:**

| Action | Who |
|---|---|
| See workflow tabs and items | Workspace members and viewers (as Tasks today); never the public |
| Create items, move stages | Whoever can create or edit tasks today; viewers can't |
| Add or remove a workflow | Owners, admins, inherited org admins (`canManageSettings`) |
| Push to child workspaces | Organization owners and admins |
| Remove a pushed workflow in a child | Nobody in the child |

#### 6. Server
- **`addWorkflowAction({ workspaceId, workflow })`**: zod: uuid + catalog id. Checks: signed in; `canManageSettings`; `workflows_enabled`; catalog entry `built` and not `parked`. Inserts or clears `hidden_at` (idempotent on the unique key). Side effects: activity "added Bugs"; workspace settings broadcast (tab rows refresh); cache tag for the workspace layout. Returns `{ undoToken }`.
- **`undoAddWorkflowAction({ undoToken })`**: valid 10 s; refuses if any item of the workflow's types was created since.
- **`removeWorkflowAction({ workspaceId, workflow })`**: same checks plus "not pushed by a parent"; sets `hidden_at`, `hidden_by`; activity "hid Bugs"; broadcast. Returns the counts shown in S3 (computed before the write).
- **`pushWorkflowAction` / `unpushWorkflowAction({ orgId, workflow })`**: org owners and admins; sets `push_to_children` on the org's own row; broadcast to child workspaces in batches.
- **`setTaskStageAction({ taskId, stage, sprintId? | toBacklog? })`**: runs inside the existing `transitionTaskTx` lock; computes `{ status, onBoard, column, needsReview }` with the pure functions; writes stage, status, `on_board`, `workflow_column_id` (default column for the status when joining, null when leaving), sprint; writes sprint events (`joined_from_workflow`, `moved_back`); then `afterTaskTransition` (notifications, broadcasts) as today.
- **Board drags** (existing move path): call `boardMove` before writing; review gating as today.
- **`createTaskAction`** gains `itemType` and `stage` (the module itself is F3); defaults: from Tasks → the join stage; from an own tab → the first stage.
- **Reads:** `fetchWorkspaceTasksAction` and `GET /api/v1/tasks` gain `type` and `stage` filters; board reads add `on_board`; the task payload gains `itemType`, `stage`, `typeFields`, `onBoard`.
- **Limits:** the existing settings write rate limit; stage moves use the task write limit.

#### 7. Rules as pure functions (`src/lib/workflows/rules.ts`) and their tests
- `statusForStage(type, stage)` → status. Tests: bug New → todo; bug Fixing → in_progress; bug Verified → done; request In review → in_progress; content Scheduled → done; unknown stage → throws.
- `isOnBoard(type, stage)` → boolean. Tests: bug Confirmed false; bug Fixing true; bug Won't fix false; task (no stage) true; project anything false.
- `stageMove(type, from, to)` → `{ joins, leaves, needsSprintChoice }`. Tests: Confirmed → Fixing joins and asks; Fixing → Confirmed leaves; Fixing → Fixed neither.
- `boardMove(type, stage, toStatus, reviewRequired)` → `{ stage, status, review }`. Tests: Fixing → blocked keeps Fixing (B2); Fixing → done without review gives Fixed; with review gives Fixing + review requested (B3); done → in_progress gives the join stage; content Drafting → done gives Scheduled.
- `effectiveWorkflows(ownRows, parentRows)` → `[{ workflow, locked, by }]`. Tests: own only; parent push only (locked); both (one entry, locked, own row kept); own hidden + parent pushed → shown locked; parent unpushed → own reappears if not hidden.
- `canChangeWorkflows(viewer)` → boolean. Tests: owner, admin, inherited org admin true; member, viewer false.
- `removalSummary(items)` → `{ total, open, onBoard }`. Tests: counts by stage closing and `on_board`.
- `defaultStageFor(type, openedFrom)` → stage. Tests: bug from Tasks → Fixing; bug from Bugs → New; request from Tasks → Accepted.

#### 8. Everything around it
- **Overview cards:** none added by F1; each own-tab round adds its card.
- **Notifications:**

  | Event | Who | Level |
  |---|---|---|
  | Workflow added, hidden, pushed | Nobody (activity only) | — |
  | An item joins the board assigned to you | The assignee | Normal (today's assignment notice) |
  | An item you're assigned is moved back off the board | The assignee | Normal |
  | Review requested from a done stage | Reviewers | as today |

- **CLI (`packages/nb-cli/lib/commands/tasks.mjs`):** `nb tasks list --type bug --stage confirmed`; `nb tasks create --type bug "Title"` (starts at the join stage, like New ▾ in Tasks); `nb tasks move NB-142 --stage fixing [--backlog]`; `nb workflows` (read-only list of added workflows). Unknown types and stages print the valid list.
- **MCP (`lib/mcp/tools.mjs`):** `networkbase_task_list` gains `type` and `stage`; `networkbase_task_create` gains `type`; `networkbase_task_move` gains `stage` and `backlog`; new read tool `networkbase_workflow_list`. No tool adds or removes workflows.
- **Agents:** move stages under the same rules (B13); never close a bug as Won't fix or Duplicate without a person's yes (tier "yes"), never add or remove workflows.
- **Search:** results show the type icon and stage; hidden-workflow items show "Hidden workflow".
- **My Work:** items show by assignee as today, with the type icon; off-board items appear under their own tab's filter, not under "In progress".
- **Public:** no workflow tab, item type or stage is public (B11).
- **Organization lock:** S2, S10 and W8.

#### 9. Rollout
1. Migration 0101 adds columns with defaults: every existing task becomes type `task`, no stage, on the board; nothing changes on screen.
2. `workflows_enabled` is false everywhere; the tab row, dialog and settings section render only when it's true.
3. Turn it on for test workspaces first; turn it on per workspace as each round ships; the catalog's `built` flag keeps unbuilt workflows in "Later · parked".
4. Older CLI versions ignore the new fields; `nb` gets `--type` and `--stage` in the next minor version.

#### 10. Tests
- **Unit:** every case in part 7.
- **Server:** a member can't add or remove; a child can't remove a pushed workflow; stage moves respect review (B3); moving back writes the sprint event; Undo refuses after an item exists; adding twice is a no-op.
- **Contract test** (`tests/unit/workflow-dialog-design-contract.test.ts`): the dialog uses the shared shell, groups in order, row anatomy, no custom colors.
- **End to end:** admin adds Bugs → creates a bug → moves to Fixing with the sprint tick → drags to Completed with review on → approves → hides Bugs → the board card shows the greyed mark → adds Bugs again → everything is back.
- **Browser check list:** desktop and phone tab rows; dialog keyboard path (Tab, Enter, Esc); screen reader names for rows and lock; live tab appearance in a second browser; organization push in a child.
