### 38.3 F2 · Document sections and live blocks (agreed 2026-11-17)

F2 gives Documents what the D rounds need: **sections** in the rail (Pages · Meetings · Decisions · Launches · Goals · Ideas · Off-site) and **live blocks** whose ticks and rows are records, not document text (B8). It adds one live block people use at once, **task rows** (action items, launch steps, checklists), plus the **decisions list**, and registers the goals and ranked-ideas blocks that D3 and D4 fill in.

#### 1. What it is and the references
| Reference | Rating / source | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **Prototype v4** (28.7) | The user's reviewed look | Rail sections, a meeting with an Action items block whose ticks are real tasks, the Decisions list with D-numbers |
| **Meetings** (Notion) | 4.8 / 200+ (11.6) | Action items inside the meeting page that are database rows with an owner and a date |
| Notion **linked database view** | Pattern | A live list inside a page, filtered to "this page", added from a menu |
| What the code has | Checked 2026-11-17 | Documents are **Markdown files** linked to Files (`linkedNodeId`), edited in the Files editor (CodeMirror, explicit **Save**); the Documents tab renders the published version with `react-markdown`; smart blocks are typed by hand as `{% project.tasks ids="…" %}` (at most 12 ids) and render **read-only** previews; the rail is a flat list except in organizations (groups) |

**Agreed changes from an exact copy:** rows belong to the document and block they were made in, not to a filter people build; there are no property columns to configure; blocks are inserted from a menu, never typed.

#### 2. The 18 layers
1. **Getting it:** sections appear in the rail when a workflow that uses them is added (F1); live blocks come in the D rounds' templates and from the editor's **Insert** menu.
2. **Setting it up:** nothing to set; a section is chosen when a document is made from a template or moved with **Move to section**.
3. **Items:** a document gets a **section**, a **kind** (e.g. Weekly) and a **date**; a task-rows block's rows are **tasks made from that document and block**; a decision is a **document in Decisions** with a D-number and the document it came from.
4. **Views:** the rail groups documents by section, newest first inside dated sections; each live block shows its rows.
5. **Actions and flow:** add a row, tick it, assign it, give it a date, reorder, remove it from the block; record a decision; move a document between sections.
6. **Surfaces:** rail sections with **+ New** per section, the live task-rows block, the decisions list, the editor's Insert menu, the item page's "From" line.
7. **Design spec:** rows use `TaskCard`'s row variant parts (checkbox, title, avatar, date chip, NB-n); blocks use the existing smart-block frame (`WorkspaceDocSmartBlock`); a contract test.
8. **Words:** Pages · Meetings · Decisions · Launches · Goals · Ideas · Off-site · Move to section · Action items · + Add action item · Record a decision · D-014 · From: Weekly · Nov 12 · Insert · Live block.
9. **Links:** Tasks (rows are tasks), My Work, sprints, review, Files (the document file), versions, search, CLI, MCP.
10. **People:** adding rows follows the document's edit permission; ticking follows the task's (B9); reading follows the document's visibility.
11. **States:** block loading (row skeletons), a row someone else ticked arrives live, a row you can't see shows as "1 more item you can't see", offline tick retries.
12. **Edges:** the document is deleted, the block's line is removed from the text, the document is copied as a template, a row's task is deleted, 200 rows.
13. **Phone:** rows are full-width with a 44 px checkbox; + Add opens a bottom sheet.
14. **Accessibility:** rows are a list of checkboxes with the task title as label; reorder by menu ("Move up / Move down").
15. **Notifications:** assigning a row uses the task assignment notice, with "From [document]".
16. **Trust and data:** live state is in tasks; the document text holds only the block line; public documents show rows only when Tasks is public.
17. **Reuse vs new:** below.
18. **How we know it works:** below.

#### 3. Step-by-step walkthroughs
**W1 · Sections appear when a workflow is added**
1. Asha adds **Meetings & decisions** (F1 dialog).
2. The Documents rail now shows, under the existing list (which becomes **Pages**): **Meetings** and **Decisions**, each with a muted "+ New meeting" / "+ Record a decision" line while empty.
3. Workspaces without any document workflow keep today's flat rail; the word "Pages" appears only once another section exists.

**W2 · Moving an existing document into a section**
1. On a document, ⋯ → **Move to section** opens a small menu: Pages · Meetings · Decisions (only sections whose workflow is added).
2. Choosing **Meetings** asks for a date (default: the document's creation date) and an optional kind; the document moves in the rail.
3. No version is written: section, kind and date live in the document's settings.

**W3 · Adding an action item in a meeting**
1. Dev opens "Weekly · Nov 12" (made from the Weekly template in D1, which already holds an Action items block).
2. Under **Action items** he clicks **+ Add action item**: an inline row opens with a title box focused, an **Assigned to** picker and a **Due** chip.
3. He types "Book the venue", picks Mei, picks **1 week**, presses Enter.
4. A task is created (**NB-150**, type Task, To do, **Backlog**, assigned to Mei, due Nov 19) with "From: Weekly · Nov 12"; the row appears at the bottom of the block; the input stays open for the next one; Esc closes it.
5. Mei gets the usual assignment notice: "Dev assigned you NB-150 · From: Weekly · Nov 12".
6. The document's text and versions don't change.

**W4 · Ticking from the document**
1. Mei ticks NB-150's box in the meeting.
2. The task moves to **Completed** (or to **In review** where review is required, the box shows a half tick and "In review").
3. Everyone viewing the document or the board sees it change live.
4. Undo: the toast's **Undo** within 10 seconds puts it back.

**W5 · Someone who can't edit the document**
1. Karan (member) opens a meeting whose edit policy is **leaders**.
2. He can tick rows assigned to him or that he can edit as tasks (B9); **+ Add action item** isn't shown; a line under the block says "Only leaders add items here."

**W6 · Recording a decision**
1. In the meeting's **Decisions** block, Asha clicks **+ Record a decision**.
2. A sheet asks for the decision in one line and optional context; **Record**.
3. A new document **D-014 · Use Postgres for search** is made in **Decisions** with "From: Weekly · Nov 12", status **Decided**; the meeting's block lists it.
4. The D-number is the workspace's next one; it never changes, even if the decision is later Superseded (D1).

**W7 · Inserting a live block while editing**
1. An editor opens the document's file (**Edit** → Files editor).
2. The toolbar shows **Insert ▾** for Markdown files linked to a document: **Action items** · **Checklist** · **Decisions** (and **Goals**, **Ranked ideas** once D3 and D4 ship).
3. Choosing **Action items** inserts one line at the cursor: `{% project.task_rows key="k7f3" label="Action items" %}` with a fresh key; Save writes a new version as today.
4. On the Documents tab the block renders live and empty: "No action items yet · + Add action item".

**W8 · Reordering and removing rows**
1. Hover a row: a ⋯ menu with **Move up**, **Move down**, **Remove from this list**, **Open task**.
2. **Remove from this list** keeps the task but detaches it ("From" line goes); deleting the task is done from the task itself.
3. Dragging rows by the handle reorders (desktop); the menu works everywhere.

**W9 · Copying a document as a template**
1. An org template or a D6 template is copied into a workspace.
2. Its blocks come across as lines; because rows belong to the original document, the copy starts with **empty blocks**.

**W10 · A block's line is deleted from the text**
1. An editor removes the block line and saves.
2. The rows stay tasks; their "From" line still links to the document; the document shows a quiet note at the end for editors: "3 items from a removed list · Show".

**W11 · Phone**
1. Sections collapse into a **Section** menu at the top of the Documents tab.
2. Rows are full width; **+ Add action item** opens a bottom sheet with title, assignee and due.

**W12 · Public reader**
1. A public meeting document in a workspace whose Tasks tab isn't public shows the block frame with "Action items are visible to members."
2. Where Tasks is public, rows show read-only with titles and states, no assignee pictures.

**W13 · An agent through MCP**
1. `networkbase_doc_rows_add` with the document and block key adds rows ("small" tier) when the agent's person can edit the document.
2. Ticking uses `networkbase_task_done` as today.

#### 4. Screen spec
**S1 · Rail (`WorkspaceDocRail`)**
- Section headers (11 px, muted, as the organization groups today) in a fixed order: Pages · Meetings · Decisions · Launches · Goals · Ideas · Off-site; only sections whose workflow is added, plus Pages.
- Inside **Meetings**: newest date first, the date before the title ("Nov 12 · Weekly"); inside **Decisions**: "D-014 · Title"; others by title.
- Each header has a **+** (editors only) that opens the section's template choice (D rounds); before those rounds, it opens Add document with the section preset.
- Collapsible headers, remembered per person (local storage).

**S2 · Move to section menu**
- Items: the available sections with icons; the current one ticked; for Meetings and Launches a date field appears; **Move**.

**S3 · Task-rows block (`WorkspaceDocLiveBlock`)**
- Frame: the smart-block frame with the label ("Action items") and a count "3 open · 2 completed".
- Row: drag handle (desktop, hover) · checkbox · title (click opens the task panel) · NB-n (muted) · type icon if not Task · assignee avatar · due chip · ⋯.
- Completed rows stay in place with a struck title for 7 days, then move under "Completed (n)" folded at the end.
- **+ Add action item** (label follows the block's label: "+ Add step", "+ Add item").
- Inline add row: title (required, 1–200 chars, error "Add a title"), Assigned to (members picker), Due (QuickChips: Today · 1 week · 2 weeks · Pick a date); Enter adds, Esc cancels.
- Rows you can't see: one muted line "1 more item you can't see".
- Empty: "No action items yet" + the add line.
- Loading: 3 skeleton rows; error: "Couldn't load these items · Try again".

**S4 · Decisions block**
- Rows: D-number · title · status chip (Proposed · Decided · Superseded · Reversed) · date; **+ Record a decision** (sheet: Decision (required, 1–200), Context (optional, up to 2,000), **Record**).

**S5 · Editor Insert menu (`TextViewer` toolbar, Markdown files linked to a document)**
- **Insert ▾** with the block names and a one-line hint each; inserts on its own line at the cursor; disabled in Raw mode.

**S6 · "From" line on the task page (`TaskDetailPanel`)**
- Under "Shows in": "From: **Weekly · Nov 12** · Action items" (link to the document at the block).

#### 5. Data
**Migration `0102_doc_sections_live_blocks.sql`:**
- `tasks.source_doc_id uuid NULL → workspace_documents(id) ON DELETE SET NULL`
- `tasks.source_block text NULL` (the block key, 4–12 chars)
- `tasks.source_position double precision NULL` (order inside the block)
- Index `tasks_source_block_idx (source_doc_id, source_block, source_position) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`
- `workspace_documents.settings` (JSON, no migration): `section` ('pages' | 'meetings' | 'decisions' | 'launches' | 'goals' | 'ideas' | 'offsite'), `kind` (text), `date` (YYYY-MM-DD), `fromDocId` (uuid), `decisionNumber` (integer), `decisionStatus` ('proposed' | 'decided' | 'superseded' | 'reversed').
- Unique index `workspace_documents_decision_number_unique (workspace_id, ((settings->>'decisionNumber')::int)) WHERE settings ? 'decisionNumber'`.
- Index `workspace_documents_section_idx (workspace_id, (settings->>'section'))`.

**Block syntax (extends `doc-blocks.ts`):**
- `{% project.task_rows key="…" label="…" %}`: rows are tasks with this document and key.
- `{% project.decisions %}`: decision documents whose `fromDocId` is this document.
- `{% project.goals period="2027-Q1" %}` and `{% project.ranked type="idea" key="…" %}`: registered now, rendered by D3 and D4 (until then they show "Available when Goals is added").
- Unknown or not-yet-available kinds render the existing "unknown block" frame.

**Worked out, never stored:** block counts, which rows the reader can see, the rail grouping.

**Permissions:**

| Action | Who |
|---|---|
| See a block's rows | Readers of the document who can also see the tasks (members; the public only when Tasks is public) |
| Add, reorder, remove rows | People who can edit the document (B9) |
| Tick, assign, date a row | People who can edit that task (B9) |
| Record a decision | People who can edit the document |
| Move a document to a section | People who can edit the document |

#### 6. Server
- **`addDocRowAction({ projectId, docId, blockKey, title, assigneeId?, dueDate?, itemType? })`**: zod; checks document edit permission, the block key exists in the published version, the row count is under 200; creates the task through `createTaskAction`'s path (type Task unless the block says otherwise, To do, Backlog) with `source_doc_id`, `source_block`, `source_position` at the end; activity "added NB-150 from Weekly · Nov 12"; task broadcast.
- **`moveDocRowAction({ taskId, beforeTaskId? })`** and **`detachDocRowAction({ taskId })`**: document edit permission; positions only.
- **`recordDecisionAction({ projectId, fromDocId, title, context? })`**: document edit permission; locks the workspace row, takes the next decision number (max + 1), creates the document (Decisions section, Decided, date today, a file under Docs as documents are made today), returns its slug.
- **`moveDocToSectionAction({ projectId, docSlug, section, date?, kind? })`**: through `updateWorkspaceDocSettingsAction`; the section must belong to an added workflow (F1) or be Pages.
- **Reads:** `readWorkspaceDocSmartBlockPreviewsAction` learns `task_rows` (query by doc and key, no 12-id limit, paged at 200) and `decisions`; `listWorkspaceDocsAction` returns section, kind, date, decision number.
- **Ticks** use the existing task transition actions; no document write.
- **Live:** the block subscribes to the task broadcasts for its rows (`task-resource`) and to "row added" events on the document's channel.

#### 7. Rules as pure functions (`src/lib/workspaces/doc-live-blocks.ts`) and their tests
- `parseLiveBlocks(markdown)` → blocks with kind, key, label, params. Tests: one `task_rows`; two with different keys; missing key gets none (rendered read-only with "Re-insert this list"); unknown kind; tokens inside code fences are ignored.
- `newBlockKey(existingKeys)` → a 4–6 char key not in use. Tests: no collision across 1,000 draws with 50 existing.
- `canAddRows(docPermission)` / `canTickRow(taskPermission)`. Tests: leaders-only doc and a member: add false, tick own task true; viewer: both false.
- `orderRows(rows, now)` → open first by position, completed in place for 7 days then folded. Tests: a row completed 8 days ago folds; 6 days ago stays.
- `visibleRows(rows, viewer)` → shown and hidden count. Tests: public reader with Tasks private sees 0 and count n.
- `nextDecisionNumber(existing)` → max + 1. Tests: empty → 1; gaps kept (1, 2, 5 → 6).
- `railSections(docs, addedWorkflows)` → ordered sections. Tests: no workflows → flat (no "Pages" header); Meetings added → Pages + Meetings + Decisions; a document in a section whose workflow was hidden falls back to Pages.

#### 8. Everything around it
- **Overview cards:** none in F2 (D1 adds "Open action items").
- **Notifications:**

  | Event | Who | Level |
  |---|---|---|
  | A row is assigned to you | The assignee | Normal, with "From [document]" |
  | Your row is due | The assignee | the existing due reminders |
  | A decision is recorded from a meeting you attended | Attendees (D1) | Summary |
  | Rows added, reordered, detached | Nobody | activity only |

- **CLI:** documents sync as Markdown; block lines appear as written; `nb docs rows "Weekly · Nov 12"` lists rows; `nb tasks create --doc weekly-nov-12 --list actions "Title"` adds a row.
- **MCP:** new `networkbase_doc_rows` (read) and `networkbase_doc_rows_add` (small); `networkbase_task_list` gains `doc`.
- **Agents:** may add and tick rows under the person's permissions; never record decisions without a person's yes (tier "yes").
- **Search:** documents show their section and D-number; tasks show "From [document]".
- **My Work:** rows are tasks, so they appear there by assignee and due date.
- **Public:** sections show in the public rail only for public documents; rows follow W12; Ideas and Goals sections are never public (28.5).
- **Organizations:** organization documents keep their own groups (§19); sections apply to workspaces only in this release.

#### 9. Rollout
1. Migration 0102 adds nullable columns and indexes; existing documents have no section and stay in the flat rail.
2. Behind F1's `workflows_enabled`: sections and the Insert menu show only when a document workflow is added.
3. Existing `{% project.tasks ids="…" %}` blocks keep working unchanged.

#### 10. Tests
- **Unit:** every case in part 7.
- **Server:** a leaders-only document refuses rows from a member but accepts their tick; decision numbers stay unique under two parallel records; rows past 200 are refused with "This list is full"; detaching keeps the task.
- **Contract test** (`tests/unit/doc-live-block-design-contract.test.ts`): the frame, row anatomy and no custom colors.
- **End to end:** add Meetings & decisions → new meeting from a template → add three action items → tick one from the board and see the document update live → record a decision → the rail shows D-001.
- **Browser check list:** rail with and without sections; keyboard add (Enter, Esc); screen reader labels on rows; public view; phone sheet.

#### 11. Calls
1. Rows belong to a document and a block key (`source_doc_id`, `source_block`), so adding or ticking never writes the document text (B8), and copies start empty. **[call]**
2. Blocks are inserted from an **Insert** menu in the Files editor, never typed by hand. **[call]**
3. New rows go to **To do in the Backlog**, not the running sprint. **[call]**
4. Completed rows stay in place for 7 days, then fold under "Completed". **[call]**
5. A block holds up to 200 rows. **[call]**
6. Decisions get workspace-wide **D-numbers** that never change. **[call]**
7. Section, kind and date live in the document's settings; moving a document writes no version. **[call]**
8. Agenda stays plain Markdown inside the templates; no live agenda block. **[call]**
9. Organization documents keep their own groups; sections are for workspaces in this release. **[call]**
10. **Correction (A0.4, 2026-11-19):** no section index migration: a workspace's documents already load together, so the index would never be used. Section, kind and date are kept by the settings normaliser (it used to drop unknown keys, so a later settings save would have undone a move). Workspace documents get the organization header's ⋯ (Document actions) with **Move to section…**, shown only once a section beyond Pages exists; a section's + adds a document straight into it. **[call]**
11. **Found while building A0.4:** viewers could edit and publish documents whose edit policy is "members" (the shared document permission counted them as members). Fixed in `resolveWorkspaceDocPermission`: viewers read, never edit. **[call]**
12. **A0.5 (2026-11-19):** rows are reordered from the row ⋯ menu (Move up, Move down); no drag in this release, so phones and keyboards get the same path. Phones add rows in the same inline row, not a bottom sheet (W11): it fits at 375 px and keeps one path. The line under a block for people who can't edit says "Only people who can edit this document add items here." for every edit policy (W5). **[call]**
13. **A0.5:** adding a row does not check that the key is in the published text; a key that is not there is shown under "items from a removed list", which never offers Add. **[call]**
14. **A0.5:** the task's "From" line names the document only (not the list), and links to it. **[call]**
15. **A0.5:** ticking a row moves the task through the usual transition (review where required) and the box ticks at once; Undo stays 10 seconds. Agents adding rows count as a small change with an undo, like creating a task. **[call]**
16. **Found while building A0.5:** the Files editor's text area had no accessible name; it is now "Edit <file name>". **[call]**
17. **A0.6 (2026-11-19):** Record a decision makes the document like any new one (a Markdown file in Docs, from the browser), then `recordDecisionAction` gives it the next D-number under a lock on the workspace row (unique index 0108 as the backstop); if numbering fails the new file is removed. The number lives in the document's settings, never in its file name or text, so a rename never changes it. **[call]**
18. **A0.6:** moving a document into Decisions gives it the next D-number; moving it out keeps its number (hidden while it is a page, back when it returns), and numbers are never reused. A decision's page shows "D-001 · Decided · date · From: Weekly" above its title. **[call]**
19. **A0.6:** the rail's Decisions **+** records a decision (with no source meeting) instead of adding an unnumbered page; Insert → **Decisions** shows only when Meetings & decisions is added. **[call]**
20. **A0.6 deferred:** the attendees' notice "A decision is recorded from a meeting you attended" waits for meeting attendees (A4.1); agents recording decisions (tier "yes") wait for a CLI command, built with A4.2. **[call]**

### 38.4 F3 · The New module and the item page (agreed 2026-11-17)

F3 is how people make and open every item type F1 defines: **one New module** (28.11) built on the existing `CreateTaskModal`, **one-line quick adds** where people are already typing, the **item panel** with the type's section and the stage, and **one filter chip row** shared by Tasks and every own tab. It also settles who may put a new item into a sprint.

#### 1. What it is and the references
| Reference | Rating / source | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **28.11** | Agreed | One shell, one section a type adds, "Starts at", the footer saying where the item shows, quick adds with **More details** |
| **Prototype v4** | The user's reviewed look | The module with type tabs, Add key result, Add idea |
| **Anthropic's project planner** (11.3) | The user's reference | The calm property list and the filter chip row (S3) |
| What the code has | Checked 2026-11-17 | `CreateTaskModal` (640 px, "What are you creating?" tabs Task · Assignment, sections Basics → Sprint and assignee → Schedule → Subtasks and files, quick due chips, footer **Create task**); `TaskDetailPanel` is a full-height side sheet with tabs (Assignment for organizations, Details, Subtasks, Comments, Files); Tasks has search and a scope menu (All · Sprint · Backlog · In review · Assignments · Mine), **no filter chips**; the server lets **owners and admins** put new tasks in a sprint (decision 146) while the module only offers it to the **owner** |

**Agreed changes from an exact copy:** the panel keeps its tabs (the 11.2 one-scroll page was for Pipeline items, which are parked); no saved views; no per-person custom fields.

#### 2. The 18 layers
1. **Getting it:** **New ▾** in Tasks and in each own tab; one-line adds in lists, document blocks and subtasks; **More details** from any quick add.
2. **Setting it up:** nothing; the tabs follow the workflows added (F1).
3. **Items:** one module creates every type; each type adds one section with its own fields (written in its round) and a **Starts at** choice.
4. **Views:** the panel shows the type's section in Details and the "Shows in" line; Tasks and own tabs share the chip row.
5. **Actions and flow:** open → pick a type → fill → **Create [type]**; quick add → Enter; filter → chips; open an item → panel.
6. **Surfaces:** New ▾ menu, the module, quick-add lines, the panel header and Details, the chip row.
7. **Design spec:** `form-parts.tsx` (`Field`, `SectionDivider`, `QuickChips`, `FORM_*`), `UnderlineTabs`, the panel as it is; one contract test for the module and one for the chip row.
8. **Words:** New · New bug · What are you creating? · Starts at · Joins Tasks at Fixing · also shows in Bugs · Goes to the Backlog · Need by · Publish date · More details · Create bug · Assigned to · Type · Due · + Filter · Clear all.
9. **Links:** F1 (types, stages), F2 (rows made from documents carry "From"), sprints, review, Files, My Work, CLI and MCP (the same create rules).
10. **People:** who may create stays as today; sprint choice is owners and admins (decision 146); viewers see no New.
11. **States:** saving, errors per field, a type removed while the module is open, two tabs open in the panel at once.
12. **Edges:** a long title, pasted Markdown, no sprint running, a member choosing a stage that joins the board, a type hidden (F1) after an item was opened.
13. **Phone:** the module is a full-height sheet; type tabs scroll; chips scroll in one row with **Filters** opening a sheet.
14. **Accessibility:** tabs are a real tablist; each field has a label and an error message tied to it; ⌘/Ctrl + Enter creates; chips are buttons with their state in the name.
15. **Notifications:** creating notifies as today (assignee); nothing new.
16. **Trust and data:** the same validation server-side; type fields are checked by the type's schema.
17. **Reuse vs new:** below.
18. **How we know it works:** below.

#### 3. Step-by-step walkthroughs
**W1 · New from Tasks (workspace with Bugs and Requests added)**
1. Dev clicks **New ▾** in Tasks. The button's main part creates a Task; the arrow opens a menu: **Task · Bug · Request** with icons (types in 28.11's fixed order, only those added).
2. He picks **Bug**. The module opens titled **Create bug**, tab **Bug** selected in "What are you creating?" (Task · Bug · Request).
3. **Basics:** Bug title (focused), Description.
4. **Bug details** (T3's section) sits after Basics.
5. **Sprint and assignee:** Sprint, Assigned to, **Starts at** (Fixing selected, because he opened it from Tasks), Priority.
6. **Schedule:** Due with Today · 1 week · 2 weeks · 4 weeks.
7. **Subtasks and files** as today.
8. Footer, left, muted: "Joins Tasks at Fixing · also shows in Bugs". Right: **Cancel** · **Create bug**.
9. He presses ⌘ + Enter: the bug is created at Fixing; it's on the board in the chosen sprint (or Backlog); the panel opens on it.

**W2 · New from an own tab**
1. In **Bugs**, Mei clicks **New bug**.
2. The module opens with **Starts at: New** (the first stage); the footer says "Shows in Bugs · not on the Tasks board yet".
3. Changing Starts at to **Fixing** updates the footer to "Joins Tasks at Fixing · also shows in Bugs" and shows the sprint field.

**W3 · Switching type mid-way**
1. Dev types a title and description under **Task**, picks Mei and a due date, then clicks **Bug**.
2. Title, description, assignee, date, sprint and files stay; Starts at appears; Bug details is empty.
3. He fills Severity, switches back to **Task**: Severity is kept (hidden) in case he returns; it's dropped only when the task is created as a Task.

**W4 · A member and the sprint**
1. Karan (member) opens the module. The Sprint field shows "Goes to the Backlog · owners and admins plan sprints" instead of a picker (decision 146).
2. A bug he starts at Fixing joins the board in the **Backlog**.
3. The same applies to F1's Join-board sheet: for members it shows "Goes to the Backlog" with no tick.

**W5 · Quick add, then More details**
1. In a meeting's Action items (F2), Asha types "Send the venue contract" and presses Enter: a Task is made at To do, Backlog, with From filled.
2. She types another and, instead of Enter, clicks **More details**: the full module opens as **Create task** with the title, From and Part of (if any) filled and shown as read-only lines under Basics.
3. The same works in own-tab lists ("+ New bug" line), subtasks and, later, check-ins.

**W6 · Opening an item**
1. Clicking NB-142 opens the side panel (as today).
2. Header: type icon · **NB-142** · title; under it "Shows in: **Tasks · In progress** / **Bugs · Fixing**" and the **Stage** menu (F1 S7); for Tasks nothing new shows.
3. **Details** tab: Description, then the type's section ("Bug details": Severity, Where, Steps to reproduce, Expected), then Properties as today (Status, Section, Priority, Assigned to, Sprint, Due, Estimate).
4. The other tabs stay: Subtasks · Comments · Files; never-on-board types swap Subtasks for **Work** (their tasks), defined in T1 and T2.

**W7 · Filtering with chips**
1. Tasks' header row: search · scope menu (as today) · **Assigned to ▾ · Type ▾ · Due ▾ · + Filter**.
2. Dev clicks **Assigned to ▾** → Me, a list of members with avatars, Unassigned; he picks Me: the chip becomes **Assigned to: Me ✕**.
3. **+ Filter** adds Priority, Labels or Sprint chips.
4. **Clear all** appears after two or more chips; the URL keeps the filters (`?assignee=me&type=bug`), so a link opens the same view.
5. The same row, with the tab's own chips (e.g. Severity in Bugs), sits in every own tab.

**W8 · Errors and edges in the module**
1. Create with an empty title: the title field shows "Add a title" and focus moves there.
2. A type is hidden by an admin while the module is open: on Create the server refuses with "Bugs was removed from this workspace"; the module offers **Create as task**.
3. A server error keeps everything typed and shows the message above the footer.

**W9 · Phone**
1. **New ▾** is a floating button on Tasks and own tabs; the menu is a bottom sheet.
2. The module is a full-height sheet; type tabs scroll sideways; the footer sticks to the bottom.
3. The chip row scrolls; **Filters** opens a sheet with every chip as a section.

**W10 · Keyboard only**
1. `N` (in Tasks, not while typing) opens the module on Task; `Shift + N` opens New ▾.
2. In the module: Tab moves through fields, ← → move between type tabs, ⌘/Ctrl + Enter creates, Esc closes (asks first if something was typed).

#### 4. Screen spec
**S1 · New ▾ (Tasks and own tabs)**
- Split button: main part **New** (Task in Tasks; the tab's type in an own tab: **New bug**); arrow opens the type menu (Tasks only).
- Menu rows: icon · type name · one muted line ("Joins Tasks at Fixing"); keyboard navigable.

**S2 · The module (extends `CreateTaskModal`)**
- Title: **Create [type]**; subtitle: the workspace name.
- "What are you creating?" `UnderlineTabs`: types added, fixed order Task · Bug · Request · Content · Project · Roadmap item · Assignment (organizations). Opened from a goals or Ideas document, the tabs are only **Key result** or **Idea** (D3, D4).
- Sections in this order, always: **Basics** → **[Type] details** (only for types with fields) → **Sprint and assignee** → **Schedule** → **Subtasks and files**. A type may hide a shared section (28.11's table) but never reorder.
- **Starts at** (types with own tabs): a select of the stages people may start at (e.g. bug: New · Confirmed · Fixing); options that join the board end with "· on the board".
- Renamed fields per type: Due → **Need by** (Request), **Publish date** (Content).
- Footer left (muted, one line): where it will show; right: **Cancel** · **Create [type]** (disabled while saving; "Creating…").

#### 6. Server
- **`createTaskAction`** (one action for every type): input gains `itemType`, `stage`, `typeFields`, `sourceDocId`, `sourceBlock`, `partOfId` (T1). Checks, in order: the type is added and not hidden (F1); `stage` is a starting stage of the type; `typeFields` pass the type's schema; `sprintId` only for owners and admins (decision 146), and only when the stage is on the board; then today's checks. On a refused sprint for a member, the item goes to the Backlog rather than failing [call].
- **`updateTaskTypeFieldsAction({ taskId, patch })`**: the task edit permission; validates the merged `typeFields`; activity "changed severity to High".
- **Reads:** the task payload carries `itemType`, `stage`, `typeFields`, `onBoard`, `source`, `partOf`.
- **UI fix:** `TasksTab` passes `canAssignSprint` for owners **and** admins, matching the server.

#### 7. Rules as pure functions (`src/lib/workflows/create-rules.ts`) and their tests
- `moduleTabs(addedTypes, openedFrom)` → ordered tabs. Tests: Tasks with Bug and Request → Task, Bug, Request; from an Ideas document → Idea only; an organization → Task, Assignment.
- `startingStages(type)` and `defaultStartingStage(type, openedFrom)`. Tests: bug from Tasks → Fixing; bug from Bugs → New; content from Tasks → Drafting.
- `footerLine(type, stage, sprintAllowed)`. Tests: bug at New → "Shows in Bugs · not on the Tasks board yet"; bug at Fixing → "Joins Tasks at Fixing · also shows in Bugs"; member at Fixing → "… · Goes to the Backlog".
- `carryOnSwitch(draft, fromType, toType)` → kept and hidden values. Tests: title, description, assignee, due and files always kept; bug fields hidden on Task, restored on Bug.
- `sectionsFor(type)` → visible sections and renamed labels. Tests: Project hides Sprint and renames Schedule to Start and End; Request renames Due to Need by.
- `filtersFromUrl(params, tab)` / `filtersToUrl(filters)`. Tests: round trip; unknown keys dropped; "me" resolves to the viewer.

### 38.5 T1 · Project planner and the Timeline, Calendar and Matrix views (agreed 2026-11-17)

T1 turns 11.3's own-tab planner into **views inside Tasks**: a **Projects** view (Timeline · Active · All) when the Project planner workflow is added, and **Calendar** and **Matrix** views every workspace gets. A project is a task of type **Project** that never goes on the board (28.1); its work tasks point to it with **Part of**.

#### 1. What it is and the references
| Reference | Rating / source | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **Anthropic's project planner** (Notion) | The user's reference (11.3) | The Timeline (status groups left, bars right, Today marker, arrows), the Active table, the project page |
| **Eisenhower Matrix** · Automated Eisenhower Matrix | 4.9 / 500+ · 4.6 / 14 (11.7) | The 2 × 2 grid placed from fields, not by hand |
| **Social Media Content Planner** | 4.9 / 800+ (14.2) | A calm month grid with a tray of undated items |
| 11.3's agreed changes | Agreed | No cover; emoji or Lucide project icons; our badge shape; **Assigned to**; Clay for Today and arrows |
| What the code has | Checked 2026-11-17 | Tasks is **one board** (`KanbanBoard`) with no view switch; tasks have **no start date** and **no parent**; **`task_dependencies` exists** with a loop check (`task-meta.ts`, used by `nb` "Waiting on"); sprints have start and end dates |

**Changes from 11.3 (own tab → blended):** no separate tab; the planner's Board view is dropped (the Tasks board is for work); 11.3's "Done" is **Completed** (28.6); "About this project" is the project's description; dependency arrows use the existing `task_dependencies`.

#### 2. The 18 layers
1. **Getting it:** **Project planner** sits in "Blends into Tasks" in Add workflow (F1): "Adds to Tasks: a Projects view with a Timeline. Tasks get Part of." Calendar and Matrix need nothing added.
2. **Setting it up:** none; project stages are fixed (below); weekend shading on; zoom Month.
3. **Items:** **Project** (type `project`, never on the board): icon, name, stage, Assigned to, people, start and end, priority, summary, description ("About"), blocked by, its work tasks, completion. Work tasks get **Part of** (one project each).
4. **Views:** Tasks gains a view switch **Board · Projects · Calendar · Matrix** (Projects only with the workflow); Projects has **Timeline · Active · All**; Board can **group by Project**.
5. **Actions and flow:** create → plan (dates, tasks, arrows) → In progress → work tasks complete → completion rises → Completed (asks about open tasks); dragging bars and days changes dates; Matrix moves change priority or due date.
6. **Surfaces:** the view switch, Projects' title row, the timeline grid, the No dates tray, the Active and All tables, the project panel's Work tab, the quick-create bubble, the shift-dependents and open-tasks dialogs, the Calendar grid and tray, the Matrix grid, the Part of chip.
7. **Design spec:** 11.3 § 7 and 11.7 § 7 as written (Instrument Sans, JetBrains Mono for dates and counts, the blueprint grid, Clay for Today and arrows, 180 ms ease-out, precision badges); contract tests below.
8. **Words:** Projects · Timeline · Active · All · Calendar · Matrix · Project · Part of · Not started · Planning · In progress · Paused · Completed · Cancelled · Completion · Blocked by · Blocking · No dates · Set dates · Group into a project · Show sprints · Do first · Schedule · Delegate · Drop · Assigned to (never Owner).
9. **Links:** the board (work tasks), sprints (bands on the timeline), My Work (projects ending this week), review (work tasks only), Documents (F2 rows can be Part of), search, CLI, MCP, organizations (the S14 portfolio stays with Organizations, 33.4).
10. **People:** members create and edit projects and dates; viewers read; the public never sees Projects (B11).
11. **States:** skeleton grid, arrows failing alone, live bar moves, last write wins with a toast, undo for every drag.
12. **Edges:** no dates, end before start, loops, a blocker moved later, a project completed with open tasks, a work task deleted, 500 projects, years-long bars, time zones, hiding the workflow.
13. **Phone:** Active is the default Projects view; Timeline becomes a list with one bar per row; Calendar becomes an agenda list; Matrix becomes four folding sections.
14. **Accessibility:** the timeline is also a table; every drag has a menu or dialog; colour never alone.
15. **Notifications:** below.
16. **Trust and data:** projects follow task permissions; never public.
17. **Reuse vs new:** below.
18. **How we know it works:** below.

#### 3. Step-by-step walkthroughs
**W1 · Adding the Project planner**
1. Asha adds **Project planner** (F1 dialog, "Blends into Tasks").
2. Tasks' header now shows the view switch **Board · Projects · Calendar · Matrix** (before: Board · Calendar · Matrix).
3. **Projects** opens on **Timeline**: an empty grid at the current month, the Today marker, three empty groups (To do 0 · In progress 0 · Complete 0) and the hint "A project groups tasks with a start and an end. Drag across the timeline to add one, or press **New project**."

**W2 · Drawing a project on the timeline**
1. Asha drags across an empty row from Dec 2 to Dec 20; a ghost bar follows.
2. On release the quick-create bubble opens at the bar: icon (🎯 default), name (focused), the dates filled, **Create** · **More details**.
3. She types "Website relaunch" and presses Enter: a Project (Not started, Assigned to Asha) appears in To do with its bar.
4. **More details** opens the New module (F3) on **Project** with the dates filled.

**W3 · Adding work to a project**
1. Asha opens the project (panel). Tabs: **Details · Work · Comments · Files**.
2. **Work** lists tasks Part of it; **+ New task** opens the New module with "Part of: Website relaunch" filled; **Add existing** searches the workspace's tasks (not projects, not tasks already in another project unless she confirms moving them).
3. Each added task shows the chip **⬡ Website relaunch** on the board and in lists.
4. From the board, selecting three tasks → ⋯ → **Group into a project** makes a new project and sets their Part of.

**W4 · Dependencies and moving a blocker**
1. On the timeline Asha drags from the end dot of "Design system" onto "Website relaunch": a Clay arrow appears; Website relaunch is **blocked by** Design system (stored in `task_dependencies`).
2. Trying the reverse arrow is refused: "That would make a loop: Website relaunch is blocked by Design system."
3. She drags Design system's end five days later, past Website relaunch's start. A dialog asks: "Move 1 project that depends on this by 5 days?" **Move them** · **Leave them**.
4. **Leave them** turns the arrow to the warning colour and the bar shows "Starts before Design system ends".

**W5 · Running and completing**
1. Asha sets the stage to **In progress** (stage menu, F1). If a blocker isn't Completed, the bar shows a "Blocked by Design system" chip; it's a warning, not a stop.
2. As work tasks complete, **Completion** rises (completed ÷ all, not counting cancelled); the bar's thin line and % follow.
3. She sets **Completed**; 2 tasks are still open: "2 tasks are still open: **Leave them** or **Move them to the Backlog**?"
4. The project moves to the Complete group; an Update offer appears ("Post an Update", off by default).

**W6 · Active and All**
1. **Active** shows the In progress group (Planning, In progress) as a table: Project · Stage · Assigned to · Dates · Priority · Completion · Blocked by; cells edit in place.
2. **All** shows every project with every field and a totals row (count, average completion); group by stage or Assigned to.

**W7 · Board grouped by project**
1. On **Board**, ⋯ → **Group by: Project** turns rows into swimlanes, one per project, plus "No project".
2. Dragging a card between swimlanes changes its Part of; between columns, its status as today.

**W8 · Calendar (every workspace)**
1. Dev opens **Calendar**: the current month, Monday first, weekends shaded; each day lists its items by due date (type icon, NB-n, title); a day with more than three shows "+2 more".
2. Items with a start date and a due date show as a span across days; projects (when the planner is added) show as thin spans at the top of the weeks.
3. **No date (12)** tray at the right lists items in the current scope with no due date; dragging one onto a day sets its due date.
4. Dragging an item to another day moves its due date (keeps its start-to-due length when it has a start); **Undo** in the toast.
5. **+** on a day (hover) opens the New module with that due date.
6. **Week** toggle shows seven columns with the same rules.

**W9 · Matrix (every workspace)**
1. Mei opens **Matrix**; scope starts at **Mine**.
2. Boxes: **Do first** (High or Urgent, due in 3 days or overdue) · **Schedule** (High or Urgent, later or no date) · **Delegate** (Low or Medium, due soon) · **Drop** (Low or Medium, later or no date).
3. Moving a card up or down changes priority (High / Medium); into the Urgent column opens Today · Tomorrow · In 3 days · Pick a date; out of it asks to clear or push the date.
4. Delegate's header **Assign…** and Drop's **Move to Backlog** act on selected cards.

**W10 · Phone**
1. Projects opens on **Active** as stacked rows; **Timeline** shows one bar per row with a sticky month header and pinch-free zoom buttons.
2. Calendar opens as an **agenda** (days down the page with their items); Month is a toggle.
3. Matrix is four folding sections, Do first open.

**W11 · Viewer and public**
1. A viewer sees every view read-only; no drag handles; menus show only Open.
2. A public visitor never sees Projects, Calendar or Matrix (B11); if Tasks is public, they see the Board as today.

**W12 · An agent**
1. `networkbase_task_list` with `type: "project"` lists projects with dates and completion; `part_of` filters work tasks.
2. `networkbase_task_create` with `type: "project"` and dates creates one; `networkbase_task_edit` sets `partOf`.

#### 4. Screen spec
**S1 · Tasks view switch** — `UnderlineTabs` under the Tasks header: Board · Projects · Calendar · Matrix (icons LayoutGrid · FolderKanban · CalendarDays · Grid2x2); remembered per person per workspace; `?view=` in the URL.

**S2 · Projects title row** — "Projects" + mono count ("5 in progress · 2 overdue"); sub-switch **Timeline · Active · All**; F3's chip row (Stage · Assigned to · Dates · + Filter: Priority, Labels, People); **New project**; ⋯ (Show sprints · Weekend shading · Export CSV).

**S3 · Timeline grid** — 11.3 S4 as written: months and week dates on top; Today as a filled Clay circle and line; zoom Week / Month / Quarter and ‹ Today ›; pinned left column with stage groups (To do: Not started · In progress: Planning, In progress, Paused · Complete: Completed, Cancelled), counts; bars with icon and name, stage badge, assignee avatar, completion % and line; stretch handles; end dot for arrows; Clay arrows, warning colour on conflict; **No dates** tray; drawing; edge markers "‹ Mar 12"; **▸** on a project row expands its work tasks as dots on their due dates (bars when they have a start).

**S4 · Active and All tables** — 11.3 S5 columns with **Stage** for Status; "Ended 3 days ago" and "Paused" chips; totals row in All.

**S5 · Project panel** — F3's panel: header (icon picker, NB-n, name, Stage ▾, "Shows in: Projects · In progress"); **Details:** About (description), Project details (summary, people, start → end, completion with "set by hand" mark when overridden), Properties (Assigned to, priority, labels, blocked by / blocking); **Work** (the tasks, + New task, Add existing, each row opening the normal panel); Comments; Files.

**S6 · Quick-create bubble** — icon, name, dates; Create · More details; Esc removes the ghost bar.

**S7 · Shift-dependents dialog** — "Move [n] projects that depend on this by [d] days?" list of names; **Move them** · **Leave them**; one Undo for the whole shift.

**S8 · Open-tasks dialog** — "[n] tasks are still open: **Leave them** or **Move them to the Backlog**?"

**S9 · Part of chip** — on cards and rows: project icon + name, 1 line, truncates; click opens the project.

**S10 · Calendar** — month grid (B2, built here first; 14.2 reuses it): header (‹ Month Year › · Today · Month / Week), day cells with up to three items and "+n more", spans for start-to-due items, project spans on top; **No date** tray (collapsible, count); hover **+** per day; F3's chips apply.

**S11 · Matrix** — 11.7 S1–S6 as written (axis labels with their rules, four boxes, compact cards, quick date picker, empty lines).

#### 5. Data
**Migration `0103_project_planner.sql`:**
- `tasks.start_date timestamptz NULL` with a check `start_date IS NULL OR due_date IS NULL OR start_date <= due_date`.
- `tasks.part_of_id uuid NULL → tasks(id) ON DELETE SET NULL`; index `tasks_part_of_idx (part_of_id) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`.
- No new table: dependencies stay in `task_dependencies`; project fields live in `type_fields`: `icon` ({ kind: 'emoji' | 'lucide', value }), `summary` (≤ 280 chars), `people` (member ids), `completionOverride` (0–100 or null).
- **Project stages (F1 registry):** Not started → todo · Planning, In progress, Paused → in_progress · Completed, Cancelled → done; never on the board.
- **Part of rules:** only on-board types can be Part of; a project can't be Part of anything (no nesting in this release); the parent must be a project in the same workspace (T2 adds roadmap items as parents).
- **Personal view choice:** local storage per workspace; nothing stored on the server.

#### 6. Server
- **`createTaskAction`** (F3) accepts `itemType: 'project'`, `startDate`, `partOfId`; checks the Project planner is added for projects and Part of.
- **`setTaskDatesAction({ taskId, startDate?, dueDate? })`**: task edit permission; validates order; returns the dependents that would conflict, without moving them.
- **`shiftDependentsAction({ taskId, days })`**: moves every project blocked by this one (transitively) by `days`, in one transaction, one activity entry, one undo token.
- **`setPartOfAction({ taskIds[], partOfId | null })`** and **`groupIntoProjectAction({ taskIds[], name })`**: edit permission on every task; refuses projects and off-board types; one undo.
- **`completeProjectAction({ projectId, openTasks: 'leave' | 'backlog' })`**: sets Completed; optionally clears the sprint of open work tasks.
- **Dependencies:** the existing `updateTaskMeta` (`/api/v1/tasks/[taskId]/meta`) and its loop check, called from the timeline.
- **Reads:** `readProjectsAction(projectId, view, filters)` returns projects with dates, stage, assignee, completion (computed in SQL from work tasks), blockers; `readCalendarAction(projectId, monthStart, filters)` returns items in the visible range plus the No date count; Matrix reuses the board read with the box worked out on the client.
- **Live:** task broadcasts already carry dates and Part of; bars and calendar items move live; your own dragged bar ignores remote moves until you drop.

#### 7. Rules as pure functions (`src/lib/workflows/planner.ts`) and their tests
- `completion(workTasks, subtasks, override)` → { percent, source }. Tests: 2 of 4 completed → 50; cancelled ignored (1 of 3 with 1 cancelled → 50); no work tasks, 1 of 2 subtasks → 50 'subtasks'; override 30 → 30 'hand'; nothing → 0 'none'.
- `conflicts(projects, deps)` → pairs where the blocked one starts before its blocker ends. Tests: overlap by a day flagged; same-day end and start not flagged.
- `dependentsToShift(projectId, deps, days)` → transitive list. Tests: chain A → B → C moves B and C; a diamond moves each once.
- `timelineRange(zoom, today)` and `barGeometry(start, end, range)`. Tests: Month shows ±2 months; a bar before the range becomes an edge marker; a 1-day bar has minimum width.
- `calendarCells(monthStart, items, tz)` → weeks of days with items and overflow counts. Tests: Monday first; a span across a week break splits into two segments; time zone keeps a 23:30 UTC due date on the workspace's local day.
- `matrixBox(task, today, urgentDays = 3)` → box. Tests: High due tomorrow → Do first; Urgent with no date → Schedule; Low overdue → Delegate; Medium in 2 weeks → Drop; completed → none.
- `canBePartOf(type)` and `canBeParent(type)`. Tests: task, bug, request, content true / project false; project parent true / task parent false.

#### 8. Everything around it
- **Overview card (new):** **Projects** (when the planner is added): "3 in progress · 1 ends this week · 1 overdue", the next ending project with its completion; links to Projects.
- **Notifications:**

  | Event | Who | Level |
  |---|---|---|
  | Assigned a project | The assignee | Normal |
  | Your project ends in 3 days and isn't Completed | The assignee | Normal |
  | Your project's blocker moved later and it now conflicts | The project's assignee | Normal |
  | Projects shifted together | The assignees of the moved projects | Summary |
  | Completed project | People on the project | Summary |

- **My Work:** "Ends Friday: Website relaunch" for projects assigned to you ending this week.
- **CLI:** `nb tasks list --type project`; `nb tasks create --type project "Website relaunch" --start 2026-12-02 --due 2026-12-20`; `nb tasks edit NB-12 --part-of NB-40`; `nb tasks list --part-of NB-40`; `nb tasks list --view matrix --mine` prints the four boxes.
- **MCP:** `networkbase_task_list` gains `partOf`; `networkbase_task_create` and `networkbase_task_edit` gain `startDate` and `partOf`.
- **Agents:** may create projects and link tasks under the person's rights; never shift dependents without a yes (tier "yes").
- **Search:** projects show their icon, stage and completion.
- **Organizations:** the portfolio of workspaces (11.3 S14) is Organizations' own (33.4 K3); T1 doesn't add it.

2. The view switch with **Calendar** and **Matrix** ships to every workspace (they read existing tasks); Projects appears only when the planner is added (F1 flag).
