### 38.6 T3 · Bugs (agreed 2026-11-18)

T3 is the first **own tab over the same tasks** (28.1): **Bugs** sorts reports before anyone works on them; a bug **joins the Tasks board at Fixing** and leaves the Bugs-only stages behind. It's 13.2's design with outside reporting, Incidents, the public list and launch links held back (28.2).

#### 1. What it is and the references
| Reference | Rating / source | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **Bug Tracker** (Notion) | **4.7 / 50** (13.2) | The calm board of bug stages, cards with severity and reporter, a report form, the severity chart |
| **Report a Bug** (Notion) | 4.7 / 36 | A fast report |
| 13.2's agreed changes | Agreed | Stages New → Confirmed → Fixing → Fixed → Verified with close reasons; Severity sets priority; similar open bugs and "I see this too"; a **Where** field; Reported by and Assigned to |
| 28.2–28.4 | Agreed | Own tab, same tasks; joins at Fixing (B1); Blocked keeps the stage (B2); review gates Fixed (B3); NB-n (B4); sprint on joining (B5); moving back recorded (B7); never public (B11) |
| What the code has | Checked 2026-11-17 | `task_links` with kind `pull_request`; labels on tasks; watchers; **Create task** on a chat message (`createTaskFromMessage`); comments and files on tasks |

**Held back (parked in 28.2):** outside reporters and the **Reported** view; **Incidents**, Postmortem and the Status page (21.2); the public **Good first issues** list; **Found in / Fixed in as launch links** and auto-verify (they wait for T2 and D2; here they're version text).

#### 2. The 18 layers
1. **Getting it:** **Bugs** in "Own tab · same tasks" (F1): "Adds a Bugs tab. Bugs join Tasks at Fixing." Wizard: ticked for Open source, Web app, Developer tool; unticked for Game dev.
2. **Setting it up:** nothing to answer; stages, severities and Where options are fixed; ready-made labels **good first issue** and **help wanted** are offered the first time someone labels a bug.
3. **Items:** a **Bug** (type `bug`): title, stage, severity, reported by, assigned to, Where, steps, expected, found in, fixed in, labels, pull requests, people who see it too, duplicate of, files.
4. **Views:** **Triage · Board · Mine · Fixed**, with the **Open by severity** strip above each.
5. **Actions and flow:** report → New → triage (Confirm with severity and assignee, or close) → Fixing (joins the board) → Fixed (asks Fixed in) → Verified; reopen any time.
6. **Surfaces:** title row, strip, views, card, triage row, bug panel, report form (the New module's Bug section), close and repro dialogs, Overview card, chat action.
7. **Design spec:** 13.2 § 7 (Instrument Sans titles; JetBrains Mono counts and versions; severity colours always with words; precision badges; Lucide Bug, ShieldAlert, CopyCheck, GitPullRequest, Users, Sprout); contract test.
8. **Words:** Bugs · Bug · Report a bug · New · Confirmed · Fixing · Fixed · Verified · Won't fix · Duplicate of · Can't reproduce · Severity · Urgent · Major · Minor · Where · Found in · Fixed in · I see this too · That's my bug · Triage · Reported by · Assigned to; never "ticket", "Owner", "Lead".
9. **Links:** the Tasks board (from Fixing), sprints, review, chat (Report as bug), My Work, search, CLI, MCP, Matrix (through priority).
10. **People:** members and viewers report; members triage, fix and verify; owners and admins add or hide the tab; never public.
11. **States:** skeleton strip and columns; live new reports; last write wins with a toast; undo for moves, closes, duplicates and severity.
12. **Edges:** duplicate chains, a bug reported twice at once, a reporter who leaves, hiding Bugs with bugs on the board (F1), 1,000 open bugs.
13. **Phone:** Triage is the phone default; Board shows one stage at a time with stage chips.
14. **Accessibility:** cards and rows have full names ("Bug NB-142, Payment gateway is down, Urgent, Confirmed"); every drag has "Move to…".
15. **Notifications:** below.
16. **Trust and data:** members only; Where holds no personal data beyond browser and version; screenshots follow task file rules.
17. **Reuse vs new:** below.
18. **How we know it works:** below.

#### 3. Step-by-step walkthroughs
**W1 · First look after adding Bugs**
1. Asha adds **Bugs** (F1). A **Bugs** tab appears after the divider (icon Bug).
2. It opens on **Board**: five columns (New · Confirmed · Fixing · Fixed · Verified), each empty; the strip "Open: Urgent 0 · Major 0 · Minor 0"; the hint "Bugs come in on the left and leave on the right. Anyone in the workspace can report one."; **Report a bug** (primary).

**W2 · Reporting a bug**
1. Dev clicks **Report a bug**; the New module (F3) opens as **Create bug**, Starts at **New**.
2. He types the title "Payment gateway is down". Under the title, **Similar open bugs** lists up to 5 matches as he types (open bugs only), each with "**That's my bug**".
3. No match fits. **Bug details:** What happened? (steps, one per line) · What did you expect? · **Where** (Web: browser ▾ + version / App: platform ▾ + version / Other: text) · Found in (version text) · Severity (**Not sure** · Minor · Major · Urgent; default Not sure).
4. Screenshot or video under **Subtasks and files**.
5. Footer: "Shows in Bugs · not on the Tasks board yet"; **Create bug**.
6. NB-142 appears in **New**, Reported by Dev; owners and admins are told (Normal).

**W3 · "That's my bug"**
1. Mei starts a report; Similar open bugs shows NB-142.
2. She clicks **That's my bug**: the module closes, she's added to NB-142's **I see this too** and its watchers; the toast says "Added you to NB-142 · Undo".

**W4 · Triage**
1. Asha opens **Triage**: New bugs, oldest first; each row: title, Where, reported by, age (mono), I see this too count, and buttons **Confirm · Close…**.
2. **Confirm** opens a small form: Severity (required here), Assigned to (optional); **Confirm** moves it to **Confirmed** and sets priority (Urgent → Urgent, Major → High, Minor → Medium).
3. **Close…** asks the reason: **Won't fix** · **Duplicate of…** (a bug picker) · **Can't reproduce** (a message to the reporter, required).

**W5 · Duplicate**
1. Asha closes NB-150 as **Duplicate of** NB-142.
2. NB-150's reporter and "I see this too" people move onto NB-142 (and its watchers); NB-150 shows "Duplicate of NB-142" and leaves open lists.
3. If NB-142 is itself a duplicate, the picker points to the oldest open bug in the chain; a bug can't be a duplicate of itself or of one of its duplicates.

**W6 · Can't reproduce**
1. Closing as Can't reproduce posts Asha's message as a comment mentioning the reporter and sets the bug to **Can't reproduce**.
2. The reporter gets a Normal notice "Details needed on NB-160" with **Reopen with details** (adds a comment and reopens to New).
3. Nothing closes or reopens on its own.

**W7 · Fixing (joins the board)**
1. Karan moves NB-142 to **Fixing** (stage menu or drag on the Bugs board).
2. F1's Join-board sheet asks the sprint (owners and admins: **Add to Week 47** ticked; members: "Goes to the Backlog", F3).
3. The bug appears on the Tasks board in In progress with the chip **Bug · Fixing**.
4. Karan attaches the pull request in the panel (**Add link** → kind Pull request): the card shows "↗ PR #418".

**W8 · Fixed and Verified**
1. Karan drags the bug to **Completed** on the Tasks board (or **Fixed** in Bugs). Without required review: stage **Fixed**; with review: In review first, Fixed after approval (B3).
2. **Fixed** asks **Fixed in** (version text, optional, e.g. "v2.4"); the card shows "➜ v2.4".
3. Dev (the reporter) checks it and moves it to **Verified**; any member can too.
4. **Reopen** on a Fixed, Verified or closed bug sends it to **Confirmed** with a required comment; I see this too on a closed bug offers **Reopen** to members.

**W9 · Moving back off the board**
1. Karan realises it's blocked by a vendor and moves it back to **Confirmed**.
2. It leaves the board; Week 47's history shows "NB-142 moved back to Bugs" (B7).
3. If instead he drags it to **Blocked** on the board, it stays on the board as **Bug · Fixing · Blocked** (B2).

**W10 · Report as bug from chat**
1. In a workspace channel, a message's ⋯ shows **Create task** and, with Bugs added, **Report as bug**.
2. It opens the New module on **Bug**, title from the message's first line, What happened? from the message, its attachments under files, and a link back to the message.

**W11 · A bug made from Tasks**
1. Mei is already fixing something: **New ▾ → Bug** in Tasks starts at **Fixing** (F3) and joins the board immediately; it still shows in Bugs.

**W12 · Mine and Fixed**
1. **Mine**: bugs assigned to you, grouped Urgent · Major · Minor, then stage.
2. **Fixed**: Fixed and Verified bugs grouped by **Fixed in** text, newest first; "No version" group last.

**W13 · Phone**
1. Bugs opens on **Triage**; rows show title, severity, age; Confirm and Close as buttons.
2. Board shows one stage with chips to switch; moving is "Move to…".

**W14 · CLI and an agent**
1. `nb bugs report "Crash on export" --steps "Open file\nExport" --expected "A PDF" --where web:firefox:132` creates NB-171 at New, Reported by the person ("via CLI").
2. An agent hitting a failure files a bug with `networkbase_bug_report`; it shows "Reported by agent for Dev".
3. An agent can move Confirmed → Fixing and attach a PR link; closing as Won't fix or Duplicate needs the person's yes.

**W15 · Hiding Bugs**
1. F1 W7: the tab hides; bugs on the board stay as plain tasks with a greyed Bug mark; the rest wait until Bugs is added again.

#### 4. Screen spec
**S1 · Title row** — Bug icon + "Bugs"; mono counts "2 urgent · 5 to triage"; view switch **Triage · Board · Mine · Fixed** (UnderlineTabs); F3's chip row with **Severity ▾ · Assigned to ▾ · Labels ▾ · + Filter** (Where, Found in, Reported by); search (titles, steps, expected); **Report a bug**; ⋯ (Export CSV).

**S2 · Open by severity strip** — three labelled bars "Urgent 2 · Major 5 · Minor 11" (open = New, Confirmed, Fixing); click filters.

**S3 · Board** — five stage columns with counts; cards: Bug icon, title, severity badge, reporter or assignee avatar, "2 people see it", "↗ PR #418", "➜ v2.4", labels (good first issue as a chip); drag between stages (Fixing asks the sprint; leaving Fixing backwards records B7); dropping on a closed reason isn't possible (close is a menu).

**S4 · Triage row** — title · Where · reported by · age · see-too count · **Confirm** · **Close…**; empty: "Nothing to triage."

**S5 · Bug panel** — F3 panel: header (Bug icon, NB-n, title, **Stage ▾**, "Shows in: Bugs · Confirmed" / "Tasks · In progress"); Details: description area holds **What happened?** and **What did you expect?** as two labelled fields, then **Bug details** (Severity, Where, Found in, Fixed in, Duplicate of, I see this too with avatars), then Properties (Assigned to, Sprint, Due, Labels; Priority shown read-only "from severity"); links section with pull requests; Comments · Files.

**S6 · Report form** — the New module's **Bug details** section (W2), with **Similar open bugs** under the title: up to 5 rows (title, stage, see-too count, **That's my bug**), shown after 4 typed characters, debounced 300 ms.

**S7 · Dialogs** — Confirm (Severity required, Assigned to); Close (reason radio; Duplicate opens a bug picker; Can't reproduce needs a message, 1–2,000 chars); Fixed in (text, optional, ≤ 40 chars); Reopen (comment required).

**S8 · Overview card** — "2 urgent · 5 to triage · 3 fixed this week"; links to Triage.

**S9 · Chat action** — **Report as bug** in the message ⋯ (when Bugs is added), next to Create task.

#### 5. Data
- **No migration.** A bug is a task with `item_type = 'bug'` (F1); stages from F1's table; its fields in `type_fields`:
  - `severity`: 'urgent' | 'major' | 'minor' | null (Not sure)
  - `where`: { kind: 'web', browser, version } | { kind: 'app', platform, version } | { kind: 'other', text }
  - `steps` (≤ 5,000 chars), `expected` (≤ 2,000)
  - `foundIn`, `fixedIn` (≤ 40 chars each)
  - `duplicateOf` (task id) and `alsoSeen` (member ids, ≤ 500)
  - `fromMessage` ({ channelId, seq }) when reported from chat
- **Priority** is written from severity on every change (Urgent → urgent, Major → high, Minor → medium, Not sure → leaves priority as is).
- **Reported by** is the task's creator; agent reports carry `via: 'agent'` as today.
- **Pull requests** stay in `task_links` (kind `pull_request`).
- **Index:** `tasks_bug_open_idx (workspace_id, stage) WHERE item_type = 'bug' AND deleted_at IS NULL` (added to F1's migration list as 0104 if F1 already shipped).

#### 6. Server
- **`createTaskAction`** (F3) with `itemType: 'bug'` validates the bug schema; New is the default start from Bugs, Fixing from Tasks.
- **`similarBugsAction({ projectId, title })`**: open bugs (New, Confirmed, Fixing) whose titles match by the workspace task search; top 5; members and viewers.
- **`seeTooAction({ taskId, on })`**: adds or removes the viewer in `alsoSeen` and watchers; idempotent.
- **`confirmBugAction({ taskId, severity, assigneeId? })`**: members; sets Confirmed, severity, priority, assignee.
- **`closeBugAction({ taskId, reason, duplicateOfId?, message? })`**: members; for Duplicate resolves the chain to the oldest open bug, moves `alsoSeen`, the reporter and watchers, refuses loops; for Can't reproduce posts the comment with a mention. Agents: tier "yes".
- **`reopenBugAction({ taskId, comment })`**: to Confirmed (or New when the reporter adds details).
- **`setBugFieldsAction`** = F3's `updateTaskTypeFieldsAction` with the bug schema.
- **`reportBugFromMessageAction({ channelId, seq })`**: like `createTaskFromMessage`, returns a module prefill.
- **Reads:** `readBugsAction(projectId, view, filters)` with strip counts in the same query.

#### 7. Rules as pure functions (`src/lib/workflows/bugs.ts`) and their tests
- `priorityForSeverity(severity)` → urgent / high / medium / null. Tests: each value; null keeps priority.
- `resolveDuplicateTarget(bugId, chain)` → the oldest open bug or an error. Tests: A → B → C (C open) gives C; A → B where B is A's duplicate → refused; self → refused; closed target → walks to its open original.
- `mergeOnDuplicate(source, target)` → target's `alsoSeen` and watchers. Tests: union without repeats; the reporter added; the 500 cap keeps the earliest.
- `openSeverityCounts(bugs)` → strip numbers. Tests: closed and Fixed not counted; Not sure counted separately and hidden when zero.
- `triageOrder(bugs)` → oldest first, ties by see-too count. Tests: two same-day reports, more see-too first.
- `whereLabel(where)` → "Web · Chrome 131". Tests: each kind; missing version.
- `fixedGroups(bugs)` → groups by Fixed in, newest first, "No version" last.

#### 8. Everything around it
- **Overview card:** S8.
- **Notifications:**

  | Event | Who | Level |
  |---|---|---|
  | New bug reported | Owners and admins | Normal (Summary if more than 5 a day) |
  | Bug assigned to you | The assignee | Normal |
  | Your bug is Fixed | The reporter and I-see-this-too people | Normal |
  | Details needed (Can't reproduce) | The reporter | Normal |
  | Your bug was closed as Duplicate or Won't fix | The reporter | Normal |
  | Urgent bug confirmed | Owners and admins | Important |

- **My Work:** bugs assigned to you; "Details needed on NB-160" for reporters.
- **CLI:** `nb bugs list [--mine] [--severity urgent] [--stage new]`, `nb bugs report …` (W14), `nb bugs move NB-142 fixing [--backlog]`, `nb bugs close NB-150 --duplicate-of NB-142` (asks to confirm).
- **MCP:** new `networkbase_bug_report` (small: title, steps, expected, where, severity); listing and moving through F1's task tools with `type: "bug"`; `networkbase_bug_close` (tier "yes").
- **Agent briefing:** lists urgent open bugs.
- **Search:** bugs show severity and stage.
- **Matrix:** severity reaches it through priority.
- **Public:** none (B11); the Good first issues page waits with the public pages.

#### 9. Rollout
1. Ships when F1–F3 are live; the catalog marks Bugs `built`.
2. Turn on for test workspaces with real bug traffic first; then per workspace through Add workflow.
3. Existing tasks labelled "bug" stay tasks; an admin can select them and **Change type → Bug** (a new action: `changeTaskTypeAction({ taskIds[], toType, stage })`, for people who can edit the tasks, one undo), which asks the stage (default Confirmed, or Fixing for tasks already in progress).

#### 10. Tests
- **Unit:** part 7.
- **Server:** confirm requires severity; duplicate loop refused; Can't reproduce needs a message; agent close needs a yes; similar bugs never show closed ones; viewers can report but not triage.
- **Contract test:** `tests/unit/bugs-design-contract.test.ts`.
- **End to end:** add Bugs → report → That's my bug from a second person → triage Confirm Major → Fixing with sprint → PR link → Completed with review on → approve → Fixed in v2.4 → Verified; then a duplicate merge and a reopen.
- **Browser check list:** strip filter, triage keyboard (J/K move, C confirm, X close), phone triage, chat Report as bug, live new report in a second browser.

#### 11. Calls
1. Outside reporting, Incidents and the public good-first-issues list stay parked. **[call]**
2. Found in and Fixed in are version text until launches exist (T2, D2); no auto-verify. **[call]**
3. Severity sets priority; on bugs, priority is shown read-only "from severity". **[call]**
4. Severity can be **Not sure** when reporting; it's required at Confirm. **[call]**
5. New bugs notify owners and admins (no separate triage person setting). **[call]**
6. Can't reproduce asks the reporter in a comment; nothing closes or reopens on its own. **[call]**
7. Reopening goes to Confirmed with a comment; a reporter adding details reopens to New. **[call]**
8. Report as bug sits beside Create task on chat messages. **[call]**
9. Existing tasks can be changed to bugs by people who can edit them. **[call]**
10. **A2.1 (2026-11-23):** Bugs ships in three units; the catalog marks it **built** only at A2.3, so until then it is switched on for test workspaces only. A bug opens in the task panel on the Tasks tab (Back returns to Bugs). A drop on the Bugs board runs the panel's Stage menu, so a move that joins the board (Fixing, or straight to Fixed) asks the sprint first; Fixed asks **Fixed in** when the move is made from Bugs (a Completed drag on the Tasks board doesn't ask; the panel's Fixed in field is there). Viewers report bugs at New and nothing else (no assignee, sprint or dates); triage is for members. Similar open bugs matches titles. Arriving later: Close… with Won't fix / Duplicate / Can't reproduce, Reopen and the triage keys (A2.2); the chip row, search, Export CSV, the PR chip on cards, Report as bug and Change type (A2.3). Own tabs count what waits at their first stage (28.4). **[call]**
11. **A2.2 (2026-11-23):** closing a bug always goes through **Close…** (the Triage row, X, or a closing stage in any Stage menu opens it); a bare stage move to Won't fix, Duplicate or Can't reproduce is refused, so the CLI and agents close through A2.3's `nb bugs close`. Leaving Fixed, Verified or a closed stage from a Stage menu opens **Reopen** (to Confirmed, comment required). Can't reproduce posts its message as a comment that mentions the reporter, and that mention is the reporter's notice (no second ping); the comment goes first, so if it can't be posted nothing closes. Reopen with details is for a reporter who can edit tasks (a viewer reporter asks in a comment). Closed bugs leave the Bugs views; they're found by search and from their duplicate. **[call]**
12. **A2.3 (2026-11-23):** **Report as bug** shows on a workspace channel message's ⋯ only while Bugs is added there; it opens the New module on Bug with the first line as the title and the message as What happened? (Similar open bugs shows as in Bugs), files the bug at New, posts its card in the conversation like Create task, and links back to the message. The message's files are named under What happened? and reached through that link; they aren't copied into the workspace's Files. **Change to a bug** (panel ⋯, `nb bugs from`) is for plain tasks only (not assignments or projects) and keeps the task's status: To do → Confirmed (or New), started → Fixing, Completed → Fixed (or Verified); a task leaving the board takes it out of its sprint, which only owners and admins do. `nb bugs list|report|move|close|from`; closing from the CLI asks first, and an agent's close (`networkbase_bug_close`) needs its person's yes; an agent reports and moves to Confirmed or Fixing on its own. A bug reported from the CLI or an agent isn't assigned to the reporter. The tab gets search (title words, or NB-12), Assigned to, Export CSV of the bugs shown, and a pull-request chip on cards (the first linked PR). The Severity chip stays the strip above the views. **[call]**

### 38.7 T4 · Requests (agreed 2026-11-18)

**Requests** is the second own tab over the same tasks: its job is **taking in asks** from people in the workspace (internal requests, design requests), deciding which to take, and keeping a **response clock**. A request **joins the Tasks board at Accepted**. T4 also builds the **request types** and the clock that K5 (33.6) later opens to a whole company.

#### 1. What it is and the references
| Reference | Rating / source | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **IT Issue Tracker** (Notion) | **4.86 / 95** (33.6) | Type chips on each ask, a board, open asks per handler |
| **Internal help desk** (Notion) | **4.85 / 40** (33.6) | One place to ask, with a short form per type and a Triage view |
| **IT Help Desk: Requests & SLAs** | 21.3 | First response and resolve times, a Breaching soon view, timers that follow working hours and pause while waiting |
| Design requests (24.6) | Agreed | What's needed, size or format, brief, assets, In review, Delivered |
| 28.3 · K5 (33.6) | Agreed | Stages New → Accepted → In progress → In review → Delivered, Declined; Waiting on you pauses the clock; Did this solve it? |
| What the code has | Checked 2026-11-18 | Workspaces have a `time_zone`; tasks have due dates, comments, files and watchers; **task reminders** fire from the hourly job `chat/due.wake` (cron `15 * * * *`); no working hours anywhere |

**Changes from 21.3 and 24.6:** times are set **per request type**, not per priority; "Waiting on customer" is **Waiting on you** (people inside the workspace); there are no support tickets from outside (parked).

#### 2. The 18 layers
1. **Getting it:** **Requests** in "Own tab · same tasks": "Adds a Requests tab. People ask; accepted requests join Tasks at Accepted."
2. **Setting it up:** two starter **request types** (**General request**, **Design request**); **working hours** (Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00 in the workspace time zone); admins edit both.
3. **Items:** a **Request** (type `request`): title, request type, the type's answers, requested by, assigned to, need by, files, stage, the clock, Waiting on you, what was delivered, Did this solve it?
4. **Views:** **Inbox · Board · Mine · My asks · Breaching soon**.
5. **Actions and flow:** ask → New → Accept (choose who) or Decline → In progress → (Waiting on you ⇄) → In review (the asker looks) → Delivered → Did this solve it? (No reopens).
6. **Surfaces:** title row, views, request card with the clock, Inbox row, request panel, the ask form (New module's Request section), type editor, working-hours editor, Overview card.
7. **Design spec:** shared parts; the clock as a mono countdown with words ("2 h 10 m left", "Breached 40 m ago"); Lucide Inbox, Timer, Hourglass, PauseCircle, CheckCheck; contract test.
8. **Words:** Requests · Request · Ask · Request type · General request · Design request · New · Accepted · In progress · In review · Delivered · Declined · Waiting on you · Need by · First reply within · Deliver within · Working hours · Breaching soon · Breached · Did this solve it? · Yes · No; never "ticket", "SLA" on screen ("response time" instead), "Lead".
9. **Links:** the Tasks board (from Accepted), Bugs (This is a bug), Files and Assets (what was delivered), the Calendar view (Need by), My Work, K5.
10. **People:** members and viewers ask; members triage and handle; admins edit types and working hours; never public.
11. **States:** clock running, paused, breached, stopped; live new asks; undo for accept, decline and stage moves.
12. **Edges:** no handler, a handler who leaves, asking for yourself, a request edited after Accepted, a type deleted with open requests, time zones and daylight saving, a request reopened twice.
13. **Phone:** Inbox is the phone default; asking is a full-height sheet.
14. **Accessibility:** the clock is text, never colour alone; types are a labelled select.
15. **Notifications:** below.
16. **Trust and data:** requests are visible to workspace members (like Tasks); private requests wait for K5 (organizations).
17. **Reuse vs new:** below.
18. **How we know it works:** below.

#### 3. Step-by-step walkthroughs
**W1 · First look**
1. Asha adds **Requests** (F1). The tab (Inbox icon) appears; it opens on **Inbox**: "No requests yet. People in the workspace ask here; you choose what to take on." and **New request**.
2. A note for admins: "Response times follow working hours: Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00 (Asia/Kolkata). **Change**".

**W2 · Asking (General request)**
1. Dev clicks **New request**; the New module opens on **Request**, Starts at **New**.
2. **Request details:** **Request type** (General request ▾), then the type's questions (General: "What do you need?" (text, required) · "Why now?" (text)).
3. **Schedule:** **Need by** (Today · 1 week · 2 weeks · 4 weeks · Pick a date).
4. Files under Subtasks and files.
5. Footer: "Shows in Requests · not on the Tasks board yet · first reply within 4 working hours"; **Create request**.
6. NB-180 lands in **Inbox**; the type's triage people are told.

**W3 · Asking for a design**
1. Mei picks **Design request**: questions **What's needed** (choice: Social graphic · Banner · Deck · Video edit · Other), **Size or format** (text), **Brief** (text, required), **Assets to use** (files).
2. The footer shows the type's times: "first reply within 1 working day · deliver within 5 working days".

**W4 · Triage in the Inbox**
1. Asha's **Inbox** lists New requests, oldest first: type chip, title, requested by, need by, and the **first-reply clock** ("3 h 20 m left").
2. **Accept** opens: Assigned to (required), sprint (owners and admins; members see "Goes to the Backlog"); **Accept** sets **Accepted**, stops the first-reply clock (a reply happened), starts the deliver clock, and the request **joins the Tasks board** in To do (F1).
3. **Decline** asks a reason (required, shown to the asker); the request closes as **Declined**, off the board.
4. **This is a bug** (when Bugs is added) changes its type to Bug at Confirmed with the asker as Reported by (T3's Change type).

**W5 · Working and waiting**
1. Karan (assigned) moves it to **In progress** (stage menu or the board).
2. He needs a logo file: **Waiting on you** (button in the panel) posts his question as a comment mentioning Mei and **pauses the clock**; the card shows "Waiting on Mei · paused".
3. Mei replies in the comments; the clock **resumes on her reply** (or when Karan clicks **Resume**).

**W6 · In review and Delivered**
1. Karan moves it to **In review**: Mei is asked to look ("Mei, does this work?"); the clock keeps running.
2. Mei comments; Karan moves it to **Delivered**, adding **What was delivered** (a file, a document or a link, optional).
3. With required review in the workspace, Delivered waits for approval first (B3).
4. Mei gets **Did this solve it?** **Yes** closes it for good; **No** asks a note and moves it back to **In progress** with the deliver clock running again.

**W7 · Breaching soon**
1. **Breaching soon** lists accepted requests whose deliver clock has under 20 % left, plus New requests close to the first-reply time; sorted by time left.
2. When a clock passes 80 %, the handler gets a Normal notice; when it breaches, the handler and admins get an Important one (once each).

**W8 · My asks**
1. Dev's **My asks** shows everything he requested: stage, handler, need by, the clock, and **Yes / No** buttons on delivered ones.

**W9 · Editing request types (admins)**
1. ⋯ → **Request types**: a list with name, icon, questions count, first reply within, deliver within, triage people; **New type** (up to 12 types).
2. A type editor: name; icon (Lucide); up to **5 questions** (text, long text, choice, date, file; required or not); **First reply within** and **Deliver within** (working hours or days, or Off); **Who triages** (default owners and admins).
3. Archiving a type keeps its requests; it disappears from the ask form.

**W10 · Working hours**
1. ⋯ → **Working hours**: days (Mon–Sun checkboxes), from and to times, the workspace time zone (read-only, from Settings), and **Holidays** (dates, optional).
2. Changing hours recalculates every open clock from the start, not only from now.

**W11 · A request made from Tasks**
1. **New ▾ → Request** in Tasks starts at **Accepted** with Assigned to = the creator (F3); the first-reply clock is skipped (it's already taken on).

**W12 · Phone**
1. Requests opens on **Inbox**; Accept and Decline are buttons; the clock shows under the title.
2. Asking is a full-height sheet with the type's questions one under another.

**W13 · CLI and agents**
1. `nb requests new --type design "Banner for the launch" --answer brief="…" --need-by 2026-12-01`.
2. `nb requests list --breaching`; an agent's briefing lists requests close to breach.
3. Agents can ask and comment; **Accept** and **Decline** are a person's (tier "yes").

#### 4. Screen spec
**S1 · Title row** — Inbox icon + "Requests"; counts "5 new · 2 breaching soon"; views **Inbox · Board · Mine · My asks · Breaching soon**; F3 chip row with **Type ▾ · Assigned to ▾ · Requested by ▾ · Need by ▾**; **New request**; ⋯ (Request types · Working hours · Export CSV).

**S2 · Card** — type chip, title, requested by avatar, need-by date, clock line ("1 d 4 h left" / "Breached 40 m ago" / "Paused · waiting on Mei"), handler avatar.

**S3 · Board** — columns New · Accepted · In progress · In review · Delivered (Declined only through Decline); dragging New → Accepted opens the Accept form.

**S4 · Inbox row** — type chip · title · requested by · need by · first-reply clock · **Accept** · **Decline**; empty: "Nothing new."

**S5 · Request panel** — F3 panel: header (Inbox icon, NB-n, title, **Stage ▾**, "Shows in: Requests · In progress" / "Tasks · In progress"); **Request details** (type, the answers as label–value rows, requested by, need by); the **clock** block (First reply: "replied in 1 h 10 m" / Deliver: "2 d 3 h left", with Paused and Breached states); **Waiting on [name]** / **Resume** button; Delivered block (what was delivered, Did this solve it? answer); Properties; Comments · Files.

**S6 · Ask form** — the New module's **Request details** section: Request type select (icons), the type's questions rendered in order with their kinds; Due renamed **Need by**; footer with the type's times.

**S7 · Request types editor** — list and editor as W9; question rows with kind select, required toggle, ⋯ (Move up / down, Delete).

**S8 · Working hours editor** — W10.

**S9 · Overview card** — "5 new · 2 breaching soon · 8 delivered this week"; links to Inbox.

#### 5. Data
**Migration `0105_requests.sql`:**
- **New table `workspace_request_types`:** `id`, `workspace_id → workspaces (cascade)`, `name` (≤ 40), `icon` (Lucide name), `questions jsonb` (≤ 5: { id, label ≤ 120, kind: 'text' | 'long_text' | 'choice' | 'date' | 'file', options[] ≤ 12, required }), `triager_ids uuid[]` (empty = owners and admins), `first_reply_minutes int NULL`, `deliver_minutes int NULL` (working minutes), `is_private boolean default false` (used by K5 only), `position int`, `archived_at`, `created_by`, timestamps. Unique `(workspace_id, lower(name)) WHERE archived_at IS NULL`.
- **`workspaces.working_hours jsonb NULL`:** { days: [1..7], from: 'HH:MM', to: 'HH:MM', holidays: ['YYYY-MM-DD'] }; null = Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00.
- **Request fields in `type_fields`:** `requestTypeId`, `answers` ({ questionId: value }), `waiting` ({ since, onUserId } | null), `pausedMinutes` (int), `firstRepliedAt`, `acceptedAt`, `deliveredAt`, `delivered` ({ kind: 'file' | 'doc' | 'link', ref }), `solved` ('yes' | 'no' | null), `declineReason`, `reopenCount`.
- **Need by** is the task's `due_date`.
- **Clock warnings** are rows in the existing `task_reminders` (system rows, `note` = 'request_clock:80' or ':breach'), sent by the hourly `chat/due.wake` job; recalculated on accept, pause, resume, reopen and working-hours changes. **No new scheduled job.**

#### 6. Server
- **`createTaskAction`** (F3) with `itemType: 'request'` validates the answers against the type's questions (required ones, choice options, file ids the asker can read).
- **`acceptRequestAction({ taskId, assigneeId, sprintId? })`**: members; New → Accepted; sets `firstRepliedAt` if empty and `acceptedAt`; schedules clock reminders; joins the board (F1).
- **`declineRequestAction({ taskId, reason })`**: members; closes as Declined; notifies the asker.
- **`setWaitingAction({ taskId, onUserId, question })` / `resumeRequestAction({ taskId })`**: the handler; posts the comment; updates `waiting` and `pausedMinutes`; moves reminders. A reply comment by the awaited person calls resume.
- **`deliverRequestAction({ taskId, delivered? })`**: to Delivered (review gating B3); asks the asker.
- **`answerSolvedAction({ taskId, solved, note? })`**: the asker (or the person it's for); No reopens to In progress, `reopenCount + 1`.
- **`saveRequestTypeAction` / `archiveRequestTypeAction`**, **`saveWorkingHoursAction`**: owners and admins; working-hours changes recalculate open clocks in batches.
- **First reply** is set by the first of: Accept, Decline, or a comment by anyone other than the asker.
- **Reads:** `readRequestsAction(projectId, view, filters)` returns clocks already worked out (time left, state).

#### 7. Rules as pure functions (`src/lib/workflows/requests.ts`) and their tests
- `workingMinutesBetween(start, end, hours, tz)`. Tests: Fri 16:00 → Mon 10:00 with 09–17 Mon–Fri = 120; a holiday skipped; across a daylight-saving change in a zone that has one; start outside hours counts from the next opening.
- `addWorkingMinutes(start, minutes, hours, tz)` → the deadline. Tests: 240 minutes from Thu 15:00 → Fri 11:00; from Sat → Mon 13:00.
- `clockState({ startedAt, budgetMinutes, pausedMinutes, waitingSince, now, hours, tz })` → { leftMinutes, state: 'running' | 'paused' | 'soon' | 'breached' | 'off' }. Tests: 85 % used → soon; paused never breaches; budget null → off.
- `reminderTimes(clock)` → the 80 % and breach instants. Tests: none when off; recomputed after a pause shifts both.
- `validateAnswers(type, answers)`. Tests: missing required; an option not in the list; a date in the past allowed; 6 questions refused at save.
- `firstReplyAt(events, askerId)`. Tests: the asker's own comment doesn't count; Decline counts.

#### 8. Everything around it
- **Overview card:** S9.
- **Notifications:**

  | Event | Who | Level |
  |---|---|---|
  | New request | The type's triage people | Normal (Summary above 10 a day) |
  | Accepted · Declined | The asker | Normal |
  | Assigned to you | The handler | Normal |
  | Waiting on you | The person asked | Normal |
  | Delivered (Did this solve it?) | The asker | Normal |
  | 80 % of the clock used | The handler | Normal |
  | Breached | The handler, then owners and admins | Important (once each) |
  | Answered No | The handler | Normal |

- **My Work:** handlers see their requests; askers see "Waiting on you" and "Did this solve it?" items.
- **CLI:** `nb requests new | list [--mine | --asked | --breaching] | accept NB-180 --to mei | decline NB-180 --reason "…" | wait NB-180 --on mei "Which logo?" | deliver NB-180 [--link …]`.
- **MCP:** `networkbase_request_create` (small), `networkbase_request_list` (read); accept, decline and deliver are tier "yes".
- **Search:** requests show type and stage; answers are searchable by members.
- **K5 (organizations):** a team workspace switches on **Take requests from the company**; `is_private` types, **Ask a team**, and "Asking for" build on this round.
- **Public:** none.

#### 9. Rollout
1. Migration 0105 adds the table and the column; nothing shows until Requests is added.
2. The two starter types are written when Requests is first added (not in the migration).
3. Clock reminders ride the existing hourly job; watch the Inngest usage check (memory: free-tier limit) for one week after the first workspaces turn it on.

#### 10. Tests
- **Unit:** part 7.
- **Server:** required answers enforced; only triage people and members accept; the asker can't accept their own request unless they're a member with rights (allowed, shown "self-accepted"); No reopens and reschedules reminders; working-hours change recalculates clocks.
- **Contract test:** `tests/unit/requests-design-contract.test.ts`.
- **End to end:** add Requests → ask a design request → accept with a handler → waiting on the asker → reply resumes → In review → Delivered with a file → No → reopen → Delivered → Yes.
- **Browser check list:** clock text in two time zones; breach notice at the hour after breaching; phone Inbox; keyboard (A accept, D decline in Inbox).

#### 11. Calls
1. Response times are set per request type (first reply, deliver), in working minutes; Off is allowed. **[call]**
2. **Working hours** are one workspace setting (days, times, holidays) in the workspace time zone. **[call]**
3. **In review** means the asker looks at the work; the workspace review queue still gates Delivered when review is required (B3). This narrows 28.3's "In review → review requested" for requests. **[call]**
4. **Waiting on you** pauses the clock without changing the stage; a reply from that person resumes it. **[call]**
5. **Did this solve it?**: No reopens to In progress with a note. **[call]**
6. Clock warnings use the existing task reminders and the hourly job; no new scheduled job (Inngest free limit). **[call]**
7. Members and viewers can ask; members accept, decline and handle. **[call]**
8. Up to 12 request types per workspace, 5 questions each. **[call]**
9. A request can become a bug (T3's Change type) with the asker as Reported by. **[call]**
10. Private request types belong to K5's company asks, not to workspace Requests. **[call]**
11. **A2.4 (2026-11-23):** Requests ships in three units (A2.4 types, asking, Inbox, Accept and Decline; A2.5 working hours, the clock and Breaching soon; A2.6 waiting, In review, Delivered, Did this solve it?, the Overview card, CLI and MCP); the catalog marks it **built** at A2.6. **Request types are a workspace setting** in `workspaces.workflow_settings.requests.types` (from 0103), not a new table: 12 types of 5 questions fit easily, and nothing waits on a migration; K5 moves them to a table when private company asks need SQL read rules. **Working hours** will sit beside them in `workflow_settings`. The starter types are written the first time anyone reads them, so every way of adding Requests gets them. A file question takes the files added in the New module (the first file question). A new request is answered only by **Accept** or **Decline**: on the Board, New → Accepted opens Accept and other moves out of New are refused; a bare move to Declined is refused without a reason. Accept or Decline sets the first reply when nothing came before. **This is a bug** turns a New request into a bug at Confirmed (T3's Change type), the asker staying Reported by. The ask form keeps Description beside the type's questions (F3 W3 carries it when switching type; corrected after the A2.5 live check). Archiving a type needs at least one other active type. **[call]**
12. **A2.5 (2026-11-23):** **Working hours** sit in `workspaces.workflow_settings.workingHours` and the clock uses `workspaces.time_zone`; ordinary workspaces had no time-zone setting, so the **Working hours** editor sets it (default: the editor's own zone; UTC until set). Wall-clock time counts, so a daylight-saving change never adds or loses an hour; a working day is 8 working hours in the clock's words ("1 d 4 h left"). Warnings are system rows in `task_reminders` (note `request_clock:<first|deliver>:<80|breach>`), rewritten on every change to the request (create, Accept, Decline, any stage move, a new handler) and to the workspace (working hours, a type's times), and closed without a notice when the request has moved on by the time they fire; people's own reminder lists never show them. Before it's accepted, the 80 % warning goes to the type's triage people (there's no handler yet). The clock shows as words with a screen-reader label ("First reply: 3 h 20 m left", "Breached 40 m ago"); colour only repeats it. The title row counts "N new · N breaching soon". **[call]**
13. **A2.6 (2026-11-23):** **Waiting on…** (panel, `nb requests wait`) is for members on accepted work; it posts the question as a comment mentioning the person (that mention is their notice) and pauses the clock; **Resume** or that person's next comment ends the pause, and the paused working minutes move the deadline by exactly that much. The first comment by anyone other than the asker counts as the first reply. **Deliver…** takes an optional https link (it's also added to the task's links) and still waits for approval where review is on; Delivered tells the asker and asks **Did this solve it?** in the panel, My asks and My work. **No** needs a note, posts it as a comment, tells the handler and reopens to In progress even when the asker couldn't move others' work (the asker's right on their own request); leaving Delivered any other way clears the answer. My work also lists a request that waits on you, or that you asked and haven't answered, with the reason as its tag. The CLI answers a type's questions with `--field name=value` (the global `--answer` already answers prompts); MCP adds `networkbase_request_create`, `networkbase_request_list` and `networkbase_request_decide` (accept, decline or deliver; a yes). Requests is **built**. **[call]**

### 38.8 T5 · Content (agreed 2026-11-18)

**Content** is the third own tab over the same tasks: its job is **deciding what's published, where and when**. A content item **joins the Tasks board at Drafting** and is Completed once it's Scheduled. This is 14.2's design for the **Blog** and **Social** setups; Podcast and Video setups stay parked, and automatic publishing to NetworkBase Updates waits for O2.

#### 1. What it is and the references
| Reference | Rating / source | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **Social Media Content Planner** | **4.9 / 800+** (14.2) | Calendar first, an Ideas rail, channel quick-add buttons |
| **Blog Editorial Calendar** (Notion) | 4.9 / 99 | Views by status and by writer; Type of content; Audience |
| **Social Media Calendar** (Notion) | 4.8 / 700+ | Posts per week by platform |
| 14.2's agreed changes | Agreed | No follower counts pulled from platforms; one item, several channels, a link each; Editing and Scheduled stages; publishing is a reminder plus **Mark published** |
| 28.3 | Agreed | Idea (off the board) → Drafting → Editing (review requested) → Scheduled → Published |
| What the code has | Checked 2026-11-18 | T1's **Calendar** part; Updates with likes and comment counts (no per-Update view count); the review queue; task reminders on the hourly job with exact-time wake events |

**Held back:** Podcast and Video setups (18.2, 19.2); **scheduled Updates** (O2 adds automatic publishing); campaigns as their own records (a label is enough).

#### 2. The 18 layers
1. **Getting it:** **Content** in "Own tab · same tasks": "Adds a Content tab. Pieces join Tasks at Drafting." Adding it asks **Blog**, **Social** or both, then **Pick your channels**.
2. **Setting it up:** channels (name, icon, audience typed, "posts on NetworkBase Updates"), **types** (Article, Newsletter, Post, Reel, Carousel, Thread, Short…) each with an optional checklist, a default publish time (10:00), the workspace time zone.
3. **Items:** a **Content item** (type `content`): title, stage, channels, publish date and time, content type, format, writer (Assigned to), editor, audience, keyword, campaign (label), draft document, assets, brief, checklist (subtasks), and per channel a published link and results.
4. **Views:** **Calendar · This week · Board · To schedule · Performance**.
5. **Actions and flow:** idea → Drafting (date set, checklist added) → Write draft → Ready for edit (Editing, review requested to the editor) → approved → Scheduled → publish reminder → Mark published (links) → results.
6. **Surfaces:** title row with channel quick-adds, the Calendar with Ideas rail, This week list, Board, To schedule, Performance table and chart, the content panel, Mark published and Results dialogs, the channels and types editor, Overview card.
7. **Design spec:** 14.2 § 7 (Today in Clay; stages with words; channels by icon and name, never colour alone; precision badges; Lucide PenLine, Lightbulb, CalendarDays, Send, Clock, BarChart3 and channel icons as small marks); contract test.
8. **Words:** Content · Idea · Drafting · Editing · Scheduled · Published · Cancelled · Channel · Cross-channel · Writer · Editor · Publish date · Write draft · Ready for edit · Mark published · Results · Performance · Campaign · Keyword · Brief · Audience.
9. **Links:** T1 Calendar part, the Tasks board, review, Documents (draft), Files (assets), Updates (pick an Update as the published link), Requests and meetings ("Save as content idea"), My Work.
10. **People:** members create, write, edit and publish; admins set channels and types; never public.
11. **States:** skeleton grid; live moves; undo for drags, stage moves and Mark published.
12. **Edges:** an item with several channels publishing at different times, a reminder for a past time, a channel removed with items, an editor who leaves, time zones, 300 items in a month.
13. **Phone:** This week is the default; quick-adds become New ▾; dragging becomes "Move to…".
14. **Accessibility:** day cells are announced with their date and items; publishing times in full with the time zone.
15. **Notifications:** below.
16. **Trust and data:** members only; NetworkBase never posts to social platforms (26.5); results are typed by people.
17. **Reuse vs new:** below.
18. **How we know it works:** below.

#### 3. Step-by-step walkthroughs
**W1 · Adding Content**
1. Asha adds **Content** (F1); a sheet asks **Blog**, **Social** (both allowed) and then **Pick your channels**: Blog shows Blog · Newsletter; Social shows Instagram · TikTok · YouTube · LinkedIn · X · Facebook; **Add your own** (name, icon).
2. For each channel, optional **Audience** (typed number) and, for Blog, **Posts on NetworkBase Updates** (on by default).
3. The Content tab (PenLine icon) opens on **Calendar**: this month, the Today marker, a row of channel quick-add buttons, the **Ideas** rail with **+ Add idea**, the hint "Plan what you'll publish and when. Ideas wait on the left until they get a date."

**W2 · Capturing ideas**
1. Mei types in **+ Add idea**: "Morning routine reel", Enter. The idea appears in the rail (type and channel optional).
2. From a meeting's action items or a request (T4), **Save as content idea** makes an idea with "From" filled.

**W3 · Planning onto the calendar**
1. Mei drags the idea onto Thu 12; it becomes **Drafting** with publish date Thu 12 at the default time (10:00).
2. The F1 Join-board sheet asks the sprint (members: Backlog). The piece is now on the Tasks board as **Content · Drafting** with the writer set to Mei.
3. If its type has a checklist (e.g. Reel: Hook · Captions · Cover image), the steps are added as subtasks.

**W4 · Making a piece directly**
1. **Instagram** quick-add opens the New module on **Content**, Channels = Instagram, Starts at **Drafting** (or **Idea** from the rail's +).
2. **Content details:** Channels (multi), Type, Format, Editor, Audience, Keyword, Brief; **Publish date** and time replace Due.
3. Footer: "Joins Tasks at Drafting · also shows in Content · publishes Thu 12 at 10:00".

**W5 · Writing**
1. In the panel, **Write draft** creates a document from the type's template (D6; until D6 a blank document titled after the piece) and links it; the panel shows "Draft · 1,240 words".
2. Assets: files attached, or picked from Files.

**W6 · Editing**
1. Mei clicks **Ready for edit**: asks Editor (default the type's editor or the last one) and a note; the piece moves to **Editing** and a review is requested from the editor (the workspace review queue).
2. Sohrab approves → **Scheduled** (Completed on the board); **Changes needed** → back to **Drafting** with his note as a comment.

**W7 · Publishing**
1. At the publish time Mei gets "Publish now: Pricing guide on LinkedIn" (reminder at the exact time).
2. She posts it on LinkedIn herself, then clicks **Mark published**: one link field per channel (LinkedIn link required to mark that channel; others can be marked later).
3. For a **NetworkBase Updates** channel she picks the Update she posted (until O2 publishes automatically); its likes and comments fill Results by themselves.
4. When every channel has a link, the stage is **Published**; with some left, the card shows "Published on 1 of 2".

**W8 · Results**
1. Seven days after publishing, Mei gets a reminder (optional, on by default): "Add results for Pricing guide".
2. **Results** dialog: per channel, views, likes, comments, clicks (all optional numbers).
3. **Performance** shows a table (piece · channel · date · numbers) and a posts-per-week chart by channel.

**W9 · Moving and cancelling**
1. Dragging a Scheduled piece to another day moves its publish reminder; a piece's time can be changed in the panel.
2. **Cancel** (stage menu) keeps it in history as Cancelled; off the board.

**W10 · This week and To schedule**
1. **This week:** days as headings, each piece with time, channel icons, stage, writer.
2. **To schedule:** pieces past Idea with no date; dragging (split with the calendar) or **Set date**.

**W11 · Phone**
1. Opens on **This week**; **New ▾** replaces the quick-add row; the Ideas rail becomes a section at the top.
2. Calendar opens as T1's agenda list; moving uses "Move to…".

**W12 · CLI and agents**
1. `nb content add "Pricing guide" --channels blog,linkedin --type article --publish 2026-12-03T10:00`.
2. `nb content list --week`; `nb content published NB-210 --link linkedin=https://…`.
3. Agents can draft ideas and briefs and write drafts; **Mark published** and approving an edit are a person's (tier "yes"); NetworkBase and agents never post to outside platforms.

#### 4. Screen spec
**S1 · Title row** — PenLine + "Content"; month and ‹ Today ›; views **Calendar · This week · Board · To schedule · Performance**; F3 chip row with **Channel ▾ · Stage ▾ · Writer ▾ · + Filter** (Campaign, Type); **New ▾**; ⋯ (Channels · Types and checklists · Export CSV).

**S2 · Channel quick-add row** — one small button per channel (icon + name) and **+ Cross-channel**.

**S3 · Calendar with Ideas rail** — T1's Calendar part (S10 of T1) with: the **Ideas** rail on the left (idea cards: title, type, channel icons; **+ Add idea**), the **Channels** list under it (name, typed audience); cards show channel icons, title, stage badge and a clock when a reminder is set.

**S4 · This week list** — days, pieces with time (mono), channel icons, title, stage, writer avatar.

**S5 · Board** — columns Idea · Drafting · Editing · Scheduled · Published; group by **Channel** or **Writer** from ⋯.

**S6 · To schedule** — table: title, type, channels, writer, stage; **Set date**.

**S7 · Content panel** — F3 panel: header (PenLine, NB-n, title, **Stage ▾**, "Shows in: Content · Editing" / "Tasks · In progress"); **Content details** (channels, publish date and time, type, format, writer, editor, audience, keyword, campaign, draft with word count, assets, brief); checklist as subtasks; after publishing **Published at** (a link per channel) and **Results** (numbers per channel); Comments · Files.

**S8 · Dialogs** — Ready for edit (editor, note); Mark published (link per channel; Update picker for NetworkBase); Results (four numbers per channel).

**S9 · Performance** — table with column sort; the posts-per-week chart (plain SVG stacked bars by channel, labelled; legend with icons and names).

**S10 · Channels and types editor** — channel rows (name, icon, audience, NetworkBase toggle, archive); type rows (name, formats, checklist steps, default editor).

**S11 · Overview card** — "3 publishing this week · 2 waiting for edit · next: Pricing guide, Thu".

#### 5. Data
**Migration `0106_content.sql`:**
- **`workspaces.content_settings jsonb NULL`:** { setups: ['blog' | 'social'], channels: [{ id, name, icon, audience?, updates: boolean, archived? }], types: [{ id, name, formats[], checklist[], editorId? }], defaultTime: 'HH:MM' }.
- **Content fields in `type_fields`:** `channels` (channel ids), `publishAt` (timestamp; also written to `due_date` so Calendar, My Work and reminders work unchanged), `contentType`, `format`, `editorId`, `audience`, `keyword`, `brief`, `draftDocId`, `published` ({ channelId: { link | updateId, at } }), `results` ({ channelId: { views, likes, comments, clicks } }), `resultsReminder` (boolean).
- **Campaign** is a task label prefixed in the picker ("campaign: Back to school").
- **Publish and results reminders** are `task_reminders` rows (exact-time wake events of the hourly job).

#### 6. Server
- **`createTaskAction`** (F3) with `itemType: 'content'`; Idea from the rail or the tab's Idea start; Drafting from Tasks; checklist subtasks added when a piece enters Drafting.
- **`saveContentSettingsAction`**: owners and admins; channels and types; archiving a channel keeps its items and links.
- **`writeDraftAction({ taskId })`**: creates the draft document (template from D6 when available), links it, returns its slug; word count read from the document's plain text at render.
- **`readyForEditAction({ taskId, editorId, note })`**: to Editing; requests review from the editor (review queue).
- **Approval / Changes needed**: the existing review actions; approval sets **Scheduled**, changes needed returns to **Drafting** with the comment.
- **`markPublishedAction({ taskId, links: { channelId: url | updateId } })`**: validates URLs (http/https, ≤ 2,048) or an Update in the workspace; never fetches the URL (26.5); Published when every channel has one.
- **`saveResultsAction({ taskId, results })`**: numbers ≥ 0; members.
- **`readContentAction(projectId, view, range, filters)`**: Calendar range plus ideas and To schedule counts; Performance rows with NetworkBase Update likes and comments joined live.

#### 7. Rules as pure functions (`src/lib/workflows/content.ts`) and their tests
- `publishState(channels, published)` → 'none' | 'partial' | 'all'. Tests: 1 of 2 → partial; all → all; an archived channel isn't required.
- `checklistFor(type)` → subtask titles. Tests: none; three steps; a renamed type keeps steps.
- `defaultPublishAt(day, defaultTime, tz)`. Tests: 10:00 in Asia/Kolkata on Dec 3 → 04:30 UTC; a day across daylight saving elsewhere.
- `weeklyCounts(items, channels, weeks)` → chart data. Tests: a cross-channel piece counts once per channel; Cancelled not counted.
- `resultsDue(publishedAt, now, enabled)` → whether the 7-day reminder is due. Tests: 6 days false; 7 true; disabled false.
- `nbUpdateResults(update)` → likes and comments; views left blank (Updates have no per-Update view count).

#### 8. Everything around it
- **Overview card:** S11.
- **Notifications:**

  | Event | Who | Level |
  |---|---|---|
  | Piece assigned to you | The writer | Normal |
  | Ready for edit | The editor | Normal (the review request) |
  | Changes needed · Approved | The writer | Normal |
  | Publish now | The writer | Important (at the time) |
  | Add results (7 days) | The writer | Summary |

- **My Work:** pieces you write, ordered by publish time; "Publish now" items on the day.
- **CLI:** W12; `nb content ideas` lists the rail.
- **MCP:** `networkbase_content_add` (small), `networkbase_content_list` (read); mark published is tier "yes".
- **Search:** pieces show channels and publish date.
- **O2 (later):** a NetworkBase Updates channel can publish the linked draft automatically at the time.
- **Public:** none (B11); published Updates are public as Updates already are.

1. Migration 0106 adds one nullable column; nothing shows until Content is added.
2. Uses T1's Calendar part; ships after T1.
3. Existing tasks can become content with T3's **Change type** (stage asked; default Drafting).

### 38.9 T2 · Roadmap (agreed 2026-11-18)

**Roadmap** is the fourth own tab over the same tasks: its job is **deciding what ships, Now / Next / Later**. A roadmap item **never goes on the board** (28.1); its **work tasks** (Part of the item) do. Launches become documents (D2); the public roadmap waits with the public pages.

#### 1. What it is and the references
| Reference | Rating / source | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **Product Roadmap Timeline** (desbyseb) | 4.8 / 40 (11.5) | Items as bars with their status, quarters on top |
| **Roadmap** (Notion) | 4.9 / 100+ | Not copied: it's task management, which Tasks does |
| 11.5's agreed changes | Agreed | Delivery order Backlog → Planned → In progress → Testing → Launched, Won't do; types Feature · Improvement · Fix; progress from linked work |
| 22.4 | Agreed | Game milestones Concept → Prototype → Vertical slice → Alpha → Beta → Release |
| 28.2, 28.11 | Agreed | Own tab, never on the board; **Now / Next / Later** column; outcome |
| What the code has | Checked 2026-11-18 | T1's Part of, Timeline and completion; F1 types; no launches yet |

#### 2. The 18 layers
1. **Getting it:** **Roadmap** in "Own tab · same tasks": "Adds a Roadmap tab: what ships Now, Next and Later. Its work tasks go on the board." Wizard: ticked for Startup, Web app, Game dev.
2. **Setting it up:** types **Feature · Improvement · Fix · Milestone** (fixed; Milestone carries the game milestone names as a choice); no other settings.
3. **Items:** **Roadmap item** (type `roadmap_item`): icon, name, outcome (one line: what changes for people), stage, column (Now · Next · Later), type, priority, Assigned to, target date (optional), ships in (a launch document, D2), built by (projects, T1), work tasks (Part of), requests it answers (T4), progress.
4. **Views:** **Now · Next · Later** (default) · **By stage** · **Timeline** · **Backlog**.
5. **Actions and flow:** capture (Backlog) → choose a column → plan (Planned) → work starts (**In progress**, automatic) → Testing (by hand) → Launched (when its launch is launched, or by hand); Won't do with a reason.
6. **Surfaces:** title row, the three-column board, stage board, Timeline (T1 grid), Backlog table, item panel with **Work**, Overview card.
7. **Design spec:** 11.5 § 7 (Map icon; stage and type badges with words; Clay launch diamonds on the timeline); contract test.
8. **Words:** Roadmap · Roadmap item · Now · Next · Later · Backlog · Planned · In progress · Testing · Launched · Won't do · Outcome · Feature · Improvement · Fix · Milestone · Ships in · Built by · Work tasks · Start building.
9. **Links:** T1 (Part of, projects, Timeline), D2 (launch documents), T4 (requests it answers), T3 (bugs linked as work), D3 (key results measured by its work), O2 (What's new groups by type).
10. **People:** members edit; viewers read; never public in this release.
11. **States:** skeleton columns; live moves; undo for moves and stage changes.
12. **Edges:** an item with no work, a launch moved to another quarter, work tasks in several sprints, an item dropped with open work, 300 items.
13. **Phone:** Now · Next · Later as three folding sections; Timeline as T1's list.
14. **Accessibility:** columns are labelled lists; "Move to Next" in every card menu.
15. **Notifications:** below.
16. **Trust and data:** members only; requests linked show the asker's name only to members.
17. **Reuse vs new:** below.
18. **How we know it works:** below.

#### 3. Step-by-step walkthroughs
**W1 · First look** — Asha adds **Roadmap**; the tab (Map icon) opens on **Now · Next · Later** with three empty columns, the hint "Put what you're building now in Now. Work tasks go on the Tasks board." and **New item**.

**W2 · Capturing an item** — **New item** opens the New module on **Roadmap item** (28.11: no sprint, no schedule, no subtasks): name, **Roadmap details** (outcome, column, type, priority, target date); footer "Shows in Roadmap · never on the Tasks board · its work tasks are". It lands in **Backlog** stage and the chosen column.

**W3 · Moving between columns** — dragging a card from Next to Now changes the column only; the stage moves to **Planned** if it was Backlog.

**W4 · Adding work** — in the item's panel, **Work** lists its work tasks; **+ New task** opens the module with Part of filled; **Add existing** picks tasks or bugs; **Link a project** adds T1 projects as **Built by** (their completion counts).

**W5 · Work starts** — when the first work task moves to In progress, the item moves to **In progress** by itself (activity: "started when NB-201 started"); progress = completed work tasks and linked projects' completion, combined by task count.

**W6 · Testing and launch** — Asha moves it to **Testing** by hand; it **Ships in** "v2.4 launch" (a D2 document). When the launch is marked Launched, the item becomes **Launched** and leaves Now; requests linked to it get "Shipped: SSO sign-in" (Summary).

**W7 · Won't do** — **Won't do** asks a reason; open work tasks stay as they are (a note lists them with **Move to Backlog**).

**W8 · Timeline** — T1's grid: items as bars from their first work start to their target date (or launch date), launches as Clay diamonds; items without dates sit in No dates.

**W9 · Backlog** — a table of Backlog items ordered by hand (drag handle), columns Item · Type · Priority · Requests · Created.

**W10 · Game milestones** — a Milestone-type item picks its name from Concept · Prototype · Vertical slice · Alpha · Beta · Release; milestones show as diamonds on the Timeline.

**W11 · Phone** — three folding sections; "Move to…" for columns and stages.

**W12 · CLI and agents** — `nb roadmap list [--now]`, `nb roadmap add "SSO sign-in" --type feature --column next`, `nb tasks edit NB-201 --part-of NB-150`; agents may add items and link work; moving an item to Launched or Won't do is tier "yes".

#### 4. Screen spec
- **S1 · Title row:** Map + "Roadmap"; counts "4 now · 6 next · next launch in 23 days"; views **Now · Next · Later · By stage · Timeline · Backlog** (Now/Next/Later is one view); chips **Type ▾ · Assigned to ▾ · Stage ▾ · + Filter** (Ships in, Priority); **New item**; ⋯ (Export CSV).
- **S2 · Column board:** three columns with counts; cards: icon, name, outcome (one line, muted), type badge, stage badge, progress bar with %, assignee avatar, "Ships in v2.4".
- **S3 · Stage board:** Backlog · Planned · In progress · Testing · Launched (Won't do via a filter).
- **S4 · Timeline:** T1 S3 with diamonds.
- **S5 · Backlog table:** S9 of 11.5 trimmed as W9.
- **S6 · Item panel:** F3 panel; header (Map, NB-n, name, Stage ▾, column chip); Details: outcome, Roadmap details (type, priority, target date, ships in, built by, requests), progress; **Work** tab (as T1's); Comments · Files.
- **S7 · Overview card:** "Now: 4 · 1 in testing · next launch v2.4 in 23 days".

#### 5. Data
- **No migration.** Type `roadmap_item` with stages Backlog (todo) · Planned (todo) · In progress (in_progress) · Testing (in_progress) · Launched (done) · Won't do (done), never on the board.
- `type_fields`: `outcome` (≤ 200), `column` ('now' | 'next' | 'later'), `itemType` ('feature' | 'improvement' | 'fix' | 'milestone'), `milestone` (name), `builtBy` (project ids), `requestIds` (T4 request ids), `launchDocId` (D2), `backlogPosition`, `wontDoReason`.
- **T1's Part of rules** gain `roadmap_item` as a parent (work tasks, bugs, requests, content can be Part of it).

#### 6. Server
- `createTaskAction` (F3) with `itemType: 'roadmap_item'`.
- `moveRoadmapColumnAction({ taskId, column, beforeId? })`; `setRoadmapStageAction` (F1's stage action) with Won't do requiring a reason.
- **Automatic stage moves:** inside `afterTaskTransition`, when a work task first enters in_progress and its parent item is Backlog or Planned → In progress; D2's launch action sets Launched.
- `linkWorkAction({ itemId, taskIds[] | projectIds[] })`, `linkRequestsAction`.
- `readRoadmapAction(projectId, view, filters)` with progress computed in SQL.

#### 7. Rules (`src/lib/workflows/roadmap.ts`) and tests
- `itemProgress(workTasks, projects)` → percent. Tests: 2 of 4 tasks + one project at 50 % (counted as its task count) → combined; nothing → null (no %).
- `autoStage(item, event)` → new stage or none. Tests: Planned + first work started → In progress; Testing + work started → none; Launched never moves back automatically.
- `columnAfterLaunch(item)` → the column is cleared when an item is Launched or Won't do. Tests: Launched items leave the column board; reopening (stage back to Testing) restores the last column.
- `milestoneOrder(name)` → index for sorting. Tests: Alpha before Beta.

#### 8. Everything around it
- **Notifications:** assigned an item (Normal); item Launched → people who asked linked requests (Summary) and the assignee (Normal); Won't do → assignee (Normal).
- **My Work:** items assigned to you in Now.
- **CLI / MCP:** W12; `networkbase_roadmap_list` (read); creation through `networkbase_task_create` with `type: "roadmap_item"`.
- **Search:** items show column and stage.
- **Public:** none (the public roadmap is parked).

#### 9. Rollout
Ships after T1 (Part of, Timeline). Without D2, Ships in is hidden and Launched is set by hand.

#### 10. Tests
Unit (part 7); server (auto stage, Won't do reason, Part of to roadmap items); contract test `roadmap-design-contract.test.ts`; end to end (add → item → work → auto In progress → Testing → launch (D2) → Launched → linked request notified).

#### 11. Calls

2. Types are Feature · Improvement · Fix · Milestone; Milestone names come from 22.4. **[call]**
3. An item moves to **In progress** by itself when its first work task starts; Testing is by hand; Launched comes from its launch (D2) or by hand. **[call]**
4. Projects link as **Built by**; they stay un-nested (T1 call 4). **[call]**
5. Requests can be linked; their askers hear when the item ships. **[call]**
6. No public roadmap in this release. **[call]**

A roadmap item is **Part of nothing** and takes work as Part of it (tasks, bugs, requests, content); **projects link as Built by** (this workspace's projects only), a project counting as its own task count in progress (an empty one as one). **In progress by itself** happens when a work task's status moves to In progress (not when an already started task is linked); it is recorded as the person who started the work, with their own checks. **Won't do** asks a reason and keeps the column, so reopening restores it; open work stays as it is and the dialog says how much. **My work** lists roadmap items only while they're in Now. **Launched** (by hand until launches, A3.1) tells the assignee and, as "Shipped: …" (Summary), the people who asked requests that are Part of it; Won't do tells the assignee. Ships in, the next launch on the Overview card and launch-driven Launched wait for A3.1. **[call]**

Roadmap is **built**. **[call]**

### 38.10 D2 · Launch checklists (agreed 2026-11-18)

A **launch** is a **document in the Launches section** (F2) with a date, a stage and a checklist whose rows are **real tasks** (F2's task rows, one block per checklist stage). It ships roadmap items (T2), and its **Launch** button marks them Launched and offers a release Update.

#### 1. What it is and the references
| Reference | Rating / source | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **Product launch checklist** (Notion) | 4.9 / 32 (11.5) | One page with numbered stages, each a short checklist |
| **Develop & launch an app** | 5.0 / 35 (20.4) | App release stages |
| **Steam Launch Checklist** | 22.4 | Store launch stages grouped by when |
| **Digital Product Launch Checklist** | 25.5 | Make · Listing · Launch · After |
| 11.5's launch half | Agreed | Planning → Getting ready → Launched → Closed (Cancelled); the Launch dialog; a What's new draft; "Close launch" after 14 days |
| What the code has | Checked 2026-11-18 | F2 sections, task-rows blocks and doc settings; Updates with type **release** |

#### 2. The 18 layers
1. **Getting it:** **Launch checklists** in "Blends into Documents": "Adds a Launches section to Documents. Every checklist step is a task." Added automatically with Roadmap (T2) [call].
2. **Setting it up:** presets **Product launch · Feature release · App release · Store launch · Digital product launch · Content launch · Blank**.
3. **Items:** a **launch document** (section Launches, kind = preset, date = launch date, stage in settings), its **steps** (tasks from task-rows blocks, one per stage), the **roadmap items it ships** (T2's `launchDocId`), a **What's new** section (Added · Improved · Fixed).
4. **Views:** the Launches section of the rail (by date, next first); inside the document: countdown, progress, stage blocks; T2's Timeline shows launches as diamonds.
5. **Actions and flow:** New launch → preset → date → steps assigned and dated → Getting ready (first step started) → **Launch** → Launched → After-launch steps → **Close launch**.
6. **Surfaces:** the launch header (date, countdown, stage, progress, Launch button), stage blocks, the Ships block, What's new, the Launch dialog, the Close dialog.
7. **Design spec:** F2's block frame; countdown in mono; Rocket icon; contract test.
8. **Words:** Launch · Launches · Planning · Getting ready · Launched · Closed · Cancelled · Launch date · Steps · Ships · What's new · Added · Improved · Fixed · Launch now · Close launch · Post an Update.
9. **Links:** T2 (items ship), T3 (bugs Fixed in this launch fill Fixed), O2 (the release Update and Changelog), Tasks (steps on the board), My Work.
10. **People:** document editors manage the launch; steps follow task permissions (B9); the Launch button is the launch's editors.
11. **States:** countdown, overdue steps, live ticks.
12. **Edges:** moving the date, cancelling, a step's task deleted, launching with open steps, two launches the same day.
13. **Phone:** the document reads top to bottom; Launch is a full-width button.
14. **Accessibility:** stage blocks are labelled lists; progress as text.
15. **Notifications:** below.
16. **Trust and data:** a launch document follows document visibility; the Ships block hides items for public readers.
17. **Reuse vs new:** below.
18. **How we know it works:** below.

#### 3. Step-by-step walkthroughs
**W1 · New launch** — in Documents → Launches **+**, or in T2 an item's **Plan a launch**: a sheet asks name ("v2.4: Faster sign-in"), date and preset; **Create** makes the document from the preset (one heading and one task-rows block per stage, e.g. Product launch: Market research · Goal identification · Marketing plan · Sales and support training · Testing and beta testing · Launch day · After launch), with the preset's steps as **unassigned tasks with no dates** in each block.

**W2 · Getting ready** — steps get people and due dates in place (F2 rows); when the first step starts, the launch moves to **Getting ready**; the header shows "Launch in 23 days · 14 of 31 steps".

**W3 · What ships** — the **Ships** block lists roadmap items with `launchDocId` = this launch; **Add item** picks from T2; items shipping also show "Ships in v2.4".

**W4 · What's new** — the **What's new** section fills itself as a draft: **Added** (Feature items), **Improved** (Improvement items), **Fixed** (bugs whose Fixed in matches the launch's version label, T3); editable text.

**W5 · Launch day** — **Launch now** (editors) opens: "3 steps are still open" (list) · **Mark roadmap items Launched** (on) · **Post an Update** (opens a release Update prefilled with What's new; never posted on its own) → **Launch**. The stage becomes **Launched**; T2 items become Launched.

**W6 · After launch and close** — After-launch steps stay open; 14 days after the date the header suggests **Close launch**: remaining steps → **Leave them · Move to the Backlog · Cancel them** → **Closed**.

**W7 · Moving the date** — changing the date asks "Also move the 31 steps' due dates by 5 days?" (Move them · Leave them).

**W8 · Cancel** — **Cancel launch**: items go back to Planned; steps are offered for cancelling.

**W9 · Phone and public** — on a phone the header and blocks stack; a public reader of a public launch sees the countdown and What's new, not steps or people.

**W10 · CLI** — `nb launches list`, `nb launches new "v2.4" --date 2026-12-12 --preset feature`, `nb launches launch v2.4` (asks to confirm); agents may tick steps; launching is tier "yes".

#### 4. Screen spec
- **S1 · Launch header:** Rocket · title · date (mono) · countdown ("in 23 days" / "Launched Dec 12") · stage badge · progress "14 of 31 steps" with a bar · **Launch now** / **Close launch**.
- **S2 · Stage blocks:** F2 task-rows blocks with the stage name as label; "+ Add step".
- **S3 · Ships block:** rows of T2 items (icon, name, type, stage); **Add item**.
- **S4 · What's new:** three groups as editable lists; "Refresh from items and bugs" button.
- **S5 · Launch dialog** and **S6 · Close dialog** as W5 and W6.
- **S7 · New launch sheet** (name, date, preset with a preview of its stages).

#### 5. Data
- **No migration.** Launch documents use F2's settings: `section: 'launches'`, `kind` (preset id), `date`, plus `launchStage` ('planning' | 'getting_ready' | 'launched' | 'closed' | 'cancelled'), `versionLabel` (e.g. "v2.4", used to match T3's Fixed in), `launchedAt`.
- Steps are tasks with `source_doc_id` and the stage's block key (F2).
- Presets are Markdown files in code (`templates/launches/*.md`) with headings and block lines plus a JSON list of default steps per stage.

#### 6. Server
- `createLaunchAction({ projectId, name, date, preset, versionLabel? })`: makes the document and its steps in one transaction.
- `launchAction({ docId, markItems, postUpdate })`: editors; sets Launched; T2 items → Launched; returns a release Update prefill (never posts).
- `closeLaunchAction({ docId, remaining: 'leave' | 'backlog' | 'cancel' })`; `moveLaunchDateAction({ docId, date, shiftSteps })`; `cancelLaunchAction`.
- Stage **Getting ready** is set when the first step leaves To do (`afterTaskTransition`).

#### 7. Rules (`src/lib/workflows/launches.ts`) and tests
- `launchProgress(steps)` → done / total (cancelled not counted). Tests: 14 of 31; all cancelled → 0 of 0 shows "No steps".
- `whatsNew(items, bugs, versionLabel)` → groups. Tests: Feature → Added; Improvement → Improved; bugs matching v2.4 → Fixed; other versions excluded.
- `shiftDates(steps, days)` → new dues (undated steps untouched).
- `closeSuggested(launchedAt, now)` → after 14 days.

#### 8. Everything around it
- **Notifications:** steps assigned (Normal); launch in 3 days with open steps → editors (Normal); Launched → people with steps and T2 assignees (Summary).
- **Overview card:** T2's card shows the next launch; Documents has none.
- **CLI / MCP:** W10; `networkbase_launch_list` (read).
- **O2:** the release Update's three groups feed the Changelog.

#### 9. Rollout
Ships with or right after T2; presets are code, so new presets need no migration.

#### 10. Tests
Unit (part 7); server (launch marks items, never posts an Update, close options); contract test `launch-design-contract.test.ts`; end to end (new launch → assign steps → Getting ready → ships 2 items → Launch → release Update prefill → Close with Backlog).

#### 11. Calls

2. Launch checklists come with Roadmap automatically and can also be added on their own. **[call]**
3. Seven presets; steps start unassigned and undated. **[call]**
4. **Launch now** marks items Launched and offers a release Update, never posting it by itself. **[call]**
5. Bugs fill **Fixed** by matching their Fixed in text to the launch's version label. **[call]**
