### 38.11 D1 · Meetings and decisions (agreed 2026-11-18)

Meetings and decisions become **documents** in the **Meetings** and **Decisions** sections (F2): a meeting is a dated document from a **meeting type**, with attendees, an agenda, live **action items** (task rows) and **decisions** (D-numbers). Meetings can repeat as a **series**; the next one carries over open action items. 1:1s stay parked (documents can't be private to two people).

#### 1. What it is and the references
| Reference | Rating / source | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **Meetings** (Notion) | 4.8 / 200+ (11.6) | One list of meetings by type; attendees, date, type; action items inside |
| Retrospective · Standup (Notion) | 11.6 | The retro's four parts; one block per person for standups |
| Decision log · ADR (13.6) | 11.6, 13.6 | Decisions with status Proposed → Decided, later Superseded or Reversed; ADR's Context · Decision · Consequences |
| Board meeting (17.5) | Agreed | Motions, quorum, approve last minutes |
| 18.3 · 19.4 · 20.6 · 21.2 · 22.3 | Agreed | Recording session, Shoot day (call sheet), User interview, Incident review (blameless), Playtest |
| What the code has | Checked 2026-11-18 | F2 sections, task rows, decisions block and D-numbers; the hourly due job with exact-time wake events (task reminders only) |

#### 2. The 18 layers
1. **Getting it:** **Meetings & decisions** in "Blends into Documents": "Adds Meetings and Decisions sections with meeting types."
2. **Setting it up:** which **meeting types** show (defaults by the workspace category, section 6); default length 30 minutes; reminder 15 minutes before (on).
3. **Items:** **meeting document** (section Meetings; kind = type; date and time; attendees; series), **action items** (F2 task rows), **decision document** (section Decisions; D-number; status; from a meeting), **motion** (a decision with votes, Board meeting).
4. **Views:** the Meetings section (newest first, upcoming on top), a **Meetings calendar** (T1's Calendar part, meetings only), the Decisions section (D-number order, status chips), **Open action items** (rows from all meetings, not completed).
5. **Actions and flow:** New meeting → type → date, time, attendees → agenda before → notes during → action items and decisions → **Finish meeting** (next in the series made, open items carried).
6. **Surfaces:** meeting header, type bodies, the decisions block, the motion card, the Finish dialog, the series menu, the Open action items view, the Meetings calendar, the Decision document header.
7. **Design spec:** F2's blocks; meeting time in mono with the time zone; icons CalendarClock (meeting), Scale (decision), Gavel (motion); contract test.
8. **Words:** Meeting · Meeting type · Attendees · Agenda · Notes · Action items · Decisions · Record a decision · Proposed · Decided · Superseded · Reversed · Series · Every week · Finish meeting · Carried over · Motion · Quorum · Approve last minutes.
9. **Links:** Tasks (action items), F2 (blocks), T3 (incident review from a bug), D4 (insights become ideas), D3 (planning meetings link goals), My Work, the calendar (.ics), search.
10. **People:** document permissions; attendees are members; ticking follows the task (B9).
11. **States:** upcoming, now (during the meeting time), finished, approved (Board).
12. **Edges:** moving one meeting of a series, ending a series, an attendee who leaves, finishing twice, a decision superseded by a later one.
13. **Phone:** the Meetings list by date; the document reads top to bottom; action items add with the bottom sheet (F2).
14. **Accessibility:** times in full with the time zone; motions' counts as text.
15. **Notifications:** below.
16. **Trust and data:** meetings follow document visibility; no private 1:1s; Board minutes can be leaders-only.
17. **Reuse vs new:** below.
18. **How we know it works:** below.

#### 3. Step-by-step walkthroughs
**W1 · New meeting** — Documents → Meetings **+** (or **New meeting** in the Meetings calendar): a sheet with **Type** (cards: Weekly · Standup · Planning · Retrospective · Kickoff · Client · and the types switched on), **Title** (default "Weekly · Dec 3"), **Date and time**, **Length**, **Attendees** (members picker), **Repeat** (Doesn't repeat · Every week · Every 2 weeks · Every weekday · Monthly). **Create** makes the document from the type's body.

**W2 · Type bodies** (Markdown with F2 blocks):
- **Weekly / Team:** Agenda · Notes · Decisions block · Action items block.
- **Standup:** one heading per attendee with Yesterday · Today · Blockers (filled before or during).
- **Planning:** Goal · What's in · What's out · Action items (can link a sprint).
- **Retrospective:** What went well · What needs improvement · Ideas · Action items.
- **Kickoff:** Why · Scope · People · Dates · Risks · Action items.
- **Client:** Agenda · Notes · Next steps (action items).
- **Board meeting:** Agenda · Reports · Motions · Decisions · Minutes (W6).
- **Recording session:** Tech checklist · Prep questions · Timings.
- **Shoot day:** Call time · Location · Crew and cast · Equipment · Shots to get · Weather and notes (prints as a call sheet).
- **User interview:** Participant · Consent to record (checkbox, required before recording) · Research goal · Questions · Notes · Insights (each insight has **Save as idea**, D4).
- **Incident review:** linked bug (T3) · Timeline · Root cause · Actions · Lessons (blameless wording in the guidance).
- **Playtest:** Build · Tester · Minutes played · What I saw · Fun moments · Confusion · Bugs (each with **Report as bug**, T3) · Ideas.
- **Blank:** Notes.

**W3 · Before and during** — attendees get a reminder 15 minutes before ("Weekly starts at 10:00 · Open notes"); during the meeting time the document shows **Now** and **Finish meeting**.

**W4 · Action items and decisions** — F2's rows and **Record a decision** (D-numbers); a decision document's header: D-014 · status (Proposed · Decided) · From: Weekly · Dec 3 · date; body Context · Decision · Consequences (the ADR shape for every decision).

**W5 · Finish meeting** — **Finish meeting** asks: "3 action items are open: carry them to the next meeting?" (on) and, for a series, makes the **next meeting** (date by the repeat rule, same attendees, a fresh body) whose Action items block shows **Carried over** rows (the same tasks, now listed in both). The finished meeting is marked Finished.

**W6 · Board meeting** — **Motions**: **+ Motion** (text, proposed by, seconded by) → **Record vote** (For · Against · Abstain counts) → Passed or Failed (passed creates a Decided decision, D-number); **Quorum** line from the series' board size and the attendees marked present; at the next board meeting **Approve last minutes** locks the previous one's published version (edits refused, "Approved Dec 10").

**W7 · Superseding a decision** — on D-009, **Supersede** opens Record a decision; the new D-015 links back; D-009 shows "Superseded by D-015". **Reverse** asks a reason.

**W8 · Series** — the meeting menu: **Edit this meeting** · **Edit the series** (time, attendees, type for future meetings) · **End the series** (no more meetings made).

**W9 · Open action items** — Documents → **Open action items** lists every open row across meetings: title, assignee, due, from which meeting; ticks work here too.

**W10 · Calendar and .ics** — the Meetings calendar shows meetings on their days; each person can copy a private **.ics link** for meetings they attend (read-only feed).

**W11 · Phone and public** — phone: list by date, meeting document full screen; public: only meetings set public show, without attendees' names (F2's public rule for rows).

**W12 · CLI and agents** — `nb meetings list [--week]`, `nb meetings new --type weekly --at "2026-12-03 10:00" --repeat weekly`, `nb decisions list`; agents can draft agendas and notes and add action items; recording decisions and votes are a person's (tier "yes").

#### 4. Screen spec
- **S1 · New meeting sheet** (W1 fields; type cards with icon and one line).
- **S2 · Meeting header:** CalendarClock · title · date, time and length (mono) with time zone · type chip · attendees avatars (+n) · series chip ("Every week") · **Now** chip during · **Finish meeting** / Finished.
- **S3 · Motion card:** text, proposed and seconded by, counts, result badge, **Record vote**.
- **S4 · Finish dialog** (carry over toggle, next date shown).
- **S5 · Decision header:** D-number, status select, From, date, Superseded by / Supersedes links.
- **S6 · Open action items:** a table (title, assigned to, due, meeting) with ticks.
- **S7 · Meetings calendar:** T1's Calendar with meeting chips (time + type icon).
- **S8 · Settings → Meetings:** meeting types on/off, default length, reminder minutes (0, 5, 15, 30).

#### 5. Data
**Migration `0107_meetings.sql`:**
- **`workspace_meeting_series`:** id, workspace_id, type, title, rule ('weekly' | 'biweekly' | 'weekdays' | 'monthly'), time ('HH:MM'), length minutes, attendee ids, board_size (int, Board), ended_at, created_by.
- **`workspace_document_reminders`:** id, doc_id, user_id, remind_at, sent_at (fired by the existing hourly due job beside task reminders, with its exact-time wake events).
- **Meeting document settings (F2 JSON):** `section: 'meetings'`, `kind` (type), `date`, `startsAt`, `lengthMinutes`, `attendeeIds`, `seriesId`, `finishedAt`, `present` (ids, Board), `approvedAt`.
- **Decision document settings:** F2's `decisionNumber`, `decisionStatus`, `fromDocId`, plus `supersedes` / `supersededBy` (doc ids), `reverseReason`; **motion** fields: `motion` ({ text, proposedBy, secondedBy, for, against, abstain, result }).
- **Carried over** rows: the task's `source_doc_id` stays the first meeting; the next meeting's block lists open rows from the previous meeting in the series by a block parameter `carry="previous"`.
- **.ics feed:** a per-person token (the existing token pattern for feeds; read-only, revocable).

#### 6. Server
- `createMeetingAction({ projectId, type, title, startsAt, lengthMinutes, attendeeIds, repeat? })`: makes the document (and the series), schedules reminders.
- `finishMeetingAction({ docId, carryOver })`: sets finished; makes the next series meeting.
- `editSeriesAction`, `endSeriesAction`, `moveMeetingAction` (one meeting).
- `addMotionAction`, `recordVoteAction` (document editors; a passed motion records a decision through F2's `recordDecisionAction`), `markPresentAction`, `approveMinutesAction` (locks the previous meeting's published version; later edits refused).
- `supersedeDecisionAction`, `reverseDecisionAction`.
- `readMeetingsAction(projectId, range)`, `readOpenActionItemsAction(projectId)`.
- `icsFeedRoute` (`/api/v1/feeds/meetings/[token].ics`): attendee's meetings, no notes.

#### 7. Rules (`src/lib/workflows/meetings.ts`) and tests
- `nextOccurrence(rule, from, tz)`. Tests: weekly; weekdays skip Sat and Sun; monthly on the 31st → last day; daylight saving keeps local 10:00.
- `isNow(startsAt, length, now)`.
- `quorum(present, boardSize, rule = 'majority')` → met or not. Tests: 4 of 7 met; 3 of 7 not.
- `motionResult(for, against)` → passed on a simple majority of votes cast; ties fail.
- `carryRows(prevRows)` → open rows only.
- `decisionChain(decisions)` → current decision for a topic. Tests: D-9 superseded by D-15 → D-15; reversed shows none current.

#### 8. Everything around it
- **Notifications:** invited to a meeting or series (Normal); reminder before (Normal, at the time); action item assigned (F2); decision recorded from a meeting you attended (Summary); minutes approved (Summary).
- **Overview card:** "Next: Weekly · Thu 10:00 · 4 open action items".
- **My Work:** today's meetings you attend; your action items.
- **CLI / MCP:** W12; `networkbase_meeting_list`, `networkbase_decision_list` (read).
- **Search:** meetings by type and date; decisions by D-number.

#### 9. Rollout
Migration 0107; ships after F2; meeting types come from code (`templates/meetings/*.md`).

#### 10. Tests
Unit (part 7); server (carry-over doesn't duplicate tasks; approved minutes refuse edits; vote counts can't exceed attendees present for Board); contract test `meetings-design-contract.test.ts`; end to end (weekly series → items → finish → next meeting with carried rows; board meeting motion → decision → approve minutes).

#### 11. Calls
1. Meetings and decisions are documents; 1:1s stay parked. **[call]**
2. Every decision uses the ADR shape (Context · Decision · Consequences); there's no separate ADR type. **[call]**
3. Series make the next meeting on **Finish**, carrying open action items (the same tasks, not copies). **[call]**
4. Meeting reminders use a small document-reminders table on the existing hourly job. **[call]**
5. Meeting types shown by default follow the workspace category; admins switch types on and off. **[call]**
6. Board meetings: simple-majority motions, majority quorum, approved minutes lock. **[call]**
7. A personal read-only **.ics** feed of your meetings; no calendar sync. **[call]**
8. Lessons stay as text in retrospectives; there's no lessons log in this release. **[call]**
9. **A4.1 (2026-11-23):** A4.1 ships in two parts. **A4.1a:** Meetings' **+** opens **New meeting** (type, title defaulting to "Meeting · Jan 7", date and time in the workspace's zone, length, attendees from the workspace's members, repeat); the browser writes the document from the type and `createMeetingAction` files it (Meetings section, start, length, attendees, series), schedules a reminder 15 minutes before for each attendee (migration **0115**: `workspace_meeting_series`, `workspace_document_reminders` fired by the hourly due job, `meeting_feed_tokens` for the .ics link) and tells attendees ("Invited"). The **meeting header** shows the time in full with the zone, the type and series chips, **Now** during the meeting, attendees and open action items, **Finish meeting** and **Edit this meeting** / **End the series**. **Finish** in a live series makes the next meeting (next date by the rule at the same local time, same attendees, a fresh body) and lists the open action items there as **Carried over** (the same tasks: the next meeting keeps their ids, the rows keep their first meeting); finishing twice changes nothing. **Open action items** is a Documents view (rail → Meetings → Open action items). Titles are stored with the meeting (`meetingTitle`). **A4.1b (2026-11-23):** the **Meetings calendar** is a Documents view beside Open action items (rail → Meetings → Calendar; month grid in the workspace's zone, a list by date on phones). **Your calendar link** (call 7) is made from there: a random token whose SHA-256 is all that's kept, shown once and copied; **New link** stops the old one, **Stop the link** ends it. The feed (`/api/feeds/meetings/<token>`, outside `/api/v1` because calendar apps can't sign in) holds the meetings you attend in workspaces you still belong to, as times, titles and a link (no notes, attendees or action items); leaders-only meetings only for owners and admins. The **Overview card** reads "Next: WT Weekly · Mon 20:50 · 1 open action item"; **My work** shows today's meetings you attend above Next up. **CLI/MCP:** `nb meetings list [--week | --past]`, `nb decisions list`, `networkbase_meeting_list`, `networkbase_decision_list`; `nb meetings new` waits for documents from a template in the CLI (A6.35). Migration renamed **0115_meeting_series_reminders** (governance wants two words; the production ledger row was renamed with it). Meetings and decisions stays unbuilt until the A4 wave ends; types beyond Blank come in A4.3–A4.15. **[call]**
10. **A4.2 (2026-11-23):** every decision is written in the ADR shape (`# title` · Context · Decision · Consequences) when recorded. The **decision header** (S5): Scale icon · D-number · a **Proposed / Decided** select for people who can edit while the decision stands (a badge for everyone else, and always once Superseded or Reversed: those are final) · date · From · **Supersedes D-n** / **Superseded by D-n** (plus "stands now: D-n" from `decisionChain` when the chain is longer) · **Supersede** and **Reverse**. **Supersede** opens Record a decision titled "Supersede D-n"; the new decision stores `supersedes`, the old one becomes Superseded with `supersededBy`, and only a decision that still stands can be superseded (a second Supersede of the same one is refused, checked in the same update). **Reverse** needs a reason (1–500), kept as `reverseReason` and shown as "Reversed: …"; the D-number never changes. A decision recorded from a meeting tells the meeting's attendees, except whoever recorded it, at Summary ("D-004 recorded in Weekly · Jan 7"). `nb decisions list` shows "superseded by D-n"; the API adds `supersededBy` and `reverseReason`. A4.1 W11: on phones the Meetings row also offers **Calendar** and **Open action items**. **[call]**
11. **A4.3–A4.8, A4.10, A4.11, A4.13, A4.14 (2026-11-23):** the meeting types are data in `MEETING_TYPES` (headings in order, an optional one-line guide under a heading, Decisions on or off, the Action items block's own label), shown in New meeting as **cards** with an icon and one line (S1), Weekly first and Blank last; all types show until Settings → Meetings (A4.16, call 5). Bodies as W2: **Weekly** Agenda · Notes · Decisions · Action items; **Standup** one heading per attendee picked ("Everyone" when none) with Yesterday · Today · Blockers, and Finish writes the next one for the same attendees; **Planning** Goal · What's in · What's out · Action items; **Retrospective** What went well · What needs improvement · Ideas · Action items; **Kickoff** Why · Scope · People · Dates · Risks · Action items; **Client** Agenda · Notes · **Next steps** (the action items block, so Finish carries it); **Recording session** Tech checklist · Prep questions · Timings; **Shoot day** Call time · Location · Crew and cast · Equipment · Shots to get · Weather and notes; **User interview** Participant · Consent to record (a checkbox line: "They agreed to be recorded") · Research goal · Questions · Notes · Insights; **Incident review** Linked bug · Timeline (blameless guide) · Root cause · Lessons · **Actions** (action items); **Playtest** Build · Tester · Minutes played · What I saw · Fun moments · Confusion · Bugs · Ideas. Not yet: Planning's sprint link, Playtest's **Report as bug** per bug and Incident review's bug picker (people write NB-n, which links), User interview's **Save as idea** (A5.3) and Shoot day's call-sheet print layout (A6.28's Call sheet). Board meeting is its own unit (A4.9: motions, votes, quorum, approve minutes). **[call]**
12. **A4.9 (2026-11-23):** **Board meeting** is a type (Agenda · Reports · Motions · Minutes · Decisions) with a **Board size** asked in New meeting and kept by the series. Under the meeting header a **board panel** shows the **quorum** line ("Quorum: 2 present of 3 · 2 needed · Quorate", in words), **present** ticks (attendees only), the **motions** (Gavel · text · Proposed by · seconded by · For / Against / Abstain in mono · Passed or Failed · the D-number it made), **+ Motion** (text, proposed and seconded by from the attendees; nobody seconds their own) and **Record vote**. Quorum is a majority of the board size (anyone present when no size is set); a motion passes with more For than Against (a tie fails); the votes can't add up to more than those present, and nothing is recorded without quorum (refused, with the counts); a motion votes once. A passed motion records a Decided decision from the meeting (ADR body with the counts); if that step fails, **Record the decision** stays on the motion. At the next board meeting of the series **Approve last minutes (title)** approves the previous one: its motions and present list stop changing, and every file write (the app, the editor extension, the CLI, GitHub sync, restoring or deleting a version) refuses its file: "These minutes were approved on 7 Jan and can't be edited." Blank is always on. A switched-off type is refused on the server too; meetings already made keep their type. Reminders are scheduled with the minutes set when the meeting is made or moved. A4.15 (Blank) needed nothing beyond A4.1. **[call]**

### 38.12 D3 · Quarterly goals (agreed 2026-11-18)

Goals live in **one document per period** in the **Goals** section (F2), with a live **goals block**: objectives and their key results, each key result **checked in** with a value and a confidence, and a **pace** that says On track, At risk or Off track. Objectives and key results are tasks that never go on the board (28.1). The Goals tab of 11.4 stays parked.

#### 1. What it is and the references
| Reference | Rating / source | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **Sentele OKR Tracker** | 4.9 / 80 (11.4) | Objectives with key results, progress bars, check-ins with confidence |
| **OKRs** (Notion) | 4.7 / 13 | Team + period as the frame; guidance on writing good OKRs |
| 11.4's design | Agreed | Period (Quarter by default), check-in day, pace bands, statuses, Measured by, Close period, carry forward, Contributes to |
| K3 (33.4) | Agreed | The organization's D3 document and Contributes to |
| What the code has | Checked 2026-11-18 | F2 (`{% project.goals period="…" %}` registered), F1 types `objective` and `key_result`, comments, the hourly due job |

#### 2. The 18 layers
1. **Getting it:** **Quarterly goals** in "Blends into Documents": "Adds a Goals section with one goals document per quarter."
2. **Setting it up:** period length (**Quarter** by default; Month, Half year, Year), the first month (January), the check-in day (Monday), pace bands (−10 / −25 points).
3. **Items:** **goals document** (section Goals, `period`), **objective** (type `objective`: name, assigned to, description, contributes to), **key result** (type `key_result`, Part of an objective: direction, unit, start, target, current, measured by, confidence, assigned to), **check-in** (value, confidence 1–10, note, date).
4. **Views:** the goals document (objectives with KRs and progress), the **Goals** rail section (one document per period, current first), a **Mine** filter in the block.
5. **Actions and flow:** set (2–4 KRs per objective) → weekly check-ins → pace → **Close period** (final values, Done or Missed, carry forward).
6. **Surfaces:** the goals block, objective row, key result row with Check in, the check-in sheet, the history sparkline, the Close period dialog, Overview card.
7. **Design spec:** 11.4 § 7 (progress bars with % in mono; statuses always with words; Target icon); contract test.
8. **Words:** Goals · Objective · Key result · Check in · Confidence · On track · At risk · Off track · Done · Missed · Measured by · Start · Target · Current · Lower is better · Close period · Carry forward · Contributes to · set by hand.
9. **Links:** T1 (a project's completion), T2 (a roadmap item's work), T3 (open bugs count), Tasks (tasks done with a label), K3 (Contributes to an organization goal), My Work (check-ins due), D1 (planning meetings link the document).
10. **People:** members check in on their KRs; document editors set objectives; never public (28.5).
11. **States:** live progress, missing check-in this week, closed period (read-only).
12. **Edges:** a KR measured by a deleted project, target equal to start, lower is better, mid-period target change, an objective with no KRs, reopening a closed period.
13. **Phone:** objectives as folding sections; Check in as a bottom sheet.
14. **Accessibility:** progress and status as text; the sparkline has a table alternative.
15. **Notifications:** below.
16. **Trust and data:** goals documents are members-only at most (never public).
17. **Reuse vs new:** below.
18. **How we know it works:** below.

#### 3. Step-by-step walkthroughs
**W1 · First goals document** — after adding, the Goals section shows **Set Q1 2027 goals**; it makes "Goals · Q1 2027" with a guidance paragraph (from Notion's OKRs: an objective is a direction, key results are numbers that prove it) and the goals block for Q1 2027.

**W2 · Adding an objective** — **+ Objective** in the block: a one-line add (name, Enter); **More details** opens the module on **Objective** (no sprint, no schedule).

**W3 · Adding key results** — under an objective, **+ Key result** opens the module on **Key result** with Part of filled: name, **direction** (Increase · Decrease), unit (%, people, ₹, custom), start, target, **measured by** (A number we check in · A project's completion · A roadmap item's work · Tasks done with a label · Open urgent bugs), assigned to. A soft note warns below 2 or above 5 KRs.

**W4 · Check in** — on the check-in day each KR's assignee gets "Check in on 3 key results". **Check in** (row button or My Work) asks the new value (or shows the linked value for measured ones), confidence (1–10), note; progress, status and the sparkline update.

**W5 · Pace and status** — status is worked out after every check-in and nightly from progress versus the expected straight line for the period: On track (≥ pace − 10), At risk (within 25 below), Off track (further). The assignee can **set by hand** with a reason until the next check-in.

**W6 · Close period** — after the period ends the document shows **Close period**: each KR's final value; KRs at or above target → **Done**, others **Missed**; **Carry forward** ticks copy chosen objectives and KRs into the next period's document (new tasks, start = final value); the closed document becomes read-only.

**W7 · Measured by** — a KR measured by a project shows "from Website relaunch · 60 %"; by open urgent bugs (lower is better) counts T3 bugs live; by label counts tasks completed with that label in the period.

**W8 · Organizations** — in an organization's goals document, **Contributes to** links an objective to a parent organization's objective (K3); the parent's block shows "2 team objectives contribute".

**W9 · Phone** — folding objectives; Check in sheet with a number keypad.

**W10 · CLI and agents** — `nb goals list [--mine]`, `nb goals checkin NB-301 --value 42 --confidence 7 --note "…"`; agents may draft objectives; check-ins are recorded only for the person who confirms (tier "yes").

#### 4. Screen spec
- **S1 · Goals block:** header "Q1 2027 · week 7 of 13" (mono); objective rows: icon, name, assigned to, progress bar and %, status badge; under each, KR rows: name, measured-by icon, current / target with unit, progress, confidence (mono), status, last check-in ("4 d ago"), **Check in**.
- **S2 · Check-in sheet:** value (or the linked value read-only), confidence slider 1–10 with words (Low · Medium · High), note; a sparkline of past check-ins.
- **S3 · Close period dialog:** a table of KRs with final value, Done / Missed, Carry forward ticks.
- **S4 · Overview card:** "Q1: 3 objectives · 2 on track · 1 at risk · 4 check-ins due".

#### 5. Data
**Migration `0108_goals.sql`:**
- **`key_result_check_ins`:** id, task_id (key result) → tasks (cascade), value numeric, confidence smallint (1–10), note text (≤ 1,000), created_by, created_at; index (task_id, created_at desc).
- **`workspaces.workflow_settings jsonb NULL`** (one column for the document workflows): `goals` { period: 'quarter' | 'month' | 'half' | 'year', firstMonth: 1–12, checkInDay: 1–7, bands: { atRisk: 10, offTrack: 25 } }; D4 adds `ideas`, D6 adds `docs`.
- **Objective `type_fields`:** `period` (e.g. '2027-Q1'), `contributesTo` (an organization objective id), `statusOverride` ({ status, reason, until }).
- **Key result `type_fields`:** `direction`, `unit`, `start`, `target`, `current`, `measuredBy` ({ kind: 'checkins' | 'project' | 'roadmap' | 'label' | 'bugs', ref }), `final` and `result` ('done' | 'missed') after close.
- **Goals document settings (F2):** `section: 'goals'`, `period`, `closedAt`.

#### 6. Server
- `createTaskAction` with `objective` / `key_result` (KRs require Part of an objective).
- `checkInAction({ taskId, value?, confidence, note })`: the KR's assignee or an editor; writes the check-in and `current`.
- `measuredValue(kr)` worked out on read for linked kinds.
- `setStatusOverrideAction`, `closePeriodAction({ docId, carry: taskIds[] })` (one transaction; makes the next document if missing).
- **Check-in reminders:** on the check-in day, the existing hourly job adds task reminders for KRs without a check-in that week (one per person, grouped).

#### 7. Rules (`src/lib/workflows/goals.ts`) and tests
- `krProgress({ start, target, current, direction })` → 0–100. Tests: increase 10→50 at 30 = 50 %; decrease 20→5 at 10 = 66 %; target = start → 100 when met, else 0; overshoot capped at 100.
- `expectedPace(periodStart, periodEnd, now)` → 0–100.
- `status(progress, pace, bands)`. Tests: pace 50, progress 45 → On track; 30 → At risk; 20 → Off track.
- `objectiveProgress(krs)` → average of KR progress.
- `periodOf(date, settings)` → '2027-Q1'. Tests: first month April → Apr–Jun is Q1.
- `closeResult(kr)` → done if progress ≥ 100 else missed.

#### 8. Everything around it
- **Notifications:** check-ins due (Normal, on the day); KR moved to At risk or Off track (Normal to the assignee); period closes in 7 days (Summary to editors); objective you contribute to updated (Summary, organizations).
- **My Work:** "Check in on 3 key results".
- **CLI / MCP:** W10; `networkbase_goal_list` (read), `networkbase_goal_checkin` (tier "yes").
- **Search:** objectives and KRs with status.
- **Public:** never.

#### 9. Rollout
Migration 0108; ships after F2; the K3 organization document uses the same block.

#### 10. Tests
Unit (part 7); server (KR without an objective refused; closed periods read-only; carry forward makes new tasks with start = final); contract test `goals-design-contract.test.ts`; end to end (document → objective → 3 KRs → check-ins → At risk → close → carry one forward).

#### 11. Calls
1. Goals are one document per period with a live block; the Goals tab stays parked. **[call]**
2. Check-ins are their own small table (value, confidence, note), not comments. **[call]**
3. Pace bands −10 / −25 points; status can be set by hand with a reason until the next check-in. **[call]**
4. Measured by: check-ins, a project, a roadmap item's work, tasks with a label, or open urgent bugs. Money and volunteer hours wait (parked tabs). **[call]**
5. Close period marks Done or Missed and carries chosen goals forward as new items. **[call]**
6. Goals are never public. **[call]**
7. **A5.1a (2026-11-23):** A5.1 ships in two parts. **A5.1a:** Goals' **+** opens **Set goals** (this period or the next three; one goals document per period, members only, never public); the document holds a short guide and the period's block (`{% project.goals period="2027-Q1" %}`). The **goals block** (S1): "Q1 2027 · week 7 of 13", **Mine**, objectives that fold (Target · name · owner · progress bar with % · status in words) with their key results (Gauge · name · current / target with unit, "lower is better" · progress · confidence n/10 · status · last check-in · **Check in**), **+ Key result** (name, Increase or Decrease, unit, start, target, assigned to; a soft note at 0 and at 5+) and a one-line **+ Objective**. **Check in** (S2) takes the value, a confidence 1–10 with words (Low · Medium · High) and a note, with past check-ins as a small line and a table for screen readers; the newest check-in is the current value (migration **0116** `key_result_check_ins`). Status is worked out on every read from progress against the straight-line pace (bands 10 / 25); **Status…** sets it by hand with a reason until the next check-in. The assignee or anyone who can edit the goals checks in; objectives and key results are tasks of types `objective` and `key_result` that never go on the board, and a key result is always Part of an objective. **A5.1b:** Measured by (project, roadmap item, label, open urgent bugs), check-in reminders on the hourly job, the Overview card, My work's check-ins, `nb goals`. Quarterly goals stays unbuilt until A5.2. **[call]**
8. **A5.1b (2026-11-24):** **Measured by** in + Key result (W7): a number we check in (default), a project's completion or a roadmap item's work (its work tasks done, canceled ones left out; picking one sets % 0→100), tasks done with a label in the period, or open urgent bugs (New, Confirmed, Fixing; Decrease). Linked values are worked out on every read and shown with "from Website relaunch"; Check in shows the linked value read-only and records confidence and a note; a deleted project leaves the last value. **Check-ins due** are key results without a check-in since the last check-in day (Monday by default) in the workspace's zone. The hourly job sends "Check in on 3 key results" (Normal) on the check-in day from 09:00 workspace time, once a day per person. The **Overview card** reads "Q1: 3 objectives · 2 on track · 1 at risk · 4 check-ins due"; **My work** shows "Check in on N key results" per workspace. **CLI/MCP:** `nb goals list [--mine]`, `nb goals checkin NB-301 --value 42 --confidence 7 --note "…"` (POST /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/goals, task:write), `networkbase_goal_list` (read) and `networkbase_goal_checkin` (needs a yes). The "KR moved to At risk / Off track" and "period closes in 7 days" notices come with A5.2. **[call]**
9. **A5.2 (2026-11-24):** **Close period** shows on the goals block once the period has ended (Set goals also offers last period, for goals set late). The dialog (S3) lists every key result's final value with Done (at or past target) or Missed, and **Carry forward** ticks per objective, on for objectives that missed. Closing marks key results Done or Missed with their final value, objectives Done when all their key results are, carries ticked objectives into the next period's document (made if missing) as new items starting from where they ended (same target, unit, owner, measured by), then makes the document read-only; closing twice changes nothing. Notices: a check-in that moves a key result to At risk or Off track tells its owner (Normal, unless they checked in themselves); "Q1 2027 goals close in 7 days" reaches the owner and admins (Summary, hourly job, once). Reopening a closed period is not built. Security review: objectives and key results are left out of every task read for anyone outside the workspace (the shared task read rule), so a public Tasks tab never shows goals. Quarterly goals is built. **[call]**

### 38.13 D4 · Ideas (agreed 2026-11-18)

Ideas live in an **Ideas document** (section Ideas, F2) with a **ranked table block**: each idea scores **Impact × Ease × Confidence**, moves Idea → Validating → Building → Launched (or Dropped), and **Start building** turns it into a project, a roadmap item or a task. Ideas are tasks that never go on the board and are never public.

#### 1. What it is and the references
| Reference | Rating / source | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| Ideas board (25.2) | Agreed | Stages, the ICE score, a validation checklist, Start building, Dropped with a reason |
| Ideapad / rank & prioritize | 25.2 | The Ranked view, highest first |
| What the code has | Checked 2026-11-18 | F2's `{% project.ranked type="idea" %}` (registered), F1 type `idea`, T1 projects, T2 roadmap items |

#### 2. The 18 layers (short form; layers 7, 13, 14 as F2)
1. **Getting it:** **Ideas** in "Blends into Documents": "Adds an Ideas section with a ranked list." 2. **Setting it up:** the validation checklist (default: Talk to 5 people · Landing page · First sign-up), editable. 3. **Items:** **Idea** (type `idea`): name, pitch (one line), impact, ease, confidence (1–5 each), score, stage, validation steps (subtasks), assumptions doc (optional), built as (link), dropped reason. 4. **Views:** the ranked block (sorted by score), filters by stage. 5. **Flow:** capture → score → Validating (steps) → **Start building** → Building → Launched (when what it became completes) / Dropped. 6. **Surfaces:** ranked rows with inline score pickers, the Start building sheet, the Drop sheet. 8. **Words:** Idea · Pitch · Impact · Ease · Confidence · Score · Validating · Building · Launched · Dropped · Start building · Validation. 9. **Links:** T1, T2, Tasks, D1 (Save as idea from interviews and retros), T4 (requests as ideas). 10. **People:** members add and score; never public. 11–12. **States and edges:** ties, unscored ideas (bottom, "Not scored"), the built item deleted, re-scoring. 15. **Notifications:** below. 16. **Trust:** members only, never public (28.5). 17–18. below.

#### 3. Step-by-step walkthroughs
**W1** — Documents → Ideas **+** makes "Ideas" (one document per workspace by default; more allowed) with the ranked block. **W2 · Capture** — **+ Idea** (one line, Enter) or **Save as idea** from a meeting insight (D1) or a request (T4); unscored ideas sit at the bottom. **W3 · Score** — three inline pickers (1–5) per row; the score (product, 1–125) and rank update at once. **W4 · Validate** — moving to **Validating** adds the validation steps as subtasks; the row shows "2 of 3". **W5 · Start building** — a sheet: **Make a project** (T1) · **Make a roadmap item** (T2) · **Make a task**; the new item links back ("From idea"), the idea moves to **Building** with "Built as NB-320". **W6 · Launched** — when what it became is Completed (task, project) or Launched (roadmap item), the idea becomes **Launched** by itself. **W7 · Drop** — **Drop** asks a reason; dropped ideas fold under "Dropped (n)". **W8 · Phone** — rows stack with the score; pickers open as a sheet. **W9 · CLI** — `nb ideas list`, `nb ideas add "Template shop" --impact 4 --ease 3 --confidence 2`; agents may add and draft pitches; Start building is tier "yes".

#### 4. Screen spec
- **S1 · Ranked block:** columns Rank · Idea (name + pitch) · Impact · Ease · Confidence · Score (mono) · Stage · Validation (n of m) · ⋯; ties ordered by confidence then age.
- **S2 · Start building sheet** (three choices with what each makes, footer "Idea moves to Building").
- **S3 · Drop sheet** (reason, required).

#### 5. Data
No migration. Type `idea`: stages Idea (todo) · Validating (in_progress) · Building (in_progress) · Launched (done) · Dropped (done), never on the board. `type_fields`: `pitch` (≤ 200), `impact`, `ease`, `confidence` (1–5), `builtAs` (task id), `assumptionsDocId`, `droppedReason`. The validation steps live in `workflow_settings.ideas` (the column D3 adds).

#### 6. Server
`createTaskAction` (`idea`); `scoreIdeaAction({ taskId, impact?, ease?, confidence? })`; `startBuildingAction({ taskId, as: 'project' | 'roadmap_item' | 'task' })` (one transaction; links both ways); `dropIdeaAction`; Launched set in `afterTaskTransition` when the built item completes or launches.

#### 7. Rules (`src/lib/workflows/ideas.ts`) and tests
`iceScore(i, e, c)` → product or null if any missing (tests: 4·3·2 = 24; missing → null). `rankIdeas(ideas)` (tests: score desc; ties by confidence then oldest; nulls last; Dropped excluded). `launchedFromBuilt(builtItem)` (tests: completed task → Launched; roadmap Launched → Launched; Cancelled → stays Building).

#### 8. Around it
Notifications: an idea you added moves to Building or is Dropped (Normal); nothing else. Overview: none. CLI / MCP: W9; `networkbase_idea_list` (read). Search: ideas show score and stage.

#### 9–10. Rollout and tests
Ships after F2, T1, T2. Unit (part 7); server (Start building makes exactly one item and links); contract test `ideas-design-contract.test.ts`; end to end (capture → score → validate → build as project → project completed → idea Launched).

#### 11. Calls
1. Score = Impact × Ease × Confidence (1–5 each); unscored ideas rank last. **[call]**
2. Validating adds the workspace's validation steps as subtasks. **[call]**
3. **Start building** makes a project, a roadmap item or a task, linked both ways. **[call]**
4. An idea becomes Launched by itself when what it became completes or launches. **[call]**
5. Ideas are never public. **[call]**
6. **A5.3 (2026-11-24):** Ideas' **+** makes an **Ideas** document at once (members only) holding the ranked block `{% project.ranked type="idea" %}`. The block (S1): # · Idea (name, pitch, "Built as AC-320") · Impact · Ease · Confidence as 1–5 pickers · Score (mono, "Not scored") · Stage in words · Validation "2 of 3" · ⋯ (**Start validating**, **Start building…**, **Drop…**); a one-line **+ Idea**; **Dropped (n)** folds with reasons; it scrolls sideways on phones. Members (not viewers) add, score, validate, build and drop; ideas are left out of every task read for people outside the workspace. **Start validating** adds the workspace's checklist (default Talk to 5 people · Landing page · First sign-up) as subtasks, once. **Start building** (S2) makes a project, a roadmap item (pitch as its outcome) or a task with the idea's name and pitch; the idea moves to Building with "Built as" (once), and its author is told. When that item completes (task, project) or launches (roadmap item), the idea becomes **Launched** by itself; canceled leaves it Building. **Drop** (S3) needs a reason; the author is told. A User interview shows **Save an insight as an idea** once Ideas is added, into the workspace's first Ideas document. **CLI/MCP:** `nb ideas list`, `nb ideas add "Template shop" --impact 4 --ease 3 --confidence 2` (agents may add), `networkbase_idea_list`. The validation checklist is edited later with Settings → Documents. Ideas is built. **[call]**

### 38.14 D5 · Team off-site (agreed 2026-11-18)

A **team off-site** is a **document in the Off-site section** (F2): dates, a place, who's coming, an **agenda** (Markdown, F2 call 8) and **checklists** whose rows are tasks (travel, rooms, sessions). It's 16.2's Team off-site setup without the parked Event planner's registrations and budget.

#### 1. References
| Reference | Rating / source | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **Off-Site Planning Kit** | 5.0 / 5 (16.1) | Travel, rooms, agenda, a checklist of what to book; private, no public page |
| 16.2 Team off-site setup | Agreed | Private; agenda by day; tasks for bookings |
| What the code has | Checked 2026-11-18 | F2 sections and task rows; T1 Calendar; members |

#### 2. The 18 layers (short form)
1. **Getting it:** **Team off-site** in "Blends into Documents": "Adds an Off-site section: plan a team trip in one document." 2. **Setting it up:** none. 3. **Items:** the off-site document (dates, place, attendees, agenda by day), checklists (**Before** · **Travel and rooms** · **Sessions** · **After**) as task rows, **Who's coming** (each attendee: Going · Can't go · Not answered). 4. **Views:** the document; the Off-site section by date; the dates on T1's Calendar as a span. 5. **Flow:** create → invite → people answer → book (rows) → the days (agenda) → After (notes, photos, action items). 6. **Surfaces:** header, Who's coming block, checklist blocks, agenda. 8. **Words:** Off-site · Dates · Place · Who's coming · Going · Can't go · Agenda · Before · Travel and rooms · Sessions · After. 9. **Links:** Tasks, Calendar, D1 (sessions can be meetings), Files (photos). 10. **People:** members; never public (16.2). 11–14. As F2. 15. **Notifications:** invited (Normal); 7 days before with open Before rows (Normal to their assignees). 16. **Trust:** members only; no budget or payments (parked); no personal travel details beyond what people type. 17–18. below.

#### 3. Walkthroughs
**W1** — Documents → Off-site **+**: name, dates (from–to), place (text), invite (members picker) → the document with the four checklist blocks prefilled (Before: Pick dates · Book venue · Share agenda; Travel and rooms: Book travel (one row per attendee, assigned to them) · Book rooms; Sessions: from the agenda; After: Share notes · Upload photos). **W2 · Answering** — each invited member sees **Going / Can't go** on the document and in My Work; the block shows counts and names. **W3 · Booking** — rows are tasks; "Book travel — Asha" is Asha's. **W4 · Agenda** — the agenda is Markdown by day ("Day 1 · Thu Mar 5"); a session line can become a D1 meeting with **Make a meeting**. **W5 · After** — action items from the sessions (F2 rows) and a photos link to Files. **W6 · Phone** — Going / Can't go as two big buttons. **W7 · CLI** — `nb offsites list`; agents may draft agendas.

#### 4. Screen spec
Header (MapPin icon, name, dates in mono, place, "6 going · 1 can't go · 2 not answered"); **Who's coming** block (names grouped by answer; buttons for the viewer); checklist blocks (F2); agenda (Markdown).

#### 5. Data
No migration beyond F2: document settings `section: 'offsite'`, `dateFrom`, `dateTo`, `place`, `invitedIds`, `answers` ({ userId: 'going' | 'cant' }). Answers are document settings, written without a version (F2 call 7).

#### 6. Server
`createOffsiteAction` (document + rows in one transaction; one Book travel row per invitee); `answerOffsiteAction({ docId, answer })` (invitees only); **Make a meeting** uses D1's `createMeetingAction`.

#### 7. Rules and tests
`offsiteCounts(invited, answers)`; `travelRows(invitees)` (one per person, assigned); tests for re-invites and people who leave the workspace (answers removed, rows unassigned).

#### 8–10. Around it, rollout, tests
Overview: an off-site within 30 days shows "Off-site in 12 days · 2 not answered". CLI as W7. Ships after F2. Unit and end to end (create → answers → rows → session made a meeting).

#### 11. Calls
1. An off-site is a document with checklists as tasks; registrations and budgets stay with the parked Event planner. **[call]**
2. **Who's coming** is a simple Going / Can't go per invited member, stored on the document. **[call]**
3. One "Book travel" row per invitee, assigned to them. **[call]**
4. Never public. **[call]**

### 38.15 D6 · Document templates, Docs site and Snippets (agreed 2026-11-18)

D6 makes the **32 workspace document templates** (26.3) real: they're offered in **New document** under "Start from", each a Markdown file in code with its sections and F2 blocks. It adds two Documents views: the **Docs site** (a three-column reading layout, optionally public) and **Snippets** (code snippets with Copy).

#### 1. References
| Reference | Rating / source | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| The template sections | 11.8, 12.5, 13.4–13.5, 14.4–14.7, 15.3, 17.7, 18.7, 19.7, 20.2–20.7, 21.2, 21.5, 22.2, 24.4, 24.7 | Each template's headings, guidance and blocks, as written there |

#### 2. The 18 layers (short form)
1. **Getting it:** templates show in **New document** for everyone; the Docs site and Snippets are Documents views switched on in Settings → Documents (both off by default). 2. **Setting it up:** which template groups show (defaults by category, section 6). 3. **Items:** a template = a Markdown file + a default section and kind; a snippet = a document with kind `snippet` and `language`. 4. **Views:** **Pages** (today) · **Docs site** · **Snippets**. 5. **Flow:** New document → Start from → a template → title → the document opens in Files' editor with the template's text. 6. **Surfaces:** the Start from list, the Docs site layout, the Snippets list. 8. **Words:** Start from · Blank · NetworkBase templates · From [organization] · Docs site · Show on docs site · Search docs · On this page · Previous · Next · Snippets · Language · Copy. 9. **Links:** F2 blocks inside templates; T3 (Report a bug from a Test plan); T5 (Write draft uses Blog post / Newsletter); O2 (release notes); CLI. 10. **People:** document permissions; the public Docs site shows only docs switched on. 11–14. As F2; the Docs site menu is a drawer on phones. 15. **Notifications:** none. 16. **Trust:** drafts never leak to the public Docs site. 17–18. below.

#### 3. The templates (where each lands)
| Group | Template (source) | Section · kind | Live blocks |
|---|---|---|---|
| Startup and business | Assumptions check · Value proposition · Business model canvas · Investor update (11.8) · Business plan (20.7) | Pages | BMC renders as a 3 × 3 canvas from its headings; Investor update has a goals block (D3) |
| Clients and creative | Client report (12.5) · Creative brief · Brand questionnaire · Case study (24.7) · Brand guide (14.7) | Pages | Client report's time and money parts show "Available when Money is added" |
| Product and engineering | Tech spec (13.4) · API docs (13.5) · PRD · FAQ · Persona (20.2–20.6) · Postmortem (21.2) · Test plan (21.5) | Pages | PRD links roadmap items (T2); Test plan's cases table with **Report a bug** on failed rows (T3); Postmortem links a bug |
| Content | Blog post · Newsletter · Content brief (14.4–14.6) · Show notes · Episode run sheet · Sponsor read (18.7) · Video script · Beat sheet · Short film script (19.7) · Call sheet (19.4) | Pages | Used by T5's Write draft |
| Learning | Class notes (15.3) | Pages | — |
| Non-profit | Grant proposal · Impact report (17.7) | Pages | Money parts hidden until Money; X4's report for organizations |

Meeting types (D1), launch presets (D2), goals (D3), ideas (D4) and off-sites (D5) are made from their own sections' **+**, not from this list.

#### 4. Walkthroughs
**W1 · Start from a template** — **New document** → **Start from**: Blank · **NetworkBase templates** (groups as above, each row with a one-line purpose) · **From [organization]** (as today) · **Markdown file from Files** (as today). Picking **Tech spec** asks a title and makes `/Docs/Tech spec – Sign-in.md` with the template's text; the editor opens.

**W2 · Test plan** — cases are a Markdown table (Case · Steps · Expected · Result · Tester · Date); the rendered document shows "Pass 14 · Fail 2 · Blocked 1 · 82 %" worked out from the Result column, and **Report a bug** on each Fail row (opens T3's module with steps and expected filled, linked back).

**W3 · Docs site** — Settings → Documents → **Docs site** on: Documents gains the **Docs site** view: Menu (sections from F2 plus the docs' own headings order, drag to order) · the page · On this page (headings, current one marked) · ⌘K search across docs · Previous / Next. Each document's ⋯ has **Show on docs site** (off by default).

**W4 · Public Docs site** — when the workspace's Documents tab is public, visitors get the Docs site view with only docs switched on; others don't exist for them ("Page not available").

**W5 · Snippets** — Settings → Documents → **Snippets** on: **New snippet** (name, language, code, what it's for, tags, source link) makes a small document (kind `snippet`); the Snippets view lists them with **Copy**; snippets appear in ⌘K.

**W6 · CLI** — `nb docs new --template tech-spec "Sign-in"`; `nb snippets list`, `nb snippets get "Retry with backoff"` prints the code; agents read snippets with a member's access.

#### 5. Data
No migration. Templates are files in `templates/docs/*.md` with a front-matter line (group, section, kind, description). Document settings (F2 JSON) gain `docsSite` (boolean), `docsOrder` (number), and for snippets `language`, `tags`. `workflow_settings.docs` (D3's column) holds `siteEnabled`, `snippetsEnabled` and the template groups shown.

#### 6. Server
`createDocFromTemplateAction({ projectId, templateId, title })` (makes the file and the document, applies section and kind); `setDocsSiteAction({ docId, on, order? })`; `searchDocsAction({ projectId, query })` (titles, headings and text; public callers see only docs-site documents); `createSnippetAction`; `readSnippetsAction`.

#### 7. Rules and tests
`testPlanSummary(markdownTable)` (tests: Pass/Fail/Blocked/Not run counts; unknown values counted as Not run); `docsSiteMenu(docs)` (tests: sections order, "Other" for docs with no section, hidden docs excluded); `publicDocVisible(doc, workspace)` (tests: off → hidden; Documents not public → hidden).

#### 8–10. Around it, rollout, tests
CLI and MCP (`networkbase_doc_create` gains `template`; `networkbase_snippet_get`, read). Ships after F2; templates can be added one group at a time. Contract tests for the Start from list and the Docs site layout; end to end (template → document; Docs site public with one doc on; snippet copy).

#### 11. Calls
1. Templates are Markdown files in code, shown under **Start from** next to organization templates. **[call]**
2. Parts that need parked tabs (Money, Pipeline) show "Available when [tab] is added". **[call]**
3. The Business model canvas renders as a 3 × 3 grid from its headings; no separate canvas block. **[call]**
4. Test plan results are a Markdown table; the pass rate and **Report a bug** are worked out when it's shown. **[call]**
5. The Docs site and Snippets are off by default; public Docs site shows only documents switched on. **[call]**

### 38.16 O1 · Assets (agreed 2026-11-18)

**Assets** is a view in **Files**: a gallery of the workspace's images, video, audio, fonts and brand colors, with **asset details** (type, tags, usage rights, production status), **Used in** (which content and documents use it), new-version notices, and **comments pinned to a spot on an image or a moment in a video or audio file**. Assets stay files (decision 1).

#### 1. References
| Reference | Rating / source | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **Brand Assets** (Notion) | 4.8 / 68 (14.3) | A gallery by type with details and usage notes |
| Simple Design Moodboard | 14.3 | A board-like gallery view |
| 18.5 · 19.5 · 19.6 · 22.5 · 24.3 | Agreed | Audio takes, footage types and outside-storage links, timestamped comments, production status for game assets, pinned image comments |
| 28.4 smaller rule | Agreed | Pinned and timestamped comments share one anchor shape: a spot (x, y) or a moment (seconds) |
| What the code has | Checked 2026-11-18 | `workspace_nodes` with `mime_type`, `current_version` and a **`metadata` JSON**; file versions that only grow; **comments exist only on change sets and merge requests** (line anchors); no comments on plain files |

#### 2. The 18 layers (short form)
1. **Getting it:** **Assets** in "Blends into Files": "Adds an Assets view to Files with details, Used in and pinned comments." 2. **Setting it up:** asset types (Logo · Photo · Illustration · Video · Footage · Audio · Font · Template · Other), production statuses (Concept · Work in progress · Review · Final, on by default for Game dev), brand colors. 3. **Items:** an asset = a file with `metadata.asset` (type, tags, usage rights, credit, production status, notes); a color (name, hex); an **outside link** (a typed URL to storage elsewhere, never fetched). 4. **Views:** **Assets** gallery (grid, by type, filters), **Colors**, the file viewer with comments. 5. **Flow:** upload or mark a file as an asset → details → used in content or documents → new version → people using it are told. 6. **Surfaces:** gallery card, details panel, Used in list, color swatches, comment pins on images, comment markers on the media timeline. 8. **Words:** Assets · Asset type · Tags · Usage rights · Credit · Production status · Concept · Work in progress · Review · Final · Used in · New version · Colors · Pin a comment · At 0:42 · Outside link. 9. **Links:** T5 (content assets), F2 / D6 documents (images), T3 (screenshots on bugs), Files versions. 10. **People:** file permissions; comments for members; public only where Files is public (comments never public). 11–14. Gallery skeleton; live new uploads; phone gallery two columns; comments reachable by keyboard (pins listed in order). 15. **Notifications:** below. 16. **Trust:** outside links are never fetched (26.5); usage rights are text. 17–18. below.

#### 3. Walkthroughs
**W1** — Files → **Assets** view: images, video, audio and fonts in the workspace shown as a grid (other files hidden); empty: "Upload images, video or audio, or mark files as assets." **W2 · Details** — selecting a card opens the details panel: type, tags, usage rights, credit, production status, notes; **Used in** lists content items (T5) and documents that include it. **W3 · Pinned comment on an image** — in the viewer, **Pin a comment** → click a spot → a numbered pin and a comment thread; pins belong to the version they were made on ("on version 3"). **W4 · Comment at a moment** — on video or audio, **Comment at 0:42** (the current time); markers appear on the timeline; clicking jumps there. **W5 · New version** — uploading a new version keeps comments on the old one (shown "on version 3", **Show**); people assigned to items in **Used in** get "New version of Logo-dark.svg". **W6 · Production status** — game assets move Concept → Work in progress → Review → Final; the gallery groups by status (a board-like grouping, no drag). **W7 · Colors** — **Colors** lists swatches (name, hex, copy); a Brand guide document (D6) can show them. **W8 · Outside link** — **Add outside link** (name, URL, type) for footage stored elsewhere; shown as a card with a link icon; never opened by the server. **W9 · Phone** — two-column grid; comments as a list with pins numbered. **W10 · CLI** — `nb assets list --type logo`, `nb assets tag Logo-dark.svg brand`.

#### 4. Screen spec
Gallery card (thumbnail, name, type chip, production status chip, version "v3"); details panel (fields above, Used in, versions); viewer with **Pin a comment** / **Comment at [time]** buttons, pins as numbered circles with a list beside; Colors grid.

#### 5. Data
**Migration `0109_assets_file_comments.sql`:**
- **`file_comments`:** id, workspace_id, node_id → workspace_nodes (cascade), version int, anchor jsonb NULL ({ x, y } in 0–1 of the image, or { t } seconds), parent_comment_id, content, author_id, resolved_at, created_at, deleted_at; index (node_id, version).
- **Asset details** in `workspace_nodes.metadata.asset` (no migration): { type, tags[], usageRights, credit, productionStatus, notes }.
- **Outside links** are entries in `workflow_settings.assets.outsideLinks` (name, URL, type, tags), not files.
- **Colors** in `workflow_settings.assets.colors` (D3's column).
- **Used in** is worked out on read from T5's `type_fields.assets`, documents' image links and task file attachments.

#### 6. Server
`setAssetDetailsAction({ nodeId, details })` (file edit permission); `addFileCommentAction({ nodeId, version, anchor?, content, parentId? })`, `resolveFileCommentAction`; `readAssetsAction(projectId, filters)`; `usedInAction(nodeId)`; new-version notices sent from the existing file version save path when an asset has Used in entries; `saveColorsAction`; `addOutsideLinkAction` (URL validated, never fetched).

#### 7. Rules and tests
`isAssetMime(mime)` (tests: image, video, audio, font true; zip false); `anchorValid(anchor, kind)` (x and y within 0–1 for images; t within duration for media); `usedIn(nodeId, items, docs)` (tests: counts each place once); `versionComments(comments, version)`.

#### 8–10. Around it, rollout, tests
Notifications: a comment on an asset you uploaded (Normal); new version of an asset your item uses (Normal, assignees). Search: assets by tags. Ships after F1 (catalog) and independently of T5. Tests: unit; server (comments on a version stay on it; outside links never fetched); contract test `assets-design-contract.test.ts`; end to end (upload → details → pin comment → new version → notice).

#### 11. Calls
1. Assets are files; details live in the file's metadata. **[call]**
2. A new `file_comments` table gives every file comments, with an optional spot or moment anchor. **[call]**
3. Comments stay on the version they were made on. **[call]**
4. New versions notify the people assigned to items that use the asset. **[call]**
5. Outside links are stored as typed URLs and never fetched. **[call]**
6. Production status is a field shown as a grouping, not a board. **[call]**

### 38.17 O2 · Changelog and scheduled Updates (agreed 2026-11-18)

O2 adds two things to **Updates**: a **Changelog** filter that shows release Updates as versions with **Added · Improved · Fixed**, and **scheduled Updates** that post themselves at a set time (also used by T5's NetworkBase channel).

#### 1. References
| Reference | Rating / source | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| **Changelog** | 4.8 / 9 (13.7) | A dated list of changes per version |
| 13.7 · 14.2 | Agreed | Release Updates only; three groups; scheduled Updates from a content item |
| What the code has | Checked 2026-11-18 | Updates with type **release**; **one draft per person per workspace** (`workspace_update_drafts`, no publish time); the hourly due job with exact-time wake events |

#### 2. The 18 layers (short form)
1. **Getting it:** **Changelog and scheduled Updates** in "Blends into Updates": "Adds a Changelog view and lets Updates post at a set time." 2. **Setting it up:** none. 3. **Items:** a release Update with a version and three groups; a **scheduled Update** (content, type, visibility, media, publish time). 4. **Views:** Updates gets **All updates · Changelog · Scheduled** (Scheduled for members). 5. **Flow:** write → **Schedule** (date and time) → it waits in Scheduled → posts at the time → (from T5) the content item becomes Published with its link. 6. **Surfaces:** the composer's **Schedule** option, the Scheduled list, the changelog blocks. 8. **Words:** Changelog · Added · Improved · Fixed · Schedule · Scheduled · Posts at · Post now · Cancel. 9. **Links:** D2 (release Update prefill), T5 (NetworkBase channel), T3 (Fixed). 10. **People:** members who can post Updates can schedule; the public sees Changelog when Updates is public (13.7). 11–14. Empty "No releases yet"; phone one release per card. 15. **Notifications:** below. 16. **Trust:** a scheduled Update posts with its author's permissions at the time; if they lost the right, it doesn't post. 17–18. below.

#### 3. Walkthroughs
**W1 · Schedule** — in the Updates composer, the Post button's arrow → **Schedule…** (date and time in the workspace time zone) → **Schedule**; the draft clears and the Update appears in **Scheduled** with "Posts Thu 10:00". **W2 · Edit or cancel** — in Scheduled: **Edit**, **Post now**, **Cancel**. **W3 · Posting** — at the time the hourly job's exact wake posts it as the author (likes, comments as any Update); a content item linked to it (T5) becomes Published with this Update as its link. **W4 · Release Update** — D2's **Post an Update** opens the composer with type **release**, a version line and three groups; the author edits and posts or schedules. **W5 · Changelog** — Updates → **Changelog**: release Updates only, each as "v2.4 · Dec 12, 2026" with Added / Improved / Fixed lists; a release written by hand without groups shows as one block. **W6 · Phone** — Scheduled and Changelog as lists. **W7 · CLI** — `nb updates schedule --at "2026-12-03 10:00" --file post.md`, `nb updates scheduled`, `nb changelog`.

#### 4. Screen spec
Composer split button (**Post** · **Schedule…**); schedule sheet (date, time, time zone shown); Scheduled rows (excerpt, type, visibility, posts at, author, Edit · Post now · Cancel); changelog block (version in mono, date, three group labels with lists, "Show older" paging).

#### 5. Data
**Migration `0110_scheduled_updates.sql`:**
- **`workspace_scheduled_updates`:** id, workspace_id, author_id, content, update_type, visibility, media jsonb, entity_refs jsonb, publish_at, published_update_id NULL, cancelled_at NULL, failed_reason NULL, source_task_id NULL (T5), created_at; index (publish_at) WHERE published_update_id IS NULL AND cancelled_at IS NULL.
- **Release structure:** a release Update's content follows a fixed Markdown shape (first line `## v2.4`, then `### Added`, `### Improved`, `### Fixed`); the Changelog reads it; no new column.

#### 6. Server
`scheduleUpdateAction`, `editScheduledUpdateAction`, `cancelScheduledUpdateAction`, `postScheduledNowAction`; the due job's new step `fireDueScheduledUpdates()` (batch of 50, re-checks the author's right to post, writes `published_update_id` or `failed_reason`, sets T5's published link); `readChangelogAction(projectId, cursor)`.

#### 7. Rules and tests
`parseRelease(content)` → { version, added[], improved[], fixed[] } or plain (tests: all three groups; missing groups empty; no version → plain); `dueScheduled(rows, now)` (tests: cancelled and posted excluded); `canStillPost(author, workspace)`.

#### 8–10. Around it, rollout, tests
Notifications: your scheduled Update posted (Normal) or failed (Important, with the reason). Rides the existing hourly job (Inngest free limit respected; no new function). Tests: unit; server (posting rechecks rights; one post per row even if the job runs twice); end to end (schedule → post → T5 item Published; release → Changelog).

#### 11. Calls
1. Scheduled Updates get their own small table; drafts stay one per person. **[call]**
2. Posting rides the existing hourly job's exact-time wake events. **[call]**
3. A scheduled Update rechecks the author's right to post at the time; if it's gone, it fails with a notice. **[call]**
4. The Changelog reads a fixed Markdown shape in release Updates; no new column. **[call]**

### 38.18 O3 · Learning path (agreed 2026-11-18)

A **learning path** is a **Path** view in **Sprints**: the workspace's steps (sprints, which can now have **no dates**) in order, each with its **lessons**, and each person ticking lessons **Done** for themselves. It's 15.2's self-paced Learning path, blended into Sprints; Coaching organizations use C2's version (31.3).

#### 1. References
| Reference | Rating / source | What we take |
|---|---|---|
| Python · AI Engineering · Power BI Roadmap | 4.8–4.9 / 10–100+ (15.1) | Ordered steps with lessons, no dates, progress per person |
| Study & Learning OS · Online Course Tracker | 4.8 (15.1) | Mark done, notes, links per lesson |
| 15.2 · C2 (31.3) | Agreed | `class_lesson` items; undated phases; a progress table (step × learner), not copies; no streaks or points; agents can't mark done |
| What the code has | Checked 2026-11-18 | Sprints require **start and end dates** (`workspace_sprints` not null) and can auto-start; **assignments exist only in organizations**, so 28.4's "reuse everyone assignments" doesn't work for ordinary workspaces |

#### 2. The 18 layers (short form)
1. **Getting it:** **Learning path** in "Blends into Sprints": "Adds a Path view to Sprints. Steps can be undated; everyone ticks their own lessons." 2. **Setting it up:** pacing **Self-paced** (undated steps) or **Scheduled** (dated sprints as today); lock in order (off). 3. **Items:** a **step** (a sprint, dates optional, order), a **lesson** (type `class_lesson`, in a step: before / during / after sections, links, files, estimated minutes), a **progress mark** (person × lesson, done at). 4. **Views:** **Path** (steps down the page, lessons inside, my ticks), **Progress** (people × steps, for admins). 5. **Flow:** admins build steps and lessons → people open the path → tick lessons Done → the step shows their progress → next step. 6. **Surfaces:** Path, lesson panel, Progress table, the step header. 8. **Words:** Learning path · Step · Lesson · Mark done · Done · Up next · Self-paced · Scheduled · Lock in order · Progress. 9. **Links:** Sprints, Documents (lesson notes, F2), Files, My Work ("Up next"), C2 for organizations. 10. **People:** admins build; members and viewers tick their own; admins see Progress; a self-paced path can be made public read-only by an admin (15.2's call) without anyone's progress. 11–14. Live ticks; phone shows one step at a time; checkboxes labelled with the lesson title. 15. **Notifications:** none for ticks; a new step added → members (Summary). 16. **Trust:** progress is seen by the person and admins only; agents can't mark lessons done. 17–18. below.

#### 3. Walkthroughs
**W1** — Asha adds **Learning path**; Sprints gains **Path** and **Progress**; a sheet asks **Self-paced** or **Scheduled**. **W2 · Steps** — **+ Step** (name, optional dates when Scheduled); steps reorder by drag or "Move up / down". **W3 · Lessons** — **+ Lesson** in a step opens the New module on **Lesson** (type `class_lesson`; Before · During · After sections, links, files, minutes); lessons never go on the board. **W4 · Learning** — Dev opens Path: each step shows "3 of 7 done", his next lesson is marked **Up next**; **Mark done** ticks it for him only. **W5 · Lock in order** — when on, a step's lessons open only after the previous step is done (for that person); a locked step shows "Finish Step 2 first". **W6 · Progress** — admins see a table of people × steps with "3/7" cells and the last activity date; no ranking. **W7 · Public path** — an admin can make a self-paced path public: visitors see steps and lessons, never progress. **W8 · Phone** — one step at a time with big Mark done buttons. **W9 · CLI** — `nb path`, `nb path done NB-410` (people only; agents refused).

#### 4. Screen spec
Path: step headers (order number, name, dates if any, "3 of 7 done" for the viewer), lesson rows (checkbox, title, minutes, Up next chip, lock icon); lesson panel (F3 panel with Before · During · After, links, files); Progress table (people rows, step columns, cells "3/7", sortable by name only).

#### 5. Data
**Migration `0111_learning_path.sql`:**
- `workspace_sprints.start_date` and `end_date` become **nullable**; a check keeps both null or both set; **auto-start skips sprints without dates** (C2's need, done here).
- `workspace_sprints.path_position int NULL` (order on the path).
- **`lesson_progress`:** task_id → tasks (cascade), user_id → profiles (cascade), done_at; primary key (task_id, user_id).
- Workspace setting in `workflow_settings.path`: { pacing: 'self' | 'scheduled', lockInOrder, public }.
- Lesson `type_fields`: `before`, `during`, `after` (Markdown ≤ 20,000 each), `minutes`, `links[]`.

#### 6. Server
`createStepAction` (a sprint with optional dates and a path position), `reorderStepsAction`, `markLessonAction({ taskId, done })` (the person themselves; refused for agents), `readPathAction(projectId, viewerId)`, `readProgressAction(projectId)` (admins). Every query that assumed sprint dates handles nulls (sprint lists show "No dates").

#### 7. Rules and tests
`stepProgress(lessons, marks, userId)`; `upNext(steps, marks, userId)` (tests: first undone lesson in the first unfinished step); `isLocked(step, steps, marks, userId, lockInOrder)`; `sprintDatesValid(start, end)` (both null or start ≤ end); `autoStartEligible(sprint)` (tests: undated never auto-starts).

#### 8–10. Around it, rollout, tests
My Work: "Up next: Lesson 4 · Step 2". Notifications: none for ticks. Rollout: migration 0111 relaxes sprint dates; audit every sprint date read first (a list of call sites is part of the plan). Tests: unit; server (agents can't mark done; undated sprints never auto-start; Scheduled paths keep dates required); end to end (self-paced path → lessons → ticks → Progress).

#### 11. Calls
1. Progress is a small `lesson_progress` table (person × lesson), not assignment copies; this replaces 28.4's smaller rule for ordinary workspaces. **[call]**
2. Sprint dates become optional for path steps, and undated sprints never auto-start (also unblocks C2). **[call]**
3. Lock in order is off by default. **[call]**
4. Admins see Progress as plain counts; no ranking, streaks or points. **[call]**
5. A self-paced path can be made public without anyone's progress. **[call]**
6. Agents can't mark lessons done. **[call]**

**Section 38 complete:** all 17 blend rounds are designed at the inch-by-inch depth.
